The interface of $I$ therefore transmits the $4^a$ product ready states of $\{Q_j:j\in A\}$ without error to registers outside $I$, and since discarding output registers does not raise a capacity, $C_{\partial I}\ge a\ln4$. For $I_A$ the registers outside $I_A$ whose final state depends on the input are the $B_j$, $j\in A$: $E_j$, $Q_j$ and $F_j$ belong to $I_A$, and the clocks, enable registers and drives carry prescribed states. The input-dependent output is supported on the $4^a$-dimensional space of ready labels of $\{B_j\}$, and on its $k$-fold tensor power for $k$ parallel uses, so the Holevo bound gives $C_{\partial I_A}\le a\ln4$. At the early cut $R$ is in the pure product state $|1\rangle^{\otimes n}$, so $S(\rho_{RI})-S(\rho_I)=0$ and $F_0(I)=C_{\partial I}$. At the late cut the exchanges have moved the content of $H_j$ to $R_j$, so $\rho_{QR}$ is the pure product of the $n$ states (K.3d.1e.3) on $(Q_j,R_j)$ and the global state is $\rho_{QR}\otimes\rho_{\mathrm{rest}}$. Then $S(\rho_{RI})-S(\rho_I)=S(\rho_{RQ_A})-S(\rho_{Q_A})=(n-a)\ln4-a\ln4$, and $F_{t_{\mathrm{comp}}}(I)=C_{\partial I}+(n-2a)\ln4\ge(n-a)\ln4$. Equality for $I_A$ follows from $C_{\partial I_A}=a\ln4$.

Item 2. By (K.3d.1f.1) the early minimum over all candidates is $0$, attained by $\varnothing$, and $a\ge1$ gives $F_0\ge\ln4$. The late minimum is $0$, attained by $I_{\mathrm{full}}$, and $a\le n-1$ gives $F_{t_{\mathrm{comp}}}\ge\ln4$; $F_{t_{\mathrm{comp}}}(\varnothing)=S(\rho_R)=n\ln4$. Candidates with the same key set can tie, for instance when they differ by a body whose final state does not depend on the keys.

Item 3. $I_A\setminus I_{\{j\}}=I_{A\setminus\{j\}}$ is a candidate and $\Delta C=a\ln4-(a-1)\ln4$. By the entropies of item 1, $I_{\mathrm{pred}}(R;I_{\{j\}}\mid I_{A\setminus\{j\}})$ is $0$ at the early cut and $(n-2a+2)\ln4-(n-2a)\ln4$ at the late cut, and (K.3c.1a.2) gives the two deletion values and, with item 3 of Proposition K.3c.1a, deletion-minimality. If $E_j\notin I$, the registers $(B_j,E_j)$ outside $I$ receive the eight distinct images of the basis states of $Q_j$ under (K.3d.1e.4), so the capacity of that key's interface is $\ln8$.

Item 4 is $C_{\partial I_A}=a\ln4$ with the value of $G_{\mathrm{op}}$ in (K.3d.1e.1); the $n$ admission services act on disjoint registers and clocks and their product is $\mathcal G^{\otimes n}$.

Item 5. The two formulas in (K.3d.1f.3) are (K.3d.1f.1) divided by $n$, with $|U_A|=a/n$. Lower bound: if $U_m\to U$ in $L^1$ with finite $\liminf$, then along that subsequence the $U_m$ are cell unions and $|U_m|\to|U|$. Recovery: let $U_m$ be the union of the cells of the $m$-grid in which $U$ has more than half the measure; then $\|1_{U_m}-1_U\|_{L^1}\le2\|\mathbb E_m1_U-1_U\|_{L^1}\to0$, where $\mathbb E_m$ is the average over the cells of the $m$-grid, and $|U_m|\to|U|$. The last statement is read off (K.3d.1f.3).

Item 6. By item 9 of the construction the metric near $z=z_c$ is the product $-c^2dt^2+dz^2+g_T$, so the section is totally geodesic and has area $A_n$. By item 4 every body is at a positive distance from the section at $t_{\mathrm{comp}}$, and no event window meets $(t_s-\tau,t_s)$. A sufficiently small normal variation therefore contains the same bodies and has the same future interface, so $C_{\partial I}$ and the entropies are unchanged. $\square$

<a id="definition-k3d4-horizon-moment-operator-and-frame-potential-k-design-certificate"></a>**Definition K.3d.4 (Horizon Moment-Operator and Frame-Potential $k$-Design Certificate).** A horizon $k$-design certificate is a finite record
$$
\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{Hdesign}}
=
\left(
\mathcal H_{\mathrm{edge}},
\nu_H,
t_{\mathrm{des}},
\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}},
\mathcal M_t,
\mathcal F_t,
\gamma_t,
N_t,
\varepsilon_t^{\mathrm{mom}},
\varepsilon_t^{\mathrm{frame}},
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{emit}},
\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{tr}},
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Page}},
\chi_{\mathrm{Hdesign}}
\right)
\tag{K.3d.4}
$$
where:

1. $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{edge}}$ is the finite horizon edge-code Hilbert space on the branch.

2. $\nu_H$ is a finitely supported probability measure on horizon update unitaries generated by the retained MPU edge dynamics.

3. $t_{\mathrm{des}}\ge2$ is the design order required for the Page or scrambling estimate being claimed.

4. $\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}}$ is the Haar moment projection on $\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{edge}}^{\otimes t_{\mathrm{des}}})$.

5. The one-step moment operator is
$$
\mathcal M_t(\nu_H)(X)
=
\mathbb E_{U\sim\nu_H}
\left[
U^{\otimes t_{\mathrm{des}}}X(U^\dagger)^{\otimes t_{\mathrm{des}}}
\right].
\tag{K.3d.4.1}
$$
It satisfies the certified gap inequality
$$
\left\|
\left(\mathcal M_t(\nu_H)-\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}}\right)
\left(I-\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}}\right)
\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le
1-\gamma_t,
\qquad
0<\gamma_t\le1.
\tag{K.3d.4.2}
$$

6. $N_t$ is the certified number of horizon update steps and
$$
\varepsilon_t^{\mathrm{mom}}
\ge
\left\|\mathcal M_t(\nu_H^{*N_t})-\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{emit}}
\tag{K.3d.4.3}
$$
is the moment-operator error entering the radiation channel.

7. $\mathcal F_t$ is the normalized $t_{\mathrm{des}}$-frame potential of $\nu_H^{*N_t}$ and
$$
0
\le
\mathcal F_t(\nu_H^{*N_t})-\mathcal F_t(\mathrm{Haar})
\le
\varepsilon_t^{\mathrm{frame}}
\tag{K.3d.4.4}
$$
is the certified frame-potential error.

8. $\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the trace-continuity conversion record. It is either absent, in which case the certificate supplies moment/Page-purity control only, or it supplies a coupling of $\rho_E^{\mathrm{PU}}(t)$ with a Haar reduced state $\rho_E^{\mathrm{Haar}}(t)$ having the dimensions registered in Theorem K.3. For almost every paired state, the record proves
$$
\frac12\left\|\rho_E^{\mathrm{PU}}(t)-\rho_E^{\mathrm{Haar}}(t)\right\|_1
\le
\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{tr}}
\left(\varepsilon_t^{\mathrm{mom}},\varepsilon_t^{\mathrm{frame}},d_E,d_L,t_{\mathrm{des}}\right)
=:\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Page}},
\qquad
0\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Page}}\le1-\frac1{d_E}.
\tag{K.3d.4.5}
$$

9. $\chi_{\mathrm{Hdesign}}$ records that the update support, moment gap, frame potential, step count, emission error, trace-continuity conversion, and Page error follow from the declared finite source independently of any Page-curve reconstruction used for comparison.

A base moment-design certificate is accepted for Page-purity estimates when items 1--7 and 9 hold. A von Neumann Page-curve estimate additionally requires the trace-continuity slot in item 8.
**Definition K.3d.4a (Horizon Golay-Expander Design Certificate).** A horizon Golay-expander design certificate is a finite record
$$
\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{HGol}}
=
\left(
\mathcal G_{24}^{H},
\mathcal S_H,
\nu_H,
t_{\mathrm{des}},
\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}},
\gamma_t^{G},
N_t,
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{emit}},
S_H,
p_t,
\chi_{\mathrm{HGol}}
\right)
\tag{K.3d.4a.1}
$$
where:

1. $\mathcal G_{24}^{H}$ is the marked horizon Golay-Leech syndrome frame inherited from the retained horizon edge code;

2. $\mathcal S_H$ is a finite symmetric support of horizon update unitaries generated by syndrome permutations, syndrome phase gates, and ND-RID refresh-compatible edge moves preserving $\mathcal G_{24}^{H}$;

3. $\nu_H$ is a probability measure supported on $\mathcal S_H$;

4. $t_{\mathrm{des}}\ge2$ is the required design order;

5. $\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}}$ is the Haar moment projection on $\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{edge}}^{\otimes t_{\mathrm{des}}})$;

6. the moment operator
$$
\mathcal M_t^{G}(\nu_H)(X)
=
\mathbb E_{U\sim\nu_H}
\left[
U^{\otimes t_{\mathrm{des}}}X(U^\dagger)^{\otimes t_{\mathrm{des}}}
\right]
\tag{K.3d.4a.2}
$$
has a certified Golay-expander gap
$$
\left\|
\left(\mathcal M_t^{G}(\nu_H)-\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}}\right)
\left(I-\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}}\right)
\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le
1-\gamma_t^{G},
\qquad
0<\gamma_t^{G}\le1;
\tag{K.3d.4a.3}
$$

7. $S_H=A_H/(4L_P^2)$ is the horizon capacity in nats on the branch, and $p_t$ is the certified polynomial overhead for the $t_{\mathrm{des}}$ moment representation;

8. if a capacity-scaled lower bound is claimed, the certificate supplies finite $S_H>0$, finite $p_t>0$, and a constant $c_t>0$ such that
$$
\gamma_t^{G}\ge \frac{c_t}{S_Hp_t};
\tag{K.3d.4a.4}
$$

9. $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the finite emission-channel mismatch used in Definition K.3d.4;

10. $\chi_{\mathrm{HGol}}$ records that $\mathcal S_H,\nu_H,\gamma_t^{G},N_t,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{emit}}$, and any constants in (K.3d.4a.4) were fixed before Page-curve comparison.

**Theorem K.3d.4b (Golay-Expander Certificate Supplies the Horizon Design Gate).** An accepted $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{HGol}}$ canonically supplies the moment-operator part of a horizon $k$-design certificate $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{Hdesign}}$ of Definition K.3d.4 with
$$
\gamma_t=\gamma_t^{G},
\qquad
\varepsilon_t^{\mathrm{mom}}
=
(1-\gamma_t^{G})^{N_t}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{emit}}.
\tag{K.3d.4b.1}
$$
Consequently
$$
\left\|
\mathcal M_t^{G}(\nu_H^{*N_t})-
\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}}
\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le
(1-\gamma_t^{G})^{N_t}.
\tag{K.3d.4b.2}
$$
If the accepted Golay-expander record also supplies the frame-potential evaluation, then
$$
0\le
\mathcal F_t(\nu_H^{*N_t})-
\mathcal F_t(\mathrm{Haar})
\le
\varepsilon_t^{\mathrm{frame}}.
\tag{K.3d.4b.3}
$$
If, in addition, it supplies the trace-continuity conversion $\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{tr}}$, then the von Neumann Page error is the certified value
$$
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Page}}
=
\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{tr}}
\left((1-\gamma_t^{G})^{N_t}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{emit}},\varepsilon_t^{\mathrm{frame}},d_E,d_L,t_{\mathrm{des}}\right).
\tag{K.3d.4b.4}
$$
If the capacity-scaled gap (K.3d.4a.4) is part of the accepted record, then for every $0<\varepsilon<1$, every integer $N_t$ satisfying
$$
N_t
\ge
\frac{S_Hp_t}{c_t}
\log\frac{1}{\varepsilon}
\tag{K.3d.4b.5}
$$
obeys
$$
(1-\gamma_t^{G})^{N_t}
\le
e^{-N_t\gamma_t^{G}}
\le
\varepsilon.
\tag{K.3d.4b.6}
$$

*Proof.* Definition K.3d.4a supplies a finite edge Hilbert space, update measure, design order, Haar moment projection, one-step moment gap, step count, emission error, and structural-independence record. Forgetting the Golay-origin labels gives the moment part of Definition K.3d.4 with $\gamma_t=\gamma_t^G$. Repeated application of the moment gap gives (K.3d.4b.2), and adding the emission mismatch gives the first equality in (K.3d.4b.1). Frame-potential and trace-continuity statements require the additional records displayed in Definition K.3d.4; when supplied, they give (K.3d.4b.3) and (K.3d.4b.4) by their definitions. The capacity-scaled gap estimate is the same exponential contraction calculation as before. ∎

<a id="definition-k3d4c-horizon-entropy-continuity-promotion-certificate"></a>**Definition K.3d.4c (Horizon Entropy-Continuity Promotion Certificate).** A horizon entropy-continuity promotion certificate is a finite record
$$
\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{PageTV}}
=
(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{base}},d_E,d_L,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Page}},\chi_{\mathrm{PageTV}})
\tag{K.3d.4c.1}
$$
where $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{base}}$ is either an accepted horizon moment-operator certificate $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{Hdesign}}$ of Definition K.3d.4 or an accepted Golay-expander certificate $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{HGol}}$ of Definition K.3d.4a. The base certificate supplies the registered moment/Golay branch only; the additional promotion data, not $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{base}}$ by itself, certify a coupling of the PU reduced early-radiation state and the Haar reduced state satisfying
$$
\frac12
\left\|
\rho_E^{\mathrm{PU}}(t)-\rho_E^{\mathrm{Haar}}(t)
\right\|_1
\le
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Page}},
\qquad
0\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Page}}\le1-\frac1{d_E(t)}
\tag{K.3d.4c.2}
$$
for the registered evaporation time and dimensions. The record $\chi_{\mathrm{PageTV}}$ verifies that the coupling protocol, dimension ledger, norm, and error ceiling are determined by the stated source and bounds independently of the compared Page curve. This promotion certificate is stronger than a moment-design certificate: a bare $t_{\mathrm{des}}=2$ moment certificate controls the Haar Page-purity observable, while the von Neumann entropy estimate of Theorem K.3 requires the trace-coupled condition (K.3d.4c.2).

**Remark K.3d.4c.a (Status of the Promotion Data).** The trace-coupled bound (K.3d.4c.2) is an additional certified hypothesis, not a consequence of the base moment-design certificate alone. A derivation of (K.3d.4c.2) from $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{Hdesign}}$ would have to supply an explicit high-moment-to-trace-norm upgrade theorem, including the required scaling of $t_{\mathrm{des}}$ in $d_E$ and the associated error constants. No general logarithmic lower bound on $t_{\mathrm{des}}$ is claimed without a specified approximation theorem and norm-to-entropy conversion. Alternatively, the certificate may supply a separate dynamical coupling or trace-mixing estimate directly in trace norm. Construction K.3d.4h supplies the original physical horizon code's separately proved trace coupling and moment certificate; Proposition K.3d.4g distinguishes its completed-cut output from full-carrier mixing and continuous partial-route Page claims.

**Definition K.3d.4d (Relative-Entropy Contraction Trace-Coupling Certificate).** A relative-entropy contraction trace-coupling certificate is a finite record
$$
\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{REC-TV}}
=
(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{base}},\Gamma_t,D_0,\gamma_{\mathrm{REC}},N_t,\chi_{\mathrm{REC}})
\tag{K.3d.4d.1}
$$
where $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{base}}$ is an accepted certificate of Definition K.3d.4 or K.3d.4a, $\Gamma_t$ is a certified coupling of the PU reduced early-radiation state $\rho_E^{\mathrm{PU}}(t)$ and the Haar reduced state $\rho_E^{\mathrm{Haar}}(t)$ on the same early-radiation Hilbert space, $D_0<\infty$ is an initial relative-entropy ceiling, $\gamma_{\mathrm{REC}}>0$ is a certified entropy-contraction rate per retained cycle, and $N_t$ is the retained-cycle counter. The record is accepted only if the relative entropy is finite on the certified support and it certifies, before Page-curve comparison, that every paired state in the support of $\Gamma_t$ obeys
$$
D(\rho_E^{\mathrm{PU}}(t)\|\rho_E^{\mathrm{Haar}}(t))
\le
D_0e^{-2\gamma_{\mathrm{REC}}N_t}
\tag{K.3d.4d.2}
$$
under the natural-log convention. The named Landauer-tight substatus records the special subcase $\gamma_{\mathrm{REC}}=\varepsilon_0=\ln2$ when, and only when, the branch separately proves that the retained-cycle entropy-contraction rate equals the structural binary reset-support value of Proposition 5 and Definition 28. This numerical equality does not identify the contraction rate with physical reset heat; a registered physical reset is governed separately by Theorem 31. Absent such a separate proof on a concrete horizon branch, the Landauer-tight substatus is empty and the certificate is just a generic relative-entropy contraction certificate. The contraction estimate (K.3d.4d.2), not the Landauer-tight label, is the certificate entry used for promotion.

**Theorem K.3d.4e (Certificate-to-Trace-Coupling Promotion).** An accepted relative-entropy contraction trace-coupling certificate supplies the trace-coupled promotion data of Definition K.3d.4c with
$$
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Page}}^{\mathrm{REC}}(t)
=
\sqrt{\frac{D_0}{2}}e^{-\gamma_{\mathrm{REC}}N_t},
\tag{K.3d.4e.1}
$$
provided $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Page}}^{\mathrm{REC}}(t)\le1-1/d_E(t)$.

*Proof.* For every paired state in the certified coupling $\Gamma_t$, quantum Pinsker under the natural-log convention gives
$$
D(\rho\|\sigma)\ge\frac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1^2.
$$
Combining this with (K.3d.4d.2) yields
$$
\frac12\|\rho_E^{\mathrm{PU}}(t)-\rho_E^{\mathrm{Haar}}(t)\|_1
\le
\sqrt{\frac{D_0}{2}}e^{-\gamma_{\mathrm{REC}}N_t}.
$$
Thus the trace-distance input in (K.3d.4c.2) holds almost surely under $\Gamma_t$, with the stated ceiling condition. The record $\chi_{\mathrm{REC}}$ supplies structural independence because the coupling, entropy ceiling, contraction rate, retained-cycle counter, and norm are determined independently of the compared Page curve. ∎

<a id="corollary-k3d4f-conditional-page-entropy-promotion"></a>**Corollary K.3d.4f (Conditional Page-Entropy Promotion).** The von Neumann Page-curve estimate is theorem-level on a horizon branch only when that branch carries either the original trace-coupled promotion certificate of Definition K.3d.4c or an accepted certificate of Definition K.3d.4d satisfying Theorem K.3d.4e. A bare Landauer entropy ledger, a second-moment design certificate, or a Golay-expander moment certificate without (K.3d.4c.2) remains Page-purity or certificate-pending data rather than a full entropy-curve theorem.

*Proof.* Theorem K.3 applies Audenaert continuity to the trace-distance input (K.3.1), and Definition K.3d.4c supplies exactly that input. Theorem K.3d.4e promotes an accepted relative-entropy contraction certificate to the same trace-distance datum by quantum Pinsker. In contrast, Theorem K.3d.5 supplies only moment-norm control; at second order this controls purity by Corollary K.3.1 but does not imply (K.3d.4c.2). Thus precisely the two stated certificate routes license the entropy conclusion. ∎

<a id="proposition-k3d4g-fixed-source-moment-and-relative-entropy-obstructions"></a>**Proposition K.3d.4g (Fixed-Source Moment and Relative-Entropy Obstructions).** The finite keyed source of Constructions E.9.5f.36, E.9.5f.50, E.9.5f.51 and E.9.5f.53 retains its original almost-sure trace coupling and conditional Page-entropy output. The stronger full-carrier mixing and relative-entropy certificates have exact obstructions, and the continuous routing trajectory has the following distinct comparison law.

1. For any fixed unitary $V$ on a $D$-dimensional carrier with $D\ge2$, its two-copy conjugation $\mathcal V_2$ and full-carrier Haar projection $\Pi_{2,D}$ obey
$$
\| (\mathcal V_2-\Pi_{2,D})(I-\Pi_{2,D})\|_{2\to2}=1.
$$
The same equality holds for a probability mixture of unitaries preserving one common nonzero proper projection on that carrier. Thus a fixed complete chronological word, a fixed-key signal word, and a seed-preserving full-carrier ensemble have no positive full-unitary moment gap of the form (K.3d.4.2) on those respective domains.

2. Let $b\ge2$, $a\ge1$, and let $\{p_s,\rho_s\}_{s\in\mathcal S}$ be any finite ensemble of density matrices on $\mathbb C^b$, with $p_s>0$. Let $\sigma=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbb C^a}|\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|$, where $\Psi$ is Haar distributed on $\mathbb C^b\otimes\mathbb C^a$. Under every coupling $\Gamma$ of these two laws,
$$
\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{\Gamma}D(\rho_s\|\sigma)=+\infty.
$$
If $b>a$, the stronger statement $D(\rho_s\|\sigma)=+\infty$ holds almost surely under every such coupling. In particular no finite $D_0$ and finite retained-cycle count can satisfy (K.3d.4d.2) for this finite ensemble and the stated Haar comparison.

3. After the original encoder completes, the same key/Haar coupling has half-trace radius at most $\eta$ under every subsequent common physical emission prefix, uniformly in its proper time. At completed whole-block cuts its Haar comparison is the original Page marginal. During a partially executed route that transported comparison need not have the original Page marginal law. In particular, on the first route the conditional code entropy of the fixed complete receiver bank cannot satisfy the original $\eta$-scale Page estimate at every continuous proper time with any assignment of the original dimension pairs $(4^j,4^{22-j})$.

*Proof.* Two-copy conjugation is a Hilbert--Schmidt isometry. The Haar projection is the orthogonal projection onto the span of $I$ and the full swap $F_D$; both are fixed by every two-copy conjugation. Therefore $\mathcal V_2\Pi_{2,D}=\Pi_{2,D}\mathcal V_2=\Pi_{2,D}$, and
$$
(\mathcal V_2-\Pi_{2,D})(I-\Pi_{2,D})
=\mathcal V_2(I-\Pi_{2,D}).
$$
The Haar-orthogonal subspace is nonzero for $D\ge2$, and the right side is an isometry on that subspace, giving norm exactly one. This argument applies to every deterministic chronological product, with no assumption of a time-independent Hamiltonian or an involution.

For the mixture, let its common projection be $P$, of rank $0<r<D$, and set $A=P-(r/D)I$, $X=A\otimes I$. Then $X\ne0$, $\operatorname{Tr}X=0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}(F_DX)=\operatorname{Tr}A=0$, so $\Pi_{2,D}X=0$. Every supported two-copy conjugation fixes $X$. The mixture's norm on the Haar-orthogonal subspace is therefore at least one and at most one, the latter by convexity of the norm. This proves part 1.

For part 2, choose a unit vector $v$ such that $\rho_s\ne|v\rangle\langle v|$ for every $s$. Such a vector exists because $b\ge2$ and the ensemble is finite. A finite selection uses $|\mathcal S|+1$ distinct rays $(e_1+r e_2)/\sqrt{1+r^2}$, $r=0,\ldots,|\mathcal S|$; at most $|\mathcal S|$ of them can equal a pure ensemble atom. Put
$$
Q=I-|v\rangle\langle v|,\qquad
c=\min_s\operatorname{Tr}(Q\rho_s)>0,\qquad
q=\operatorname{Tr}(Q\sigma).
$$
The strict inequality follows because a positive trace-one matrix with zero weight on $Q$ is precisely $|v\rangle\langle v|$. Monotonicity of quantum relative entropy under the binary projective measurement $\{Q,I-Q\}$ gives, with $p=\operatorname{Tr}(Q\rho_s)\ge c$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
D(\rho_s\|\sigma)
&\ge p\ln\frac p q+(1-p)\ln\frac{1-p}{1-q}\\
&=p\ln\frac1q+(1-p)\ln\frac1{1-q}-h_2(p)\\
&\ge c\ln\frac1q-\ln2.
\end{aligned}
$$
The extended-value convention covers $q=0$ and singular second arguments. The imported measurement monotonicity is the finite-dimensional quantum data-processing inequality; see Frenkel (2023).

This bound holds simultaneously for every source atom. Its divergent tail has positive probability fixed by the Haar marginal, independently of the coupling. In fact $q=\|(Q\otimes I_a)\Psi\|^2$ has the $\beta$ density
$$
\frac{\Gamma(ab)}{\Gamma(a(b-1))\Gamma(a)}
q^{a(b-1)-1}(1-q)^{a-1},\qquad 0<q<1.
$$
To obtain this law, generate a Haar vector by normalizing $ab$ independent standard complex Gaussian coordinates. The squared moduli are independent exponentials; the sum on the $a(b-1)$-dimensional range of $Q\otimes I_a$ and the sum on its $a$-dimensional complement are independent $\gamma$ variables. The change of variables from those sums to their total and their ratio gives the displayed $\beta$ density. Writing $r=a(b-1)$, for $0<\delta<1$ it yields the explicit positive bound
$$
\Pr(q<\delta)\ge
\frac{\Gamma(ab)}{\Gamma(r)\Gamma(a)}
\frac{(1-\delta)^{a-1}\delta^r}{r}>0.
$$
For any finite $R\ge0$, choose $\delta=\exp[-(R+\ln2+1)/c]$. On $q<\delta$ every possible paired atom obeys $D(\rho_s\|\sigma)>R$. Every coupling consequently assigns positive probability to that event. This proves the essential-supremum assertion.

When $b>a$, represent $\Psi$ by a normalized $b$-by-$a$ complex Gaussian matrix $G$. Almost surely $G$ has rank $a$, and $\operatorname{supp}\sigma=\operatorname{ran}G$. Choose a nonzero vector $w_s\in\operatorname{supp}\rho_s$ for each atom. For each fixed $w_s$, the event $w_s\in\operatorname{ran}G$ has probability zero: adjoining the fixed column $w_s$ gives a $b$-by-$(a+1)$ matrix, one of whose $(a+1)$-minors is a nonzero polynomial in the Gaussian entries, and rank at most $a$ forces that polynomial to vanish. A nonzero polynomial has zero probability under their continuous density. The finite union of these null events is still null. Off that union, $\operatorname{supp}\rho_s\not\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\sigma$ for every atom. Quantum relative entropy is then infinite, proving the stronger assertion.

For part 3, condition on the original key $s$ and pair its encoder with the original Haar matrix $U_{\mathrm H}$ as in E.9.5f.CC4. Their output vectors on each fixed pure input differ in norm by at most $\eta$. Tensor the same prepared receiver, clock, controller, background and reference factors onto both states, and apply the same actual emission propagator through proper time $\tau$. Its state channel is CPTP, including all retained controls and outputs. The trace distance of the pair, and of every common receiver restriction, remains at most $\eta$ by contractivity. This is simultaneous for all $\tau$ because the original operator bound holds for every paired key/Haar sample and every deterministic prefix. The original exact enabled gates, holds and routes supply these prefixes; no clock-readout outcome or good-key event is conditioned upon. At a registered completed cut, E.9.5f.36.A11 identifies the compared logical state with the Haar marginal on $4^j$ by $4^{22-j}$. A partially executed physical swap instead acts on an emitted block and a charged ready receiver block, so that completed-cut identification is not asserted there.

For the claimed obstruction take the actual first route after the key has arrived. Include every installed receiver code block in one fixed bank, with unreceived blocks initially ready, and subtract the explicit unchanged key and independent background terms of E.9.5f.36.A12. Let $f(\tau)$ be its conditional code entropy. Finite smooth physical propagation makes each key-conditioned density matrix continuous; finite-dimensional entropy and the finite weighted key sum are continuous. Initially $f=0$. At the completed first route $|f-P_1|\le r_1$, where $P_1=S_{\mathrm{Page}}(4,4^{21})>4/5$ and $r_1\le(86\ln2+1)2^{-40}<1/5$. The strict rise/fall ledger E.9.5f.36.A2 and symmetry show that every original Page target $P_j$, $j=0,\ldots,22$, is either zero or at least $P_1$. In particular $P_1-r_1>P_1/2$. The intermediate value theorem supplies a proper time $\tau_*$ on this finite route with $f(\tau_*)=P_1/2$, and hence
$$
\min_{0\le j\le22}|f(\tau_*)-P_j|=P_1/2>2/5.
$$
This exceeds every original entropy-error radius. Thus a uniform continuous-time estimate for that fixed bank with the unchanged integer dimension ledger is false, while the uniformly propagated trace coupling to the transported comparator remains true. $\square$

On the original source, $\rho_s=\rho_{B_j}^s$, $b=4^j$ and $a=4^{22-j}$ for every fixed pure logical input. The ensemble includes every original key and both recovery outcomes. Part 2 therefore excludes Definition K.3d.4d at every nontrivial cut $j=1,\ldots,22$, with infinite relative entropy almost surely at $j=12,\ldots,22$. At $j=0$ the radiation factor is one-dimensional and its relative entropy is zero. The exact final conditional entropy is also zero, despite the infinite relative entropy to an independently Haar-marginal comparison under every finite-key coupling. This separates an entropy output from the stronger directed-relative-entropy certificate.

The almost-sure trace coupling E.9.5f.CC4--CC5 is unchanged: its radius is $\eta=\pi2^{-42}$ simultaneously at all registered cuts, and E.9.5f.36.A11--A12 keeps the actual read-only key and background entropies explicitly separate. Arbitrarily small trace distance does not imply a finite directed-relative-entropy ceiling. For this finite source the available conversion route is the original PageTV coupling, rather than REC-TV.

The moment domains are also distinct. The averaged signal law $\sum_sp_s\delta_{U_s}$ retains E.9.5f.CC6's gap estimate. Part 1 applies to the actual fixed complete unitary of E.9.5f.53, to the signal word after fixing its key, and to any seed-preserving ensemble on the enlarged carrier with the read-only seed included. Transporting a key register between sites only conjugates its conserved projection; the statement is invariant under that recorded input/output identification. The selected source executes its finite $\widehat Q_c^*\widehat X_T\widehat Q_c$ word once and then the separately clocked routes under the declared holds. Replaying that word twice gives identity because $\widehat W^2=I$; the alternative constant logarithm of E.9.5f.9 is not the selected emission schedule. The original physical clock, controlled programme, seed preparation and purifying archive remain charged source data. Treating the averaged signal law as independent successive horizon updates still requires the actual retained-update admission and chronological law; repeatedly reusing the same seed is not the convolution law of Theorem K.3d.5.

<a id="construction-k3d4h-design-and-pagetv-certificate-of-the-original-horizon-code"></a>**Construction K.3d.4h (Design and PageTV Certificate of the Original Horizon Code).** Fix exactly the prescribed-material, exact enable/phase-clock horizon source selected in Construction E.9.5f.51 and frozen in Construction E.9.5f.53. Use its original Page preparation, full chronological circuit, read-only key, hidden purifying archive, complete physical output dictionary and all original completed whole-block cuts. The horizon edge code is its $22$ signal ququarts,
$$
\mathcal H_{\mathrm{edge}}=(\mathbb C^4)^{\otimes22},\qquad
 d=4^{22},\quad K=4,\quad M=2^{130},\quad
 L=d^2,\quad m_S=M^L,\quad \eta=\pi2^{-42}.
$$
The code dimension $d$, logical sender dimension $K$, key dimension $m_S$ and full tested source dimension $D$ remain distinct. The certificate is for this actual code's conditional unitary law and its original conditional Page output, not the full $D$-dimensional unitary law of Proposition K.3d.4g.

**The full-code source identity.** In the original effective matrices of E.9.5f.9, $Q$ prepares the key/copy and applies the controlled $U_s$ to the signal. With every original key and workspace factor ready, for every $\psi\in\mathbb C^d$,
$$
Q(|0\rangle_{CF}\otimes|\psi\rangle)
 =\sum_s\sqrt{p_s}|s\rangle_C|s\rangle_F\otimes U_s|\psi\rangle.
$$
Here and below the fixed ready and returned workspace factors are suppressed, not removed. Since $Q_c=|0\rangle\langle0|_T\otimes Q+|1\rangle\langle1|_T\otimes I$, its entire actual sandwich obeys
$$
Q_c^*X_TQ_c
 (|0\rangle_T|0\rangle_{CF}|\psi\rangle)
 =|1\rangle_T\sum_s\sqrt{p_s}|s\rangle_C|s\rangle_F U_s|\psi\rangle.
$$
Indeed $Q_c$ first applies $Q$, $X_T$ changes the toggle to $1$, and $Q_c^*$ is identity on that toggle sector. This is an identity on the entire $d$-dimensional signal code, not just the $K$-dimensional subspace prepared for the communication task. E.9.5f.36.A3 intertwines every compiled gate on that entire code; the exact E.9.5f.38.C3--C4 enable sector gives precisely its specified gate, with the phase clock a product factor. Induction over the actual finite word therefore gives the same identity under the source's physical code isometries, retaining all field, controller, clock, gauge, support and non-ready sectors. The full physical propagator is still defined on every sector; only its displayed code identity uses the original ready-source isometry.

Consequently, restriction to the read-only key and code gives the complete channel
$$
\rho\longmapsto
 \sum_s p_s|s\rangle\langle s|_C\otimes U_s\rho U_s^*,
$$
for every full-code input and every external reference. The probabilities are the original exact algebraic bin weights, independent of that input. The hidden copy $F$ is the existing physical reason that the accessible key is classical. The full-code identity is a certificate about the existing source matrices; it grants no new sender preparation, key editing or purifier access. The actual Page test still uses precisely $J:\mathbb C^K\to\mathbb C^d$ and its fixed pure input independent of $s$.

**Horizon source and physical time.** This conditional law is produced by the complete original $\widehat W=\widehat Q_c^*\widehat X_T\widehat Q_c$ interval, not by a replacement random circuit or a selected encoding subword. Each of its actual layers is the complete retained pair/free propagator of E.9.5f.38.C1--C2; its ordinary realization and physical characteristic source are the same E.9.5f.48--E.9.5f.50 records used in E.9.5f.51. Thus the code law is generated by the already admitted retained horizon dynamics through the displayed source isometry and key restriction. The appended port, adapter and diagnostic degrees of freedom have their full generators held during these original Page windows; E.9.5f.51 and Theorem E.9.5f.53a preserve both the old complete code channels and their actual source/clock tests.

Let $\mathscr W$ be that original ordered list of physical layer boundaries and guard intervals. Its duration is
$$
\tau_{\mathrm{enc}}=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathscr W}\Delta\tau_\alpha>0,
$$
where each $\Delta\tau_\alpha$ is the actual independently calibrated proper-time duration in the frozen source. A simultaneous matching is one physical interval in this sum. Preparation before the ready-source boundary is separately included in the original preparation ledger. Let $\mathscr R_j$ be the original key route and radiation routing prefix through cut $j$, including its fixed guards and holds. Its original observation time is
$$
t_j=t_{\mathrm{ready}}+\tau_{\mathrm{enc}}
       +\sum_{\alpha\in\mathscr R_j}\Delta\tau_\alpha,
\qquad j=1,\ldots,22.
$$
Retain the original empty-radiation initial boundary separately; its one-dimensional output is exact and requires no design estimate. The displayed times are the completed whole-block times specified before sampling in E.9.5f.36, not a new observation schedule. The independently calibrated phase frequency and guard of E.9.5f.38.C3--C4 cover these finite intervals; its stated replica count pays for each nominated timing confidence and readout precision. The Page law is unconditional on those readouts. One design step means this entire physical encoder interval of duration $\tau_{\mathrm{enc}}$, and the step count at all these emitted cuts is $N_{t_j}=1$. The record contains no convolution power of $\nu_H$ and no mixing rate.

**Populated moment and trace records.** In Definition K.3d.4 take:

| Entry | Value on the original source |
|:--|:--|
| Edge Hilbert space | $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{edge}}=(\mathbb C^4)^{\otimes22}$, with the full-code physical intertwiner above. |
| Actual update measure | $\nu_H=\sum_sp_s\delta_{U_s}$, obtained from the complete original encoder and its retained key, with no key selection or replacement. |
| Design order and Haar projection | $t_{\mathrm{des}}=2$ and $\Pi_2^{\mathrm{Haar}}$ on $\mathcal B(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{edge}}^{\otimes2})$. |
| Moment operator, norm and gap | $\mathcal M_2(X)=\sum_sp_sU_s^{\otimes2}X(U_s^*)^{\otimes2}$ in Hilbert--Schmidt $2\to2$ norm; $\gamma_2=1-4\eta>0$. |
| Step, emission and moment errors | $N_{t_j}=1$, $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{emit}}=0$, $\varepsilon_{t_j}^{\mathrm{mom}}=4\eta$. The emission identity is the original exact whole-block restriction after its physical route. |
| Normalized frame potential | $\mathcal F_2=d^{-4}\sum_{s,r}p_sp_r\lvert\operatorname{Tr}(U_s^*U_r)\rvert^4$, $\mathcal F_2(\mathrm{Haar})=2/d^4$, $\varepsilon_{t_j}^{\mathrm{frame}}=(1-2/d^4)(4\eta)^2$. |
| Trace conversion and Page error | The original common bin/Haar coupling, transported through the actual cut dictionary, with $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Page}}(t_j)=\eta$ for $j\ge1$ and the exact empty output at $j=0$. |
| Structural independence | The original finite binning and algebraic key weights, source word, initial factors, key/purifier ownership, physical clock, completed cuts, dimensions, norm, and error ceilings follow from the source and proof. The compared Page curve supplies none of these entries. |

The row defining $\mathcal F_2$ specifies its normalization explicitly. Its unnormalized value is $d^4\mathcal F_2$, the convention in E.9.5f.CC6. The trace-conversion entry is a separately proved source coupling; it is not inferred from the small second moment or from the frame potential.

To verify the moment entries, couple each original quantized matrix to its Haar matrix as in E.9.5f.CC4. The original telescoping bound is $\|U_s-U_{\mathrm H}\|\le\eta$ almost surely. Hence $\|U_s^{\otimes2}-U_{\mathrm H}^{\otimes2}\|\le2\eta$, and their conjugations differ by at most $4\eta$ in Hilbert--Schmidt operator norm. Averaging this exact coupling gives
$$
\|\mathcal M_2-\Pi_2^{\mathrm{Haar}}\|_{2\to2}\le4\eta.
$$
Every supported unitary fixes the Haar invariant space, and its conjugation commutes with the Haar projection. Therefore the restriction to the Haar-orthogonal space has norm at most $4\eta=1-\gamma_2$. That space has dimension $d^4-2$; orthogonality and the Hilbert--Schmidt norm bound give
$$
0\le\mathcal F_2-2/d^4
=d^{-4}\|\mathcal M_2-\Pi_2^{\mathrm{Haar}}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2
\le(1-2/d^4)(4\eta)^2.
$$
This verifies every moment and frame inequality at the actual one step. No independent-successive-update assumption is used when $N=1$.

For the trace entry, use one and the same Haar draw and its quantized key at every cut. The pure encoded vectors on the original fixed input differ in norm by at most $\eta$; common physical routing, the code isometry and partial trace preserve the resulting half-trace bound. Thus for all $j=1,\ldots,22$ on the same probability-one event,
$$
\tfrac12\|\rho_{B_j}^s-\rho_{B_j}^{\mathrm H}\|_1\le\eta,
\qquad d_E(t_j)=4^j,\qquad d_L(t_j)=4^{22-j}.
$$
Since $\eta<2^{-40}<3/4\le1-1/4^j$, these are the accepted trace-conversion values of Definition K.3d.4 and populate $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{PageTV}}$ of Definition K.3d.4c on the same horizon code. They require no finite relative-entropy ceiling, which Proposition K.3d.4g excludes for this finite law.

Theorem K.3 now gives, simultaneously at every original completed cut,
$$
\left|\sum_sp_sS(\rho_{B_j}^s)-S_{\mathrm{Page}}(4^j,4^{22-j})\right|
\le r_j:=\eta\ln(4^j-1)+h_2(\eta),\qquad 1\le j\le22.
$$
Every $r_j\le(86\ln2+1)2^{-40}$. The initial and final conditional code entropies are exactly zero, so their entropy-error entries can be sharpened to zero. The E.9.5f.36.A2 adjacent target gaps exceed $4/5$, greater than the sum of any two radii; therefore the original strict rise, turnover and fall, and the same late reference-safe recovery cuts, hold on this one source. The raw physical entropy still contains the actual $H(S)$ and background terms in E.9.5f.36.A12. They are neither discarded resources nor part of the conditional Page target.

The complete finite error/time vector is
$$
\left(t_j,\,\tau_{\mathrm{enc}},\,N_{t_j}=1,\,
 d_E=4^j,\,d_L=4^{22-j},\,
 \varepsilon^{\mathrm{mom}}=4\eta,\,
 \varepsilon^{\mathrm{frame}}=(1-2/d^4)(4\eta)^2,\,
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{emit}}=0,\,
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{Page}}=\eta,\,r_j\right)_{j=1}^{22},
$$
with the exact empty-output entry and endpoint entropy entries stated above. The source also retains its timing-readout errors and confidences, rather than converting them into unrecorded data errors. The effective key and purifier each occupy $65L$ ququarts; all $256$-dimensional physical block sectors, ready receiver blocks, route/scratch registers, flags, source purification, finite enables/phases, both sandwich halves, generator cancellations, guard durations, pulse strengths and complete stress/work payers remain those of E.9.5f.36--E.9.5f.38 and E.9.5f.50--E.9.5f.53. The certificate adds no sampler, seed, gate, reset, access path or free physical service.

This is a prescribed-background driven finite horizon-code certificate at the source's original registered completed cuts. Proposition K.3d.4g identifies the different continuous partial-route comparator and the obstruction to extending the same integer Page ledger to every such proper time. Full-carrier Haar mixing, autonomous scheduling, a fast-scrambling rate and continuous shrinking-area evaporation are separate outputs; none is used in this certificate.

<a id="theorem-k3d5-certified-horizon-k-design-mixing"></a>**Theorem K.3d.5 (Certified Horizon $k$-Design Mixing).** If $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{Hdesign}}$ is accepted, then after $N_t$ horizon update steps the moment channel obeys
$$
\left\|
\mathcal M_t(\nu_H^{*N_t})-\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}}
\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le
(1-\gamma_t)^{N_t}.
\tag{K.3d.7}
$$
The corresponding radiation channel is an
$$
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mom}}
=
(1-\gamma_t)^{N_t}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{emit}}
\tag{K.3d.8}
$$
approximate $t_{\mathrm{des}}$-design input in moment norm. This moment bound is sufficient for the Page-purity law of Corollary K.3.1 when the controlled observable is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_E^2)$. It becomes a von Neumann Page-curve input for Theorem K.3 only when paired with the trace-coupled promotion certificate $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{PageTV}}$ of Definition K.3d.4c, in which case the certified trace error is denoted $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Page}}$.

*Proof.* Since $\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}}$ is the Haar fixed-point projection,
$$
\mathcal M_t(\nu_H)\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}}=\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}},
\qquad
\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}}\mathcal M_t(\nu_H)=\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}}.
$$
Let $N_t$ be a nonnegative integer. In the mixing estimates of this section, a zero-step scalar power is the empty product $1$, including when $\gamma_t=1$. On the orthogonal complement of the Haar-invariant subspace, the one-step contraction norm is at most $1-\gamma_t$ by (K.3d.4.2). For $N_t\ge1$, the identities above give
$$
\left\|
\left(\mathcal M_t(\nu_H)\right)^{N_t}
-
\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}}
\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
=
\left\|
\left[
\left(\mathcal M_t(\nu_H)-\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}}\right)
\left(I-\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}}\right)
\right]^{N_t}
\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le
(1-\gamma_t)^{N_t}.
$$
For $N_t=0$, the convolution is the identity update and the left side is $\|I-\Pi_t^{\mathrm{Haar}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le1$, which gives the zero-step bound directly.
The convolution law for independent horizon update steps gives
$$
\mathcal M_t(\nu_H^{*N_t})=\left(\mathcal M_t(\nu_H)\right)^{N_t},
$$
so (K.3d.7) follows. The emission channel differs from the certified horizon moment channel by at most $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{emit}}$ in the same moment norm, hence the triangle inequality gives the moment-norm error (K.3d.8). Moment-norm control alone does not imply the trace-coupled entropy-continuity estimate (K.3.1); that stronger conclusion is exactly the additional content of Definition K.3d.4c. ∎

<a id="corollary-k3d6-page-curve-promotion-gate"></a>**Corollary K.3d.6 (Page-Curve Promotion Gate).** The von Neumann Page-entropy estimate of Theorem K.3, pointwise in the registered time and for the ensemble mean, is theorem-level only on a branch carrying an accepted horizon entropy-continuity promotion certificate $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{PageTV}}$ of Definition K.3d.4c. A bare accepted moment-design certificate $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{Hdesign}}$ with $t_{\mathrm{des}}\ge2$ supplies moment control; for $t_{\mathrm{des}}=2$ the closed theorem-level output is the Page-purity law of Corollary K.3.1. A rise/turnover/fall conclusion additionally requires a time-ordered dimension ledger whose adjacent Page-target gaps dominate the sums of the certified entropy-error radii, or whose adjacent moment-level bands of Corollary K.3.1b are separated as in Corollary K.3.1c; half-entropy and zero-endpoint claims require their separate coarse-conservation and final-state gates. Without $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{PageTV}}$, the structural information-conservation, edge-inflow, and island-blanket results remain theorem-level on their stated branches, but no von Neumann Page-entropy estimate follows.

*Proof.* Theorem K.3 assumes the trace-distance coupling (K.3.1), not merely equality of finitely many Haar moments. Theorem K.3d.5 supplies a certified moment-norm estimate; applying that estimate to the degree-$(2,2)$ purity observable gives Corollary K.3.1. To use Audenaert's entropy-continuity inequality in Theorem K.3, one additionally needs the trace-coupled bound certified by Definition K.3d.4c. Therefore the full entropy Page-curve estimate is promoted exactly on the $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{PageTV}}$ branch. ∎

**Current Status:** The retained no-deletion theorem, thermodynamic bounds, horizon edge-inflow consistency, Page-purity control on an accepted moment-design branch, and the finite predictive-island Markov-blanket formula are rigorous on their stated branches. The SPAP reading of horizon retrieval and the Perspectival Information Channel are interpretive models until their horizon protocol, response, capacity, clock, and extraction-cost certificates are constructed. The full von Neumann Page-curve estimate is theorem-level only on the stronger trace-coupled entropy-continuity promotion branch of Definition K.3d.4c. Construction K.3d.4h supplies the actual moment-operator and $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{PageTV}}$ certificates for the original finite horizon code at all its registered completed cuts. Theorem K.3d.1f proves an exhaustive strict switch of the predictive-island minimizer, with a continuum extremal representative, on the courier source of Construction K.3d.1e. Explicit information-extraction rates and a quantum-extremal-surface realization of the minimizer on the common horizon source remain development obligations.

### K.3.6 Finite-Budget Predictive Uncertainty Gate

The finite-channel-capacity bounds of Appendix E and the predictive island Markov-blanket cost of Definition K.3b constrain the declared information and reconstruction ledgers on their accepted branches. This subsection proves a complementary norm bound for configuration and update-momentum supports of a specified finite cyclic Fourier map. When the support-size product is below the cycle budget, it gives positive one-step leakage.

<a id="definition-k3e-finite-budget-update-group-and-discrete-fourier"></a>**Definition K.3e (Finite-Budget Update Group and Discrete Fourier).** Let $\Lambda\in\mathbb N$, $\Lambda\geq1$, be the SPAP cycle budget on a registered evaporation branch. Choose the cyclic quotient $\mathbb Z/\Lambda\mathbb Z$ of the integer update-count group in Definition Q.0.6a.1 as an additional periodic-update model. A finite budget alone does not identify counts modulo $\Lambda$. The *finite-budget discrete Fourier operator* $F_\Lambda$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}/\Lambda\mathbb{Z})$ is the unitary

$$
(F_\Lambda \psi)(k)
:=
\frac{1}{\sqrt{\Lambda}}
\sum_{N=0}^{\Lambda-1}
\psi(N)\,e^{-2\pi i N k/\Lambda},
\qquad
k \in \mathbb{Z}/\Lambda\mathbb{Z}.
\tag{K.3e.1}
$$

For subsets $X \subset \mathbb{Z}/\Lambda\mathbb{Z}$ (configuration support) and $P \subset \mathbb{Z}/\Lambda\mathbb{Z}$ (update-momentum support), the associated projections are

$$
\Pi_X = \operatorname{diag}(\mathbf{1}_X),
\qquad
\Pi_P = \operatorname{diag}(\mathbf{1}_P),
\tag{K.3e.2}
$$

acting diagonally on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}/\Lambda\mathbb{Z})$ and on its Fourier dual respectively. Whenever logarithmic dimensions are used below, assume $\Lambda\ge2$ and $X,P$ are nonempty; if either support is empty, the restricted norm is $0$.

<a id="theorem-k3e-finite-budget-predictive-uncertainty-gate"></a>**Theorem K.3e (Finite-Budget Predictive Uncertainty Gate).** *For every budget $\Lambda \geq 1$ and every pair of supports $X, P \subset \mathbb{Z}/\Lambda\mathbb{Z}$, the operator norm satisfies*

$$
\bigl\|\Pi_X\,F_\Lambda\,\Pi_P\bigr\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq
\sqrt{\frac{|X|\cdot|P|}{\Lambda}}.
\tag{K.3e.3}
$$

*If $\Lambda\ge2$ and $X,P$ are nonempty, then with finite-budget resolution $h := 1/\Lambda$ and effective dimensions $\delta_X := \log_\Lambda|X|$, $\delta_P := \log_\Lambda|P|$,*

$$
\bigl\|\Pi_X\,F_\Lambda\,\Pi_P\bigr\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\leq
h^{(1 - \delta_X - \delta_P)/2}.
\tag{K.3e.4}
$$

*The Hilbert--Schmidt estimate is sharp in the subgroup-dual saturation case $|X|\cdot|P|=\Lambda$. No sharpness claim is made for arbitrary supports.*

*Proof.* By definition of $F_\Lambda$ in (K.3e.1), the matrix entries of $F_\Lambda$ in the standard basis satisfy $|(F_\Lambda)_{kN}| = 1/\sqrt{\Lambda}$ for every $k, N$. The composition $\Pi_X F_\Lambda \Pi_P$ has matrix entries

$$
(\Pi_X F_\Lambda \Pi_P)_{kN}
=
\mathbf{1}_X(k)\,(F_\Lambda)_{kN}\,\mathbf{1}_P(N),
$$

a $|X| \times |P|$ submatrix of $F_\Lambda$ (extended by zeros to $\Lambda \times \Lambda$). The Hilbert-Schmidt norm satisfies

$$
\|\Pi_X F_\Lambda \Pi_P\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2
=
\sum_{k \in X, N \in P}|(F_\Lambda)_{kN}|^2
=
\frac{|X|\cdot|P|}{\Lambda}.
$$

Since the operator norm is bounded by the Hilbert-Schmidt norm, $\|\Pi_X F_\Lambda \Pi_P\|_{\mathrm{op}} \leq \|\Pi_X F_\Lambda \Pi_P\|_{\mathrm{HS}} = \sqrt{|X||P|/\Lambda}$, which is (K.3e.3). For $\Lambda\ge2$ and nonempty supports, Equation (K.3e.4) follows by substituting $|X| = \Lambda^{\delta_X}$, $|P| = \Lambda^{\delta_P}$ into (K.3e.3) and rewriting in terms of $h = 1/\Lambda$. For saturation, let $X$ be a subgroup of $\mathbb Z/\Lambda\mathbb Z$ and let $P=X^\perp$. Then $|X||P|=\Lambda$, and the normalized indicator of $P$ is mapped by $F_\Lambda$ to the normalized indicator of $P^\perp=X$ up to phase. This unit input lies in $\operatorname{ran}\Pi_P$ and its unit output lies in $\operatorname{ran}\Pi_X$, so $\|\Pi_XF_\Lambda\Pi_P\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1$, matching (K.3e.3). For general supports the Hilbert--Schmidt estimate is only an upper bound. $\square$

<a id="corollary-k3f-no-hidden-remnant-theorem"></a>**Corollary K.3f (No-Hidden-Remnant Theorem).** *Let an evaporation-branch protocol have budget $\Lambda\ge2$ and let its predictive response functional be supported jointly on a configuration trapped set $X$ and an update-momentum trapped set $P$ with nonempty supports satisfying $|X|\cdot|P| < \Lambda$. Then for every initial state $\psi$ supported on $P$ and every readout test vector $O\in\ell^2(\mathbb Z/\Lambda\mathbb Z)$ with $\Pi_XO=O$, using the Hilbert-space inner product and norm,*

$$
\bigl|\langle O,\,F_\Lambda \psi\rangle\bigr|
\leq
\sqrt{\frac{|X|\cdot|P|}{\Lambda}}\,
\|O\|\,\|\psi\|.
\tag{K.3f.1}
$$

*Equivalently, for every unit vector $\psi$ supported on $P$, the leakage probability outside $X$ obeys*

$$
\left\|({\rm id}-\Pi_X)F_\Lambda\psi\right\|^2
\ge
1-\frac{|X|\cdot|P|}{\Lambda}
=
1-h^{1-\delta_X-\delta_P} >0.
\tag{K.3f.2}
$$

*Proof.* Inequality (K.3f.1) is the operator-norm identity applied to vectors with $\Pi_P\psi = \psi$ and readout test vectors with $\Pi_X O = O$:

$$
|\langle O, F_\Lambda \psi\rangle|
=
|\langle \Pi_X O, F_\Lambda \Pi_P \psi\rangle|
\leq
\|\Pi_X F_\Lambda \Pi_P\|_{\mathrm{op}}\,\|O\|\,\|\psi\|,
$$

and Theorem K.3e bounds the right factor. For unit $\psi$ with $\Pi_P\psi=\psi$, unitarity gives
$$
1
=
\|F_\Lambda\psi\|^2
=
\|\Pi_XF_\Lambda\psi\|^2
+
\|({\rm id}-\Pi_X)F_\Lambda\psi\|^2.
$$
By Theorem K.3e, $\|\Pi_XF_\Lambda\psi\|^2\le |X||P|/\Lambda$. Substitution gives (K.3f.2). $\square$

<a id="remark-k3f1-status-and-scope"></a>**Remark K.3f.1 (Status and Scope).** Theorem K.3e and Corollary K.3f are operator-norm statements for the specified discrete Fourier map on a finite-budget cyclic group. For a unit vector supported on $P$, they give one-step leakage outside $X$ of at least $1-h^{1-\delta_X-\delta_P}$ when $\delta_X+\delta_P<1$. Applying this estimate to a physical evaporation or remnant sector requires a separate protocol map identifying its state and readout supports with $P$ and $X$ and identifying the relevant update with $F_\Lambda$. Excluding indefinite storage additionally requires an iterated-dynamics or mixing theorem.

<a id="remark-k3f2-conditional-connection-to-the-center-ledger-area-law-criterion"></a>**Remark K.3f.2 (Conditional Connection to the Center-Ledger Area-Law Criterion).** On the rootless flux-tube branch of Proposition Z.8d, Theorem X.9.5d.4 gives a finite center-ledger criterion for Wilson-loop area law when its unbroken-center and positive-surface-gap hypotheses hold, including the aggregate bound on normalized sheet weights. Corollary K.3f can be applied to that sector only if an additional finite representation identifies the physical Wilson-line protocol with the cyclic Hilbert space, identifies the trapped flux and conjugate update sectors with $\Pi_X$ and $\Pi_P$, and intertwines the physical update with $F_\Lambda$. Under that representation, the condition $\delta_X+\delta_P<1$ gives the leakage bound of Corollary K.3f.

<a id="theorem-k3f3-closed-update-storage-floor-and-emission-depletion"></a>**Theorem K.3f.3 (Closed-Update Storage Floor and Emission Depletion).** Let $U$ be a unitary on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ with spectral decomposition $U=\sum_{\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}U}\lambda E_\lambda$, and put $m:=|\operatorname{spec}U|$. For every orthogonal projection $\Pi$ and every unit vector $\psi$ with $\Pi\psi=\psi$,
$$
\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac1T\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\|\Pi U^t\psi\|^2
=\sum_{\lambda}\|\Pi E_\lambda\psi\|^2
\ge\sum_{\lambda}\|E_\lambda\psi\|^4
\ge\frac1m
\ge\frac1{\dim\mathcal H},
\qquad
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\|\Pi U^t\psi\|^2=1.
\tag{K.3f.3.1}
$$
The value $1/m$ is attained by $\Pi=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$ when $\psi$ has weight $1/m$ in each eigenspace. For the update of Definition K.3e, $F_\Lambda^4=\mathrm{id}$, so $m\le4$: a unit vector supported on $P$ returns to itself after every fourth cycle and keeps Cesàro-averaged weight at least $1/4$ in $P$, for every support pair, including every pair with $|X|\cdot|P|<\Lambda$.

Register the emission instrument that, after each application of $F_\Lambda$, measures $\{\Pi_X,\mathrm{id}-\Pi_X\}$, transfers the outcome $\mathrm{id}-\Pi_X$ to the exterior record, and retains the outcome $\Pi_X$. For a unit vector $\psi$ supported on $P$, the probability of retention through $t\ge1$ cycles is
$$
p_{\mathrm{ret}}(t)
=\bigl\|(\Pi_XF_\Lambda)^t\psi\bigr\|^2
\le\frac{|X|\cdot|P|}{\Lambda}\left(\frac{|X|^2}{\Lambda}\right)^{t-1},
\tag{K.3f.3.2}
$$
so the retained weight tends to zero geometrically when $|X|^2<\Lambda$.

*Proof.* Unitarity gives $U^t=\sum_\lambda\lambda^tE_\lambda$ with $|\lambda|=1$, so
$$
\|\Pi U^t\psi\|^2=\sum_{\lambda,\mu}(\bar\lambda\mu)^t\langle E_\lambda\psi,\Pi E_\mu\psi\rangle.
$$
For $\lambda\ne\mu$, the number $\bar\lambda\mu\ne1$ has modulus one and $\bigl|T^{-1}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}(\bar\lambda\mu)^t\bigr|\le2/(T|1-\bar\lambda\mu|)\to0$, so only the diagonal terms survive the Cesàro limit. Since $\Pi\psi=\psi$ and $\|\psi\|=1$, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality gives $\|\Pi E_\lambda\psi\|\ge|\langle\psi,\Pi E_\lambda\psi\rangle|=|\langle\psi,E_\lambda\psi\rangle|=\|E_\lambda\psi\|^2$. The weights $w_\lambda:=\|E_\lambda\psi\|^2$ sum to one over at most $m$ eigenvalues, so $\sum_\lambda w_\lambda^2\ge1/m$, and $m\le\dim\mathcal H$. For $\Pi=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$ one has $\|\Pi E_\lambda\psi\|^2=w_\lambda^2$, which sums to $1/m$ in the equal-weight case. For the recurrence statement, compactness of the unitary group gives a convergent subsequence $U^{t_k}$ with $t_{k+1}-t_k\to\infty$; then $U^{t_{k+1}-t_k}=U^{t_{k+1}}(U^{t_k})^{-1}\to\mathrm{id}$ and $\|\Pi U^{t_{k+1}-t_k}\psi\|^2\to\|\Pi\psi\|^2=1$. Two applications of (K.3e.1) give $(F_\Lambda^2\psi)(N)=\psi(-N)$, hence $F_\Lambda^4=\mathrm{id}$ and every eigenvalue of $F_\Lambda$ is a fourth root of unity; taking $\Pi=\Pi_P$ gives the stated recurrence and floor.

For the emission instrument, the unnormalized retained vector after $t$ cycles is $(\Pi_XF_\Lambda)^t\psi$, and its squared norm is the retention probability. Because $\Pi_X^2=\Pi_X$ and $\Pi_P\psi=\psi$,
$$
(\Pi_XF_\Lambda)^t\psi=(\Pi_XF_\Lambda\Pi_X)^{t-1}\,\Pi_XF_\Lambda\Pi_P\psi.
$$
Theorem K.3e with the support pairs $(X,P)$ and $(X,X)$ bounds the two factors in operator norm by $\sqrt{|X||P|/\Lambda}$ and $(|X|/\sqrt\Lambda)^{t-1}$, and squaring gives (K.3f.3.2). ∎

Theorem K.3f.3 is the iterated-dynamics statement called for in Remark K.3f.1: closed finite unitary iteration of a trapped sector retains at least the fraction $1/m$ on Cesàro average and returns arbitrarily close to full weight, while the registered emission instrument depletes the sector geometrically when $|X|^2<\Lambda$.

<a id="proposition-k3f4-retained-archive-coherence-on-the-common-horizon-source"></a>**Proposition K.3f.4 (Retained Archive Coherence on the Common Horizon Source).** Fix the exact prescribed-material source of Constructions E.9.5f.36, E.9.5f.51 and E.9.5f.53, extended by the restored scattering/diagnostic service of Theorem Q.0.7v.6. Retain its original physical placements, complete carriers, buffered receiver cuts and passive access grammar. Put
$$
d=4^{22},\qquad M=4^{65},\qquad r=\frac{d(d+1)}2.
$$
For the original pure Page input, immediately after its encoder the effective code/key/archive state is
$$
|\Psi\rangle=\sum_s\sqrt{p_s}|s\rangle_C|s\rangle_F|\psi_s\rangle,
\qquad |\psi_s\rangle=U_sJ|\psi\rangle.
\tag{K.3f.4.1}
$$
All statements concern one fixed finite source stage. Its physical image includes the original fixed finite-dimensional spectator state and every retained preparation factor; all displayed von Neumann entropies are therefore finite. Select one of the original uniformly binned phase coordinates, write its bin index as $k(s)\in\{0,\ldots,M-1\}$, and define on the existing archive
$$
Z_F=\sum_s(-1)^{k(s)}|s\rangle\langle s|_F.
\tag{K.3f.4.2}
$$
The physical representative of $Z_F$ is the code-preserving full-sector completion of the diagonal gate on the least significant ququart digit of this archive coordinate. The two retained states are $\rho_0=|\Psi\rangle\langle\Psi|$ and $\rho_1=Z_F\rho_0Z_F$, with their unchanged physical spectator factors understood. They are compared as states of the source's complete retained algebra; the communication sender retains its original logical-input permission.

Write $T(\rho,\sigma)=\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$. Then:

1. $T(\rho_0,\rho_1)=1$, whereas every complete record generated by the original passive emission protocol, its original receiver-local decoder/live adapter, and any finite sequence of the specified restored diagnostic/scattering calls has identical laws on these two states. All outcomes, adaptive choices and charged receiver memories are included. For its record channel $\mathcal N$ and every CPTP reconstruction $\mathcal D$,
$$
\mathcal N(\rho_0)=\mathcal N(\rho_1),\qquad
\max_{i=0,1}T\bigl(\mathcal D\mathcal N(\rho_i),\rho_i\bigr)\ge\frac12.
\tag{K.3f.4.3}
$$
The comparison includes all original completed cuts and the complete finite transfer record. The independent diagnostic output remains independent of the old state at every completed restored call.

2. Let $\Delta_F$ dephase the existing archive in its original key basis and act identically on all other factors. On its physical archive carrier, use the mutually orthogonal represented key projections together with their non-code complement as the pinching projections; this defines a CPTP unital completion on every sector. On the actual prepared state,
$$
\begin{aligned}
T\bigl(\rho_0,\Delta_F(\rho_0)\bigr)
&\ge 1-\sum_s p_s^2\ge1-M^{-r},\\
S\bigl(\Delta_F(\rho_0)\bigr)-S(\rho_0)
&=H(S)\ge r\ln M.
\end{aligned}
\tag{K.3f.4.4}
$$
These differences are unchanged by the original full physical isometries and by adjoining the same independent finite-dimensional spectator state. The dephasing has a nonzero kernel on the retained response algebra. Its archive coherence therefore survives the source's zero response-null quotient.

3. If an implemented record channel $\widetilde{\mathcal N}$ satisfies $T(\widetilde{\mathcal N}(\rho_i),\mathcal N(\rho_i))\le\varepsilon$ for both states, every CPTP reconstruction obeys
$$
\max_{i=0,1}T\bigl(\mathcal D\widetilde{\mathcal N}(\rho_i),\rho_i\bigr)
\ge\max\{0,\tfrac12-\varepsilon\}.
\tag{K.3f.4.5}
$$
Its use requires a whole-record error certificate on both retained inputs.

*Proof.* Theorem E.9.5f.7 constructs $r$ independent uniform phase-bin variables, each with $M$ values, independently of every angle-bin variable. Their full labels are retained in $C$ and $F$ by Proposition E.9.5f.9. Since $M$ is even,
$$
\langle\Psi|Z_F|\Psi\rangle
=\sum_s p_s(-1)^{k(s)}
=\frac1M\sum_{k=0}^{M-1}(-1)^k=0.
$$
Thus the two pure core states have orthogonal supports. Tensoring the same spectator density and applying a common isometry preserve orthogonality and half-trace distance. $$

$$
in the two cases. The buffered two-sided matrix-unit identity supplies the same full raw receiver state, including its actual multiplicity, field, gauge, clock and support factors. on its charged complete service carrier. Its subsequent pointer/scoring operations act on the service. For dephasing, the vectors $|s\rangle_C|s\rangle_F|\psi_s\rangle$ are orthonormal, independently of overlaps among the $|\psi_s\rangle$.  +2\varepsilon
 +T(\mathcal D\widetilde{\mathcal N}(\rho_1),\rho_1),
$$
which proves (K.3f.4.5). ∎

## K.5 Throughput and Finite-Resolution Certificate Boundary

**Puzzle:** Under their stated causal and energy hypotheses, the Hawking--Penrose singularity theorems establish causal-geodesic incompleteness; they do not in general prove divergence of a curvature scalar. Weak cosmic censorship separately asks whether singular behavior arising from admissible data is hidden from future null infinity.

**PU Status:** Theorem K.5.1 bounds information throughput only on its registered finite-area channel and clock branch, while Theorem K.5.4 proves finite-resolution exit of a certified Fermi expansion before a formal framewise curvature divergence. These results exclude neither a naked singularity nor its causal visibility; they supply an operational information bound and a continuum-certificate failure criterion.

<a id="definition-k51-predictive-throughput"></a>**Definition K.5.1 (Predictive Throughput).**
For a protocol $\mathcal P_n$ consisting of $n$ registered boundary rounds, let $M_n$ be a finite classical message encoded into admissible interior preparations, let $\mathcal R_n$ be the exterior classical record, and let $T_n$ be the actual elapsed physical time. On the registered round-clock branch, $T_n\ge n\tau_{\min}$ with $\tau_{\min}>0$. Define
$$
L(S):=\sup_{\{\mathcal P_n\}}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{I(M_n;\mathcal R_n)}{T_n},
$$
where the supremum is over admissible message ensembles and protocols satisfying that clock certificate. This message-rate definition does not become trivial merely because a fixed interior Hilbert space has finite dimension.

<a id="theorem-k51-finite-area-conditional-nd-rid-throughput-bound"></a>**Theorem K.5.1 (Finite-Area Conditional ND-RID Throughput Bound).**
Assume geometric regularity, the boundary-density certificate of Theorem E.3, and the throughput hypotheses of Theorem 14.2.4.1: every effective crossing link is a memoryless refresh-branch channel $\mathcal E_N=(1-p)\Psi+pT_\sigma$ with $p>0$; the aggregate boundary capacity is at most the sum of the registered link capacities; no bypass channel is present; and each link is used at most once per registered round of duration at least $\tau_{\min}>0$. Then
$$L(S) \leq \frac{N_{\mathrm{eff\,links}}(S)C_{\max}}{\tau_{\min}} = \frac{\sigma_{\mathrm{eff\,link}}A(S)C_{\max}}{\tau_{\min}} + o(A),$$
where $C_{\max}:=C(\mathcal E_N)<\ln d_0$ by Theorem E.2 and $\sigma_{\mathrm{eff\,link}}=\chi/(\eta\delta^2)$ by Theorem E.3.

*Proof.* The aggregate-capacity hypothesis bounds one boundary round by $N_{\mathrm{eff\,links}}(S)C_{\max}$ nats. The registered clock gives at most one round per $\tau_{\min}$, and the density certificate gives the area form. ∎

<a id="lemma-k52-uniform-cyclewise-trace-distance-contraction"></a>**Lemma K.5.2 (Uniform Cyclewise Trace-Distance Contraction).**
Let
$$
\mathcal E_\gamma
=\mathcal U_n\circ\mathcal N_n\circ\cdots\circ
\mathcal U_1\circ\mathcal N_1,
\qquad n=n(\gamma),
$$
where every $\mathcal U_j(\rho)=U_j\rho U_j^\dagger$ is unitary and every CPTP map $\mathcal N_j$ obeys
$$
D_{tr}(\mathcal N_j(\rho),\mathcal N_j(\sigma))
\le f_{RID}D_{tr}(\rho,\sigma),
\qquad 0\le f_{RID}<1,
$$
for all states in the retained branch. Then
$$
D_{tr}(\mathcal E_\gamma(\rho_1),\mathcal E_\gamma(\rho_2))
\le f_{RID}^{n(\gamma)}D_{tr}(\rho_1,\rho_2).
$$

*Proof.* Unitary invariance of the trace norm gives
$$
D_{tr}(\mathcal U_j(\rho),\mathcal U_j(\sigma))
=D_{tr}(\rho,\sigma).
$$
Applying the assumed contraction at the first dissipative step and unitary invariance at the following holonomy gives a factor $f_{RID}$. Repeating this argument through all $n$ pairs yields by induction
$$
D_{tr}(\mathcal E_\gamma(\rho_1),\mathcal E_\gamma(\rho_2))
\le\left(\prod_{j=1}^n f_{RID}\right)D_{tr}(\rho_1,\rho_2)
=f_{RID}^nD_{tr}(\rho_1,\rho_2).
$$
Thus the unitary holonomies preserve trace distance and the declared dissipative maps supply all strict contraction. ∎

<a id="lemma-k53-framewise-curvature-criterion-for-a-controlled-local-expansion"></a>**Lemma K.5.3 (Framewise Curvature Criterion for a Controlled Local Expansion).**
Let $\gamma$ be a timelike geodesic in a Lorentzian manifold and let $e_a$ be a parallel orthonormal frame along $\gamma$ and extend it over the Fermi-normal neighborhood by parallel transport along the orthogonal coordinate geodesics. On that framed neighborhood of radius $\delta$, define
$$
\|R\|_{\mathrm{fr},\delta}
:=
\sup_{x\in U_\delta}\max_{a,b,c,d}|R_{abcd}(x)|.
$$
Assume the Fermi-normal expansion has a uniform remainder bound
$$
g_{ab}(x)=\eta_{ab}+Q_{ab}(R(0),x)+\mathcal R_{ab}(x),
\qquad
|Q_{ab}|\le C_1\|R\|_{\mathrm{fr},\delta}|x|^2,
\qquad
|\mathcal R_{ab}(x)|\le C_2|x|^3
$$
on $U_\delta$. A sufficient condition for the quadratic curvature correction to remain perturbative at resolution $\delta$ is
$$
C_1\|R\|_{\mathrm{fr},\delta}\delta^2\ll1
$$
together with $C_2\delta^3\ll1$. If the first dimensionless quantity is large, this Fermi-normal perturbative certificate fails. No equivalence with a single Lorentzian scalar curvature invariant is asserted.

*Proof.* For $|x|\le\delta$, the assumed estimate gives
$$
|g_{ab}(x)-\eta_{ab}|
\le C_1\|R\|_{\mathrm{fr},\delta}\delta^2+C_2\delta^3.
$$
Both terms are small under the displayed conditions, so the local expansion is controlled. If $C_1\|R\|_{\mathrm{fr},\delta}\delta^2\gg1$, the displayed upper estimate no longer certifies that the quadratic term is small; this sufficient Fermi-expansion certificate is therefore inconclusive at scale $\delta$. It does not prove that the actual correction is large or that no other manifold certificate exists. Lorentzian contractions can cancel and therefore cannot replace the framewise bound. ∎

<a id="theorem-k54-finite-resolution-exit-of-the-certified-fermi-expansion"></a>**Theorem K.5.4 (Finite-Resolution Exit of the Certified Fermi Expansion).**
Assume the hypotheses and framewise norm of Lemma K.5.3 along a curve, with constant $C_1>0$ in the quadratic estimate and constant operational resolution $\delta>0$ along that curve. If
$$
\|R\|_{\mathrm{fr},\delta}\longrightarrow\infty,
$$
then the sufficient perturbative condition
$$
C_1\|R\|_{\mathrm{fr},\delta}\delta^2\ll1
$$
fails at a finite value of the framewise curvature scale. Therefore the certified Fermi-normal continuum approximation cannot be continued all the way to the formal curvature divergence. This result does not prove formation of a horizon, a continuation of the underlying MPU dynamics, or weak cosmic censorship.

*Proof.* Since $C_1>0$ and $\delta>0$ are constant on the declared branch, divergence of $\|R\|_{\mathrm{fr},\delta}$ implies that $C_1\|R\|_{\mathrm{fr},\delta}\delta^2$ eventually exceeds every perturbative threshold. Lemma K.5.3 then ceases to certify the local expansion. No statement about the causal structure or microscopic successor dynamics follows from loss of this continuum certificate. ∎
