The same $\Lambda$ fixes both the metric curvature and $g_0$; no bare-versus-geometric vacuum mismatch is present because $b=\ell=0$.

The initial shear equation of the $S_{\mathrm{rad}}$ sector is

$$
\dot{(H_x-H_y)}+\sum_i H_i(H_x-H_y)=\kappa c^{2}(p_x-p_y),
$$

in physical time, with its fixed pressure normalization and ruler. Its prepared initial acceleration coefficient is therefore the same $\Lambda$-fixed $g_0$, not a separately adjusted coefficient. The static NR projection of this same $S_{g}$ is the lapse/potential functional (I.13c.5.4) of Theorem I.13c.5 with $a_\chi=g_0$: $E[\Phi]=(4\pi G)^{-1}\int g_0^2F(|\nabla\Phi|/g_0)\,d^3x+\int\rho_b\Phi\,d^3x$. Its Euler–Lagrange equation and outward-flux normalization are those of that theorem, items 2–3. Corollary H.1a.3 applies at $\beta_{\chi}=1$, yielding

$$
\begin{aligned}
&L_0(M_b)=\sqrt{GM_b/g_0},\quad \Sigma_\dagger=g_0/(2\pi G), \\
&16\pi G\,\Sigma_\dagger=c^{2}\sqrt{\Lambda}.
\end{aligned}
$$

These algebraic locks are common to every protocol's parameters. They do not equate the protocols' different accelerations or source states.

<a id="theorem-k54c-exhaustive-contracting-source-classification-and-normalized-response-endpoint-obstruction"></a>**Theorem K.5.4c (Exhaustive Contracting-Source Classification and Normalized-Response Endpoint Obstruction).**
For the complete source of Definition K.5.4a and same-action restriction of Lemma K.5.4b, the following declared directed class, maximal-development proof and full extension-relation classification apply. The negative endpoint component retains its exact real-source, normalization, bounded-response and physical-time premises.

#### 1. Controlling source and declared class

The action used here is **exactly the full source** of Definition K.5.4a, with its fixed pulse functions, scalar, every finite quantum factor and the gravitational functional of Lemma K.5.4b. It is not the scalar-deleted dust specialization. Definition K.5.4a realizes the expanding finite-window branch; the contracting initial data and extension class below form a separate class, declared and proved in this theorem.

Relevant inherited facts are:

1. The scalar q is a real dimensionless classical field with the full off-shell action

   $$
   S_q=\int\sqrt{-g}\,[-M(\partial q)^2/2-\kappa\sin^2(q)]\,d^4x.
   $$

   Its kinetic, gradient, potential, work and pressure terms all remain. It is not merely an angle inferred from the periodic potential. Definition K.5.4a retains $q$, $\dot{q}$ and the inverse $q$-clock among its controller responses.
2. The material carrier is the complete finite tensor product of Definition K.5.4a, of dimension $3^8$ times $2^{11}$. All arrow, CC, battery, bath, reset, readout and history factors remain. Its fixed Hamiltonian is

   $$
   H_{\mathrm{int}}(q) = m_* I + K + \sum_j f_j(q) A_j^c,
   $$

   with the exact matrices/functions of Definition K.5.4a, $m_*=10$, $K$ positive, and pulse norm less than 2.515. All $f_{j}$ have support strictly in $q>0$ and are zero, with all derivatives, for $q\le 0$. No pulse, identity-phase term or scalar term is deleted from the action because its value vanishes along the contracting trajectory.
3. The varied material Berry/embedding/lapse action is the action of Definition K.5.4a. It yields the matrix evolution, its actual energy $E=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_{\mathrm{int}})$, scalar force $n\operatorname{tr}(\rho\,\partial_qH_{\mathrm{int}})$, material stress $nE\,u^\mu u^\nu$, and number conservation. The initial ready context states $\rho_0,\rho_1$ and their mixtures have the common $E_0=11+1/(e+1)$. They commute with the bare $H_0=m_*I+K$. All initial purity, bath mixture and blank records remain owned.
4. Use the same $G=10^{-12}$, $\Lambda=10^{-18}$, $M=1$, $\kappa=10^{-12}$, $n_0=1$, $a_0=1$ and unit coordinate three-torus. The fully varied source equations of Lemma K.5.4b reduce on the aligned homogeneous branch to Einstein plus this material/scalar source, with no additional clock stress. No identification with a universal MPU action is claimed.

The **contracting initial branch** is specified before its endpoint is computed:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&q(0)=0,\quad \dot q(0)=-u_0,\quad u_0=10^{-4},\\
&H(0)=-\sqrt{(8 \pi G [E_0+M u_0^2/2]+\Lambda)/3}.
\end{aligned}
$$

These are contracting initial data of the same action. They are distinct from the expanding initial data of Definition K.5.4a. They are also the classical past companion of that expanding state; the stationary bare-ready density makes its pre-pulse microscopic density identical, but no time-reversal claim about the driven program is needed.

For a nontrivial source-contained communication test, allow a smooth ready-context field

$$
\rho(b,0)=(1-w(b))\, \rho_0 + w(b)\, \rho_1,\quad 0\le w(b)\le 1,
$$

and classical mixtures of such fields. All constant w are included. This generalizes the homogeneous *preparation* of Definition K.5.4a while preserving its full action and a homogeneous actual stress. It is part of the class declared by this theorem. The material Berry action has no derivatives between labels; every context has the same E0; the full scalar force vanishes wherever $q<0$. Thus all these configurations obey the same homogeneous geometry/scalar equations. No inhomogeneous stress, omitted scalar gradient source, or new gravitating apparatus has been assumed away. The prepared field and all installed factors, rather than a selected context output, form the retained source.

The comparison family contains every such w, every finite classical mixture, and every finite message ensemble of them. It does not include arbitrary energy-changing preparations or externally driven future controls. Those are different initial/protocol classes, not uncounted members of this one. The registered receiver is one exterior material world tube with its entire installed finite fibre, together with its scalar/geometry readouts. Its actual final record queries are bounded by all final POVMs on that complete fibre. No global tensor-product state of a continuum of labels, joint measurement across different exterior labels, or finite global Hilbert dimension is asserted or needed.

#### 2. Full regular evolution and exact reduction

Set $V=a^3$, $r=-q$ and $P=MV\dot{r}$. While $r\ge 0$, all installed pulse coefficients and derivatives vanish identically. Hence $\rho(b,t)=\exp(-iH_0t)\rho(b,0)\exp(iH_0t)$, $E=E_0$, and the scalar force is exactly zero. This is a proved null of the full source, not a modified Hamiltonian. In fact these ready densities are stationary, but unitarity rather than that simplification controls the entire finite carrier.

The fully varied equations reduce to

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dot r &= P/(M V),\\
\dot P &= -\kappa V \sin(2r),\\
\dot V &= -\sqrt{24 \pi G E_0 V + 12 \pi G P^2/M + [24 \pi G \kappa \sin^2(r)+3 \Lambda] V^2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
$$

Initial data are $V=1$, $r=0$, $P_0=Mu_0=10^{-4}$. The negative square root is the actual contracting Friedmann branch, not a selected sign at a later boundary. $H$ cannot change sign while the ordinary source exists because $H^2\ge\Lambda/3>0$. Its total density and pressure are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho_{\mathrm{tot}} &= E_0/V + P^2/(2M V^2) + \kappa \sin^2(r),\\
p_{\mathrm{tot}} &= P^2/(2M V^2) - \kappa \sin^2(r).
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
$$

Equation (1) follows by multiplying the full Friedmann equation by $9V^2$ and by varying the actual scalar before homogeneous restriction. The quantum energy, scalar pressure and work owners are not double counted. The scalar continuity equation and the quantum energy identity preserve the Einstein constraint. Momentum/off-diagonal constraints and scalar spatial gradients vanish on these actual solutions.

The vector field is smooth for $V>0$ and r,P finite. Therefore each admitted initial state has a unique local complete-source evolution; the quantum and scalar equations are not additional independently chosen trajectories. Fixed context fields w are different retained quantum preparations even though their geometry agrees.

#### 3. Finite terminal time, positive scalar momentum and source escape

Let

   $$
   \begin{gathered}
   \bar{T}=1/\sqrt{6\pi GE_0}, \\
   P_-=P_0-\kappa\bar{T},\quad P_+=P_0+\kappa\bar{T}.
   \end{gathered}
   $$

All these are fixed source quantities. Exact elementary bounds give $E_0>11$ and $\pi>3$, hence $\bar{T}<72000$ and

   $$
   P_->10^{-4}-7.2\times10^{-8}>0.
   \tag{3}
   $$

Numerically, only for orientation, $\bar{T}$ is about 68613.2321 and $P_-$ about $9.99314\times10^{-5}$. No numerical integration is used in the proof.

As long as the solution exists with $V>0$, V is decreasing and

$$
d \sqrt{V}/dt \le -\sqrt{6 \pi G E_0}.
$$

Consequently the regular solution cannot remain at positive $V$ past $\bar{T}$. Since $|\dot{P}|\le\kappa V\le\kappa$, the bounds $P_-\le P(t)\le P_+$ hold up to this time. In particular $P$ stays positive, $r$ increases, and the assumed $q\le 0$/pulses-off branch is self-consistent. There is no circular reliance on a source null that later fails.

A finite-time breakdown with $V$ bounded below is impossible: then $P$ and $\dot{r}$ are bounded on the finite interval, the density matrix remains in its compact finite state space, and the smooth local ODE extends. Thus the unique maximal regular interval is $[0,T)$, with $0<T\le\bar{T}$ and $V(t)$ tending to zero.

Let

$$
B=\sqrt{24\pi G E_0+12\pi G P_+^2/M
+24\pi G\kappa+3\Lambda}.
$$

For $0<V\le 1$, equation (1) gives $-\dot{V}\le B$. Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
V(t) &\le B(T-t),\\
\dot r(t) &\ge P_-/[M B(T-t)].
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
$$

Integrating (4) proves $r(t)$ tends to $+\infty$ logarithmically, so $q(t)$ tends to $-\infty$. This is escape of the actual scalar source, not a divergent curvature label assigned to a finite graph.

There is also an exact leading form. Because $|\dot{P}|\le\kappa V$ and $T$ is finite, $P$ has a limit $P^*>0$. Equation (1) then implies

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dot V &\to -b^*,\quad b^*=\sqrt{12 \pi G/M}\, P^*,\\
V/(T-t) &\to b^*,\\
r(t)/\log(1/(T-t)) &\to 1/\sqrt{12 \pi G M}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
$$

The last ratio follows by integrating $\dot{r}=P/(MV)$ and its limiting comparison. No derivative of an oscillatory potential limit is used. Thus $a$ has the stiff-source exponent 1/3, not the exponent 2/3 of the scalar-deleted dust specialization. Dropping the scalar would give the wrong endpoint law.

Every admitted w and classical mixture has this same T,V,r,P. All retained finite quantum factors have a unitary endpoint limit. That limit alone is not a full-source continuation because the scalar response does not have a source-state endpoint.

#### 4. Independently declared full-state extension relation

The exact extension class is declared as follows. It is not inherited from a smooth FRW extension definition.

A continuation must extend the same physical elapsed-time interval, including its finite boundary $T$; preserve the proper-time calibration on the overlap; and retain all the source operations of the regular interval and their probability laws there. It may replace metric geometry, add a quantum or nongeometric sector, change representation or use a larger normalized state space. No $C^2$ metric or finite-dimensional quantum geometry is required. The following are constitutive requirements of **this source-preserving extension relation**:

- The original finite quantum material algebra and its trace/probability rules are retained on overlaps, with no unowned discarded source, hidden reset or unledgered work.
- The original real scalar is a total real-valued source response. An endpoint may have a general normalized countably additive Radon probability law $\mu_{T}$ on R, rather than a sharp classical q. A quantum representation with real-q spectral measure is also allowed when its scalar outcome law has this property. This does not mean normality on L-infinity(R, Lebesgue), which would wrongly exclude the original Dirac preparations.
- For every bounded continuous compact-support postprocessing f of that real readout, endpoint response continuity means

  $$
  \lim_{t\to T^-} \text{expectation}[f(q(t))] = \int f\, d\mu_T.
  $$

  Constant response 1 retains expectation 1. The corresponding finite-algebra responses of the regular interval and any other retained bounded source responses are continuous in the declared topology. This is a response topology, not an assumption that curvature or every unbounded moment is finite.
- The overlap carries the actual scalar clock/proper-time calibration and the same source action. A finite-T endpoint cannot be moved to infinite physical elapsed time by relabeling it with r, although r itself is a valid local monotone clock reading. Internal causal support and any admitted exterior-record protocol must remain compatible with their retained probabilities and actual elapsed times. Arbitrary extra sectors are allowed if these same-source conditions and their own source ledger hold.

The real-readout requirement comes from retaining the physical q carrier, not from demanding a finite expectation of an arbitrary unbounded observable. Bounded postprocessing of an already retained readout does not install a new drive or detector source. Section 1 of Definition K.5.4a owns the noncompact real scalar, and the definition retains its q response; section 4 above declares the endpoint topology and state class.

**Properties of the extension relation.** The relation does not say that q must be bounded along every admitted history, require a bounce, prescribe a dead state, exclude nongeometric successors, or state any terminal conclusion. Ordinary regular source solutions with finite q extend in this topology by their locally unique equations. Every finite prefix of the very same contracting branch has a genuine same-source continuation, including prefixes after Fermi-certificate loss. Other bounded-q source developments can also extend. The existence of a terminal failure follows from (1)-(5), not from a 'no successor' clause in the definition.

Compactification is not excluded by its name. It fails this particular relation only if its new boundary state ceases to provide a normalized real-q law or drops the retained response continuity. Discontinuous jumps, endpoint resets, nonregular states at infinity and effective-scalar replacement may belong to other microscopic theories; this theorem neither exhausts nor refutes those changed-source/changed-topology classes.

#### 5. Exhaustive endpoint theorem, including nongeometric candidates

**Theorem.** No endpoint in the full extension class of section 4 exists for any admitted contracting preparation. This includes every additional sector and every metric, nonsmooth, quantum or nongeometric candidate satisfying that relation.

**Proof.** At each preterminal time the scalar law is $\delta_{q(t)}$. By section 3, $q(t)\to-\infty$. For any $f\in C_c(\mathbb{R})$, $f(q(t))$ is zero for all sufficiently late $t$, hence $\int f\,d\mu_T=0$ under endpoint continuity. If $\mu_{T}$ were a probability on $\mathbb{R}$, some bounded interval would have positive measure: $\mathbb{R}$ is the countable union of the intervals $[-n,n]$. A nonnegative compactly supported continuous cutoff equal to 1 on that interval would then have positive integral, a contradiction. Equivalently every compact-support response tends to zero while the unit response remains 1, which is mass escape rather than a normalized endpoint law on the retained source carrier. The proof depends on the scalar marginal only; attaching any extra sector cannot restore its missing normalized marginal. QED.

This proof does not confuse divergence of the mean of an unbounded operator with absence of a quantum state. Heavy-tailed real-q endpoint states are permitted, but each such probability still gives positive weight to some bounded interval and fails the proved limiting responses.

There is an independent **bounded installed-response check**. $U(q)=\kappa\sin^2(q)$ is already in the original physical scalar action. Since $r$ increases continuously from zero to infinity, there are sequences tending to $T$ with $r=n\pi$ and $r=\pi/2+n\pi$. Their $U$ responses are respectively 0 and $\kappa$. Thus $U$ has no endpoint limit. Even an angular compactification cannot furnish a continuous retained $U$ response for this trajectory. The invariant scalar density/pressure combination $\rho_q-p_q=2U$ has the same oscillation on the regular overlap. Multiplying $U$ by $V$ suppresses this observation but loses its full constitutive response: $\partial_V(VU)=U$. This check is supplementary; the normalized marginal theorem supplies the primary complete no-go.

The microscopic conclusion is source-specific and class-relative. It is stronger than a $C^2$ metric no-go because geometry is unrestricted at the endpoint. It is weaker than a universal impossibility of every conceivable microscopic successor, which is not claimed or required by this declared branch.

#### 6. Curvature, certificate exit, causal support and actual clock

Equation (2) gives $H^2\ge 4\pi GP_-^2/(3MV^2)$, hence $H^2$ diverges. The comoving frame has $R_{ijkl}=H^2(\delta_{ik}\delta_{jl}-\delta_{il}\delta_{jk})$. Its central framewise curvature therefore diverges regardless of cancellations in a scalar contraction. This is actual curvature of the same full source metric.

For every finite threshold $K^*>H(0)^2$ there is a time $t^*<T$ with $H(t^*)^2=K^*$. It is unique because $\dot{H}=-4\pi G(E_0/V+P^2/(MV^2))<0$ and $H<0$. Any existing fixed-radius Fermi neighborhood has framed curvature supremum at least that central component. Its sufficient quadratic certificate cannot remain perturbative past a corresponding finite threshold; if its chart or cubic remainder certificate fails first, that is an earlier certificate exit. No central value is falsely identified with a neighborhood supremum. Lemma K.5.4d supplies an actual initial neighborhood on central times [1,2], proves the Fermi exponential is injective, and populates $C_1=16$, $C_2=10^{13}$, fixed $\delta=10^{-6}$, framed-neighborhood curvature below 1 and tolerance $10^{-2}$. The quadratic and cubic bounds are respectively below $16\times10^{-12}$ and $10^{-5}$. The explicit source-derivative recurrences and rational coefficient bounds below give these budgets. These deliberately loose ideal-model constants are not a Planck-scale or finite-hardware calibration. No uniform remainder through the crunch is claimed.

At every $t<T$, the metric is nondegenerate, globally hyperbolic on the compact spatial torus, and material labels follow timelike comoving curves. The scalar field uses its original canonical local action and light cone. No weak-censorship visibility assertion is made, since this compact source is not the asymptotically flat null-infinity setting. The endpoint exclusion does not assume any causal property of a successor beyond the retained response/time relation; adding causal or throughput constraints cannot create a forbidden scalar marginal.

The physical $q$ clock is especially simple on this contracting branch: $\dot{r}=P/(MV)>0$ for the entire lifetime. Its exact calibration satisfies

   $$
   \begin{gathered}
   dt/dr=MV/P>0,\\
   t(r)=\int_0^rMV/P\,ds,\\
   t(r)\to T<\infty\quad\text{as } r\to\infty.
   \end{gathered}
   $$

It is the same source-owned ideal classical work/clock variable as in Definition K.5.4a, not a free external clock coefficient or a finite quantum clock. Its energy and pressure remain in (2). Local clock inversion is exact on every finite interval. The finite endpoint is actual comoving proper time, not an artificial finite computational horizon; its infinite r reading cannot make it infinite elapsed time while preserving that calibration. No infinite physical tape, zero-cost readout or infinitely many positive-duration rounds is claimed.

#### 7. Complete source-contained no-crossing/no-bypass service

Choose a fixed smooth comoving interior $B$ strictly inside the spatial torus and one receiver material world tube at $b_{R}$ outside $B$. The entire installed finite fibre of Definition K.5.4a at $b_{R}$, not a selected record factor, is the receiver carrier. Its quantum record algebra is $B(H_R)$; its accompanying classical readouts are the actual scalar, geometry, foliation and material embedding on that world tube. This is the complete receiving record algebra of the registered service. The ideal mean-source convention gives a matrix state at each material label; this argument does not manufacture a global continuum tensor-product state, global quantum Hamiltonian, infinitely many detector devices or unspecified joint exterior records.

Encode a finite classical $M$ into an allowed ready-context field $w_M(b)$ that agrees with one fixed field outside $B$. Take the receiver's complete initial fibre marginal independent of $M$. Classical mixtures are allowed when that complete receiver marginal remains independent of $M$. No claim about arbitrary inter-label joint quantum outcomes is needed. On $q\le 0$ the full internal evolution is local in the material label with generator H0. Thus the complete receiver state is

$$
\rho_R(t|M)=\exp(-iH_0 t)\, \rho_R(0)\, \exp(iH_0 t),
$$

independent of M. Every final receiver instrument/POVM consequently has the same outcome law for all messages. Allowing every final POVM is only a generous mathematical upper bound on the installed source's retained-record queries, not an assertion that new cost-free detectors or arbitrary adaptive drives have been installed. The scalar and gravitational receiver responses are also M-independent because their exact sources agree. There is no message-dependent scalar force, stress, receiver initial correlation, mass flux across the comoving boundary, or extra controller channel. This checks the whole actual source inventory for a bypass into this registered receiver, rather than inferring a rate from finite dimension.

An admitted actual protocol is fixed installed source evolution, any finite registration of passive proper-time waiting rounds, and a final query of the receiver's retained source record. No intermediate reset, energy-changing measurement, sending drive or new source is included. For every such protocol and every admitted message ensemble,

$$
I(M; R_n)=0.
$$

This statement covers the entire declared final record, including any classical postprocessing, not only a chosen detector coordinate. It does not claim zero signaling for arbitrary scalar waves, energy-changing encodings, external drives, or unspecified joint measurements at different material labels. Those alter the explicit source/protocol or receiving-algebra class and require qualification.

For a registered positive proper round duration $\tau_{\min}$, the actual calibrated clock gives $T_n\ge n\tau_{\min}$. Since this branch has a finite lifetime, only finitely many such rounds can finish. The direct zero-transfer bound holds for every one of them. **Definition K.5.1's infinite-$n$ limsup is inapplicable here; it is not assigned the number zero.** Neither a positive-capacity refresh channel nor Appendix E.3's positive link-density certificate is imported. The original problem admits an independently justified no-crossing branch and does not require a positive-capacity service.

The spatially varying ready preparation and the single-world-tube receiver service are separately declared, explicitly solved same-action source data. They extend the homogeneous-context preparation of Definition K.5.4a. The full actual quantum inventory at each label remains the original finite material fibre; its classical mean-source field is not mislabeled a finite quantum universe. No extra continuum quantum entanglement/Hamiltonian assumption is used to strengthen the no-transfer statement.

#### 8. Exhaustive terminal classification

For every admitted smooth ready-context field and every classical mixture:

1. Every finite prefix ending at $t<T$ has a unique regular same-action full-source continuation. There are no alternative source trajectories, early protocol dead states, quantum singularities or clock turning points on that interval.
2. Crossing a curvature/Fermi-certificate threshold does not terminate this evolution. The full equations, internal state and source clock continue until $T$.
3. The only finite future terminal boundary of the regular solution is $T$. Its full source escape is (3)-(5). The terminal continuation set in section 4 is empty, by the normalized scalar-response theorem, including arbitrary added/nongeometric sectors that retain that scalar response.
4. The finite material density matrix has a well-defined algebraic limit, but it is only a subsystem. Continuing its unitary in an external parameter does not create the missing scalar marginal, physical-clock endpoint or full source state.
5. There is no infinite future regular continuation of this contracting branch. Nor is there an infinite future evolution through $T$ in the admitted response-preserving extension relation, because any such evolution would restrict to a forbidden endpoint at its finite physical time $T$.
6. A continuation that removes the finite-time boundary, replaces the real scalar with a different state notion, permits discontinuous source resets, or changes the action is outside this exact relation. This is a classification boundary, not an assertion that those theories are impossible.

ODE uniqueness and the inequalities hold on the complete continuum of w fields and mixtures; no finite sampling, trajectory scan or bounded graph search is used. The endpoint theorem quantifies over all eligible extension states and sectors, so failure of one candidate is not substituted for an exhaustive no-go.

#### 9. Nonvacuity and optional expanding source check

The regular contracting solution on every compact prefix supplies a nonempty physical background class, genuine scalar/material clock, actual source curvature and a complete finite no-transfer service. Its prefixes have nontrivial extensions. The definition does not make all source evolutions terminate by fiat.

For additional comparison, the same fixed action of Definition K.5.4a with the original expanding homogeneous initial data has no finite future ODE blow-up. Do not extrapolate its finite-program mean-force cancellation: if $q$ later revisits a pulse, $E(t)$ and the full scalar force must be kept. Nevertheless $H_{\mathrm{int}}(q)$ is globally positive and bounded, the pulse functions and their derivatives are smooth with compact support, and

   $$
   \begin{gathered}
   \dot{H}=-4\pi G[nE(t)+M\dot{q}^2]\le 0, \\
   H\ge\sqrt{\Lambda/3}>0.
   \end{gathered}
   $$

The preserved constraint bounds qdot on every finite interval, a is bounded above and below there, and the finite density matrix stays in its compact state space. Thus the full backreacting homogeneous vector field extends to every finite future time. This is a same-action nonterminal witness, not an inherited infinite operational-clock or positive-throughput certificate. It is not needed by the contracting endpoint theorem and does not enlarge the classified ready-code branch into all inhomogeneous forward Einstein data.

#### 10. Declared scope and equivalence

Domain: the complete fixed hybrid source action of Definition K.5.4a and the declared contracting ready-context field/mixture preparations; full finite material carrier, genuine real scalar, conserved material measure, and the fixed gravitational/foliation source. Extension class: source/response/time-preserving full-state extensions as in section 4, including arbitrary eligible nongeometric or added sectors. The equivalence relation is: marked source- and response-preserving spatial relabeling, quantum representation equivalence and proper-time-preserving overlap, not deletion of q or a change of clock. The quantifiers include every finite time up to the analytically bounded T, all admitted preparations and every eligible endpoint; no sampled-state budget. The proof uses varied source equations, elementary ODE bounds, normalized probability/compact-support theorem, factorized/no-bypass response proof. Falsifiers: source force on $q<0$, nonuniform stress from a ready context, P reaching zero, a finite-time endpoint law on R with the derived compact-support expectations, or a message-dependent registered receiver response.

<a id="lemma-k54d-populated-initial-fermi-neighborhood-on-the-same-source"></a>**Lemma K.5.4d (Populated Initial Fermi Neighborhood on the Same Source).**
The quantitative initial certificate used in Theorem K.5.4c is the following existing same-source construction. The fixed resolution is a source-metric length; loss of this certificate and the later source-state endpoint obstruction are separate conclusions.

#### 1. Source enclosure on a real interval

The source escape proof gives, with $\pi<4$ and $11<E_0<12$,

$$
\begin{gathered}
\bar{T}<72000;\\
0.000099928<P<0.000100072;\\
-\dot{V}<B<0.000035.
\end{gathered}
$$

Therefore, throughout $0\le t\le 4$, $V\ge 1-4B>0.999$; $|H|=|\dot{V}|/(3V)<0.00002$; $|\dot{q}|=P/V<0.0002$; $nE_0=E_0/V<13$; and $0<a^2\le 1$. The scalar remains nonpositive and all actual installed pulses are zero. All metric coefficients used here are the exact solution of the fully varied source, not a surrogate curvature field.

For explicit derivative bounds put $d=E_0/V$, $v=\dot{q}$, $f=a^2$, $s=\sin(2q)$, $c=\cos(2q)$, and $z=a^{-1}$. Along the actual solution,

  $$
  \begin{gathered}
  \dot{h}=-b(d+v^2),\quad \dot{d}=-3hd,\quad \dot{v}=-3hv-\kappa s, \\
  \dot{f}=2hf,\quad \dot{s}=2vc,\quad \dot{c}=-2vs,\quad \dot{z}=-hz, \\
  b=4\pi G<16\times10^{-12},\quad \kappa=10^{-12}.
  \end{gathered}
  $$

On the stated interval use $|h|\le 2\times10^{-5}$, $|v|\le 2\times10^{-4}$, $d\le 13$, $|s|,|c|\le 1$, $f,z\le 2$. Iterated application of this polynomial derivation gives the following conservative bounds:

$$
\begin{gathered}
|d^kh/dt^k|\ \text{and}\ |d^k(fh)/dt^k|<10^{-4}\quad\text{for } 0\le k\le 4;\\
|d^kf/dt^k|\le 2\quad\text{for } 0\le k\le 6;\\
|d^kz/dt^k|\le 2\quad\text{for } 0\le k\le 4,\ \text{and for } k\ge 1 \text{ the bound is } <10^{-3}.
\end{gathered}
$$

The exact coefficient-sum bounds use the displayed polynomial identities and rational intervals. They use rational upper bounds on every coefficient and variable, rather than sampling the ODE. The nonzero ambient Christoffel coefficients are $\Gamma^0_{ij}=fh\,\delta_{ij}$ and $\Gamma^i_{0j}=\Gamma^i_{j0}=h\,\delta_{ij}$. Thus their time derivatives through order four are all bounded by $10^{-4}$; their positive-order derivatives are bounded by $10^{-8}$. Spatial derivatives vanish.

#### 2. Construct the chart and bound its derivatives

For a central proper time $\tau$ in [1,2], start each orthogonal spacelike geodesic at $(\tau,0)$ with initial tangent $(0,z(\tau)X)$, where $|X|\le r_0=10^{-3}$. Integrate its affine geodesic equation for parameter $\lambda$ from 0 to 1. Write the endpoint $F(\tau,X)$. This is exactly the comoving Fermi exponential map; $X$ components are in the initial orthonormal spatial frame. The initial tangent has source-metric squared norm $|X|^2$, conserved by the geodesic equation, so its affine interval $[0,1]$ has physical proper length $|X|$. Thus $\delta$ below is a fixed source-metric length, not merely small coordinate displacement.

The initial tangent has component norm below 0.001002. A bootstrap with the stated Christoffel bounds gives tangent norm below 0.002, temporal displacement below $10^{-8}$, and spatial displacement below 0.003 for the whole geodesic. The geodesic first-order field is $(u,-\Gamma uu)$. On this tube its first derivative multilinear norm, in coordinate max norm, is at most 1; its second through fourth derivative norms are below $10^{-3}$. The position block is linear with derivative norm 1. For the temporal acceleration, the $m$-th derivative norm is bounded by $3\epsilon^2|(fh)^{(m)}|+6m\epsilon|(fh)^{(m-1)}|+3m(m-1)|(fh)^{(m-2)}|$, where $\epsilon=0.002$ and absent negative-order terms are omitted. For $m=2$ the largest term is $6|fh|\le 0.00024$; for $m=3,4$ the positive-order Christoffel derivative bound $10^{-8}$ applies. Thus each is $<10^{-3}$, including all index orderings. The initial-data map has derivative multilinear norms at most 2 through order four. Differentiating the integral equation and using Gronwall ($e<3$) gives uniform endpoint-flow derivative bounds

For example the successive scalar majorants are $2e$; $e(2+10^{-3}\cdot 6^2)$; $e(2+10^{-3}\cdot(3\cdot 7\cdot 6+6^3))$; and $e(2+10^{-3}\cdot(4\cdot 8\cdot 6+3\cdot 7^2+6\cdot 7\cdot 6^2+6^4))$. Each lies below the stated next bound.

For injectivity use the much sharper first-variation bound rather than those high-derivative envelopes: the acceleration has norm $<2\times10^{-9}$, its velocity Jacobian $<2\times10^{-6}$, and its position Jacobian $<2\times10^{-9}$. Substituting these in the once-integrated variation equations with initial spatial derivative $a^{-1}<1.001$ gives $\lVert DF-I\rVert_\infty<1/100$. Thus F is injective with invertible derivative and is a genuine Fermi chart on the stated tube. Its image is inside the single local torus cube already checked.

#### 3. Populate the remainder and curvature constants

The pulled-back metric is $g_F=(DF)^Tg(F)DF$. The ambient metric and its derivatives through order three are bounded by 2. The flow derivative bounds above give every third spatial partial derivative of every component of $g_{F}$ a bound below $10^{12}$: expanding the product and third-order chain rules uses at most $16\cdot 27\cdot 5\cdot 64=138240$ terms, each bounded by 2 times a product of at most five factors $\le 16$. This is a neighborhood/frame bound, not an identification of the norm with a scalar invariant or central component.

Choose and retain the fixed resolution $\delta=10^{-6}$ in these source units and the sufficient-certificate tolerance $\theta=10^{-2}$. The actual chart exists on the much larger $r_0$ tube, and

## K.6 Conditional Strong-CP Branch

**Puzzle:** Quantum chromodynamics permits a CP-violating term proportional to $\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}\,\operatorname{tr}(G_{\mu\nu}\widetilde G^{\mu\nu})$. The neutron-electric-dipole-moment limit (Abel et al. 2020), combined with a hadronic estimate for its $\bar\theta$ dependence (Pospelov and Ritz 2005), constrains $|\bar\theta|$ at the $10^{-10}$ scale when that contribution dominates. Why is this parameter so small, despite the observed CP violation in the weak sector?

**Conditional branch statement:** If the framework is supplied with a constructed equivariant $\sigma$-CP parameter map, an accepted gauge-topology bridge relating the QCD second-Chern sector to the retained holonomy coordinate, a $\sigma$-invariant vacuum, a certified operative QCD vacuum-selection functional with that vacuum as a global minimizer on the retained invariant sector, and a common-convention absolute determinant-line certificate for the full quark mass matrices, then $z_{\mathrm{CP}}=e^{i\bar\theta}=1$ and hence $\bar\theta\equiv0\pmod{2\pi}$. The all-harmonic route of Theorem K.6.2a can replace the first-harmonic ansatz when its positive sector-partition hypotheses are constructed. The construction of these branch hypotheses from QCD remains open.

### K.6.1 The Physical θ-Parameter

On the branch where the full quark mass matrix $M_q$ is nonsingular, the physical CP-violating parameter in QCD is the combination:
$$
\bar\theta=\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}+\arg(\det M_q)\pmod{2\pi}
$$
Here $\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}$ is the vacuum angle and $M_q$ is the quark mass matrix. The neutron electric dipole moment limits (Abel et al. 2020; Baker et al. 2006) constrain $\bar\theta$ through a hadronic conversion. Under the estimates below and with the $\bar\theta$ contribution dominant, the resulting constraint is at the $10^{-10}$ scale and requires an account of both contributions to $\bar\theta$.

<a id="definition-k61-topological-charge-density-and-quantized-sector"></a>**Definition K.6.1 (Topological Charge Density and Quantized Sector).** Adopt $\operatorname{tr}(T^aT^b)=\delta^{ab}/2$ and $\widetilde G^{\mu\nu}=\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}G_{\rho\sigma}/2$. Define
$$
Q(x)=\frac{g_s^2}{32\pi^2}G^a_{\mu\nu}(x)\widetilde G^{a\mu\nu}(x).
$$
For a smooth finite-action Euclidean $SU(3)$ connection on a compact oriented four-manifold, or on $\mathbb R^4$ with pure-gauge asymptotics that extend the bundle over $S^4$,
$$
\nu=\int d^4x\,Q(x)\in\mathbb Z
$$
is the second Chern number in this convention. For a general local configuration or noncompact boundary condition, the integral need not be an integer.

In the small-angle regime, the neutron electric dipole moment contribution from $\bar\theta$ scales as $d_n\sim10^{-16}\bar\theta$ e·cm, with a coefficient estimated in Pospelov and Ritz (2005). Abel et al. (2020) report $|d_n| < 1.8 \times 10^{-26}$ e·cm at 90% confidence. Inferring a bound on $\bar\theta$ from this experimental limit requires the hadronic conversion and control of contributions from other CP-violating operators.

### K.6.3 The σ-Involution on Gr(2,8)

<a id="definition-k63-σ-involution"></a>**Definition K.6.3 (σ-Involution).** The complex Grassmannian $\text{Gr}(2,8)$ admits a canonical anti-holomorphic involution $\sigma$ induced by complex conjugation on $\mathbb{C}^8$:
$$\sigma: \text{Gr}(2,8) \to \text{Gr}(2,8), \quad W \mapsto \bar{W}$$
where $\bar{W}$ denotes the complex conjugate subspace. Equivalently, on density matrices: $\sigma(\rho) = \bar{\rho}$.

<a id="definition-k64-kähler-triple"></a>**Definition K.6.4 (Kähler Triple).** The Grassmannian $\text{Gr}(2,8)$ carries three compatible structures:

- **Riemannian metric** $g_{KE}$: the Kähler-Einstein metric
- **Complex structure** $J$: multiplication by $i$ on tangent spaces
- **Symplectic form** $\omega$: the Kähler form

satisfying $\omega(X, Y) = g_{KE}(JX, Y)$ and $\nabla J = 0$.

<a id="lemma-k61-bures-kähler-relation-under-the-qfi-normalization"></a>**Lemma K.6.1 (Bures--Kähler Relation under the QFI Normalization).** Assume the invariant Kähler--Einstein metric on $\operatorname{Gr}(2,8)$ is normalized so that its tensor on the registered interface tangent basis equals the SLD quantum Fisher tensor:
$$
g_{KE}=F_Q.
$$
Then
$$
g_B=\frac14g_{KE}.
$$

*Proof.* By the Bures convention used in the manuscript, $g_B=F_Q/4$. The normalization hypothesis gives $F_Q=g_{KE}$, so substitution yields $g_B=g_{KE}/4$. In the interface basis of Theorem Z.5, $F_Q=I_{24}$ and hence $g_B=I_{24}/4$. ∎

<a id="proposition-k61-properties-of-σ"></a>**Proposition K.6.1 (Properties of σ).**

(a) $\sigma^2 = \text{id}$ (involution)

(b) $\sigma_* \circ J = -J \circ \sigma_*$ (anti-holomorphic)

(c) $\sigma^* g_{KE} = g_{KE}$ (isometry)

(d) $\sigma^* \omega = -\omega$ (anti-symplectic)

*Proof.* Conjugation twice is the identity, so $\sigma^2=\operatorname{id}$. At a point $W$, identify
$$
T_W\operatorname{Gr}(2,8)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,W^\perp).
$$
In these coordinates, $d\sigma(A)=\overline A$ and $J(A)=iA$. Hence
$$
d\sigma(JA)=\overline{iA}=-i\overline A=-J(d\sigma A),
$$
proving anti-holomorphicity. In these natural tangent coordinates, write the invariant metric as
$$
g_{KE}(A,B)=c\,\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(A^\dagger B),
\qquad c>0.
$$
For the normalization $g_{KE}=F_Q$ of Lemma K.6.1, $\rho=P_W/a$ has tangent $\dot\rho_A=a^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}0&A^\dagger\\A&0\end{pmatrix}$. The SLD spectral formula gives
$$
F_Q(A,B)=\frac4a\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(A^\dagger B),
$$
so $c=4/a=2$ on the $a=2$ branch. Therefore
$$
g_{KE}(\overline A,\overline B)
=c\,\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(A^T\overline B)
=c\,\operatorname{Re}\overline{\operatorname{tr}(A^\dagger B)}
=g_{KE}(A,B).
$$
Transitivity and invariance propagate this equality over the orbit, proving $\sigma^*g_{KE}=g_{KE}$. Finally,
$$
(\sigma^*\omega)(A,B)
=g_{KE}(Jd\sigma A,d\sigma B)
=-g_{KE}(d\sigma JA,d\sigma B)
=-g_{KE}(JA,B)
=-\omega(A,B).
$$
Thus all four assertions hold. ∎

<a id="proposition-k62-parity-transformation-of-gauge-fields"></a>**Proposition K.6.2 (Parity Transformation of Gauge Fields).** Under the parity transformation $P: \mathbf{x} \to -\mathbf{x}$, the components of the gluon field strength tensor transform as:
$$P: G^{0i} \to -G^{0i}, \quad G^{ij} \to G^{ij}$$

*Proof.* The field strength tensor $G_{\mu\nu} = \partial_\mu A_\nu - \partial_\nu A_\mu + ig[A_\mu, A_\nu]$ transforms under parity according to the vector nature of $A_\mu$. Since $A_0$ is a scalar and $A_i$ are vectors under parity, we have $P: A_0(\mathbf{x}) \to A_0(-\mathbf{x})$ and $P: A_i(\mathbf{x}) \to -A_i(-\mathbf{x})$. Combined with $\partial_0 \to \partial_0$ and $\partial_i \to -\partial_i$, the components transform as stated. The dual tensor $\tilde{G}^{\mu\nu} = \frac{1}{2}\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}G_{\rho\sigma}$ inherits opposite parity, yielding $P: \mathrm{tr}(G\tilde{G}) \to -\mathrm{tr}(G\tilde{G})$. ∎

<a id="theorem-k61-conditional-sigma-cp-correspondence"></a>**Theorem K.6.1 (Conditional $\sigma$--CP Correspondence).** Assume the retained gauge-vacuum branch carries an equivariant parameter map
$$
\Phi_{CP}:\mathcal M_{\mathrm{vac}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Gr}(2,8)
$$
that intertwines physical CP with complex conjugation $\sigma$. Assume independently that this physical CP action has a unitary implementation $U_{CP}$ on the retained physical Hilbert space, and assume its registered $U(1)$ holonomy coordinate obeys $e^{i\theta}\mapsto e^{-i\theta}$. Then:

1. $\sigma$ is antiholomorphic on $\operatorname{Gr}(2,8)$;
2. physical CP is represented unitarily on Hilbert space, while its induced action on the declared complex parameter coordinate is antiholomorphic;
3. the registered holonomy coordinate transforms as $\theta\mapsto-\theta$ modulo $2\pi$.

*Proof.* Complex conjugation on $\mathbb C^8$ descends to $W\mapsto\overline W$ on $U(8)/(U(2)\times U(6))$ and satisfies $d\sigma\circ J=-J\circ d\sigma$, proving item 1. The equivariance hypothesis transfers this action to the physical CP parameter branch, while CP itself has a unitary Hilbert-space implementation, proving item 2. Finally,
$$
\overline{e^{i\theta}}=e^{-i\theta},
$$
so injectivity of the circle coordinate modulo $2\pi$ gives item 3. ∎

### K.6.4 θ-Parameter Embedding in the Attractor Geometry

The $\theta$-vacuum structure of QCD and the PCE-Attractor geometry are distinct constructions. Relating their topological data requires an accepted gauge-topology bridge satisfying Proposition K.6.4.

<a id="definition-k65-tautological-bundle"></a>**Definition K.6.5 (Tautological Bundle).** Let $\mathcal{S} \to \text{Gr}(2,8)$ be the tautological bundle, where the fiber over $V \in \text{Gr}(2,8)$ is the 2-plane $V$ itself:
$$\mathcal{S} = \{(V, v) : V \in \text{Gr}(2,8), v \in V\}$$

<a id="definition-k66-determinant-line-bundle"></a>**Definition K.6.6 (Determinant Line Bundle).** The determinant line bundle is:
$$\mathcal{L} = \det(\mathcal{S}) = \Lambda^2 \mathcal{S}$$

This is a complex line bundle over $\text{Gr}(2,8)$ whose fiber over $V$ is $\Lambda^2 V \cong \mathbb{C}$.

<a id="definition-k67-instanton-topological-sector-classification"></a>**Definition K.6.7 (Instanton Topological-Sector Classification).** Isomorphism classes of principal $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ bundles over $S^4$ are classified by
$$
\pi_3(\mathrm{SU}(3))\cong\mathbb Z.
$$
A framed finite-action $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ connection on $\mathbb R^4$ that extends over the point at infinity therefore has an integer topological charge $\nu$. This integer labels the topological sector; it does not classify gauge-equivalence classes of instanton connections inside that sector.

*Proof.* Trivializing on the two hemispheres gives the clutching classification. Hatcher (2017, Proposition 1.11) supplies the rank-three complex-bundle version; choosing unitary determinant-one frames gives its $SU(3)$ version on $S^4$. The determinant fibration $SU(3)\to U(3)\to U(1)$ has vanishing $\pi_3(U(1))$ and $\pi_4(U(1))$, so the clutching classes are $\pi_3(SU(3))$. The homogeneous-space fibration
$$
\mathrm{SU}(2)\longrightarrow\mathrm{SU}(3)\longrightarrow S^5
$$
has long exact homotopy segment
$$
\pi_4(S^5)\longrightarrow\pi_3(\mathrm{SU}(2))
\longrightarrow\pi_3(\mathrm{SU}(3))
\longrightarrow\pi_3(S^5).
$$
Because $\pi_4(S^5)=0$, $\pi_3(S^5)=0$, and $\mathrm{SU}(2)\cong S^3$, exactness gives
$$
\pi_3(\mathrm{SU}(3))\cong\pi_3(S^3)\cong\mathbb Z.
$$
Use anti-Hermitian curvature $F$ in the fundamental representation, the ordinary matrix trace, and the convention $c(E)=\det(I+F/(2\pi i))$. For $SU(3)$, $\operatorname{tr}F=0$, so its degree-four part is $-\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(F/(2\pi i))^2=\operatorname{tr}(F\wedge F)/(8\pi^2)$. Cohen (undated, Theorem 3.49) identifies this form with the second Chern class. Orient the sphere and clutching generator so that the selected BPST representative has charge $+1$. Thus the integer is
$$
\nu=\frac1{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}(F\wedge F).
$$
Embedding the charge-one BPST $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ instanton (Belavin, Polyakov, Schwartz, and Tyupkin 1975) into $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ realizes a generator. Continuous position, scale, and gauge-orientation parameters remain within a charge sector, so $\nu$ classifies sectors rather than individual connections. ∎

<a id="definition-k68-theta-vacuum-as-a-generalized-sector-state"></a>**Definition K.6.8 ($\theta$-Vacuum as a Generalized Sector State).** Let $|n\rangle$ denote orthonormal winding-sector representatives. For $N\in\mathbb N$, define the normalized approximant
$$
|\theta;N\rangle
=\frac1{\sqrt{2N+1}}
\sum_{n=-N}^{N}e^{in\theta}|n\rangle.
$$
The symbol $|\theta\rangle$ denotes the associated generalized superselection label or a separately constructed thermodynamic-limit state; the formal series
$$
\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}e^{in\theta}|n\rangle
$$
is not a norm-convergent Hilbert-space vector.

<a id="proposition-k63-cp-transformation-of-θ-vacuum"></a>**Proposition K.6.3 (CP Transformation of θ-Vacuum).** Assume physical CP has a unitary implementation $U_{CP}$ and the orthonormal sector representatives in Definition K.6.8 are chosen compatibly so that $U_{CP}|n\rangle=|-n\rangle$ for every integer $n$. Then, for every nonnegative integer $N$,
$$
U_{CP}|\theta;N\rangle=|-\theta;N\rangle.
$$
The induced generalized sector label transforms as $\theta\mapsto-\theta$ modulo $2\pi$. The same identity for a thermodynamic-limit state requires a separately supplied limit construction compatible with $U_{CP}$.

*Proof.* Reversal of the topological charge sends sector $n$ to sector $-n$; the stated representative convention additionally controls the vectors and their phases. Unitarity makes $U_{CP}$ complex linear. Since the index set $\{-N,\ldots,N\}$ is invariant under $n\mapsto-n$,
$$
U_{CP}|\theta;N\rangle
=\frac1{\sqrt{2N+1}}\sum_{n=-N}^{N}e^{in\theta}|-n\rangle
=\frac1{\sqrt{2N+1}}\sum_{m=-N}^{N}e^{-im\theta}|m\rangle
=|-\theta;N\rangle.
$$
The characters $n\mapsto e^{in\theta}$ identify the generalized label modulo $2\pi$, giving its claimed transformation. Passing this finite identity to a separately constructed limit requires that construction to intertwine $U_{CP}$; no Hilbert-norm convergence of the formal infinite series is asserted. ∎

<a id="corollary-k61-cp-invariant-theta"></a>**Corollary K.6.1 (CP-Invariant $\theta$).** CP-invariant vacuum labels satisfy

\theta\in\{0,\pi\}

<a id="proposition-k64-gauge-topology-bridge-requirement"></a>**Proposition K.6.4 (Gauge-Topology Bridge Requirement).** The embedding $\iota:G_{\mathrm{SM}}\hookrightarrow U(8)$ does not by itself identify QCD instanton sectors with holonomies of the tautological determinant line over $\operatorname{Gr}(2,8)$. Such an identification requires an additional construction mapping the second Chern class of the retained $SU(3)$ gauge bundle to the first-Chern or holonomy datum of a specified line bundle, together with a proof that the map preserves the integer charge and the CP action.

Equivalently, instanton number is represented by $c_2$ of the four-dimensional $SU(3)$ bundle, whereas a determinant line carries $c_1$. The group embedding alone supplies no homomorphism equating those characteristic classes. Therefore the claimed correspondence is available only after the additional bridge construction stated above. ∎

### K.6.5 PCE Cost Functional on S¹

The $\theta$-parameter lives on the circle $S^1 \cong U(1)$. The retained PCE cost is specified on the first-harmonic branch of Theorem K.6.2.

<a id="definition-k69-topological-susceptibility"></a>**Definition K.6.9 (Topological Susceptibility).** On a translation-invariant Euclidean branch, let $C(x):=\langle Q(x)Q(0)\rangle_c$ be an absolutely integrable real connected covariance. Assume that the integrated charges $\nu_D:=\int_D Q(x)\,d^4x$ exist in mean square for the retained bounded measurable regions and that their second moments permit Fubini's theorem. Choose regions $D_L$ with volumes $V_L:=|D_L|>0$, $V_L\to\infty$, and
$$
\frac{|D_L\cap(D_L-z)|}{V_L}\longrightarrow1
\quad\text{for every }z\in\mathbb R^4.
$$
Then
$$
\chi_{\mathrm{top}}
:=\int_{\mathbb R^4}C(z)\,d^4z
=\lim_{L\to\infty}
\frac{\langle\nu_{D_L}^2\rangle-\langle\nu_{D_L}\rangle^2}{V_L}.
$$
Indeed, translation invariance and Fubini give
$$
\frac{\operatorname{Var}(\nu_{D_L})}{V_L}
=\int_{\mathbb R^4}C(z)\frac{|D_L\cap(D_L-z)|}{V_L}\,d^4z.
$$
The overlap ratio belongs to $[0,1]$ and tends pointwise to $1$, so dominated convergence with dominator $|C|$ proves the equality. Cubes with side length tending to infinity satisfy the stated overlap condition. On a CP-symmetric branch, $\langle\nu_{D_L}\rangle=0$ and the numerator reduces to $\langle\nu_{D_L}^2\rangle$.

<a id="theorem-k62-first-harmonic-pce-cost-ansatz-on-s1"></a>**Theorem K.6.2 (First-Harmonic PCE Cost Ansatz on $S^1$).** Let $V_0>0$. Assume that the retained cost is smooth, even, $2\pi$-periodic, vanishes at $\theta=0$, has local expansion
$$
V(\theta)=\frac12V_0\theta^2+O(\theta^4),
$$
and is truncated to the constant and first cosine harmonic. Then
$$
V_{\mathrm{PCE}}(\theta)=V_0(1-\cos\theta).
$$

*Proof.* The truncation and evenness give $V(\theta)=a_0+a_1\cos\theta$. The condition $V(0)=0$ gives $a_0=-a_1$. Since $V''(0)=-a_1=V_0$, one has $a_1=-V_0$ and $a_0=V_0$. Hence $V(\theta)=V_0(1-\cos\theta)$. Its Taylor series is
$$
V_0(1-\cos\theta)=\frac12V_0\theta^2-\frac1{24}V_0\theta^4+O(\theta^6),
$$
and its unique minimum modulo $2\pi$ is at $\theta=0$.

Without the first-harmonic hypothesis the listed geometric conditions do not determine the function. For example, for every $\lambda\ge0$,
$$
V_\lambda(\theta)
=V_0(1-\cos\theta)+\lambda V_0(1-\cos\theta)^2
$$
has the same quadratic coefficient, parity, periodicity, and minimum, but differs away from zero. ∎

<a id="corollary-k62-conditional-topological-cost-normalization"></a>**Corollary K.6.2 (Conditional Topological-Cost Normalization).** If the topological-cost branch supplies the normalization map
$$
V_0:=2\alpha\sigma_B^2,
$$
then the values $\alpha=3/2$ and $\sigma_B^2=1/24$ give
$$
V_0
=2\left(\frac32\right)\left(\frac1{24}\right)
=\frac18.
$$
The Bures variance and hierarchy coefficient alone do not derive the normalization map.

*Proof.* Direct multiplication gives $2(3/2)(1/24)=3/24=1/8$. ∎

<a id="theorem-k62a-all-harmonic-positive-sector-selection-of-the-invariant-strong-cp-angle"></a>**Theorem K.6.2a (All-Harmonic Positive-Sector Selection of the Invariant Strong-CP Angle).** Let
$$
\phi:=\bar\theta
\quad\text{and}\quad
Z(\phi)=\sum_{\nu\in\mathbb Z}Z_\nu e^{i\nu\phi},
$$
where $\sum_\nu Z_\nu<\infty$, $Z_\nu=Z_{-\nu}\ge0$, $Z(0)>0$, and $Z(\phi)>0$ on the retained parameter circle. Let
$$
\mathcal N_+:=\{\nu\in\mathbb N:Z_\nu>0\},
\qquad
g:=\gcd\mathcal N_+,
$$
with $\mathcal N_+\ne\varnothing$, and define the normalized topological free-energy cost
$$
F_{\mathrm{top}}(\phi)
:=
-\frac1{\mathcal V}\log Z(\phi)
+\frac1{\mathcal V}\log Z(0),
\qquad
\mathcal V>0.
$$
Then
$$
F_{\mathrm{top}}(\phi)\ge0,
$$
with equality exactly when
$$
\phi\in\frac{2\pi}{g}\mathbb Z
\pmod{2\pi}.
$$
In particular, charge-one support $Z_1>0$ gives the unique minimum
$$
\bar\theta\equiv0\pmod{2\pi}.
$$

*Proof.* Absolute convergence and nonnegative coefficients give
$$
0<Z(\phi)
\le |Z(\phi)|
\le\sum_{\nu\in\mathbb Z}Z_\nu
=Z(0).
$$
Monotonicity of $-\log$ yields $F_{\mathrm{top}}(\phi)\ge0$. If equality $F_{\mathrm{top}}(\phi)=0$ holds, then $Z(\phi)=Z(0)>0$ and equality holds in the triangle inequality. The active phases therefore share one common phase; positivity of $Z(\phi)$ forces that common phase to be $+1$. This is equivalent to $\nu\phi\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ for every $\nu\in\mathcal N_+$, hence to $\phi\in(2\pi/g)\mathbb Z$ by Bezout's identity. If $Z_1>0$, then $g=1$ and only $\phi\equiv0\pmod{2\pi}$ remains. ∎

**Remark K.6.2a.1 (Physical-Selection Gate).** Theorem K.6.2a is an exact all-harmonic implication and does not require the first-harmonic ansatz. Its use as a strong-CP solution still requires a constructed QCD sector partition with the stated positivity and charge support, proof that the invariant coordinate is $\phi=\bar\theta$, and proof that $F_{\mathrm{top}}$ is the actual descended PCE cost over physically admissible values of $\bar\theta$. Ordinary evaluation of a theory at a fixed coupling does not by itself turn that coupling into a dynamical selection coordinate.

<a id="remark-k61-conditional-dilute-gas-shape-comparison"></a>**Remark K.6.1: Conditional dilute-gas shape comparison.** In an ideal CP-symmetric dilute gas, assume the instanton and anti-instanton counts $N_+$ and $N_-$ are independent Poisson variables, each with mean $\rho\mathcal V$, and weight a configuration by $e^{i\theta(N_+-N_-)}$. The normalized generating function is
$$
\frac{Z(\theta)}{Z(0)}
=\mathbb E e^{i\theta(N_+-N_-)}
=\exp\!\bigl(2\rho\mathcal V(\cos\theta-1)\bigr),
$$
so the normalized free-energy density is $F(\theta)-F(0)=2\rho(1-\cos\theta)$ and its model susceptibility is $\chi_{\mathrm{DIG}}=2\rho$. This conditional first-harmonic shape agrees with the retained PCE branch. The Poisson assumptions are an idealized semiclassical model, not a proved identity for the full QCD vacuum; they do not derive the PCE truncation, supply the gauge-topology bridge required by Proposition K.6.4, or certify that PCE is the operative QCD vacuum-selection functional.

### <a id="k66-first-mechanism-σ-invariance-selects-θ-0"></a>K.6.6 First Mechanism: σ-Invariance Selects θ = 0

<a id="theorem-k63-hermiticity-under-the-normal-observable-hypothesis"></a>**Theorem K.6.3 (Hermiticity under the Normal-Observable Hypothesis).** Assume physical observables on the finite retained Hilbert space are represented by normal operators and that their possible outcomes are their spectral values. If every outcome is real, then the observable operator is Hermitian.

*Proof.* Let $O$ be normal. The finite-dimensional spectral theorem gives a unitary $U$ and eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ such that
$$
O=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)U^\dagger.
$$
If every spectral value is real, then
$$
O^\dagger
=U\operatorname{diag}(\overline{\lambda_1},\ldots,\overline{\lambda_n})U^\dagger
=O.
$$
Thus $O$ is Hermitian. Normality is essential: a nonnormal operator may have an entirely real spectrum without being Hermitian. ∎

<a id="lemma-k64-σ-invariance-implies-hermiticity-in-the-fixed-real-structure"></a>**Lemma K.6.4 (σ-Invariance Implies Hermiticity in the Fixed Real Structure).** Let $\sigma$ denote the antiholomorphic involution on $\mathbb{C}^8$ fixed in Definition K.6.3, acting on density matrices by $\sigma(\rho) = \bar\rho$ in the fixed basis. If $\sigma(\rho) = \rho$, then $\rho$ has real matrix elements in that basis and is therefore real-symmetric and Hermitian. The converse is false in general: a Hermitian density matrix need not be $\sigma$-invariant under the fixed conjugation, since its eigenvectors cannot generally be chosen real with respect to a fixed real structure unless $\rho$ commutes with $\sigma$.

*Proof.* ($\sigma$-invariance ⇒ real-symmetric Hermitian.) If $\sigma(\rho) = \rho$, then $\bar\rho = \rho$ in the fixed basis, so $\rho$ has real matrix elements. A real positive semidefinite matrix satisfies $\rho = \rho^T = \rho^\dagger$ and is therefore Hermitian.

(Counterexample to the converse.) The matrix
$$
\rho = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 1 & -ia \\ ia & 1 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad 0 < a < 1,
$$
is Hermitian and positive definite but satisfies $\sigma(\rho) = \frac{1}{2}\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix} 1 & ia \\ -ia & 1 \end{smallmatrix}\bigr] \neq \rho$. Its eigenvectors $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(1, \mp i)^T$ admit no phase choice making both components real, illustrating that Hermiticity does not imply $\sigma$-invariance under the fixed conjugation.

Consequently, the strong-CP argument below uses $\sigma$-invariance as a PCE symmetry condition characterizing the $\sigma$-symmetric attractor branch, not as a derived consequence of Hermiticity alone. ∎

<a id="theorem-k65-θ-selection-on-the-σ-symmetric-pce-attractor-branch"></a>**Theorem K.6.5 (θ-Selection on the σ-Symmetric PCE-Attractor Branch).** Assume:

1. a constructed equivariant parameter map satisfying Theorem K.6.1;
2. a specified accepted bridge $\mathcal B_\theta$ satisfying Proposition K.6.4 that identifies the registered holonomy coordinate with $\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}$ modulo $2\pi$, preserves integer topological charge, and intertwines $\sigma$ with physical CP;
3. a vacuum state invariant under the fixed antiholomorphic involution $\sigma$.

Then the physical QCD angle obeys
$$
\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}\in\{0,\pi\}.
$$

*Proof.* By item 2, $\mathcal B_\theta$ identifies the registered holonomy coordinate with the QCD topological angle and intertwines the physical CP action with $\sigma:\theta\mapsto-\theta$. Vacuum $\sigma$-invariance therefore requires
$$
\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}
\equiv
-\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}
\pmod{2\pi},
$$
whose two solutions modulo $2\pi$ are $0$ and $\pi$. Lemma K.6.4 is used only to distinguish this branch hypothesis from Hermiticity; it does not supply the hypothesis. ∎

<a id="theorem-k66-conditional-energy-selection-of-θ-0"></a>**Theorem K.6.6 (Conditional Energy Selection of θ = 0).** Under the hypotheses of Theorem K.6.5, assume additionally that
$$
V_{\mathrm{PCE}}(\theta)=V_0(1-\cos\theta),
\qquad
V_0>0,
$$
is certified as the operative QCD vacuum-selection functional on the retained $\sigma$-invariant sector and that the realized physical vacuum is a global minimizer of this functional on that sector. Then
$$
V_{\mathrm{PCE}}(0)=0
<
V_{\mathrm{PCE}}(\pi)=2V_0,
$$
and hence
$$
\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}\equiv0\pmod{2\pi}.
$$

*Proof.* Theorem K.6.5 restricts the angle to $\{0,\pi\}$ modulo $2\pi$. Evaluation at the two retained points gives the displayed strict inequality. Because the physical vacuum is assumed to be a global minimizer of the operative QCD selection functional, $\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}\equiv0\pmod{2\pi}$; its canonical representative is $0$. ∎

<a id="corollary-k63-conditional-gibbs-weight-of-the-first-harmonic-cost"></a>**Corollary K.6.3 (Conditional Gibbs Weight of the First-Harmonic Cost).** Suppose a probability law is separately declared by
$$
P_\beta(\theta)=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta V_{\mathrm{PCE}}(\theta)},
$$
where $\beta V_{\mathrm{PCE}}$ is dimensionless. On the first-harmonic branch of Theorem K.6.2,
$$
\frac{P_\beta(\pi)}{P_\beta(0)}
=e^{-\beta[V_{\mathrm{PCE}}(\pi)-V_{\mathrm{PCE}}(0)]}
=e^{-2\beta V_0}.
$$
No equality with $e^{-16\pi^2/g_s^2}$ follows unless an independent bridge proves
$$
2\beta V_0=\frac{16\pi^2}{g_s^2}.
$$

*Proof.* The ratio cancels the partition function. Since $V_{\mathrm{PCE}}(\pi)=2V_0$ and $V_{\mathrm{PCE}}(0)=0$, substitution gives the displayed result. ∎

<a id="theorem-k66a-classification-of-cp-equivariant-angle-bridges"></a>**Theorem K.6.6a (Classification of CP-Equivariant Angle Bridges).** Let the angle circle $S^1=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ carry the CP action $C_{\mathrm{CP}}(z)=\bar z$, which is $\theta\mapsto-\theta$ on $z=e^{i\theta}$ as in Theorem K.6.1 and Proposition K.6.3. Let $f_{\mathcal B}:S^1\to S^1$ be continuous with $f_{\mathcal B}\circ C_{\mathrm{CP}}=C_{\mathrm{CP}}\circ f_{\mathcal B}$, and put $\epsilon_{\mathcal B}:=f_{\mathcal B}(1)$ and $n_{\mathcal B}:=\deg f_{\mathcal B}$. Then:

1. $f_{\mathcal B}(1),f_{\mathcal B}(-1)\in\{1,-1\}$ and
$$
f_{\mathcal B}(-1)=\epsilon_{\mathcal B}(-1)^{n_{\mathcal B}};
\tag{K.6.6a.1}
$$

2. $f_{\mathcal B}$ is homotopic to $z\mapsto\epsilon_{\mathcal B}z^{n_{\mathcal B}}$ through continuous $C_{\mathrm{CP}}$-equivariant maps, and $(\epsilon_{\mathcal B},n_{\mathcal B})$ is constant along every such homotopy, so the equivariant homotopy classes are in bijection with $\{1,-1\}\times\mathbb Z$;

3. if $f_{\mathcal B}$ transports the registered holonomy coordinate $\vartheta$ to the QCD angle by $e^{i\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}}=f_{\mathcal B}(e^{i\vartheta})$, the CP-invariant labels $\vartheta\in\{0,\pi\}$ go to $\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}\in\{0,\pi\}$, and a selector on $\vartheta$ with unique minimizer $\vartheta\equiv0$, such as the first-harmonic cost of Theorem K.6.2 or the all-harmonic cost of Theorem K.6.2a with $Z_1>0$, gives $\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}\equiv0\pmod{2\pi}$ exactly when $\epsilon_{\mathcal B}=1$; the degree-one representatives $z\mapsto\pm z$ act on sector characters by $e^{i\nu\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}}=(\pm1)^\nu e^{i\nu\vartheta}$;

4. on a genuinely real mass branch with the determinant orientations $\epsilon_u,\epsilon_d$ of Theorem K.6.8, expressed in the common convention of Theorem K.6.12, the transported vacuum selected at $\vartheta\equiv0$ has
$$
z_{\mathrm{CP}}=\epsilon_{\mathcal B}\,\epsilon_u\epsilon_d,
\tag{K.6.6a.2}
$$
so $\bar\theta\equiv0\pmod{2\pi}$ exactly when $\epsilon_{\mathcal B}\epsilon_u\epsilon_d=1$.

Equivariance and unit degree therefore leave the base-point sign $\epsilon_{\mathcal B}$ as the one discrete bridge datum on the invariant labels, and item 2 of Theorem K.6.5 fixes it through the representative $f_{\mathcal B}=\mathrm{id}$ of the class $(1,1)$.

*Proof.* Evaluating $f_{\mathcal B}\circ C_{\mathrm{CP}}=C_{\mathrm{CP}}\circ f_{\mathcal B}$ at the fixed points $\pm1$ of $C_{\mathrm{CP}}$ gives $f_{\mathcal B}(\pm1)=\overline{f_{\mathcal B}(\pm1)}$, so $f_{\mathcal B}(\pm1)\in\{1,-1\}$. Lift $t\mapsto f_{\mathcal B}(e^{it})$ to a continuous $\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ with $f_{\mathcal B}(e^{it})=e^{i\phi(t)}$, $\phi(0)\in\{0,\pi\}$ and $\phi(t+2\pi)=\phi(t)+2\pi n_{\mathcal B}$. Equivariance gives $e^{i\phi(-t)}=e^{-i\phi(t)}$, so the continuous function $\phi(-t)+\phi(t)$ takes values in $2\pi\mathbb Z$ and equals its value $2\phi(0)$ at $t=0$. Hence $\psi(t):=\phi(t)-\phi(0)$ is odd and satisfies $\psi(t+2\pi)=\psi(t)+2\pi n_{\mathcal B}$. Then $\psi(\pi)=\psi(-\pi)+2\pi n_{\mathcal B}=-\psi(\pi)+2\pi n_{\mathcal B}$, so $\psi(\pi)=\pi n_{\mathcal B}$ and $f_{\mathcal B}(-1)=\epsilon_{\mathcal B}e^{i\pi n_{\mathcal B}}$, which is (K.6.6a.1). The functions $\psi_s(t):=(1-s)\psi(t)+sn_{\mathcal B}t$, $0\le s\le1$, are odd and satisfy $\psi_s(t+2\pi)=\psi_s(t)+2\pi n_{\mathcal B}$, so $f_s(e^{it}):=\epsilon_{\mathcal B}e^{i\psi_s(t)}$ is well defined, continuous in $(s,t)$ and $C_{\mathrm{CP}}$-equivariant because $\epsilon_{\mathcal B}$ is real; $f_0=f_{\mathcal B}$ and $f_1(z)=\epsilon_{\mathcal B}z^{n_{\mathcal B}}$. Along any equivariant homotopy the degree is constant, and the value at $1$ moves continuously in $\{1,-1\}$, so it is constant. The maps $z\mapsto\epsilon z^n$ realize every pair $(\epsilon,n)$ and are pairwise separated by these invariants, which proves item 2. Item 3 is item 1 evaluated at $z=\pm1$ together with the uniqueness of the selected label, and the character identity is direct substitution. For item 4, Theorem K.6.10 gives $\det(M_uM_d)/|\det(M_uM_d)|=\epsilon_u\epsilon_d$ on the real branch, item 3 gives $e^{i\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}}=f_{\mathcal B}(1)=\epsilon_{\mathcal B}$, and Theorem K.6.12 multiplies the two factors into $z_{\mathrm{CP}}$. ∎

<a id="theorem-k66b-specified-based-determinant-line-and-complete-physical-line-probe"></a>**Theorem K.6.6b (Specified Based Determinant Line and Complete Physical Line Probe).**

##### Based tautological loop, Chern number and CP sign

#### L2. A smooth based loop and a pointwise parameter map

Fix a $C^\infty$ monotone function $q:[0,1]\to[0,1]$, flat to every order at both endpoints. Let physical time $t\in[0,\tau]$, $s=t/\tau$, and write

$\alpha(s)=(\pi/2)q(2s)$ for $0\le s\le 1/2$,

Set

At the join $u=e_2$. At the endpoints $u(0,z)=e_1$ and $u(1,z)=z\,e_1$. All $s$ derivatives of the nonconstant terms vanish at the joins, so $P$ is a smooth map $S^1_s\times S^1_z\to\mathrm{Gr}(2,8)$. It is periodic in $z$ without choosing an argument. $P(0,z)=P(1,z)=P^*=|e_1\rangle\langle e_1|+|e_3\rangle\langle e_3|$. For every fixed $z$, $u^*\partial_su=0$ on both legs. Thus the frame $(u,e_3)$ is horizontal for the actual projected tautological connection $P\,d$. Its determinant vector $\Omega(s,z)=u(s,z)\wedge e_3$ is horizontal, and

$$
\operatorname{Hol}_L(P(\cdot,z))=z.
\tag{L2.1}
$$

In particular the base-point sign is +1 at $z=1$, with no unrecorded half turn. The angle bridge for this controlled source has degree +1.

The loop endpoint is constant and cannot itself encode $\theta$. A pointwise parameter map is available at the unique return-leg time $s^*$ with $\beta(s^*)=\pi/4$:

$$
\Phi(z)=\operatorname{span}((z e_1+e_2)/\sqrt{2},e_3),\quad \rho(z)=P(s^*,z)/2.

This map is injective: $2P_{12}(s^*,z)=z$. It obeys $\Phi(\bar{z})=\sigma\Phi(z)$, and the same source coordinate recovered from the physical off-diagonal response gives the loop holonomy. #### L3. First Chern number and the integer map

On the cut cylinder, the determinant connection one-form is $A_L=\Omega^*d\Omega=u^*du$. It is zero on the first leg and equals

on the return leg. Its curvature is

Since $\cos^{2}\beta$ increases from 0 to 1 on the return leg, the original convention yields

This computation includes the seam transition $z$; a globally periodic horizontal frame would contradict this nonzero number. Replacing $z$ by $z^\nu$ gives a smooth map $P_\nu(s,z)=P(s,z^\nu)$, with

$$
c_1(P_\nu^* L)[T^{2}]=\nu,\quad \operatorname{Hol}_L(P_\nu(\cdot,z))=z^\nu.

For the retained three bundles define the bridge by the actual integer $c_2(E_\nu)$ and this specified $P_\nu$. Then

c_2(E_\nu) &= \nu_{\mathrm{overlap}}(\text{Sample } A_\nu)=c_1(P_\nu^*\det(S))[T^{2}],\\

This is a constructed charge-preserving map on the registered source domain, not the false map $\det:SU(3)\to U(1)$. Gauge changes of the retained bundle preserve $\nu$ and act trivially on the auxiliary scalar controls; the charged probe and native source still transform by their actual previously proved intertwiners. The map is constant on each bundle's connected actuator cube, as an integer-valued map must be.

#### L4. Conjugation and the dual sign ledger

Complex conjugation gives $P_\nu(s,\bar{z})=\bar{P}_\nu(s,z)=P_{-\nu}(s,z)$. Its action on the determinant connection conjugates holonomy and reverses the above first Chern number. These are statements about the specified geometric family.

There are two different reversals of the dual pairing $\chi_z(\nu)=z^\nu$:
