(|0\rangle+e^{i\nu\theta}|1\rangle)/\sqrt{2} \otimes \Omega_*.
$$

This Ramsey experiment is a different registered preparation from the unreferenced Slater experiment in F2. At intermediate times, tracing the reference gives the normalized one-particle density $(P_*+P(t,\nu\theta))/4$, because the reference arm carries $\Omega_*$ and the driven arm carries $\Omega(t,\nu\theta)$. At the endpoint both projectors equal $P_*$, so it returns $P_*/2$. Only the unreferenced Slater protocol is assigned that rank-two response. The registered $X$ and $Y$ reference measurements have means $\cos(\nu\theta)$ and $\sin(\nu\theta)$. There is no fermion-parity-superselection violation. The path reference preparation, controlled drive, phase calibration, its clock, and both readout settings are charged. Discarding that reference would erase the phase and would change the retained task.

#### F3. A linear unitary on a paired protocol family

For the conjugate geometric path,

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_{-\theta} &= \bar P_\theta, & K_{-\theta} &= \bar K_\theta,\\
H_{-\theta} &= -\bar H_\theta, & U_{-\theta} &= \bar U_\theta.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F3.1}
$$

The minus sign in the Hamiltonian is essential at the same forward time. Replacing H by bar H alone does not implement conjugate transport.

When a linear parameter-family symmetry is needed, retain a classical copy tag $b\in\{+1,-1\}$ and the direct-sum carrier

$$
\begin{aligned}
H_{\mathrm{pair}}&=F_8\oplus F_8\cong\mathbb{C}^{2}_b\otimes F_8,\\
\hat H_{\mathrm{pair}}(\theta)&=\operatorname{diag}(d\Gamma H_\theta,d\Gamma H_{-\theta}).
\end{aligned}
$$

This is two alternative protocol blocks, not two extra charged quark determinants. Both complete 256-dimensional blocks and their preparations are paid. The initial density is

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{pair}}(0)=1/2\, |+\rangle\langle +|_b\otimes|\Omega_*\rangle\langle\Omega_*| + 1/2\, |-\rangle\langle -|_b\otimes|\Omega_*\rangle\langle\Omega_*|.
$$

The fixed linear unitary Jcopy swaps the two blocks. It obeys

$$
\begin{aligned}
J_{\mathrm{copy}}\hat H_{\mathrm{pair}}(\theta)J_{\mathrm{copy}}^*&=\hat H_{\mathrm{pair}}(-\theta),\\
J_{\mathrm{copy}}\rho_{\mathrm{pair}}(t,\theta)J_{\mathrm{copy}}^*&=\rho_{\mathrm{pair}}(t,-\theta).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F3.2}
$$

This implements a source-family parameter intertwiner on this physical carrier. It is not a unitary implementing conjugation on arbitrary C8 inputs, and it has not yet been identified with the physical CP operator of the entire native charged/weak source.

Read out the copy tag and $M_{j}$ jointly. The full outcome law is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Pr(b,j|\theta) &= 1/2\, \operatorname{tr}(P(t,b\theta)E_j)/2,\\
\Pr(b) &= 1/2,\\
\rho_{\text{one-particle}} \text{ conditioned on } b &= P(t,b\theta)/2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F3.3}
$$

The tag is retained. Tracing it out instead yields

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{marginal}}=(P(t,\theta)+P(t,-\theta))/4,
$$

which is generally rank three in this particular family (at most four in a general pair), not the rank-two density $P(t,\theta)/2$. Conditional use of one block costs its probability $1/2$ and cannot be reported as a deterministic rank-two preparation. $J_{\mathrm{copy}}$ maps the $b$-resolved effect to the opposite block effect; a conditional $+$ readout is transformed to a conditional $-$ readout. It is not invariant merely because the initial paired density is invariant.

For pointwise conjugate one-particle measurements, the separate identity $\operatorname{tr}(\bar{P}E)=\operatorname{tr}(P\bar{E})$ pairs the geometric parameter with the conjugated probe $E$. The linear copy intertwiner itself swaps the actual block effect with the same matrix $E$. These two descriptions must not be conflated. For Ramsey readout the $X$ result is even and $Y$ is odd under $\theta\to-\theta$; the transformed protocol retains that sign and the full outcome distribution.

#### F4. Common clock and quantitative C² error

One concrete smooth pulse is $q(x)=g(x)/(g(x)+g(1-x))$, $g(x)=\exp(-1/x)$ for $x>0$ and $g(x)=0$ for $x\le 0$. It is flat at $0,1$. Direct differentiation gives certified bounds

$$
0\le q'\le 8,\quad |q''|\le 320.
\tag{F4.1}
$$

For completeness, on $[1/4,3/4]$ write $q=\operatorname{logistic}(v)$, $v=-1/x+1/(1-x)$. Then $|v'|\le 32$, $|v''|\le 256$ and $q(1-q)\le 1/4$ give the bounds 8 and 320. For $x\le 1/4$, $q\le\exp(4/3-1/x)$, $|v'|\le x^{-2}+16/9$ and $|v''|\le 2x^{-3}+128/27$. The functions $y^k e^{-y}$ for $y\ge 4$ and $k\le 4$ attain their maximum at 4, bounding the resulting derivatives by less than 8 and 320. The other tail follows by $q(1-x)=1-q(x)$.

Consequently $|\dot{\alpha}|,|\dot{\beta}|\le 8\pi/\tau$ and $|\ddot{\alpha}|,|\ddot{\beta}|\le 640\pi/\tau^{2}$. Each leg has integrated norm $\pi/2$, giving

$$
\int_0^\tau \lVert\hat H_\theta\rVert\, dt/\hbar=\pi
\tag{F4.2}
$$

for every $\theta$. For $\theta$-jets use $\lVert F\rVert_{(2)}=\sum_{k=0}^{2}\sup_\theta\lVert\partial_\theta^kF\rVert/k!$, and its mixed-source analogue from the retained-bundle packet. $R_\theta$ conjugation gives $\lVert\partial_\theta^kK\rVert\le 2^k\lVert K\rVert$ on the second leg, while the first leg is independent of $\theta$. The same bounds hold on full Fock space because all derivative generators remain traceless on the same two active modes. For $|\nu|\le 1$ and the paired direct sum,

$$
\begin{aligned}
A &:= \int\lVert\hat K\rVert_{(2)}\,dt\le 3\pi,\\
L &:= \sup_t \lVert\partial_t \hat K\rVert_{(2)}\le 3200\pi/\tau^{2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{F4.3}
$$

A common continuous piecewise-linear skew-Hermitian interpolation on a mesh of width $h$ therefore has $\delta_h\le\tau L h=3200\pi h/\tau$ and

$$
\lVert\Gamma(U)-U_h\rVert_{(2)}\le\exp(2A+\delta_h)\,\delta_h.
\tag{F4.4}
$$

##### General finite-dimensional mixed two-jet estimate

Fix a finite set of real source coordinates and a compact box on which the full H, preparation and effect families are smooth. Fix a finite response family and all its mixed derivatives through total order two before choosing a discretization. The family may contain matrix-valued responses, all native fermion coefficients, all path probes and their required products. Define a weighted jet norm

$$
\lVert F\rVert_{2,w} = \sum_{|\alpha|\le 2} (w^{\alpha}/\alpha!) \sup_{\mathrm{source}} \lVert\partial^{\alpha} F\rVert,
$$

with fixed positive weights. Leibniz's formula makes this a submultiplicative norm on truncated two-jets. It counts every mixed derivative, not merely separate single-coordinate second derivatives.

Suppose $K(t)$ is continuously differentiable in time in this norm, with

$$
\begin{aligned}
A&=\int_0^{\tau} \lVert K(t)\rVert_{2,w}\,dt, \\
L&=\sup_t \lVert\partial_tK(t)\rVert_{2,w}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Take one source-independent time partition with mesh $h$ and interpolate the skew-Hermitian values $K(t_j)$ linearly. The resulting $K_{h}$ is continuous and skew-Hermitian. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\delta_h&=\int\lVert K-K_h\rVert_{2,w}\,dt \le \tau L h, \\
A_h&\le A+\delta_h, \\
\lVert U-U_h\rVert_{2,w} &\le \exp(A+A_h)\, \delta_h.
\end{aligned}
\tag{T7}
$$

The last inequality follows by the exact variation-of-propagator identity in the jet algebra and the Dyson bound $\exp(\int\lVert K\rVert)$. This conservative exponential estimate is finite and computable. A common additional matrix-control approximation error $\delta_{\mathrm{comp}}$ in the same integrated jet norm is inserted into $\delta_{h}$ by the triangle inequality; a pointwise $C^0$ gate estimate alone is not a $C^{2}$ source certificate.

The preceding estimate gives (F4.4) on the full physical Fock carrier. All Hamiltonian/clock compilation errors add to $\delta$ before exponentiation; readout/preparation errors and their jets are separately retained. On the full Fock carrier, rather than lifting a one-particle error after the fact, the approximation is applied directly to Khat, as the displayed constants require. Controlled-reference and copy blocks use the corresponding maximum block norm. The first-leg/return-leg join is flat, so no unregistered switching impulse occurs. Every added source variation that moves a pulse, preparation, clock or effect is differentiated, not only the displayed $\theta$ dependence.

At the endpoint, each two-leg ideal pulse also has an exact area implementation because its generator has a constant direction on each leg. This does not remove the resolution/clock cost or the need for the common $C^{2}$ estimate when the complete task retains intermediate-time responses.

<a id="definition-k66c-intrinsic-smooth-gauss-circle-charged-reduction-and-exact-finite-density"></a>**Definition K.6.6c (Intrinsic Smooth Gauss Circle, Charged Reduction and Exact Finite Density).**

##### Smooth intrinsic Gauss circle and primitive clutch

#### G1. Bundle, physical units and connection family

Let $X$ be the rectangular spatial torus with coordinates $0\le x_i<L_i$, volume $V=L_1 L_2 L_3$, and orientation $dx_1\,dx_2\,dx_3$. All lengths are positive physical lengths. Let $L$ be the Hermitian line bundle of first Chern number $+1$ over the first $T^{2}$. Retain the splitting $E=L\oplus L^{-1}\oplus 1$, pulled back to $X$, and its unit determinant frame. Use anti-Hermitian connections and the ordinary fundamental trace. Put

$$
b=(1,-1,0),\quad e=(0,1,-1),\quad |b|^{2}=|e|^{2}=2,\quad b\cdot e=-1.
$$

In a standard rectangular line-bundle chart the base connection can be written $A_{B,2}=2\pi i\operatorname{diag}(b)\,x_1/(L_1 L_2)$, with the actual $x_1$ seam transition. Its curvature is $F_{B,12}=2\pi i\operatorname{diag}(b)/(L_1 L_2)$. Other local components vanish. The diagonal endomorphism $E_0=\operatorname{diag}(e)$ is a globally defined parallel endomorphism of the retained splitting. Define, for $q\in\mathbb{R}$,

$$
A(q)=A_B + q a,\quad a=(2\pi i/L_3)\, E_0\, dx_3.
$$

This is a family of genuine smooth connections on one spatial $SU(3)$ bundle, not a list of independent matrices. The rank-three bundle is trivial over $X$, but that fact does not trivialize its distinguished line summands.

The actual temporal coordinate is $t$ in seconds. Write $A_{t}$ for the anti-Hermitian time connection, with dimension 1/time, so $D_t=\partial_t+A_t$. The retained Minkowski Yang-Mills convention is

$$
\begin{aligned}
L_g&=(\hbar/(g_s^{2} c)) \int_X |\dot{A}-D_A A_t|^{2} \\
&\quad -(\hbar c/g_s^{2}) \int_X |F_{\mathrm{sp}}(A)|^{2},
\end{aligned}
$$

where the norm uses $-\operatorname{tr}$ and spatial components $i<j$, exactly as in the predecessor Euclidean convention after $x_0=c t$. Thus the physical action is $\int L_{g}\,dt$. No dimensionless quadrature clock is substituted for $t$.

#### G2. The exact quotient is a circle, with a nontrivial large-gauge clutch

Use $A^h=hAh^{-1}-dh\,h^{-1}$. The global bundle automorphism

$$
h(x)=\bigoplus_c \exp(-2\pi i e_c x_3/L_3)
$$

is smooth and has determinant one. It commutes with the spatial seam functions, so its diagonal local formula is globally meaningful. Exactly $A(q+1)=A(q)^h$.

Conversely, suppose $A(q')=A(q)^u$ for a smooth $SU(3)$ bundle gauge transformation $u$. Their curvatures are the same. Since $\operatorname{diag}(b)$ has three distinct eigenvalues, curvature covariance forces $u$ to preserve each of the three line summands pointwise. The equal first and second connection components then force its scalar phases to be covariantly constant in $x_1,x_2$. The third component requires winding numbers $(q'-q)e_c$ around $x_3$. Since $e$ has entries $0,1,-1$, these are integral exactly when $q'-q$ is integral. Thus there are no additional identifications or Weyl reflections within this oriented retained family. The isotropy is the same constant diagonal $T^{2}$ at every $q$. The configuration quotient of the gauge-saturated family is exactly $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$.

Take a smooth history $q(t)$ with $q(T)=q(0)+w$, integer $w$, and glue the ends with $h^{w}$. It defines a genuine bundle on $X$ times the temporal circle, using the actual spatial seam and temporal clutch. In temporal gauge $A_{t}=0$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
F_{12}&=2\pi i\operatorname{diag}(b)/(L_1 L_2), \\
F_{t3}&=2\pi i\operatorname{diag}(e)\,\dot{q}/L_3.
\end{aligned}
$$

Give the four-manifold orientation $dx_1\,dx_2\,dx_3\,dt$. Then direct wedge multiplication, including $dt\,dx_3=-dx_3\,dt$, gives

$$
(1/(8\pi^{2})) \int \operatorname{tr}(F\wedge F)=(b\cdot e)\, w=-w.
$$

This is the same anti-Hermitian $c_2$ convention used by the retained bundle source. Consequently the loop is primitive: its charge is $\nu=-1$ per positive $q$ winding. In any global $SU(3)$ trivialization of the spatial $E$, the temporal clutch is in the corresponding nonzero large-gauge component. Its chartwise diagonal appearance is not evidence of degree zero; the line summands are not globally framed.

This calculation is an actual continuum bundle identity. It is not a computation of a new finite-lattice overlap index. Any new temporal lattice must establish its own kernel gap/index map on one declared generation.

#### G3. Exact horizontal tangent and sourceless Gauss law

The affine tangent $a$ is parallel and obeys $D_A^* a=0$ for every $q$. For every smooth infinitesimal gauge parameter $\chi$, integration by parts on $X$ gives

$$
\langle a,D_A \chi\rangle_{L^2}=\langle D_A^* a,\chi\rangle_{L^2}=0.
$$

This includes every smooth gauge direction, not just Cartan parameters. For a q history,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert\dot{q}\, a-D_A A_t\rVert^{2} \\
&=\dot{q}^{2} \lVert a\rVert^{2}+\lVert D_A A_t\rVert^{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The $A_{t}$ Euler-Lagrange equation with no charged sources is $D_A^*(\dot{q}a-D_A A_t)=0$. Its minimizing solution is $D_A A_t=0$; residual constant Cartan $A_{t}$ is pure stabilizer gauge and can be set to zero. Hence the horizontal electric field is exactly $\dot{q}\,a$. No Gauss projection is being approximated.

The induced inertia and magnetic energy are therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
I&=(2\hbar/(g_s^{2} c)) \lVert a\rVert^{2} \\
&=8\pi^{2}\hbar V |e|^{2}/(g_s^{2} c L_3^{2}) \\
&=16\pi^{2}\hbar L_1 L_2/(g_s^{2} c L_3), \\
V_B&=(\hbar c/g_s^{2})\lVert F_{\mathrm{sp}}\rVert^{2} \\
&=4\pi^{2}\hbar c V |b|^{2}/(g_s^{2} L_1^{2} L_2^{2}) \\
&=8\pi^{2}\hbar c L_3/(g_s^{2} L_1 L_2).
\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced Lagrangian is $I\dot{q}^2/2-V_B$. $I$ has units energy times time squared and $V_{B}$ has units energy. Both are positive; $V_{B}$ is retained in every ground energy, preparation probability and ledger. The horizontal lift is an affine line with constant tangent; its projected curve is a geodesic of the regular fixed-isotropy quotient stratum wherever that quotient metric is used.

This proves a classical reduction on the declared gauge-saturated holonomic configuration family. It does not prove that the unrestricted Yang-Mills equations preserve the family under arbitrary perturbations, or that finite confinement has zero correction.

#### G4. Character domain, measure and intrinsic Hamiltonian

The q coordinate is a gauge-configuration degree of freedom. $\Theta$ labels a character of the large-gauge clutch and remains an external sector parameter. They must not be identified.

The topological term in the physical Lagrangian is $\hbar\nu\theta\dot{q}$, $\nu=-1$. A winding history consequently has phase $\exp(i\nu\theta w)$. In the periodic frame the intrinsic reduced Hamiltonian is

$$
H_\theta=V_B+(1/(2I))(-i\hbar\,\partial_q-\hbar\nu\theta)^{2}
$$

on L2([0,1],dq), with periodic H2 domain. The intrinsic Riemannian density is sqrt(I)dq; its constant normalization gives the same Hilbert space and operator. Equivalently remove the vector potential and impose

$$
\begin{aligned}
\psi(1)&=\exp(-i\nu\theta)\, \psi(0), \\
\psi'(1)&=\exp(-i\nu\theta)\, \psi'(0)
\end{aligned}
$$

on H2([0,1]). Both endpoint conditions are part of the self-adjoint domain. The quadratic-form domain is the corresponding twisted H1 space. Fourier analysis proves self-adjointness, compact resolvent and the exact spectrum

$$
E_n(\theta)=V_B+(\hbar^{2}/(2I))(2\pi n-\nu\theta)^{2},\quad n\in\mathbb{Z}.
$$

Changing $\theta$ by 2 $\pi$ is the full-frame unitary conjugacy by multiplication exp(2 $\pi$ i $\nu$ q). The spectrum is 2 $\pi$ periodic. This conjugacy is not a change of q winding or removal of a physical $\theta$ at fixed response labels.

For $|\theta|<\pi$ the ground is $n=0$, $E_0=V_B+\hbar^2\theta^2/(2I)$, and $E_0''=\hbar^2/I>0$. At $\theta=\pi$ the two nearest momentum branches are degenerate. Over the whole $\theta$ circle the ground-energy family has its unique minimum at $\theta=0$ modulo $2\pi$. At fixed external $\theta$ the ground is a state in that sector; preparing it does not change $\theta$. A direct integral over external $\theta$ sectors does not acquire a normalizable zero-$\theta$ eigenvector by this point minimum. No dynamic $\theta$ kinetic term or axion has been introduced.

#### G5. What the measure and geometry statement does and does not assert

The preceding quantum model explicitly chooses intrinsic quantization of the classically reduced holonomic source. Its one-dimensional scalar curvature is zero and its intrinsic metric is constant. Those facts justify the displayed intrinsic operator, not an ambient constrained-quantization identity.

If one starts instead from a larger gauge-field quantum model and introduces a finite transverse potential, its effective operator must retain: the actual transverse ground energy, the normal-bundle/Berry connection, the Born-Huang scalar, measure or ordering terms associated with the implemented quotient and normal coordinates, any curvature-induced scalar, and a proved finite-gap remainder on the same source domain. A q-dependent orbit metric or normal Hessian cannot be erased merely because the tangent norm is constant. Gauge group volume and Faddeev-Popov factors of an ambient path integral have not been equated with the intrinsic constant measure.

No finite transverse potential, normal spectrum or C2 remainder has yet been supplied here. In particular, a multiplier imposing an exact constraint is not assigned finite implementation cost by writing its symbol. The finite charged kinetic discretization of Definition K.6.6e (W4) instead consumes the explicitly declared orbit-first Laplace-Beltrami quantization, with its nonconstant measure. Neither quantization is, by itself, a proof that a finite confining perturbation of full QCD realizes it.

##### Charged orbit reduction and physical domain

#### C1. Regulator, gauge orbit and source map

Fix an integer $N\ge 2$ and a positive physical spacing $a$, so $L=Na$. On the cubic spatial $N^3$ lattice sample the smooth connections of Definition K.6.6c’s intrinsic Gauss-circle construction. At vertex $n=(n_1,n_2,n_3)$, with each coordinate modulo $N$, use backward fundamental transport

$$
\begin{aligned}
U_2(n)&=\exp(2\pi i\operatorname{diag}(b)\, n_1/N^{2}), \\
U_1(n)&=I\quad\text{if } n_1<N-1, \\
U_1(N-1,n_2,n_3)&=\exp(-2\pi i\operatorname{diag}(b)\, n_2/N), \\
U_3(q,n)&=\exp(2\pi i\operatorname{diag}(e)\, q/N).
\end{aligned}
$$

These links include the actual spatial bundle seam. Their $xy$ plaquettes are $\exp(2\pi i\operatorname{diag}(b)/N^2)$; $xz$ and $yz$ plaquettes are identity. The third Wilson loop is $\exp(2\pi i\operatorname{diag}(e)q)$. The three $xy$ curvature eigenvalues are distinct for every $N\ge 2$. The large-gauge seam is $h(n)=\exp(-2\pi i\operatorname{diag}(e)n_3/N)$, and $U(q+1)=U(q)^h$ under $U^g_{st}=g_s U_{st}g_t^{-1}$.

Let $G=SU(3)^{N^3}$. The stabilizer of every $U(q)$ is exactly the same $H=T^{2}$ of vertex-constant diagonal matrices: a stabilizer commutes with the distinct xy plaquettes, then covariant constancy on the connected graph makes its diagonal entries constant. Wilson loops then show that two $q$ representatives in this family are gauge equivalent exactly for integer $q$ difference. The restricted gauge-orbit configuration manifold is the associated mapping torus with fiber $G/H$ and clutch $h$. It is a new constrained submanifold of link configurations, not the full finite-link domain.

The continuous bundle source retains its spatial atlas and actual temporal clutch. Sampling commutes with all endpoint frame actions. No global smooth extension of every tuple in G to a continuum gauge transformation is assumed; when continuum frames are used, their actual smooth lift is retained as in the earlier bundle source. The sampled regulator does not infer a continuum integer from arbitrary links. The primitive mapping-torus charge of the retained q loop is independently the continuum value $\nu=-1$.

#### C2. Kinetic metric and the finite Gauss operator

Use the standard positive electric quadratic form with physical time t,

$$
\begin{aligned}
L_e&=C_a \sum_{\mathrm{links}} \lVert\dot{U} U^{-1}-X_s+\operatorname{Ad}(U)X_t\rVert^{2}, \\
C_a&=\hbar a/(g_s^{2} c),
\end{aligned}
$$

where $X_{s}$ is the anti-Hermitian temporal connection at vertex $s$ and $\lVert Y\rVert^2=-\operatorname{tr}(Y^2)$. The magnetic energy is the actual Wilson value

$$
\begin{aligned}
V_N&=(2\hbar c/(g_s^{2} a)) \sum_{\text{spatial plaquettes}}[3-\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr} U_p] \\
&=4\hbar c N^{3}/(g_s^{2} a)[1-\cos(2\pi/N^{2})].
\end{aligned}
$$

It is constant on the whole orbit family. It is not silently replaced by the continuum magnetic energy. Its ratio to $V_B=8\pi^2\hbar c/(g_s^2 L)$ lies between $1-\pi^2/(3N^4)$ and $1$, by the elementary cosine remainder bound.

Define the finite covariant gradient on the real Lie algebra of vertex fields,

$$
(D_q X)_{st}=X_s-\operatorname{Ad}(U_{st}(q))X_t,\quad M_q=D_q^*D_q.
$$

Its kernel is exactly the two-dimensional stabilizer algebra h. The q tangent has only third-link component 2 $\pi$ i diag(e)/N, has zero discrete covariant divergence, and is orthogonal to every $D_{q}$ X. Consequently the q kinetic coefficient has no mixed gauge-orbit term and is

$$
\begin{aligned}
I&=2 C_a \sum_{\mathrm{links}} \lVert\partial_q U\, U^{-1}\rVert^{2} \\
&=16\pi^{2}\hbar L/(g_s^{2} c),
\end{aligned}
$$

exactly the continuum pullback for the same cubic torus. On $h^{\perp}$ the vertical kinetic metric is $2C_a M_q$. Thus the metric of the restricted configuration manifold is determined, including its orbit directions, by the actual gauge kinetic action.

There is a useful explicit bound uniform in $q$. On constant-Cartan-orthogonal Cartan fields the graph Laplacian has gap $4\sin^2(\pi/N)$. On a color root $ij$, the two magnetic translations satisfy $T_1 T_2=\exp(2\pi i(b_i-b_j)/N^2)\,T_2 T_1$. For a unit vector $f$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
|\exp(i\phi)-1| &\le 2(\lVert(T_1-I)f\rVert+\lVert(T_2-I)f\rVert) \\
&\le 2\sqrt{2}\, \langle f,M_q f\rangle^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, with $m=8N^3-2$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\delta_N I &\le M_q|_{h^{\perp}} \le 12 I, \\
\delta_N&=(1/2)\sin^{2}(\pi/N^{2})>0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{C1}
$$

The upper bound follows by summing $\lVert X_s-\operatorname{Ad}(U)X_t\rVert^2\le 2\lVert X_s\rVert^2+2\lVert X_t\rVert^2$ over the six incidences per vertex. The root differences have absolute values one or two, so the displayed minimum is valid also at $N=2$. No field-theory or thermodynamic limit is needed for this estimate.

Only the third translations depend on $q$. Since $\max|e_i-e_j|=2$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert M_q'\rVert&\le 8\pi/N=:d_1, \\
\lVert M_q''\rVert&\le 32\pi^{2}/N^{2}=:d_2, \\
\lVert M_q^{(r)}\rVert&\le 2(4\pi/N)^{r},\quad r\ge 1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{C2}
$$

Inverse derivatives retain the usual ordered products: $\lVert(M^{-1})'\rVert\le d_1/\delta_N^2$ and $\lVert(M^{-1})''\rVert\le 2d_1^2/\delta_N^3+d_2/\delta_N^2$. These are actual electric Gauss-source bounds, not overlap-sign bounds.

#### C3. Quantization order and the induced physical density

Here the declared quantum source is intrinsic Laplace-Beltrami quantization of the full restricted orbit manifold, followed by the Gauss constraint. This order differs from quantizing the already reduced scalar circle. Its physical inner product is not assumed to be flat.

Relative to fixed normalized invariant measure on G/H, the volume density of the orbit metric is, up to a q-independent normalization,

$$
v(q)=\sqrt{\det(M_q|_{h^{\perp}})}.
$$

The q metric coefficient is constant. Conjugating links by h at q+1 conjugates $M_{q}$ and preserves h-perp, so v is genuinely periodic. It is smooth and positive, with

$$
\begin{aligned}
\delta_N^{m/2}&\le v(q)\le 12^{m/2}, \\
|(\log v)'|&\le m\, d_1/(2\delta_N), \\
|(\log v)''|&\le m[d_2/\delta_N+d_1^{2}/\delta_N^{2}]/2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{C3}
$$

These estimates are deliberately conservative. A constant rescaling of v changes no operator or normalized probability. The root decomposition also gives the exact finite determinant formula

$$
v(q)=\det'(\Delta_{\mathrm{graph}}) \prod_{i<j} \det(M_{ij}(q)),
$$

because the two real Cartan blocks contribute $\det'(\Delta_{\mathrm{graph}})^2$ and each complex root block contributes $\det(M_{ij})^2$ to the real determinant. This offers a direct exact verifier at $N=2$.

The density is an owned part of this quantization prescription. It is not asserted to equal an uncomputed thin-confinement measure of the unrestricted link theory. A different constraint realization can add normal-ground, geometric or ordering terms; those require separate construction.

#### C4. Actual charged carrier and Gauss covariance

Put a fundamental color probe and its conjugate reference at the origin vertex $n=0$. These are registered static finite color carriers, not mobile quark fields or an infinite-mass limit. Their actual rest, pinning and retained drift energy is a source parameter $E_{\mathrm{ref}}\ge 0$, independent of $q$ and $\theta$ on this declared degenerate internal branch. It is retained in $E_{\mathrm{base}}=V_N+E_{\mathrm{ref}}$. Any additional nonconstant drift or trap states require their own terms and a new comparison; they are not silently canceled. Before Gauss reduction their full carrier is $R=\mathbb{C}^3\otimes\overline{\mathbb{C}^3}$, equivalently $\operatorname{End}(\mathbb{C}^3)$ with Hilbert-Schmidt norm; $G$ acts by $X\to g_0 X g_{0}^*$. The physical states are equivariant wavefunctions on the restricted orbit manifold. Their value at the reference $U(q)$ must be fixed by $H$. Consequently the physical internal fiber is

$$
V_0=R^{H}=\{\operatorname{diag}(z_1,z_2,z_3):z\in\mathbb{C}^{3}\}.
$$

This three-dimensional space is not obtained by discarding a failed color outcome. The other six directions violate the stabilizer Gauss condition in this compact no-extra-charge domain. All nine preconstraint carrier states and the exact Gauss constraint are stated. Admitting separated charges, extra charge reservoirs or different representations changes the domain and must redo the reduction.

At the actual $N=2$ generation its color matrices have the same constant eigenvectors, with eigenvalues $0,3c_{\mathrm{col}}g(q),c_{\mathrm{col}}[g(q)+2k(q)]$. They commute for different $q$. Thus that trace is

$$
\begin{aligned}
&1+\exp\Bigl(-\int 3 c_{\mathrm{col}}\, g\, ds\Bigr) \\
&\quad +\exp\Bigl(-\int c_{\mathrm{col}}(g+2k)\, ds\Bigr) \ge 1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{T6}
$$

The primitive clutch acts trivially on the probe and does not alter this formula. Applying the uniform fermionic bound before integration, then taking the controlled finite-matrix limit, shows that the exact full internal closed-history factor is at least $g_{\beta}^{n}$. Its measure and all Coulomb effects have been retained, not canceled.

#### T3. Positive winding expansion of the actual finite heat trace

In normalized $q$ coordinates write the full $H_{K,\theta}$ as a block diagonal $D$ minus the oriented hopping matrix. At site $j$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
&D_j=E_{\mathrm{base}}+d_j^{\mathrm{kin}}+C_{\mathrm{tot}}(q_j)+h_F(q_j), \\
&0\le d_j^{\mathrm{kin}}\le d_{\mathrm{max}}:=2c_0 K^{2}/r_v.
\end{aligned}
$$

Expand $\exp(-\beta H_{K,\theta})$ by the norm-convergent hopping Dyson series. A term is a $q$ walk with nonnegative hopping magnitudes, nonnegative ordered holding-time measure, scalar weight $\exp[-\int(E_{\mathrm{base}}+d_j^{\mathrm{kin}})\,ds]$, and the full internal history of T2. A closed $q$ walk has integer winding $w$, scalar phase $\exp(i\nu w\theta)$, and the appropriate $SU(3)$ seam factors in its actual order. The retained interpolation identifies this winding with the primitive Chern charge; connected finite-site links alone do not supply that identification.

By T1–T2 every coefficient integrand is nonnegative. Therefore the ordinary trace of the same full physical-clock Hamiltonian has

$$
\begin{aligned}
Z_K(\beta,\theta)&=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbb{C}^{K}\otimes V}\exp(-\beta H_{K,\theta}) \\
&=\sum_{w\in\mathbb{Z}} a_w(\beta)\exp(i\nu w\theta), \\
a_w&\ge 0,\quad \sum_w a_w=Z_K(\beta,0)<\infty.
\end{aligned}
\tag{T7}
$$

Here are explicit bounds for the interchanges. Put $D_{\mathrm{int}}=9\cdot 2^n$ and $t_{\mathrm{max}}=c_0 K^2/r_v$. For every holding-time history of total length $\beta$, each Gaussian-expanded fermion factor has norm at most $\exp(\beta nL)$; all color jumps and clutches are unitary. The absolute full trace, including the $H$ projector before expansion, is bounded by $D_{\mathrm{int}}\exp(\beta nL)$. The same pointwise bound holds under all normalized Gaussian/$H$ integrals. The scalar holding-time factor is at most $\exp(-\beta E_{\mathrm{base}})$, since $d_j^{\mathrm{kin}}\ge 0$. There are at most $K\cdot 2^\ell$ oriented walks of length $\ell$. Thus the absolute $\ell$-th Dyson contribution, including nonclosed walks as an overcount, is bounded by

$$
K D_{\mathrm{int}} \exp[\beta(nL-E_{\mathrm{base}})]\, (2\beta t_{\mathrm{max}})^{\ell}/\ell!.
$$

The sum is finite and independent of Lie order, holding times, winding and $\theta$. For each fixed finite walk the Lie approximation errors converge uniformly in all holding times, which lie in $[0,\beta]$, by (T4) and finite-product telescoping. The number of holding intervals is fixed at this stage. Dominated convergence first removes the Lie approximation for that walk and then the displayed summable majorant permits integration, regrouping by winding and summation over all lengths. It also proves absolute Fourier convergence. No pointwise infinite sequence of Gaussian samples, Brownian measure or exchange with $K\to\infty$ is being invoked. The uniform positive internal bound $g_{\beta}^{n}$ is imposed before these limits and survives them unchanged. Self-adjointness makes $Z_{K}$ real for real $\theta$; uniqueness of the absolutely convergent Fourier coefficients gives $a_{-w}=a_w$. This conclusion does not assume weak-sector CP invariance.

For each starting $q$ site the clockwise $K$-step walk has winding one. The ordered holding-time simplex has volume $\beta^K/K!$, and its exact internal factor is bounded below by (T2),(T6). Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}
a_1=a_{-1} \\
&\ge K \exp[-\beta(E_{\mathrm{base}}+d_{\mathrm{max}})] \\
&\qquad (\beta^{K}/K!) \Bigl(\prod_j t_j\Bigr) g_\beta^{n} \\
&\ge K \exp[-\beta(E_{\mathrm{base}}+d_{\mathrm{max}})] \\
&\qquad (\beta^{K}/K!)(c_0 K^{2} r_v)^{K} g_\beta^{n} >0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{T8}
$$

The factor is K, not the old probe-only 3K count: the full internal contribution has been estimated by a history-uniform lower bound. No determinant attenuation or baseline factor is undone without cost.

Since $\nu=-1$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
Z_K(\beta,0)-Z_K(\beta,\theta) \\
&\ge 2K \exp[-\beta(E_{\mathrm{base}}+d_{\mathrm{max}})] \\
&\qquad (\beta^{K}/K!)(c_0 K^{2} r_v)^{K} g_\beta^{n} [1-\cos\theta].
\end{aligned}
\tag{T9}
$$

Thus the full dynamical-fermion/probe trace is strictly maximized at zero for every $\beta>0$ and $K\ge 3$. $Z_K(\beta,\theta)>0$ for every $\theta$ because it is an ordinary trace of a Hermitian finite Hamiltonian. Walk lengths and winding support are unbounded, as required by the binding bounded-Fourier-degree obstruction.

#### T4. What the comparison does not prove

The theorem compares external $\theta$ sectors of this intrinsic constrained source. It supplies a genuine ordinary Hamiltonian/thermal trace with complete dynamical colored Fock and Coulomb terms. It does not by itself prepare or choose a different sector, identify normalized free energy with a descended PCE resource cost, or realize the original QCD vacuum.

Taking $\beta\to\infty$ gives $E_{\mathrm{ground}}(\theta)\ge E_{\mathrm{ground}}(0)$, using $\log Z/\beta$. Strict finite-temperature trace comparison alone does not prove a strict many-body ground-energy minimum: winding support confined to higher spectral branches can distinguish traces while their ground energies agree. The old probe-only strict ground theorem is therefore not imported. The full ground and any selector attainment require their own analysis.

Nor does positive bare Wilson mass automatically identify the exact finite Wilson mass-phase response with the overlap anomaly of Theorem K.6.6d or a continuum renormalized mass. Those regulator/current gates are explicitly separate. Positivity of the unprobed vectorlike trace is not positivity of arbitrary inserted weak/chiral histories.

#### T5. Structural approximation boundary

The strong internal lower bound one in (T6) uses the exact $N=2$ common probe eigenbasis. A more conservative bound remains available for a structure-preserving approximation of the full inverse-Gauss matrix. This statement is scoped to the actual co-located probe $R_p=\operatorname{End}(\mathbb{C}^3)$ at the origin, not arbitrary representations or probe positions. Let $Q(q)$ be the approximated positive real symmetric $\operatorname{Ad}(H)$-invariant inverse matrix on $h^{\perp}$. Let $E_{0}$ evaluate a Lie-algebra vector at the origin. Since this probe's generator depends only on $E_{0}X$, its effective covariance is $B(q)=E_0 Q(q) E_0^T$, a positive real symmetric $\operatorname{Ad}(T^{2})$-invariant matrix on $\mathfrak{su}(3)$. The evaluation is $H$-equivariant. Thus all site multiplicities are contracted into $B$ before the representation argument; they cannot be discarded separately.

The real $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ representation of the full constant Cartan torus splits into a trivial Cartan plane and three inequivalent two-dimensional root planes. $\operatorname{Ad}(T^{2})$-invariance and real symmetry make $B$ scalar, $\lambda_{ab}(q)I$ with $\lambda_{ab}\ge 0$, on each root plane and forbid mixing distinct root planes or a root plane with the Cartan plane. Any positive Cartan block annihilates a diagonal probe $X$. In the normalized anti-Hermitian basis $(E_{ab}-E_{ba})/\sqrt{2}$, $i(E_{ab}+E_{ba})/\sqrt{2}$, the two squared Hermitian commutator generators sum, on diagonal $X=\operatorname{diag}(x)$, to

$$
2(x_a-x_b)(E_{aa}-E_{bb}).
$$

Consequently the actual compressed quadratic form is the three-vertex graph Laplacian with nonnegative edge weights $2\kappa\lambda_{ab}$. Its off-diagonal entries are nonpositive and it kills the identity vector. This proves the assertion for this co-located source even when the original site/root decomposition has multiplicities. Write $C_p^*$ for an actual uniform bound on its diagonal entries. The no-color-jump contribution to each diagonal heat product gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Tr}_{R_p^{H}} \text{ordered} \exp\Bigl(-\int C_p(q(s))\,ds\Bigr) \\
&\ge 3\exp(-\beta C_p^{*})>0.
\end{aligned}
$$

This can replace one in (T6) and multiplies the lower bound (T8) by the displayed factor. It is not necessary to claim that arbitrary approximated color matrices still commute. The full fermion/probe response errors use the entire approximated inverse-Gauss operator, not its three-dimensional probe compression.

Exact zero-angle comparison of an implemented family also requires the actual $SU(3)$ phase/clutch laws, the positive Hermitian mass margin and the total-charge structure. Generic additive matrix errors are covered by response estimates but do not automatically retain an exact minimizer. No flat-line phase error, unowned $U(3)$ scalar or omitted Coulomb term is allowed by a norm-only argument.

<a id="theorem-k66g-exact-full-carrier-positive-cone-representation"></a>**Theorem K.6.6g (Exact Full-Carrier Positive-Cone Representation).**

##### Exact complete-carrier positive cone

#### P1. Fixed one-particle rotation and full CAR map

Write the actual $\phi=0$ native Hamiltonian as $h=\tau_3A+\tau_1B$, where $A=M_E+W_E\ge\mu I$, $\mu=Q/4$, $B=\sum\sigma_i p_i$ is Hermitian, and $m=432$ is the dimension of each $\tau$ block. The native Hermitian flavor matrices remain in their given basis. The constant rotation $R=\exp(-i\pi\tau_2/4)$ gives

$$
R h R^{*}= \begin{bmatrix} -B & A \\ A & B \end{bmatrix}.
$$

It commutes with every actual color transformation. In the rotated physical Fock space write $a$ for the first block and $d$ for the second, and introduce hole operators $b=d^*$. Their vacuum is the completely filled $d$ block. This is a unitary identification of the full $2^{2m}$-dimensional Fock carrier, including all particle numbers.

In its ordered graded tensor representation, $a_i=a_i\otimes I$ and $b_j=(-1)^{N_a}\otimes b_{j}$. Let $f(N_a)=(-1)^{N_a(N_a+1)/2}$, acting on the first factor. Conjugation by $f$ sends $a_i^*(-1)^{N_a}$ to $-a_i^*$ and $(-1)^{N_a}a_i$ to $-a_i$. Finally vectorize the two occupation factors by $|I\rangle\otimes|J\rangle\to|I\rangle\langle J|$. Annihilation matrices are real in this convention. The resulting fixed unitary $U$ identifies the full physical Fock space with $\mathrm{HS}(F)$, $F=\Lambda(\mathbb{C}^m)$, and gives the exact superoperator

$$
\begin{aligned}
U\, d\Gamma(h)\, U^{*} X \\
&=\operatorname{Tr}(B)X-d\Gamma(B)X-X\,d\Gamma(B) \\
&\quad -\sum_{ij} A_{ij}\, a_i^{*} X a_j \\
&\quad -\sum_{ij} A_{ji}\, a_i X a_j^{*}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{P1}
$$

Both coefficient matrices $A$ and $A^T$ are positive Hermitian. The transpose in the second term is essential for nonreal native mass matrices. Here $\operatorname{Tr}(B)=0$, by the Pauli-spin trace; no scalar sea energy is subtracted.

For a general tau-independent Hermitian one-particle charge j, the same map gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
U\, d\Gamma(\operatorname{diag}(j,j))\, U^{*} X \\
&=\operatorname{Tr}(j)X+[d\Gamma(j),X].
\end{aligned}
\tag{P2}
$$

For a general unitary u acting identically in both blocks,

$$
\begin{aligned}
U\, \Gamma(\operatorname{diag}(u,u))\, U^{*} X \\
&=\det(u)\, \Gamma(u) X \Gamma(u)^{*}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{P3}
$$

These trace and determinant factors follow from the lower filled vacuum and must be retained. For every actual sitewise $SU(3)$ frame, including the retained charged clutch, $\operatorname{Tr}(j)=0$ and $\det(u)=1$. A general vectorlike flavor frame can have $\det(u)\ne 1$; its scalar dictionary must be retained and it is not silently a cone-preserving $\operatorname{Ad}$ action on states. The scalar cannot be inferred merely from a determinant on an unrelated total spin carrier.

The physical number operator becomes $m+N_{\mathrm{left}}-N_{\mathrm{right}}$ on $\mathrm{HS}(F)$. No fixed-number restriction was used in P1–P3. In particular half-filled physical states correspond to matrices commuting with $N$; their positivity is a conclusion below, not an input truncation.

#### P2. Probe, all compensated weights, and Coulomb form

Use the canonical isometry $\mathrm{HS}(F)\otimes\mathrm{HS}(\mathbb{C}^3)=\mathrm{HS}(E)$, $E=F\otimes\mathbb{C}^3$, dimension $d=3\cdot 2^{432}$. This preserves the original carrier dimension $d^2=9\cdot 2^{864}$; it adds no fermion species or probe. The actual co-located probe already acts by conjugation. Each total color charge therefore becomes

$$
\begin{aligned}
J_a X&=[L_a,X], \\
L_a&=d\Gamma(j_a)\otimes I+I\otimes t_a,
\end{aligned}
$$

where $t_{a}$ is zero away from the probe site. All $L_{a}$ are Hermitian. The entire actual Coulomb term is

$$
\begin{aligned}
C X&=\kappa \sum_{ab} G_{ab} [L_a,[L_b,X]], \\
G&=M_q^{-1}>0\quad\text{on the fixed 62-dimensional } h^{\perp}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Because $G$ is real symmetric, put $Z=\sum_{ab}G_{ab}L_aL_b=Z^*$. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
-C X&=2\kappa \sum_{ab} G_{ab} L_a X L_b \\
&\quad -\kappa(ZX+XZ).
\end{aligned}
\tag{P4}
$$

This identity retains both ordered fermion/probe cross terms and the complete orbit measure. It is a completely positive jump term plus a two-sided Hermitian drift; it is not a trace-only identity.

The actual stabilizer $H$ acts by conjugation on $E$. Its physical fiber $V$ is exactly the $H$-commutant in $\mathrm{HS}(E)$. The positive matrices in that commutant form a self-dual cone, containing the identity. Off-diagonal probe matrices compensated by fermion weights are precisely the off-diagonal entries within equal total-$H$ weight blocks. They are retained. Taking the separate fermion and probe commutants would be wrong.

The retained large-gauge clutch acts as $X\to V_hXV_h^*$, with $V_h=\Gamma(u_h)\otimes h_{0}$. Its determinant scalar is one by P3. This is the sampled action of the separately retained smooth clutch; it does not recover a winding character from connected finite links.

#### P3. Actual local CP generator and its irreducible algebra

On the entire $\mathrm{HS}(E)$ extension define the internal generator $L=-H_{\mathrm{internal}}$, including the actual scalar $E_{\mathrm{base}}$. By P1 and P4,

$$
\begin{aligned}
L(X)&=D X+X D^{*}+\Phi(X), \\
D&=d\Gamma(B)\otimes I-\kappa Z-E_{\mathrm{base}} I/2, \\
\Phi(X)&=\sum A_{ij} (a_i^{*}\otimes I)X(a_j\otimes I) \\
&\quad +\sum A_{ji} (a_i\otimes I)X(a_j^{*}\otimes I) \\
&\quad +2\kappa \sum G_{ab} L_a X L_b.
\end{aligned}
\tag{P5}
$$

$D$ is Hermitian in the declared frame. $\Phi$ is completely positive. Finite-dimensional Dyson expansion with the drift $X\to e^{tD}Xe^{tD^*}$ proves that $\exp(tL)$ is completely positive for $t\ge 0$. It is not necessarily trace preserving or unital before the ground transform.

The actual Gauss operator obeys $I\le M_q\le 12I$ on $h^{\perp}$: the upper bound is the sum of three covariant differences of norm at most 2, squared. Hence $G\ge I/12$. $\Phi$ contains, with positive rates, every $a_{i}\otimes I$, $a_{i}^*\otimes I$ and every $L_{a}$. The CAR creation/annihilation algebra is all $\operatorname{End}(F)$. Each localized root generator at the origin is in $h^{\perp}$; subtract its fermionic part from $L_{a}$ to obtain $I\otimes t_{\mathrm{root}}$. The six $SU(3)$ root generators generate $\operatorname{End}(\mathbb{C}^3)$. Therefore the unital associative algebra generated by this fixed jump alphabet is all $\operatorname{End}(E)$, uniformly in $q$ and the native positive mass boxes.

All actual source symmetries conjugate this algebra and preserve the cone. The CP evolution restricts to the exact H-commutant. Strict positivity and its quantitative finite-kinetic consequences are proved in the companion kernel theorem, rather than inferred from positivity of a fermion determinant.

#### P4. Responses and admissibility

$U$ is fixed and source independent. Every retained native response is exactly $U(\partial_s H)U^*$, and every higher jet transforms by the same unitary. No differentiating eigenbasis or removed scalar is involved. Weak/chiral or mass-phase insertions can leave the CP-positive class; their full signed response maps are still retained, and no positivity assertion is made for those inserted generators.

The theorem uses the same intrinsic holonomic gauge source, measure, kinetic coefficient, physical clock, complete Fock/probe carrier and retained clutch as Definition K.6.6e. No physical implementation of U is needed to prove spectral equivalence. If U were requested as a laboratory operation its control cost would need an additional ledger. The original anomaly/current identification, ambient confinement implementation and operative PCE selector remain separate admission gates.

<a id="theorem-k66h-finite-k-winding-kernel-and-faithful-ground"></a>**Theorem K.6.6h (Finite-K Winding Kernel and Faithful Ground).**

##### Finite winding kernel and faithful ground

#### Q1. The exact common finite source

Use $q_j=j/K$, $w_j=v_j/K$ and the actual midpoint conductances from W4 of Definition K.6.6e. On the full Hilbert–Schmidt extension the inner product is $\sum_j w_j\operatorname{Tr}(X_j^*Y_j)$. The original physical space is its exact $H$-commutant. In these unnormalized fiber coordinates, each directed neighbor jump of $-H$ has positive coefficient

$$

r_v&=(32/63)^{4},

and a unitary conjugation at the retained charged seam. Interior conjugations are identity. Keep the complete diagonal kinetic loss, $E_{\mathrm{base}}$, dGamma(h), and total-charge Coulomb source. No scalar energy is calibrated away.

At $\theta=0$ this is a CP generator on the finite $C^*$-algebra $A_K=\bigoplus_{j=0}^{K-1}\operatorname{End}(E)$: diagonal two-sided drifts, local CP maps P5, and neighbor CP maps. This is CP in the algebra sense; selfadjointness is with the stated weighted Hilbert–Schmidt inner product, not with an assumed unweighted trace.

A fixed scalar gauge puts the external connection phase on the seam. Expansion by directed walks gives

$$

&=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} \exp(i n\alpha)\, T_{jk,n}(\beta), \\
\alpha&=\nu\theta,\quad \nu=-1,

with CP maps $T_{jk,n}$. Reversing the convention for the oriented seam reverses both $n$ and $\alpha$ and leaves the formula and conclusions invariant. The source's section rule remains $f(q+1)=\exp(-i\nu\theta)R_h f(q)$, with positive-winding connection holonomy $\exp(+i\nu\theta)$. The smooth primitive integer is retained independently of the finite graph.

The generator is a finite bounded matrix. Its Dyson expansion in all CP jumps converges absolutely in operator norm. For example its $C^*$-norm series is dominated by $\exp(\beta C_{\mathrm{heat}})$, where $C_{\mathrm{heat}}=2D_{\mathrm{max}}+432(Q+6E_a)+2C_*+2c_0K^2/r_v$: the fermion jump map sends $I$ to $\operatorname{Tr}(A)I$ by the CAR, the color jump sends $I$ to $2\kappa Z$, and the directed hopping sum is at most $2c_0K^2/r_v$. Reindexing by winding and retaining finitely many specified event sequences is therefore legitimate. A fixed primitive graph path is not confused with a new continuum topology theorem.

#### Q2. A source-independent finite full-algebra Gram

Let $d=3\cdot 2^{432}$ and take the fixed unweighted local alphabet

$$
Z=\{a_i\otimes I,\ a_i^{*}\otimes I,\ L_a : i=1,\ldots,432,\ a=1,\ldots,62\}.
$$

Every alphabet operator has norm at most $J=866$. By P3 its associative algebra is $\operatorname{End}(E)$. The spaces spanned by words of length at most $l$ strictly increase until they are an algebra: if one stage equals the next, multiplying by every generator leaves it unchanged. Their dimension is at most $d^{2}$. Consequently all distinct alphabet words of lengths $0,\ldots,\ell$, $\ell=d^2-1$, span $\operatorname{End}(E)$.

Use all these words, counting the empty word once; let s be their finite number. Put

$$
\begin{aligned}
S&=\sum_{\mathrm{words}} |\operatorname{vec}(\mathrm{word})\rangle\langle\operatorname{vec}(\mathrm{word})|, \\
\gamma&=\det(S)/(\operatorname{Tr} S)^{d^{2}-1}>0, \\
W_2&=d\, J^{2\ell}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The fixed Gram is positive definite and $\lambda_{\mathrm{min}}(S)\ge\gamma$. Each word vector has squared norm at most $W_2$, so $\gamma\le s W_2$. This is an explicit finite algebraic definition on the actual CAR/color/probe basis. It is computationally enormous, but it contains no unknown interacting eigenstate or chosen $\theta$. An exact finite matrix construction computes it; no physical device is required to enumerate these proof words.

#### Q3. Uniform short-time lower bound for two winding blocks

The actual local generator contains every alphabet Kraus direction with rate at least $\min(\mu,\kappa/6)$, since $A\ge\mu I$ and $G\ge I/12$. Set

$$
\begin{aligned}
r&=\min(\mu,\kappa/6,c_0 K^{2} r_v)>0, \\
B_K&=E_{\mathrm{base}}+4c_0 K^{2}/r_v+C_*+864 L, \\

c&=(r\beta)^{N_{\mathrm{max}}}/N_{\mathrm{max}}!,\quad a=c\gamma/2.

Here $L=Q+9E_a$ for $r_{\mathrm{Wilson}}=1$, and $C_*=\kappa\cdot 62\cdot 866^2$. The Wilson parameter and the jump rate $r$ are distinct. The two-sided on-site drift has norm at most $B_{K}$, including the full scalar energy and kinetic loss. Also $r\le\mu=Q/4$, hence $r\beta\le 1/4$.

For each ordered pair of sites j,k select a directed path of winding0 and a path of winding1; each can have length at most 2K-1. Before its hops insert any one of the local words at the starting site. Select only the fixed-rate r part of each local jump and each hop, leaving the remaining CP terms unused. Distinct word strings give distinct ordered event sequences.

For a word of length $l$ and a path of length $p$, integrate its Dyson term over the full normalized event-time simplex. Factoring its scalar weight gives $(r\beta)^{l+p}/(l+p)!$, which is at least $c$. This factorization occurs BEFORE comparing different word lengths. CP order permits discarding the surplus coefficient and retaining the common $c$ times every normalized-simplex map.

If all intervening drift factors are replaced by identity, the Kraus operator is V word, where V is the fixed unitary product of the charged seam along that path. Thus its summed Choi Gram is unitarily equivalent to S. For every point of the event simplex, telescoping the actual drift product gives

$$

\lVert\text{Kraus-}V\text{ word}\rVert_F &\le \epsilon\sqrt{W_2}, \\
\epsilon&=\exp(\beta D_{\mathrm{max}})-1 \\
&\le \gamma/(12 s W_2)\le 1/12.

The corresponding rank-one Choi perturbation has norm at most 3 $\epsilon$ W2. Summing the s normalized-simplex terms changes the Gram by at most gamma/4. Therefore, with room to spare,

$$

\operatorname{Choi}(T_{jk,0}(\beta)) &\ge a I_{d^{2}}, \\
\operatorname{Choi}(T_{jk,1}(\beta)) &\ge a I_{d^{2}}.

This is uniform over every node, every native mass matrix in the admitted positive boxes, and every retained theta-independent source coefficient covered by the stated bounds. All coefficients in Q1 are evaluated for the actual owned spacing, inertia and coupling; none is tuned to obtain the result.

#### Q4. Faithful ground matrix and exact physical sector

Q2 implies that $T_0=\exp(-\beta H_0)$ sends every nonzero positive tuple to a tuple of strictly positive matrices. In finite dimension a strongly positive linear map on this proper cone has a simple spectral-radius eigenvector $Q_{j}>0$. One elementary proof normalizes by the sum of traces, applies the compact cone-base fixed-point theorem, and uses strict positivity to rule out a boundary eigenvector and a second extremal eigenvector by subtracting the largest positive multiple of the first. The same order argument bounds the modulus of every other eigenvalue by that radius. Since $H_{0}$ is selfadjoint in the actual weighted inner product, this is its unique lowest-energy state, with eigenvalue $E_0$.

The generator commutes with the actual stabilizer conjugations and with physical-number rotations. Those conjugations preserve positivity and the normalization $\sum_j\operatorname{Tr}Q_{j}=1$. Uniqueness therefore forces $Q$ to be in the full $H$-commutant and to commute with $N$. Under P1–P3 it is the physical $N=432$ ground state. All other physical particle sectors and compensated probe weights were present in the comparison. No unconstrained charged state was tensor-added to the physical source.

in that trace normalization. The lower estimate follows from $Q=\exp(\beta E_0)T_0Q$ and $\sum_k\operatorname{Tr}Q_{k}=1$. This controls the ground-frame inverse used next without an unowned preparation or unknown denominator.

<a id="theorem-k66i-strict-all-circle-full-source-ground-comparison"></a>**Theorem K.6.6i (Strict All-Circle Full-Source Ground Comparison).**

##### Strict external-angle ground comparison

#### S1. Ground Doob transform and stationary functional

For each $K\ge 3$ use the faithful ground tuple $Q_{j}$ from Q4, and $F_j=Q_j^{1/2}$. Define the similarity on the full complex algebra

$$
\begin{aligned}
L_\theta(Y)_j&=F_j^{-1} \\
&\quad [(-H_\theta+E_0)(F Y F)]_j\, F_j^{-1}.
\end{aligned}
$$

This is a mathematical similarity for the inverse-energy heat semigroup, not a physical real-time reduced channel or a discarded physical operation. At $\theta=0$ it is a unital CP generator. Local jumps become $W_{j,a}=F_j^{-1}V_{j,a}F_j$. A directed hopping map becomes

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\exp(i\phi_{jk})\, W_{jk} Y_k W_{jk}^{*}, \\
&W_{jk}=\sqrt{b_{jk}}\, F_j^{-1} U_{jk} F_k,
\end{aligned}
$$

where $U_{jk}$ is the actual charged seam unitary or identity. Every $W_{jk}$ is invertible. Local and hopping drifts obey $D_j+D_j^*+\sum WW^*=0$ because $L_0(I)=0$.

The stationary faithful functional is exactly

$$
\omega(Y)=\sum_j (v_j/K) \operatorname{Tr}(Q_j^{2} Y_j).
\tag{S1}
$$

Indeed weighted Hilbert–Schmidt selfadjointness of $H_{0}$ gives $\omega(L_0Y)=\langle Q,(-H_0+E_0)(FYF)\rangle_{\mathrm{weighted}}=0$. This proves stationarity directly. It does not identify the ground similarity with a unitary transformation for the GNS inner product, nor replace the weighted trace by an unweighted one.

#### S2. Exact positive-square identity and equality conditions

Define

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Gamma_\theta(Y)&=L_0(Y^{*}Y) \\
&\quad -(L_\theta Y)^{*}Y-Y^{*}(L_\theta Y).
\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the drifts using unitality gives, at each q site,

#### C2. Exact topological coefficient on the retained action

<a id="definition-k66m-complete-static-source-state-domain-and-paid-preparation"></a>**Definition K.6.6m (Complete Static Source-State Domain and Paid Preparation).**

#### S3. Existing complete response task and implementation fibres

Use the already registered finite-resolution native protocol family: the retained preparations/effects and tomography, physical-time unitary segments and their declared source ports, complete flag/reference/readout outcomes, and the native current/contact words whose bounds are supplied by the source ledger. #### S4. Explicit paid preparation of every source density

Here is a concrete uniform approximation of the whole density-state domain, avoiding an unpaid supply of arbitrary $\rho$. For $0<\epsilon<1$ define

$$
\rho_\epsilon=(1-\epsilon)\rho+\epsilon I_D/D.
$$

Then $\rho_\epsilon\ge\delta I$ with $\delta=\epsilon/D$ and

$$
(1/2)\lVert\rho_\epsilon-\rho\rVert_1\le\epsilon.
$$

Keep an actual D-dimensional reference $H_{r}$. In the fixed physical basis put

$$
|\psi\rangle=\operatorname{vec}(\sqrt{\rho_\epsilon})\in H_s\otimes H_r.
$$

Its norm is one and its source marginal is $\rho_{\epsilon}$. Choose $|e\rangle=|0\rangle_s|0\rangle_r$. Its overlap

$$
c=\langle e|\psi\rangle=(\sqrt{\rho_\epsilon})_{00}
$$

is real and $c\ge\sqrt{\delta}>0$. Write $|w\rangle=|\psi\rangle-c|e\rangle$, so $\langle e|w\rangle=0$ and $\lVert w\rVert^2=1-c^2$. In the decomposition $\mathbb{C}e\oplus e^{\perp}$ define the full unitary

$$
U_\psi = \begin{pmatrix} c & -w^{*} \\ w & I - ww^{*}/(1+c) \end{pmatrix}.
$$

Its first column is $\psi$. Direct multiplication gives the identity: the cross block is

$$
(-c+1-(1-c^{2})/(1+c))\,w^{*}=0,
$$

and the lower diagonal coefficient of $ww^*$ is

$$
1-2/(1+c)+(1-c^{2})/(1+c)^{2}=0.
$$

The other diagonal block is $c^2+\lVert w\rVert^2=1$. Thus this is a full-carrier unitary, including its complement, with no postselection.

For $w$ nonzero write $s=\lVert w\rVert$ and $\alpha=\arccos c$, and set

$$
\begin{aligned}
G&=(\alpha/s)(|w\rangle\langle e|-|e\rangle\langle w|), \\
H_{\mathrm{prep}}&=(i\hbar/T_{\mathrm{prep}})G.
\end{aligned}
$$

$G$ is anti-Hermitian, $\exp(G)=U_\psi$, and the physical evolution for positive registered duration $T_{\mathrm{prep}}$ is $\exp(-iT_{\mathrm{prep}}H_{\mathrm{prep}}/\hbar)=U_\psi$. The continuous value $\alpha/s=1$ is used at $w=0$. Hence

$$
\lVert H_{\mathrm{prep}}\rVert=\hbar\alpha/T_{\mathrm{prep}}\le\pi\hbar/(2 T_{\mathrm{prep}}).
$$

The pulse has action-norm integral at most $\pi/2$. It maps the paid basis input $|e\rangle$ to the entire purification. The reference is retained explicitly; if it is discarded or reset, that operation and its entropy/record ledger are separate physical costs. The statement about $\rho_{\epsilon}$ concerns the source marginal, not an assertion that the full service reference has disappeared or reached a unique vacuum.

The physical-sector encoding, $D^2$-dimensional source/reference support, basis input, pulse controls, source drift cancellation, readout and either fresh records or reset are charged. Binary padding uses at least $\lceil\log_2 D^2\rceil$ qubits and every unused state remains part of the carrier with its owned action. The formula specifies a legitimate finite original M.3.1 control branch; it does not derive an unpaid universal controller or a power-optimal state preparation.

#### S5. Finite coefficient words and a common source-state accuracy sequence

The regularization makes the state-preparation matrix uniformly computable from finitely accurate density data at each fixed $\epsilon$. To make the estimate explicit, let a Hermitian word matrix R approximate $\rho_{\epsilon}$ in operator norm by $\eta$, with

$$
\eta\le\delta/2,\quad D\eta\le 1/2.
$$

Then $R$ is positive, $\operatorname{Tr}R$ is in $[1-D\eta,1+D\eta]$, and the normalized matrix $\tilde{R}=R/\operatorname{Tr}R$ satisfies

$$
\begin{aligned}
\tilde{R}&\ge\delta I/3, \\
\lVert\tilde{R}-\rho_\epsilon\rVert&\le 2(D+1)\eta.
\end{aligned}
$$

These inequalities follow directly from $R\ge\rho_\epsilon-\eta I$ and the trace error $\le D\eta$. For positive $A,B$ bounded below by $aI,bI$, respectively,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sqrt{A}-\sqrt{B} \\
&= \int_0^{\infty} \exp(-t\sqrt{A})(A-B) \\
&\qquad \exp(-t\sqrt{B})\, dt,
\end{aligned}
$$

by setting $X=\sqrt{A}-\sqrt{B}$, noting $\sqrt{A}X+X\sqrt{B}=A-B$, and differentiating $\exp(-t\sqrt{A})X\exp(-t\sqrt{B})$. Its derivative is $-\exp(-t\sqrt{A})(A-B)\exp(-t\sqrt{B})$, and its terminal value vanishes. Consequently

$$
\lVert\sqrt{A}-\sqrt{B}\rVert \le \lVert A-B\rVert/(\sqrt{a}+\sqrt{b}).
$$

Applying this with $a=\delta/3$ and $b=\delta$, and bounding the Hilbert–Schmidt norm by $\sqrt{D}$ times the operator norm, gives the conservative purification error

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert\operatorname{vec}\sqrt{\tilde{R}}-\operatorname{vec}\sqrt{\rho_\epsilon}\rVert \\
&\le 2\sqrt{D}\,(D+1)\eta/\sqrt{\delta}.
\end{aligned}
$$

For pure states the trace distance is at most their vector-norm distance, and partial trace is contractive. Thus the above error plus $\epsilon$ bounds the resulting source-state error. Entrywise Hermitian coefficient words with maximum error $u$ give $\eta\le D u$. Choosing $u$ from the displayed inequalities supplies a finite uniform state-word budget for every $\rho$ at each declared $\epsilon$ and target preparation error. The finite matrix words are paid classical preparation inputs and must be supplied at that precision. This is not a procedure for learning an unknown quantum state or recovering an arbitrary exact-real matrix from no data. Equivalently, a finite sufficiently fine Hermitian word grid, retaining the certified positive normalized matrices, supplies a uniform finite preparation net for the compact density-state domain. No cost-free exact eigenvector oracle is assumed.

Compile the bounded full preparation generator and the already owned source protocols using the dense-matrix/physical-time compiler of Theorem K.6.6k (L2), with its complete apparatus and drift-cancellation bounds. Alternatively the exact finite source interaction may be registered as branch data at the original B/M level. A compiled pulse has its actual additional operator error; for a pure input its output trace distance is at most the full unitary operator error. Products with any fixed bounded finite protocol family add the already proved common generator/preparation/readout error. CPTP propagation and full-outcome readout do not increase input trace distance.

A common sequence can therefore take $\epsilon_n=2^{-n-2}$, choose $\eta_{n}$ satisfying the preceding inequalities with purification error $\le 2^{-n-2}$, and allocate all source/control/readout error $\le 2^{-n-2}$ at that same generation. Every generation uses the same $K$, $D$, native Hamiltonian family, clock and complete output contract. All support, coefficient precision and pulse-stage costs are finite, although enormous. The preparation construction is continuous on the full density-state domain. This does **not** claim uniform first/second derivatives of unregularized $\sqrt{\rho}$ at pure-state boundary points. If $\rho$ is held fixed while native source ports vary, its own derivative is zero; any moving physical encoding or state family retains its actual derivatives. The general selector transfer of Theorem K.6.6a can consume a realized minimizing architecture/output without such an operation, if its actual operative selection conditions are proved. #### S7. What this construction discharges and what it does not

It discharges the formal static candidate-domain assignment on the original finite-control branch: all angles, all density states, complete source responses, full implementation fibres, paid approximate state access, a compact source/state domain, and an exact unique source-energy minimizer with the normal output sequence of S6. <a id="definition-k66n-finite-delivery-grammar-owned-resources-and-conservative-core-qualification"></a>**Definition K.6.6n (Finite Delivery Grammar, Owned Resources and Conservative Core Qualification).**

#### 4. Whole resource bookkeeping without a postulated residual sign

The workstation's common initial stocks $A$ and native C14 are charged whether used or not. Named auxiliary endpoints except source_active have zero Hamiltonian, with all their states retained. The literal native source energy is $\operatorname{Tr}\rho H(\theta)$, and source_active separately contributes $\Delta$; their sum is denoted $\operatorname{Tr}\rho\,h(\theta)$ for the work calculation only. Its cumulative net work excursion between any two times is therefore at most $2(K+2B+1)$, independently of how often a bounded control waveform varies. This is a mean-work statement, not a stochastic two-projective-measurement work-support claim. Source preparation has its separate exact $\pi/2$ numerical bound, physically $\pi\hbar/(2T_{\mathrm{unit}})$. Each added device must supply its own finite Hamiltonian/control bound and paid reserve/initial stock. There is no uniform reserve claim for arbitrarily large added devices; their own input/output balances are included separately below.

An additional device $j$ has its own fixed ground-energy convention, $E_{\mathrm{in},j}\ge 0$ initial mean energy, $E_{\mathrm{ret},j}\ge 0$ mean energy physically returned through its specified return connector, and $E_{\mathrm{out},j}\ge 0$ nonreturned final energy. All are accounted; initial pure resources, extra ROM, control, clock and storage add nonnegative readiness/maintenance charges $P_{j}$. Its initial energy is a charged supply, not a free battery. Returned energy is credited exactly once. The first law for source plus all added stores gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
W + \sum_j E_{\mathrm{in},j} \\
&= \operatorname{Tr}\rho\, h(\theta)+\sum_j(E_{\mathrm{ret},j}+E_{\mathrm{out},j})
\end{aligned}
$$

after subtracting the separately fixed native common endpoints. Adding initial-supply charges and subtracting actual returns therefore yields

$$
\begin{aligned}
W + \sum_j(E_{\mathrm{in},j}-E_{\mathrm{ret},j})+\sum_j P_j \\
&= \operatorname{Tr}\rho\, h(\theta)+\sum_j(E_{\mathrm{out},j}+P_j).
\end{aligned}
$$

Hence $\Delta=\sum_j(E_{\mathrm{out},j}+P_j)\ge 0$ is derived bookkeeping, not the assumption that an omitted controller is free. For no additional devices and the explicit ideal witness, $\Delta=0$ exactly. No hidden dump, temperature bath, recovered source energy or unpriced purity is available. Retaining an added returned object does not both credit its energy and erase its physical ownership: its stated return connector transfers it out of this service boundary, whereas named source/reference outputs are compulsory delivered objects and never counted as returned supply.

### K.6.7 The Real Locus of Gr(2,8)

<a id="definition-k610-real-grassmannian"></a>**Definition K.6.10 (Real Grassmannian).** The fixed-point set of the $\sigma$-involution is the real Grassmannian:
$$\text{Gr}(2,8)^{\sigma} = \{W \in \text{Gr}(2,8) : \sigma(W) = W\} \cong \text{Gr}_{\mathbb{R}}(2,8)$$

<a id="proposition-k65-real-locus-properties"></a>**Proposition K.6.5 (Real Locus Properties).** The real locus $\text{Gr}_{\mathbb{R}}(2,8)$ is:

1. A totally real submanifold of $\text{Gr}(2,8)$
2. Diffeomorphic to $O(8)/(O(2) \times O(6))$
3. Of real dimension $\dim_{\mathbb{R}}(\text{Gr}_{\mathbb{R}}(2,8)) = 12$

*Proof.* Let $\sigma$ denote complex conjugation on $\mathbb C^8$, and let $W\in \mathrm{Gr}(2,8)^\sigma$. The condition $\sigma(W)=W$ means that $W$ is the complexification of a unique real 2-plane $V:=W\cap \mathbb R^8$, so $W=V\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$. Conversely, if $V\subset \mathbb R^8$ is a real 2-plane, then $V\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$ is fixed by complex conjugation. Therefore
$$
\mathrm{Gr}(2,8)^\sigma \cong \mathrm{Gr}_{\mathbb R}(2,8).
$$

The orthogonal group $O(8)$ acts transitively on real 2-planes in $\mathbb R^8$: given $V_1,V_2\in \mathrm{Gr}_{\mathbb R}(2,8)$, choose orthonormal bases of $V_1$ and $V_2$ and extend them to orthonormal bases of $\mathbb R^8$; the linear map sending one basis to the other lies in $O(8)$ and carries $V_1$ to $V_2$. The stabilizer of the standard plane $\mathbb R^2\oplus 0\subset \mathbb R^8$ consists exactly of block-diagonal orthogonal transformations preserving that plane and its orthogonal complement, namely $O(2)\times O(6)$. Hence
$$
\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathbb R}(2,8) \cong O(8)/(O(2)\times O(6)).
$$

For the dimension,
$$
\dim O(8)=\frac{8\cdot 7}{2}=28,\qquad
\dim O(2)=1,\qquad
\dim O(6)=\frac{6\cdot5}{2}=15,
$$
so
$$
\dim_{\mathbb R}\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathbb R}(2,8)=28-1-15=12.
$$

To prove total reality, let $W=V\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$ be a fixed point. The complex tangent space of $\mathrm{Gr}(2,8)$ at $W$ is
$$
T_W\mathrm{Gr}(2,8) \cong \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,W^\perp).
$$
The differential $d\sigma$ acts on this space by complex conjugation, and the tangent space of the invariant locus is the $+1$ eigenspace
$$
T_W\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathbb R}(2,8) \cong \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(V,V^\perp).
$$
The complex structure is multiplication by $i$, while $d\sigma(iA)=-i\,d\sigma(A)$. Thus no nonzero vector in the fixed tangent space is invariant after multiplication by $i$; equivalently
$$
T_W\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathbb R}(2,8) \cap i\,T_W\mathrm{Gr}_{\mathbb R}(2,8)=\{0\}.
$$
Hence the fixed locus is totally real. ∎

<a id="corollary-k64-sigma-invariant-vacuum-representative"></a>**Corollary K.6.4 ($\sigma$-Invariant Vacuum Representative).** If the PCE-Attractor vacuum is $\sigma$-invariant, then its Grassmannian representative lies in $\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb R}(2,8)$. Coordinates and tensors constructed solely and equivariantly from that representative may be chosen real. This conclusion does not constrain Berry holonomies, determinant orientations, or parameters supplied by independent sectors.

*Proof.* By definition,
$$
\operatorname{Gr}(2,8)^\sigma
=\{W:\sigma(W)=W\}
\cong\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb R}(2,8).
$$
Thus a $\sigma$-invariant representative belongs to the real locus. No statement about data not determined by that representative follows from this membership relation. ∎
