<a id="definition-k611-e_8-root-system"></a>**Definition K.6.11 ($E_8$ Root System).** The $E_8$ root system consists of 240 vectors in $\mathbb{R}^8$ of squared norm 2:

- **Type I (112 roots):** All permutations of $(\pm 1, \pm 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)$
- **Type II (128 roots):** All vectors $(\pm\frac{1}{2}, \pm\frac{1}{2}, \ldots, \pm\frac{1}{2})$ with an even number of minus signs

<a id="lemma-k62-e_8-reality"></a>**Lemma K.6.2 ($E_8$ Reality).** All $E_8$ roots have real coordinates:
$$
E_8\subset\mathbb R^8.
$$

*Proof.* In Definition K.6.11, every Type-I coordinate belongs to $\{-1,0,1\}\subset\mathbb R$, and every Type-II coordinate belongs to $\{-1/2,1/2\}\subset\mathbb R$. Both families therefore lie in $\mathbb R^8$, and their union is the stated root system. ∎

<a id="lemma-k63-e_8-distance-spectrum"></a>**Lemma K.6.3 ($E_8$ Distance Spectrum).** For distinct roots $r_i, r_j \in E_8$, the squared Euclidean distance satisfies:
$$d^2_{E_8}(r_i, r_j) = |r_i - r_j|^2 \in \{2, 4, 6, 8\}$$

*Proof.* Every root has squared norm $2$, so
$$
\|r_i-r_j\|^2
=4-2\langle r_i,r_j\rangle.
$$
The $E_8$ coordinate description gives integral inner products, and Cauchy--Schwarz gives $-2\le\langle r_i,r_j\rangle\le2$. Equality at $2$ holds only when $r_i=r_j$, which is excluded. Thus for distinct roots
$$
\langle r_i,r_j\rangle\in\{-2,-1,0,1\},
$$
and substitution yields
$$
\|r_i-r_j\|^2\in\{8,6,4,2\}.
$$
This is the asserted set. ∎

<a id="theorem-k67-yukawa-magnitude-positivity-on-the-toeplitz-kraus-probability-overlap-branch"></a>**Theorem K.6.7 (Yukawa-Magnitude Positivity on the Toeplitz-Kraus Probability-Overlap Branch).** Assume the normalized flat reference packets and Toeplitz--Kraus probability-overlap rule of Theorem T.41.5, set their amplitude-width parameter to $\sigma_B^2=1/24$ on the statistical unit-radius convention of Lemma T.41.2, and assume an accepted finite Bures--$E_8$ embedding certificate from Lemma T.41.4. The reference packets have Born covariance $(\sigma_B^2/2)I_{24}$, not the statistical covariance $\sigma_B^2I_{24}$ of Theorem T.41.1. For every certified pair define
$$
K^{\mathrm{mag}}_{ij}
:=A_f\exp\left[-\frac{d_{E_8}^2(r_i,r_j)}{16\sigma_B^2}\right],
\qquad A_f>0.
$$
Then
$$
K^{\mathrm{mag}}_{ij}\in\mathbb R_{>0},
\qquad
\alpha:=\frac{1}{16\sigma_B^2}=\frac32.
$$
For the heat-kernel realization, the corresponding positive kernel is
$$
A_f\Delta_{\mathrm{VVM}}(i,j)^{1/2}e^{-\alpha d_{E_8}^2(r_i,r_j)}(1+\epsilon_{ij}),
$$
provided the certificate verifies $\Delta_{\mathrm{VVM}}(i,j)>0$ and $\epsilon_{ij}>-1$. Neither expression is a physical Yukawa magnitude until the full-matrix realization gate of Theorem T.39 is accepted.

*Proof.* Theorem T.41.5 computes the normalized flat-packet probability overlap as $e^{-\lVert\xi_i-\xi_j\rVert^2/(2\sigma_B^2)}$, with $\xi_i=(r_i/\sqrt8,0)$. Thus $\lVert\xi_i-\xi_j\rVert^2=d_{E_8}^2/8$, and Lemma T.41.4 identifies this distance with $d_{g_B}^2$ on each certified pair. Substituting the declared amplitude-width value $\sigma_B^2=1/24$ gives $\alpha=3/2$. Positivity follows from $A_f>0$, positivity of the exponential, and, on the heat-kernel branch, the two displayed certificate inequalities. The multiplicative $A_f$ is distinct from Theorem T.39's additive logarithmic constant $C_f$. ∎

The theorem fixes only a positive model-kernel magnitude $K_{ij}^{\mathrm{mag}}$. On a flavor branch carrying Berry phases, define $K_{ij}:=K_{ij}^{\mathrm{mag}}e^{i\theta_{ij}^{\mathrm{Berry}}}$. It becomes an entry of a candidate sector matrix $Y_f$ only through Theorem T.39's accepted entrywise assembly and full-matrix checks; such a matrix need not be real.

<a id="theorem-k68-real-yukawa-orientation-decomposition"></a>**Theorem K.6.8 (Real Yukawa Orientation Decomposition).** Let $Y_f$ be a genuinely real nondegenerate $3\times3$ Yukawa matrix. Then there exist $O_{L,f},O_{R,f}\in O(3)$ and
$$
D_f=\operatorname{diag}(y_1^f,y_2^f,y_3^f),
\qquad
y_i^f>0,
$$
such that
$$
Y_f=O_{L,f}D_fO_{R,f}^T.
$$
The determinant orientation of the sector is
$$
\epsilon_f
:=
\operatorname{sgn}\det Y_f
=
\det O_{L,f}\det O_{R,f}
\in\{+1,-1\}.
\tag{K.6.8.1}
$$
This sign is independent of the singular-vector choices inside degenerate singular-value subspaces. Theorem K.6.7 fixes the positive magnitude kernel of the Gaussian overlap branch, not reality of a Berry-phased full Yukawa matrix. Even on a separately certified genuinely real branch, positive entries alone do not fix $\epsilon_f$.

*Proof.* Since $Y_f$ is real and nondegenerate, the real singular-value theorem gives orthogonal matrices $O_{L,f},O_{R,f}$ and positive singular values $y_i^f$ with $Y_f=O_{L,f}D_fO_{R,f}^T$. Taking determinants gives
$$
\det Y_f=(\det O_{L,f})(\det D_f)(\det O_{R,f}),
$$
and $\det D_f=\prod_i y_i^f>0$, hence (K.6.8.1). If a singular value has multiplicity, the corresponding singular-vector bases may be changed by the same orthogonal matrix $S$ on the left and right singular subspaces. This multiplies $\det O_{L,f}$ and $\det O_{R,f}$ by the same factor $\det S$, so their product is unchanged. Thus $\epsilon_f$ is a well-defined orientation invariant of the real nondegenerate Yukawa matrix. The final sentence follows because entrywise positivity is a condition on matrix entries, whereas $\epsilon_f$ is the connected-component sign of $GL(3,\mathbb R)$. ∎

<a id="theorem-k69-orientation-preserving-real-yukawa-branch-criterion"></a>**Theorem K.6.9 (Orientation-Preserving Real-Yukawa Branch Criterion).** Let $Y_f$ be a real nondegenerate Yukawa matrix in one fermion sector, with determinant orientation $\epsilon_f$ as in Theorem K.6.8. Suppose the branch supplies a continuous path
$$
Y_f(t)\in GL(3,\mathbb R),
\qquad
0\le t\le1,
$$
generated by the same finite flavor data, such that
$$
Y_f(0)=D_f,
\qquad
Y_f(1)=Y_f,
\qquad
\det Y_f(t)\ne0
\quad\text{for all }t\in[0,1].
\tag{K.6.9.1}
$$
Then
$$
\det Y_f>0,
\qquad
\epsilon_f=+1.
\tag{K.6.9.2}
$$
Equivalently, in any real SVD orientation decomposition of Theorem K.6.8,
$$
\det O_{L,f}\det O_{R,f}=+1.
\tag{K.6.9.3}
$$
Real positive entries of $Y_f$ alone do not imply (K.6.9.2).

*Proof.* The determinant is a continuous nonzero real-valued function along the path (K.6.9.1). Hence $\operatorname{sgn}\det Y_f(t)$ is constant on $[0,1]$. Since $Y_f(0)=D_f$ and $\det D_f=\prod_i y_i^f>0$, the endpoint satisfies $\det Y_f>0$. Formula (K.6.8.1) then gives $\epsilon_f=+1$ and (K.6.9.3).

It remains to record why the hypothesis is not automatic from entrywise positivity. Let $\gamma>0$ and set $x=e^{-2\gamma}\in(0,1)$. The following six vectors are $E_8$ roots:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\nu_1&=(0,0,-1,0,0,0,1,0),&
\nu_2&=(1/2,1/2,-1/2,1/2,1/2,-1/2,1/2,1/2),&
\nu_3&=(1/2,1/2,1/2,-1/2,-1/2,1/2,1/2,1/2),\\
w_1&=(1,0,1,0,0,0,0,0),&
w_2&=(-1,0,0,1,0,0,0,0),&
w_3&=(-1,0,1,0,0,0,0,0).
\end{aligned}
$$
Their cross squared-distance matrix is
$$
\left(\|\nu_i-w_j\|^2\right)_{ij}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
6&4&6\\
4&4&6\\
2&6&4
\end{pmatrix}.
$$
The corresponding cross-Gaussian matrix is
$$
Y(x)=
\begin{pmatrix}
x^3&x^2&x^3\\
x^2&x^2&x^3\\
x&x^3&x^2
\end{pmatrix},
$$
whose entries are strictly positive and whose determinant is
$$
\det Y(x)=-x^6(x-1)^2(x+1)<0.
$$
Thus cross-Gaussian $E_8$ positivity can lie in the negative determinant component. The orientation-preserving condition must therefore be supplied by the finite branch certificate unless the matrix is a same-root Gaussian Gram matrix. In that special same-root case, for distinct roots $r_1,r_2,r_3$,
$$
Y_{ij}=e^{-\gamma\|r_i-r_j\|^2}
$$
is positive definite because
$$
\sum_{i,j}\overline c_i c_j e^{-\gamma\|r_i-r_j\|^2}
=
C_\gamma\int_{\mathbb R^8}
\left|\sum_i c_i e^{i\omega\cdot r_i}\right|^2
e^{-\|\omega\|^2/(4\gamma)}d\omega.
$$
The integrand is nonnegative. If the integral vanished, then
$$
F(\omega):=\sum_i c_i e^{i\omega\cdot r_i}
$$
would vanish almost everywhere and hence everywhere because $F$ is real analytic. Choose a vector $v$ for which the numbers $v\cdot r_i$ are pairwise distinct. Then $F(tv)=0$ for all $t$, and differentiating at $t=0$ for orders $0,1,2$ gives a Vandermonde system in the three distinct frequencies. Its determinant is nonzero, so every $c_i=0$, a contradiction. Thus the integral is strictly positive for nonzero $c$. The same-root Gaussian matrix is positive definite and has positive determinant, while a general row-column cross-overlap construction need not. ∎

<a id="theorem-k69a-ordered-gaussian-total-positivity-orientation-theorem"></a>**Theorem K.6.9a (Ordered Gaussian Total-Positivity Orientation Theorem).** Let
$$
x_1<\cdots<x_m,
\qquad
 y_1<\cdots<y_m,
\qquad
\gamma>0,
$$
and define
$$
G_{ij}=\exp(-\gamma(x_i-y_j)^2).
\tag{K.6.9a.1}
$$
Then every square minor with the same increasing row and column order is strictly positive. In particular, for $m=3$,
$$
\det G>0.
\tag{K.6.9a.2}
$$

*Proof.* It is enough to prove the full determinant statement for arbitrary equal-size ordered sublists, since applying the same argument to those sublists proves every ordered minor. For a fixed ordered pair of sublists, write
$$
G_{ij}=e^{-\gamma x_i^2}e^{-\gamma y_j^2}e^{2\gamma x_i y_j}.
\tag{K.6.9a.3}
$$
The row and column factors are strictly positive, so the determinant sign is the sign of $\det(e^{a x_i y_j})$ with $a=2\gamma>0$. Translating all $x_i$ and all $y_j$ by constants multiplies rows and columns of $(e^{a x_i y_j})$ by strictly positive factors and does not change the determinant sign. Choose such translations so that all $x_i$ and $y_j$ are positive.

Expanding the exponential and applying Cauchy-Binet gives
$$
\det(e^{a x_i y_j})_{i,j=1}^m
=
\sum_{0\le n_1<\cdots<n_m}
\left(\prod_{r=1}^m\frac{a^{n_r}}{n_r!}\right)
\det(x_i^{n_r})_{i,r=1}^m
\det(y_j^{n_r})_{j,r=1}^m.
\tag{K.6.9a.4}
$$
For positive ordered variables and strictly increasing exponents, each generalized Vandermonde determinant is the ordinary Vandermonde determinant times a Schur polynomial with nonnegative coefficients, hence is nonnegative; for the exponent set $(0,1,\ldots,m-1)$ both determinants are the ordinary positive Vandermonde determinants. Therefore the sum contains one strictly positive term and no negative terms, so the determinant is strictly positive. ∎

<a id="corollary-k69a1-forced-positive-yukawa-orientation-from-an-ordered-heat-kernel-chamber"></a>**Corollary K.6.9a.1 (Forced Positive Yukawa Orientation from an Ordered Heat-Kernel Chamber).** If a finite flavor certificate places the three generations of a real Yukawa sector in ordered one-dimensional flag coordinates $x_1<x_2<x_3$ and $y_1<y_2<y_3$ and gives the real amplitude matrix
$$
Y_{ij}=c_i d_j\exp(-\gamma(x_i-y_j)^2),
\qquad
c_i>0,
\quad d_j>0,
\quad \gamma>0,
\tag{K.6.9a.5}
$$
then $\det Y>0$ and the sector lies in the positive determinant component.

*Proof.* Positive row and column factors multiply the determinant by $(\prod_i c_i)(\prod_j d_j)>0$. The remaining determinant is positive by Theorem K.6.9a with $m=3$. ∎

<a id="theorem-k610-quark-mass-matrix-phase-on-the-real-branch"></a>**Theorem K.6.10 (Quark Mass Matrix Phase on the Real Branch).** Let $M_f=vY_f/\sqrt2$ with $v>0$ fixed by electroweak gauge choice and $Y_f\in GL(3,\mathbb R)$. Then
$$
\arg(\det M_f)
=
\begin{cases}
0,&\det Y_f>0,\\
\pi,&\det Y_f<0,
\end{cases}
\quad\text{mod }2\pi.
\tag{K.6.10.1}
$$
In particular, any positive-orientation branch certified by Theorem K.6.9 or Corollary K.6.9a.1 gives $\arg(\det M_f)\equiv0\pmod{2\pi}$ in that sector.

*Proof.* Since $v/\sqrt2>0$,
$$
\det M_f=(v/\sqrt2)^3\det Y_f,
$$
so the phase of $\det M_f$ is exactly the phase of the nonzero real number $\det Y_f$. A nonzero real number has phase $0$ if positive and $\pi$ if negative, modulo $2\pi$. The final sentence follows from (K.6.9.2) or Corollary K.6.9a.1. ∎

<a id="corollary-k65-quark-determinant-phase-on-a-certified-positive-orientation-real-yukawa-branch"></a>**Corollary K.6.5 (Quark Determinant Phase on a Certified Positive-Orientation Real-Yukawa Branch).** On the branch where both quark Yukawa matrices either satisfy the nonzero-path criterion of Theorem K.6.9 or are certified by the ordered heat-kernel chamber of Corollary K.6.9a.1,
$$
\arg(\det M_q)\equiv0\pmod{2\pi}.
$$
On a separately certified genuinely real full-Yukawa branch, absence of a positive-orientation certificate leaves only the alternatives $\arg(\det M_f)\in\{0,\pi\}\pmod{2\pi}$ sector by sector. The $E_8$ probability-overlap construction alone fixes magnitudes and does not establish this real branch when Berry phases are retained.

*Proof.* The quark determinant entering the strong-CP parameter is
$$
\det M_q=\frac{v^6}{2^3}\det Y_u\det Y_d.
$$
The electroweak gauge choice fixes $v>0$. Theorem K.6.9 gives $\det Y_f>0$ when the branch supplies a nonzero path from the positive diagonal reference. Corollary K.6.9a.1 gives $\det Y_f>0$ when the branch supplies an ordered heat-kernel chamber. If both quark sectors satisfy either certificate, then $\det Y_u>0$ and $\det Y_d>0$, hence $\det M_q>0$ and $\arg(\det M_q)\equiv0\pmod{2\pi}$. The last sentence is Theorem K.6.10 applied before imposing a positive-orientation certificate. ∎

**Definition K.6.10a (Pfaffian Real-Orientation Certificate).** For a real quark Yukawa branch, define the real doubled skew operator
$$
\mathcal D_q(Y_u,Y_d)
:=
\begin{pmatrix}
0 & M_q\\
-M_q^T & 0
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
M_q:=M_u\oplus M_d.
\tag{K.6.10a.1}
$$
For the standard ordered block basis and $\dim M_q=6$,
$$
\operatorname{Pf}_{\mathrm{std}}(\mathcal D_q)
=(-1)^{6\cdot5/2}\det M_q
=-\det M_q.
$$
The certificate adopts the positive-reference orientation and denotes the orientation-adjusted scalar by
$$
\operatorname{Pf}(\mathcal D_q)
:=-\operatorname{Pf}_{\mathrm{std}}(\mathcal D_q)
=\det M_q.
$$
Consequently,
$$
\operatorname{Pf}(\mathcal D_q)^2
=\det\mathcal D_q
=(\det M_q)^2.
\tag{K.6.10a.2}
$$
A Pfaffian real-orientation certificate is a finite record
$$
\mathfrak O_{\mathrm{Pf}}
=
\left(
\mathcal Y_{\mathbb R}^+,
\operatorname{Pf}(\mathcal D_q),
\nabla_{\mathrm{Pf}},
w_1(\mathrm{Pf}),
\Delta_{\mathrm{gap}},
V_{\mathrm{top}},
\chi_{\mathrm{Pf}}
\right)
\tag{K.6.10a.3}
$$
such that:

1. $\mathcal Y_{\mathbb R}^+$ is a connected retained real-Yukawa chamber;

2. $M_q$ is invertible throughout $\mathcal Y_{\mathbb R}^+$;

3. the Pfaffian line is orientable on the chamber,
$$
w_1(\mathrm{Pf})=0;
\tag{K.6.10a.4}
$$

4. the accepted orientation is specified by a positive diagonal reference point $Y_{\mathrm{diag}}\in\mathcal Y_{\mathbb R}^+$;

5. the finite gap satisfies
$$
|\operatorname{Pf}(\mathcal D_q)|\ge\Delta_{\mathrm{gap}}>0
\tag{K.6.10a.5}
$$
on the retained chamber;

6. any path leaving $\mathcal Y_{\mathbb R}^+$ either crosses $\det M_q=0$ or pays topological orientation overhead
$$
\Delta V_{\mathrm{top}}\ge\varepsilon_0;
\tag{K.6.10a.6}
$$

7. $\chi_{\mathrm{Pf}}$ records that the chamber, orientation, gap, and overhead were determined by the declared chamber construction independently of the neutron electric dipole bound.

**Theorem K.6.10b (Pfaffian Orientation Forces the Quark Determinant Phase).** On a branch carrying an accepted $\mathfrak O_{\mathrm{Pf}}$,
$$
\arg(\det M_q)\equiv0\pmod{2\pi}.
\tag{K.6.10b.1}
$$
Moreover, the opposite determinant-orientation component cannot be reached inside the same finite branch without either closing the quark determinant gap or paying the explicit orientation overhead (K.6.10a.6).

*Proof.* At the positive diagonal reference point, the accepted orientation gives
$$
\operatorname{Pf}(\mathcal D_q)>0.
$$
Because $w_1(\mathrm{Pf})=0$, the Pfaffian line has a global orientation on $\mathcal Y_{\mathbb R}^+$. Because $|\operatorname{Pf}(\mathcal D_q)|\ge\Delta_{\mathrm{gap}}>0$, the Pfaffian cannot change sign along any path in the chamber. Therefore
$$
\operatorname{Pf}(\mathcal D_q)>0
$$
throughout $\mathcal Y_{\mathbb R}^+$. With the reference orientation of (K.6.10a.1), positivity of the Pfaffian is equivalent to positivity of $\det M_q$ on the same connected chamber. Hence $\det M_q>0$, and a positive real determinant has phase $0$ modulo $2\pi$.

A path to the opposite determinant component must change the sign of the Pfaffian. Since the Pfaffian is continuous, this requires $\operatorname{Pf}(\mathcal D_q)=0$ somewhere unless the path leaves the certified oriented chamber. By (K.6.10a.2), $\operatorname{Pf}(\mathcal D_q)=0$ implies $\det M_q=0$. If the path leaves the chamber without closing the gap, the certificate assigns the explicit topological overhead (K.6.10a.6), so it is not the same zero-surplus PCE branch. ∎

### K.6.9 Combined Conditional Implication

<a id="theorem-k611-conditional-barthetaequiv0pmod2pi-on-the-σ-symmetric-positive-orientation-branch"></a>**Theorem K.6.11 (Conditional $\bar\theta\equiv0\pmod{2\pi}$ on the σ-Symmetric Positive-Orientation Branch).** Assume:

1. a constructed equivariant parameter map satisfying Theorem K.6.1;
2. a specified accepted QCD gauge-topology bridge satisfying Proposition K.6.4;
3. the $\sigma$-symmetric vacuum branch of Theorem K.6.5;
4. the positive first-harmonic cost is certified as the operative QCD vacuum-selection functional, and the realized vacuum is a global minimizer on the retained invariant sector, as required by Theorem K.6.6;
5. an absolute determinant-line certificate for the full nondegenerate quark mass matrices,
   $$
   \frac{\det(M_uM_d)}{|\det(M_uM_d)|}=1.
   $$
   This may be discharged by: (a) genuinely real full Yukawa matrices, positive-orientation certificates of Corollary K.6.5 in both sectors, and a certificate that no Berry factors multiply those mass entries; (b) a registered nondegenerate reference pair $(M_u^0,M_d^0)$ with $\det(M_u^0M_d^0)>0$, together with full complex flavor transport from that pair whose determinant holonomy obeys $\det U_u\det U_d=1$ along the retained path; or (c) an accepted Pfaffian real-orientation certificate $\mathfrak O_{\mathrm{Pf}}$ of Definition K.6.10a on a genuinely real branch.

Then
$$
\bar\theta
=
\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}+\arg(\det M_q)
\equiv
0
\pmod{2\pi}.
$$

*Proof.* Items 1–4 and Theorem K.6.6 give $\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}\equiv0\pmod{2\pi}$ in the fixed common chiral convention. Item 5 fixes the determinant phase of the full mass matrices in that same convention; alternatives (a)–(c) are sufficient ways to discharge it. Their invariant product is therefore $z_{\mathrm{CP}}=1$, equivalently $\bar\theta\equiv0\pmod{2\pi}$. Without items 1–4 the gauge angle has not been selected; without item 5, neither positive magnitudes nor separately assigned Berry phases fix the determinant line of the full quark mass matrices. ∎

<a id="theorem-k612-basis-covariant-strong-cp-bookkeeping"></a>**Theorem K.6.12 (Basis-Covariant Strong-CP Bookkeeping).** For nondegenerate full quark mass matrices $M_u$ and $M_d$, define
$$
z_{\mathrm{CP}}
:=
e^{i\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}}
\frac{\det(M_uM_d)}{|\det(M_uM_d)|}
=e^{i\bar\theta}.
$$
Under an anomalous chiral rephasing by an angle $\chi$, the two displayed factors transform oppositely,
$$
\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}\longmapsto\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}-\chi,
\qquad
\arg\det(M_uM_d)\longmapsto\arg\det(M_uM_d)+\chi,
$$
so $z_{\mathrm{CP}}$ is invariant although its two terms are not. Consequently the following may be supplied as separate constructions only after one common chiral-basis and determinant-line convention is fixed:

1. a gauge-vacuum construction fixing the first factor in that convention; and
2. a full mass determinant-line construction fixing the second factor in the same convention.

*Proof.* The anomalous Jacobian of the chiral rephasing shifts the coefficient of the topological term by the negative of the mass-determinant phase shift. Their sum modulo $2\pi$, and hence $z_{\mathrm{CP}}$, is unchanged. Therefore the individual zero statements are convention-dependent bookkeeping statements, whereas $z_{\mathrm{CP}}=1$ is the physical conclusion. Theorem K.6.11 is valid only when its gauge and flavor certificates use the same convention and jointly establish that invariant conclusion. ∎

<a id="remark-k62-contrast-with-fine-tuning"></a>**Remark K.6.2: Contrast with Fine-Tuning.** In standard treatments, $\bar\theta\approx0$ can be written in a fixed convention as a cancellation between $\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}$ and $\arg\det(M_uM_d)$. In the conditional branch of Theorem K.6.11, the common-convention gauge and full-mass determinant-line certificates jointly give the invariant statement $z_{\mathrm{CP}}=1$ without a fitted cancellation. The $E_8$ input supplies the positive Yukawa magnitude kernel.

### K.6.10 $E_8$ Triad Selection

<a id="definition-k612-mass-ratio-invariant"></a>**Definition K.6.12 (Mass Ratio Invariant).** For a Dirac-type generation sector with ordered positive masses $m_3>m_2>m_1$, define
$$
\mathcal R:=\frac{\ln(m_3/m_1)}{\ln(m_3/m_2)}.
$$
On a preregistered path-additive, diagonal-alignment branch whose Theorem-T.39 realization certificate verifies a common exponent coefficient and residuals satisfying
$$
\frac{\varepsilon_{31}}{d_{31}^2}
=
\frac{\varepsilon_{32}}{d_{32}^2}
$$
(in particular, both residuals may vanish), one additionally has
$$
\mathcal R=\frac{d_{31}^2}{d_{32}^2}.
\tag{K.6.12.1}
$$
For nonzero certified residuals, Definition R.5.1 supplies a bounded interval only after a uniform separation of the logarithmic denominator from zero is certified. For Majorana neutrinos, the anchored quantity $\mathcal R_\nu=\Delta_1/\Delta_2$ belongs to its separately registered Takagi branch.

<a id="theorem-k613-discrete-ℛ-values"></a>**Theorem K.6.13 (Discrete ℛ Values).** Under the proportional-residual branch of (K.6.12.1), if
$$
d_{31}^2,d_{32}^2\in\{2,4,6,8\},
\qquad d_{31}^2>d_{32}^2,
$$
then
$$
\mathcal R\in\left\{\frac43,\frac32,2,3,4\right\}.
$$

*Proof.* Equation (K.6.12.1) reduces the claim to finite arithmetic. Enumerating the ordered pairs $(d_{32}^2,d_{31}^2)$ gives $(6,8)$, $(4,6)$, $(2,4)$, $(4,8)$, $(2,6)$, and $(2,8)$, whose distinct ratios are exactly the displayed set. Without the branch equality, this enumeration is a candidate diagnostic and not a mass theorem. ∎

<a id="theorem-k614-distance-pair-enumeration-for-the-mass-ratio-invariant"></a>**Theorem K.6.14 (Distance-Pair Enumeration for the Mass-Ratio Invariant).** Let
$$
d_{31}^2,d_{32}^2\in\{2,4,6,8\},
\qquad d_{31}^2>d_{32}^2.
$$
Then the pairs compatible with each value of $\mathcal R=d_{31}^2/d_{32}^2$ are
$$
\begin{array}{c|c}
\mathcal R&(d_{32}^2,d_{31}^2)\\ \hline
4/3&(6,8)\\
3/2&(4,6)\\
2&(2,4),(4,8)\\
3&(2,6)\\
4&(2,8).
\end{array}
$$
This enumeration does not select a unique $E_8$ triad. Moreover, for $\alpha>0$ the function
$$
C(a,b)=e^{-\alpha a}+e^{-\alpha b}
$$
is strictly decreasing in each argument, so minimizing this particular expression cannot justify selection of the smallest admissible distances.

*Proof.* Enumerating the six ordered pairs
$$
(2,4),(2,6),(2,8),(4,6),(4,8),(6,8)
$$
gives the table by direct division. For the cost claim,
$$
\frac{\partial C}{\partial a}=-\alpha e^{-\alpha a}<0,
\qquad
\frac{\partial C}{\partial b}=-\alpha e^{-\alpha b}<0.
$$
Thus larger arguments lower $C$. Distances alone also leave the actual root labels and their mutual geometry unspecified. ∎

**Table K.6.1: $E_8$ Triad Assignments**

| Sector | $\mathcal{R}_{\text{input}}$ | Nearest $\mathcal{R}$ | $(d^2_{32}, d^2_{31})$ | Relative deviation from $\mathcal{R}_{\text{input}}$ |
|:-------|:---------------------------|:----------------------|:-----------------------|:----------|
| Charged leptons | 2.889 | 3 | (2, 6) | 3.8% |
| Down quarks | 1.79 | 2 | (2, 4) | 12% |
| Up quarks | 2.30 | 2 | (4, 8) | 13% |

### K.6.11 Absolute Strong-Sector Classes and Relative CP Responses

The framework distinguishes absolute strong-sector phase data from relative CP-response data. On the complete conditional Appendix K branch, the absolute strong-sector class is trivial, while a separately certified weak-sector Berry phase may remain nonzero.

<a id="definition-k613-type-i-absolute-strong-sector-class"></a>**Definition K.6.13 (Type I Absolute Strong-Sector Class).** The basis-invariant absolute determinant-line class is
$$
z_{\mathrm{CP}}=e^{i\bar\theta}.
$$
Its nontriviality means $z_{\mathrm{CP}}\ne1$. Under the registered physical CP action, $z_{\mathrm{CP}}\mapsto\overline{z_{\mathrm{CP}}}=z_{\mathrm{CP}}^{-1}$. Both $z_{\mathrm{CP}}=1$ and $z_{\mathrm{CP}}=-1$ are self-conjugate; a nontrivial absolute class alone is therefore not a certificate of CP violation. A class outside $\{1,-1\}$ is a non-invariant parameter record. At either self-conjugate class, the CP status of the realized vacuum and any spontaneous breaking require separate vacuum and response data. The separate values of $\theta_{\mathrm{QCD}}$ and $\arg\det(M_uM_d)$, and the mere presence of complex Yukawa entries, are not individually invariant criteria.

<a id="definition-k614-type-ii-cp-violation"></a>**Definition K.6.14 (Type II CP Violation).** Type II CP violation is a
nontrivial relative determinant-line holonomy class on a certified flavor or
other response branch that acts nontrivially on a retained CP-sensitive
protocol. A Berry holonomy without the response certificate is geometric
data, not yet physical CP violation. Naming it as CKM or PMNS additionally
requires the corresponding accepted full-matrix, diagonalizer, rephasing,
label, matching, and residual record inside the common structurally independent
$\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{fl}}$.

<a id="theorem-k615-strong-sector-type-i-gate"></a>**Theorem K.6.15 (Strong-Sector Type I Gate).** Under all five hypotheses of Theorem K.6.11, with the gauge and full-mass determinant records expressed in one common chiral convention, the strong-sector Type I class vanishes.

*Proof.* Theorem K.6.11 gives the invariant statement $z_{\mathrm{CP}}=1$, so the absolute Type I class of Definition K.6.13 is trivial. Positive magnitude data alone do not establish the result. ∎

<a id="theorem-k616-real-locus-kähler-holonomy-constraint"></a>**Theorem K.6.16 (Real-Locus Kähler-Holonomy Constraint).** The invariant locus $\operatorname{Gr}(2,8)^\sigma$ is Lagrangian. Consequently, if a contractible loop $\gamma$ bounds a surface $\Sigma$ contained in that locus and the Berry curvature is the restricted Kähler form, then
$$
\int_\Sigma\omega_{KE}=0.
$$
A nonzero continuous curvature holonomy therefore requires a certified relative loop or spanning surface that is not contained in the real locus. A flat topological holonomy not represented by the curvature integral requires its own bundle certificate.

*Proof.* At a point of the invariant locus, every tangent vector $X$ satisfies $d\sigma(X)=X$. Since $\sigma^*\omega_{KE}=-\omega_{KE}$,
$$
\omega_{KE}(X,Y)
=\omega_{KE}(d\sigma X,d\sigma Y)
=-\omega_{KE}(X,Y),
$$
so $\omega_{KE}(X,Y)=0$ for all tangent $X,Y$. Proposition K.6.5 gives real dimension $12$, half the ambient real dimension $24$, hence the invariant locus is Lagrangian. The curvature integral over any surface contained in it vanishes. ∎

<a id="theorem-k617-certificate-gated-type-classification"></a>**Theorem K.6.17 (Certificate-Gated Type Classification).** Under all five hypotheses of Theorem K.6.11:

- **Type I** strong-sector phases vanish.
- **Type II** phases are permitted only when a retained response branch supplies a nontrivial relative determinant-line or Berry-loop certificate whose holonomy obeys the declared $\sigma$/CP transformation law and changes a retained CP-sensitive protocol. On a flavor branch, naming the phase as CKM or PMNS additionally requires the corresponding full flavor record satisfying Definition T.79.4. A continuous Kähler-curvature realization must satisfy the off-real-locus condition of Theorem K.6.16.

*Proof.* Theorem K.6.11 gives $z_{\mathrm{CP}}=1$, so the Type-I conclusion follows invariantly. For Type II, a connection and loop define
$$
\delta=\arg\operatorname{Hol}_\gamma(\mathcal A_B)
$$

only after the bundle, connection, and loop are specified. Nonzero holonomy plus the response condition makes that relative phase physical. Theorem K.6.16 excludes a nonzero continuous Kähler-curvature integral for a spanning surface wholly inside the real locus, so the stated additional certificate is necessary. ∎

This is an absence from the branch's assumed field content, not a derivation that QCD axions do not exist. Detection of an axion would refute this branch only if an independent completeness theorem identified the branch as exhaustive of the physical field content; no such theorem is supplied here.

Retain the full total-charge Coulomb form, its fermion/probe cross terms, the smooth charged clutch and every allowed particle-number sector. For every $q\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ and every native mass matrix in these boxes, $H_{\mathrm{fib}}(q)$ has a unique ground and spectral gap at least $Q/200$. The ground has particle number $432$ and probe singlet character, as conclusions of the full sector comparison.

This is an instantaneous fiber statement. The quantum-$q$ kinetic term of Definition K.6.6e is not part of $H_{\mathrm{fib}}$. The physical scalar $E_{\mathrm{sea}}(q)+E_{\mathrm{base}}$ remains in its energy and source responses.

**Part I. Exact compression and all-sector complement.** Let $P$ be the negative one-particle projector and $\Omega$ its occupied Slater determinant. The constant spin involution $\Gamma=i\beta_D\gamma_5$ of Definition K.6.6e (W2) anticommutes with $h_W$ and commutes with $|h_W|$. Hence the partial spin trace of $h_W|h_W|^{-1}$ vanishes, and $P=(I-h_W|h_W|^{-1})/2$ obeys $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{spin}}P=2I$ on site/color/flavor coordinates. In particular the local spin/flavor trace is $18I_3$. Consequently
$$
 \langle\Omega,d\Gamma(j_a)\Omega\rangle=\operatorname{Tr}(Pj_a)=0
\tag{K.6.6q.2}
$$
for every local traceless color charge, including the stabilizer directions. This identity is covariant under the actual sitewise gauge frames.

The free physical cluster is $\Omega\otimes\operatorname{End}(\mathbb C^3)^H$, of rank three. The singlet and adjoint probe representations are exact reducing sectors of the full Hamiltonian. Constant-Cartan invariance makes the three color occupation numbers equal after an integral probe-root shift; that shift has zero total. Every allowed fermion number is therefore divisible by three. The sea has $144$ occupied modes per color. At $\phi=0$ the one-particle gap exceeds $\mu=Q/4$. A non-sea state at number $432$ needs a particle and a hole; every other allowed number differs by at least three. Hence, after subtracting $E_{\mathrm{sea}}$ for spectral comparison, the complete free complement is bounded below by
$$
 g=Q/2.
\tag{K.6.6q.3}
$$
Compensated off-diagonal probe states are included in that complement. Positivity of the full Coulomb operator preserves its lower bound.

Whiten the real inverse Gauss form $G=M_q^{-1}|_{\mathfrak h^\perp}$, and write $x_a$ for the whitened one-particle color charges and $Y_a$ for the corresponding probe charges. Put $\bar P=I-P$ and
$$
 A_a=Px_aP,\quad D_a=\bar Px_a\bar P,\quad B_a=\bar Px_aP,\quad
 K=\sum_a(D_aB_a-B_aA_a),\quad S_{ab}=\operatorname{Tr}(B_a^*B_b),
$$
$$
 \kappa=\pi\rho Q/24,\qquad e=\kappa\operatorname{Tr}S,\quad
 k=\kappa\|K\|_{\mathrm{HS}},\quad w=\kappa\|S\|.
\tag{K.6.6q.4}
$$
The nine-flavor sum is inside $S$ and the direct-sum one-hole norm. The full Coulomb form is $\kappa\sum_a[d\Gamma(x_a)+Y_a]^2$. Wick expansion, followed by (K.6.6q.2), gives its cluster compression $eI+C_p$, where $C_p=\kappa\sum_aY_a^2$ on the diagonal probe space. The probe identity is its zero eigenvector. The two positive eigenvalues are those of the actual co-located color Green function in Definition K.6.6c (N3); its bounds give
$$
 \gamma_p\ge\frac{3\pi\rho Q}{56}>\frac{471Q}{16000},\qquad
 \lambda_p\le\frac{9\pi\rho Q}{112}<\frac{99Q}{2240}.
\tag{K.6.6q.5}
$$
Here $G_0(s)=6(28-s)/(s^2-88s+784)$ lies between $3/14$ and $9/28$ on $0\le s\le4$, and the compressed eigenvalues are $0$, $3c_{\mathrm{col}}G_0(2+2\cos2\pi q)$ and $c_{\mathrm{col}}[G_0(2+2\cos2\pi q)+2G_0(4\cos^22\pi q)]$, with $c_{\mathrm{col}}=\pi\rho Q/12$.

The orthogonal one-hole and two-hole amplitudes in $\sum_ad\Gamma(x_a)^2\Omega$ are $K$ and
$$
 T_{rs,ij}=2\sum_a[(B_a)_{ri}(B_a)_{sj}-(B_a)_{rj}(B_a)_{si}],\qquad r<s,\ i<j.
$$
The exact full cluster leakage Gram is
$$
 \kappa^2\left[(\|K\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2+\|T\|^2)I
 +4\sum_{a,b}S_{ab}P_HY_aY_bP_H\right].
\tag{K.6.6q.6}
$$
This is obtained by expanding both Coulomb factors before projecting the final probe output. In particular $P_HY_aY_bP_H$ is retained even when $P_HY_aP_H=0$.

For the normalized antisymmetric embeddings $W_{\mathrm{in}},W_{\mathrm{out}}$,
$W_{\mathrm{out}}^*(\sum_aB_a\otimes B_a)W_{\mathrm{in}}=T/2$. Therefore
$$
 \|T\|^2\le4\operatorname{Tr}(S\overline S)
 \le4\|S\|\operatorname{Tr}S,\qquad \kappa^2\|T\|^2\le4we.
\tag{K.6.6q.7}
$$
The first contraction contains complex squares, not absolute squares. Positivity of $S,\overline S$ proves the second inequality. On this source $S$ is real: cyclicity gives $S_{ab}-S_{ba}=\operatorname{Tr}P[x_a,x_b]=0$ by (K.6.6q.2). This reality property is not imposed on arbitrary weak or chiral insertions. The adjoint leakage is consequently bounded by $k^2I+4w(eI+C_p)$, with all cross-flavor two-hole terms retained.

**Part II. Sufficient uniform caps and the exact Schur margin.** Suppose
$$
 e<Q/10,\qquad k<13Q/200,\qquad w<3Q/500.
\tag{K.6.6q.8}

The singlet trial energy is $e$ and its second eigenvalue is at least $g$. At comparison energy $e+Q/200$, the full adjoint complementary denominator is at least $(79/200)Q$. Its Schur lower margin is bounded below, in units $Q$, by

 \frac{471}{16000}-\frac1{200}
 -\frac{(13/200)^2+4(3/500)(1/10+99/2240)}{79/200}
 =\frac{44063}{8848000}>0.

The adjoint sector has no energy at or below $e+Q/200$, whereas the singlet ground is at most $e$. Min–max and this exact finite-dimensional Schur comparison prove the stated full physical gap. No small norm of the whole Coulomb operator is required.

**Part III. Actual rational nodes and finite certificates.** Fix $L=192$ and

 q_j=\frac2\pi\arctan(j/192),\quad

At each node the three site links are, for $n\in\{0,1\}^3$ and $b=(1,-1,0)$,

 U_1(n)=\operatorname{diag}_c(-1)^{b_cn_1n_2},\quad

Use $\beta=\sigma_3\otimes I_2$, $\alpha_i=\sigma_1\otimes\sigma_i$ in the equivalent spin frame $\gamma_i=-i\beta\alpha_i$. The $64$-coordinate Gauss matrix is reconstructed from every link by $M=D^*D$. Its two constant-Cartan null directions are retained through
$G=(M+N)^{-1}-N$, with $N$ their orthogonal projector. The exact identities $MG=GM=I-N$ and $GN=0$ specify the inverse without numerical spectral data.

For comparison, a rational approximate eigenframe $V$, diagonal ordered Ritz matrix $E$ and Hermitian approximate projector $\widetilde P$ obey the following residual bound. For an actual mass box include its maximum representative-to-endpoint deviation $d_m$. Frobenius upper bounds give:
$$
 g_V=\|V^*V-I\|_{\mathrm{HS}},\quad r=\|h_{\mathrm{rep}}V-VE\|_{\mathrm{HS}},\quad

$$
 d_P=\|V_-V_-^*-\widetilde P\|_{\mathrm{HS}},\quad

\tag{K.6.6q.12}

These formulas are dimensionless in units $Q$. Under the stated residual inequalities, $\delta_P$ bounds the operator norm $\|P-\widetilde P\|$. The quantities $g_V,r,d_P$ in (K.6.6q.12) use Hilbert–Schmidt norm, while $d_m$ is a mass operator-norm deviation. The signs are $48$ negative and $48$ positive; $g_V<1/4$, $\|E\|<3$, $\varepsilon<\gamma_R/2$, and $\widetilde P=\widetilde P^*$ are the required residual hypotheses. The source and representative norms are below $3$, since $0<m<1$ and $1+9\rho<3$. Polar normalization of $V$ and the Hermitian straight-line interpolation to the true matrix give the first term in $\delta_P$ by the gapped off-diagonal Sylvester formula; the remaining $5g_V+d_P$ bounds replacement of the polar negative projector by $\widetilde P$. Thus (K.6.6q.12) controls the entire native box, not its midpoint alone.

For unnormalized Gell-Mann numerators $\lambda_a$ with $n_a=\operatorname{Tr}\lambda_a^2=(2,2,2,2,2,2,2,6)$, the complete CP map is
$$
 \mathcal L_G(X)=\sum_{a,b}\frac{G_{ab}}{n_a}\lambda_aX\lambda_b,
 \qquad\|\mathcal L_G\|=\|\mathcal L_G(I)\|\le8/3.
\tag{K.6.6q.13}
$$
Site and spin indices are retained in the finite sums of Part VI. Only matched normalizations occur at nonzero $G_{ab}$. The bound follows from $G\le I$ and $\sum_a\lambda_a^2/n_a=(8/3)I$. It controls the exact rational evaluations
$$
 e/\kappa=\sum_f\operatorname{Tr}[P_f\mathcal L_G(I)-P_f\mathcal L_G(P_f)],\qquad
 K_f=(I-P_f)[\mathcal L_G(I)-2\mathcal L_G(P_f)]P_f.
$$
With $\delta=10^{-7}$ and $s_0=8/3$, each block's errors are bounded by

 |\Delta e_f/\kappa|\le96\delta s_0(3+\delta),\qquad
 \|\Delta K_f\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\le10\delta s_0(8+7\delta+2\delta^2).
\tag{K.6.6q.14}
$$
These follow by expanding every changed projector and the middle CP factor; $\sqrt{96}<10$. Multiplicities enter before the variance sum and squared one-hole sum. A conservative sum of the error norms is then added. Use the exact bound $\kappa/Q<11/480$.

The unwhitened full charge covariance is $C_{ab}=\sum_f\operatorname{Tr}[P_fj_a(I-P_f)j_b]$. For any real unit coefficient vector $u$, one flavor has $\|j(u)\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2=4$. Expanding its quadratic form gives
$$
 \|C-\widetilde C\|\le36\delta(3+\delta)=\frac{270000009}{25000000000000}=:\epsilon_C.
$$
Let $\widehat C$ be the integer covariance numerator produced from the rational approximate projectors and define $\widetilde C_{\mathrm{unnormalized}}=\widehat C/\mathsf s^2$. Writing $D_n=\operatorname{diag}(n_a)$ in all $64$ coordinates, the exact positive comparison is

 \frac{47997029999901}{275000000000000}D_n(M+N)-\widetilde C_{\mathrm{unnormalized}}>0,
\tag{K.6.6q.15}

with the rounded covariance divided by $\mathsf s^2$. Its threshold equals $(1/250)/(11/480)-\epsilon_C$. All off-block entries vanish; the three real root-pair blocks and the full two-Cartan block have size $16$ each. Rational LDL identities with positive pivots, or equivalently positive fraction-free leading minors, certify positivity. Congruence by $D_n^{-1/2}$ and $M\ge I$ on $\mathfrak h^\perp$ absorb $\epsilon_C$ and give $w<Q/250$. The null-coordinate comparison is a strengthening; the physical inverse remains on $\mathfrak h^\perp$.

For each of the $193$ nodes the finite inequalities of Part VI give

 e_j<9Q/100,\qquad k_j<9Q/200,\qquad w_j<Q/250.

Uniform rational upper bounds for the first two quantities, in units $Q$, are

**Part IV. Full-source reflection.** At $q'=1-q$, $z'=-\overline z$. With the actual magnetic frame and charged clutch put
$$
 f(n)=\operatorname{diag}_c(-1)^{b_cn_1n_2+e_cn_3},\qquad e=(0,1,-1),\qquad
 \mathcal U=i\alpha_3\otimes f.
$$
Direct substitution of (K.6.6q.11), including its spatial seam, gives
$$
 h(q',M_E^T)=-\mathcal U h(q,M_E)^T\mathcal U^*,\qquad
 P(q',M_E^T)=I-\mathcal U P(q,M_E)^T\mathcal U^*.
\tag{K.6.6q.18}
$$
For a real color-root pair $(c,d)$, the adjoint-frame signs are $(-f_cf_d,+f_cf_d)$; both Cartan signs are $-1$. The resulting real orthogonal $O$ gives $M(q')=OM(q)O^T$, $G(q')=OG(q)O^T$, and transforms every local charge by

j'_a=-\mathcal U(\sum_bO_{ab}j_b)^T\mathcal U^*.

The occupied and empty spaces exchange; the whitened particle-hole amplitudes and one-hole map transform as $B'_a=-\mathcal U B_a^T\mathcal U^*$ and $K'=-\mathcal U K^T\mathcal U^*$. Transpose preserves the complex Hilbert–Schmidt inner product, so the full Gram is orthogonally conjugate and $e,k,w$ are unchanged.

The particle-hole lift on Fock space is $d\Gamma(A)\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}A-d\Gamma(\mathcal U A^T\mathcal U^*)$, with its trace retained. This proves reflection of the complete source-domain certificate; omitting the mass transpose for nonreal Hermitian native masses would be incorrect. It does not identify arbitrary fixed weak-source insertions by CP or infer the smooth clutch from finite-site topology.

**Part V. Continuous propagation between certified nodes.** The full root characteristic polynomials in Definition K.6.6c (N1) have eigenvalue pairs $a+t,a-t$ with $a>2$, $|t|\le2$. Their reciprocal sum increases with $|t|$. Its endpoint traces are $57/28$ for each complex $|d_b|=1$ block and $18/7$ for $|d_b|=2$. Counting both real root partners and both Cartans gives

 \operatorname{Tr}G\le2[2(57/28)+18/7]+29/12=1319/84<16,\qquad G\le I.

For a nearby lifted point set $x=|q-q_0|$, $d=4\pi x<1$, $\beta=(1-d)^{-1}$ and $\epsilon=\beta-1$. The inverse-Gauss order is

(1+d)^{-1}G_0\le G(q)\le\beta G_0,

because $M\ge I$, $\|M'\|\le4\pi$. Fixed native masses have heavy one-particle gap above $Q/4$ and light gap above $7Q/10$. The Sylvester derivative estimate $\|P_f'\|\le\|h_f'\|/(2m_f)$ and $\|h_f'\|\le\pi E_a$ give

 \delta_h=(11/10)x,\qquad\delta_l=(11/28)x,\qquad

At fixed metric $G_0$,
$(I-P_1)x_aP_1-(I-P_0)x_aP_0=(I-P_1)x_a(P_1-P_0)-(P_1-P_0)x_aP_0$.
The full tuple changes in Hilbert–Schmidt norm by at most $4\sqrt{\operatorname{Tr}G_0}D<16D$. Combining the node cap with $\sqrt{\kappa/Q}<4/25$ gives

 \overline e/Q\le[3/10+(704/125)x]^2,\qquad e(q)\le\beta\overline e.

For $K_G(P)=(I-P)[\mathcal L_G(I)-2\mathcal L_G(P)]P$, the middle factor has norm at most $s_0$. Expanding its endpoints and middle factor gives per flavor
$\|K_G(P_1)-K_G(P_0)\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\le4\sqrt{96}s_0\delta_f$. Thus
$\overline k/Q\le9/200+(242/45)x$. For the metric change write $G-G_0=G_0^{1/2}EG_0^{1/2}$ with $\|E\|\le\epsilon$. Its exact signed-map change is

\sum_{a,b}E_{ab}(D_aB_b-B_aA_b).

The $A,D$ tuple row/column norms are at most $\sqrt{s_0}$ and the $B$ tuple norm is $\sqrt{\overline e/\kappa}$, so

 |k-\overline k|\le2\epsilon\sqrt{\kappa s_0\overline e},\qquad
 k/Q<9/200+(242/45)x+(4/25)\epsilon
\tag{K.6.6q.22}

when $\overline e<Q/10$. This treats $K$ as a signed map, not an ordered energy. For $w$, a unit coefficient charge has one-flavor Hilbert–Schmidt norm at most $2$. Its particle-hole map changes by at most $4D$, giving

 \overline w/Q<[8/125+(176/125)x]^2,\qquad w(q)\le\beta\overline w.
\tag{K.6.6q.23}

The last inequality follows on the common particle-hole output space from $G(q)\le\beta G_0$, without identifying different square-root frames.

The direct and reflected nodes give $385$ lifted points on $[0,1]$, or $384$ positions after the charged seam identification. Since $|\arctan'|\le1$, every circle point is within
$x\le1/(192\pi)<25/15072$ of a node. At the latter rational endpoint, with $\pi<22/7$, (K.6.6q.21)–(K.6.6q.23) give exactly

 e/Q<\frac{14859943}{152050575}<1/10,\qquad

The intermediate $\overline e<Q/10$ and $1-d>0$ hold before their use. Hence (K.6.6q.8) holds continuously, and Part II proves the theorem.

**Part VI. Finite rational spectral calculation.** The source matrices and the following recurrences determine the finite calculation without eigenvector data.

For a lifted node $j$, let $\mathcal X=\{0,1\}^3$, in lexicographic order, and let $T_i$ act on $\mathbb C^{\mathcal X}\otimes\mathbb C^3$ by
$$
 (T_i\psi)(n)=U_i(n)\psi(n+e_i),
$$
where addition in $\mathcal X$ is modulo two and the links are (K.6.6q.11). In the spin-first order, the dimensionless one-flavor matrix is
$$
 h_{j,m}=\beta\otimes(m+3\rho)I_{24}
 +\frac\rho2\sum_{i=1}^3
 \left[\alpha_i\otimes\frac{T_i-T_i^*}{i}
       -\beta\otimes(T_i+T_i^*)\right].
$$
Here $m$ is the mass divided by $Q$, $\rho=7/40$, $\beta=\sigma_3\otimes I_2$ and $\alpha_i=\sigma_1\otimes\sigma_i$. The Pauli matrices have their usual entries $0,\pm1,\pm i$. The links are unitary, hence
$$
 \|h_{j,m}\|\le m+9\rho<1+\frac{63}{40}<3.
$$
This norm bound holds in all six boxes, with either sign of the mass term. On the positive branch write $h=\beta(m+W)+\sum_i\alpha_iP_i$, where $W=(\rho/2)\sum_i(2I-T_i-T_i^*)\succeq0$ and $P_i=(\rho/2i)(T_i-T_i^*)$ is Hermitian. Since $\beta\alpha_iP_i$ is skew-adjoint,
$$
 \operatorname{Re}\langle\psi,\beta h\psi\rangle
 =m\|\psi\|^2+\langle\psi,W\psi\rangle\ge m\|\psi\|^2.
$$
Cauchy–Schwarz gives $\|h\psi\|\ge m\|\psi\|$. Every positive mass box has $m>1/4$, proving the required gap from the source itself.

The normalized color basis is $\lambda_a/\sqrt{n_a}$, where the three symmetric and antisymmetric off-diagonal pairs are ordered $(1,2),(1,3),(2,3)$, followed by
$$
 \lambda_7=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,0),\qquad
 \lambda_8=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,-2),\qquad
 (n_1,\ldots,n_8)=(2,2,2,2,2,2,2,6).
$$
For every oriented link $(n,i)$ form the row map
$$
 (D_{n,i}v)=v_n-\operatorname{Ad}_{U_i(n)}v_{n+e_i},
 \qquad M=\sum_{n\in\mathcal X}\sum_{i=1}^3D_{n,i}^*D_{n,i}.
$$
Both orientations are included by this sum. Let $N$ be the orthogonal projection onto the two constant Cartan vectors; its entries are $1/8$ between equal Cartan coordinates at any two sites and zero otherwise. Thus
$$
 G=(M+N)^{-1}-N.
$$
All these entries are rational at (K.6.6q.10). The identities $MG=GM=I-N$ and $GN=0$ follow by multiplication. They retain the full $64$-coordinate form, including its two null directions.

**Spectral projection by a rational recurrence.** For a Hermitian rational matrix $h$ with $\gamma I\le |h|\le3I$, set
$$
 X_0=h/3,\qquad X_{n+1}=\tfrac12(X_n+X_n^{-1}),
 \qquad P_n=\tfrac12(I-X_n).
$$
Every inverse exists. For $n\ge1$, scalar diagonalization gives, with $u=|\lambda|/3$ and $a=(1-u)/(1+u)$,
$$
 x_n(\lambda)=\operatorname{sgn}(\lambda)
 \frac{1+a^{2^n}}{1-a^{2^n}},\qquad
 \|P_n-1_{(-\infty,0)}(h)\|
 \le\frac{r^{2^n}}{1-r^{2^n}},\qquad
 r=\frac{3-\gamma}{3+\gamma}.
$$
Indeed $(x+x^{-1})/2$ squares the Cayley parameter, proving the identity by induction. For $\gamma=1/4$, $n=9$ makes the displayed error less than $2^{-100}$. The inequality follows, for example, from $r=11/13$, $\log(13/11)>1/6$ and $\log2<7/10$. This proof is uniform over the positive-mass source boxes.

Rational inverses and determinants in this calculation can be generated by the same fraction-free recurrence. For a matrix $A^{(0)}=A$ put $p_{-1}=1$ and, after a simultaneous row and column permutation when needed,
$$
 A^{(k+1)}_{ij}
 =\frac{A^{(k)}_{kk}A^{(k)}_{ij}-A^{(k)}_{ik}A^{(k)}_{kj}}{p_{k-1}},
 \quad i,j>k,\qquad p_k=A^{(k)}_{kk}.
$$
Zero pivots are bypassed by the first available nonzero pivot; if no pivot exists, the determinant is zero. Adjugate cofactors divided by the determinant give the inverse. The recurrence is the two-by-two determinant identity applied to successive Schur complements, so it is exact over the rationals. No approximate eigenvector is an input.

To obtain rational matrix intervals, round the real and imaginary parts of $P_n$ to the nearest multiple of $1/\mathsf s$, retaining Hermitian symmetry and the exact color blocks. On a diagonal use real rounding; on an upper-triangular entry round both components and reflect by conjugation. Ties use the even integer. The Frobenius error of this operation is at most $96/\mathsf s$. With $\mathsf s=2^{40}d$ and $n=9$, its operator error, together with the spectral error above, is bounded by
$$
 \delta_0=\frac{96}{2^{40}d}+2^{-100}.
$$
For a representative $m_0$ of a mass interval, add its actual mass deviation $d_m$. The gapped Sylvester integral gives
$$
 \|P(m)-P(m_0)\|
 \le\frac{d_m}{2(\gamma_0-d_m)},\qquad
 \gamma_0\le\min|\operatorname{spec}h_{j,m_0}|,
$$
whenever $d_m<\gamma_0$. This follows by differentiating the two spectral blocks and integrating $\int_0^\infty e^{-t|h_-|}B e^{-t|h_+|}\,dt$ along the mass segment. Thus the common allowance $\delta=10^{-7}$ in (K.6.6q.14) dominates both rounding and every stated mass-box error. The finite interval calculation below uses the exact rational midpoint of each box of Theorem K.6.6d. Rounding is applied only to intermediate evaluation matrices, with the displayed error bounds.

**Exact CP and covariance contractions.** In the $96$-coordinate space let
$$
 J_{n,a}=I_4\otimes|n\rangle\langle n|\otimes\lambda_a.
$$
The full CP map is the finite sum
$$
 \mathcal L_G(A)=\sum_{n,a,m,b}\frac{G_{(n,a),(m,b)}}{n_a}
 J_{n,a}A J_{m,b}.
$$
Every nonzero coefficient has $n_a=n_b$. The identities $0\le G\le I$ and $\sum_a\lambda_a^2/n_a=(8/3)I$ prove $\|\mathcal L_G\|\le8/3$. For a rational approximation $\widehat P_f$, form
$$
 v_f=\operatorname{Tr}[\widehat P_f\mathcal L_G(I)
               -\widehat P_f\mathcal L_G(\widehat P_f)],\qquad
 K_f=(I-\widehat P_f)[\mathcal L_G(I)-2\mathcal L_G(\widehat P_f)]\widehat P_f,
$$
$$
 C_{ab}=\sum_{f=1}^6\nu_f\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}
 [\widehat P_fJ_a(I-\widehat P_f)J_b],
 \qquad(\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_6)=(2,2,2,1,1,1).
$$
These are finite rational sums. Apply (K.6.6q.14) before the multiplicity sum, and bound the square root of the summed one-hole squared norms by the next $10^{-12}$-rational. More explicitly, for $z=A/B\ge0$ use
$$
 \sqrt z\le10^{-12}\left\lceil\sqrt{\left\lceil10^{24}A/B\right\rceil}\right\rceil.
$$
The elementary integer-square-root inequalities prove this bound. The covariance error is (K.6.6q.15), with its full null-coordinate strengthening.

For each of the three real root-pair blocks and the two-Cartan block, retain all $16$ coordinates in their natural site-first order. A real symmetric block $T$ is positive exactly when its leading principal minors are positive. Equivalently its rational $LDL^{\mathsf T}$ recurrence is
$$
 d_i=T_{ii}-\sum_{k<i}\ell_{ik}^2d_k,\qquad
 \ell_{ji}=\frac{T_{ji}-\sum_{k<i}\ell_{jk}\ell_{ik}d_k}{d_i},\quad j>i,
$$
with unit diagonal in $L$. Induction gives $T=LDL^{\mathsf T}$; positive $d_i$ then proves the required positive quadratic form. This is a criterion for the complete blocks, rather than a sampled set of charge directions.

**Reduced finite evaluation and error propagation.** Color is an exact reducing label. Within each color, order third-site parity as even and odd. Equal diagonal and equal off-diagonal parity blocks give their two normalized sum/difference blocks. Each is $16$ dimensional and has the form
$$
 h_{c,\pm}=\begin{pmatrix}M&D\\D&-M\end{pmatrix},\qquad M=M^*,\quad D=D^*.

All six blocks are retained, including the $q$-dependent third color. For $A=M+iD$, a fixed unitary changes this block to $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&A^*\\A&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Thus the full rational sign recurrence is equivalent to
$$
 A_0=A/3,\quad A_{k+1}=\tfrac12[A_k+(A_k^*)^{-1}],\quad
 M_k=(A_k+A_k^*)/2,\quad D_k=(A_k-A_k^*)/(2i).
$$
Reassemble $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}M_k&D_k\\D_k&-M_k\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, take its negative projector and undo the fixed parity transform. The resulting matrix is exactly the $96$-dimensional sign iterate above.

Here is a rational interval rule to evaluate it. For a rational approximate inverse $R$ of a rational matrix $Z$, let $\eta=\|I-ZR\|_{\mathrm{HS}}<1$. The geometric series for $(I-(I-ZR))^{-1}$ gives
$$

If the current approximation error from the ideal iterate is $d<a$, where the ideal least singular value is at least $a$, the inverse difference identity gives the next error bound
$$
 d'\le\frac d2\left(1+\frac1{a(a-d)}\right)

The final term bounds dyadic entry rounding of an $8\times8$ complex matrix. Frobenius norms use the integer-square-root ceiling, so every error bound is rational. With $S=2^{48}$, initial error $16/S$, $a=1/12$ at the first step and $a=1$ thereafter, nine steps give, including the actual mass-box half-widths,
$$
 \delta_{\mathrm{circ}}\le
 \frac{875624737601}{200000000000000000000000}<10^{-9}.
$$
For finite interval evaluation use each exact box midpoint; the half-width is propagated by the Sylvester bound. The exact rational recurrence requires no rounding and is enclosed by the same intervals.

Strengthen (K.6.6q.15) by subtracting $10^{-6}D_n$. The four generated $16\times16$ blocks have all their leading principal minors positive. Replacing a certified projector by its ideal sign iterate changes the normalized covariance by at most

$$
so the strict reserve proves the comparison for the ideal rational iterate and its exact spectral limit. Expanding the finite CP and charge-covariance sums gives equal energy contractions at each node.

<a id="corollary-k66r-global-ground-graph-and-same-source-response-bounds"></a>**Corollary K.6.6r (Global Ground Graph and Same-Source Response Bounds).** Under Theorem K.6.6q, let $P_0(q)$ be the free-sea/probe-identity line and $P_g(q)$ the actual ground line.  \|b\|^2\le k^2+4we<53Q^2/8000.

$$
 \psi=\frac{(\psi_0,v)}{\sqrt{1+\|v\|^2}},\quad
 v=-(D-E)^{-1}b\psi_0,\quad E=e-b^*(D-E)^{-1}b.
\tag{K.6.6r.2}
$$
Since $D-E>(2Q/5)I$,
$$
 \|v\|^2<53/1280,\quad\operatorname{Tr}(P_gP_0)>1280/1333>24/25,
$$
$$
 \|P_g-P_0\|^2<53/1333<1/25,\qquad0\le e-E<53Q/3200.
\tag{K.6.6r.3}
$$
These follow immediately by applying the denominator bound to (K.6.6r.1). The nonzero Feshbach self-energy in (K.6.6r.2) is retained.

The intrinsic positive graph isometry and full direct rotation are
$$
 J=P_gP_0(P_0P_gP_0)^{-1/2},\qquad
 \mathcal W=[P_gP_0+(I-P_g)(I-P_0)]\,[I-(P_g-P_0)^2]^{-1/2}.
\tag{K.6.6r.4}
$$
Their denominators are uniformly positive, $J^*J=P_0$, $JJ^*=P_g$, and $\mathcal W$ is unitary with $\mathcal WP_0\mathcal W^*=P_g$. Spectral calculus in the two projections proves these identities and smoothness. Since the expressions are intrinsic, the actual charged clutch intertwines them. For a local normalized sea section $u$ the Berry connections satisfy

$$
\mathcal A_g=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{sea}}+u^*J^*(dJ)u;
$$

the correction is not set to zero. This line isomorphism alone supplies neither a Berry-holonomy value nor mass-phase-torus topology.

For the mathematical homotopy $H_0+tC_{\mathrm{tot}}$, $0<t\le1$, the singlet trial energy and leakage scale as $te,tb$. The adjoint splitting scales as $t\gamma_p$ and the squared leakage as $t^2[k^2+4w(e+\lambda_p)]$. For fixed actual native masses, put

 C_* =\kappa\,62\,866^2,\qquad B_1=288\pi E_a+4\pi C_*,\qquad
 B_2=288\pi^2E_a+40\pi^2C_*,\qquad\gamma=Q/200.

The identities $G'=-GM'G$ and $G''=2GM'GM'G-GM''G$, with $G\le I$, $\|M'\|\le4\pi$ and $\|M''\|\le4\pi^2$, bound the full Coulomb derivatives by $4\pi C_*$ and $40\pi^2C_*$. <a id="proposition-k66s-opposite-corner-barrier-for-the-free-complement-sea-trial-method"></a>**Proposition K.6.6s (Opposite-Corner Barrier for the Free-Complement Sea-Trial Method).** Keep the complete source of Definition K.6.6e, the nine native Hermitian mass matrices and all six boxes of Theorem K.6.6d, with multiplicities $(2,2,2,1,1,1)$. <a id="theorem-k7a-exact-homogeneous-ew6-saw1-convexity"></a>**Theorem K.7a (Exact Homogeneous EW6–SAW1 Convexity).** Fix the production mass $m=Q>0$, the Yukawa coefficient $y=1/10$, and the three-flavor source of Theorem T.78.14a. Let $V_{\mathrm{EW6}}$ be its complete zero-temperature, infinite-volume constant-Higgs potential-density envelope, including the prescribed reference action and the once-counted fermion determinant. Let $V_\theta$ be the complete production mean-action/work potential-density envelope of Theorem X.9.6h.5b for $\theta=(a_1,a_2,a_3)\in[1,2]^3$, with its fixed production references. Use $\hbar=c=1$ for the potential densities; restored physical densities and Hessians carry the common factor $(\hbar c)^{-3}$. Set the gauge source to zero, and write the raw doublet coordinates as
$$
H=(h_1+ih_2,h_3+ih_4),\qquad h\in\mathbb R^4,
\qquad \rho=|h|=|H|\le Q.
\tag{K.7a.1}
$$
The Hessian is taken in the Euclidean metric $\sum_{a=1}^4dh_a^2$. Define
$$
d=\frac{8991}{2000000\pi^2}>0.
\tag{K.7a.2}
$$
For either $V=V_{\mathrm{EW6}}$ or $V=V_\theta$, throughout this entire homogeneous source ball,
$$
\nabla_h^2V(h)\succeq(2+d)Q^2I_4,
\qquad
h\cdot\nabla_hV(h)\ge(2+d)Q^2|h|^2+4|h|^4.
\tag{K.7a.3}
$$
Hence $H=0$ is the unique stationary point and unique minimum on the closed ball. The statement uses the complete source potentials, including all higher powers of $H$. Under a constant positive field normalization $H_{\mathrm{can}}=\sqrt ZH$, the ball is $|H_{\mathrm{can}}|\le\sqrt ZQ$ and the Hessian lower bound is $(2+d)Q^2I_4/Z$.

*Proof.* Put $t=\rho/Q\in[0,1]$ and
$$
f(x)=x^4\left(\log x^2-\frac32\right).
$$
The exact potential (T.78.14a.D1), together with its fixed reference coefficients, gives
$$
\frac{V_{\mathrm{EW6}}(H)-V_{\mathrm{EW6}}(0)}{Q^4}
=t^2+t^4+E(t),
\qquad
E(t)=-\frac3{16\pi^2}
\left[f(1+yt)+f(1-yt)-2f(1)\right].
\tag{K.7a.4}
$$
Direct differentiation gives $f''(x)=4x^2(3\log x^2-1)$. For $9/10\le x\le11/10$, the inequalities $\log x^2\le\log(121/100)\le21/100$ and $x^2\ge81/100$ imply
$$
f''(x)\le-4\frac{81}{100}\frac{37}{100}
=-\frac{2997}{2500}.
$$
Consequently
$$
E''(t)=-\frac{3y^2}{16\pi^2}
\left[f''(1+yt)+f''(1-yt)\right]\ge d.
\tag{K.7a.5}
$$
Evenness gives $E'(0)=0$, so $E'(t)/t\ge d$ for $t>0$, with the continuous limiting value at zero. For a radial function $Q^4w(|h|/Q)$, the real Hessian eigenvalues are $Q^2w''(t)$ in the radial direction and $Q^2w'(t)/t$ in the three tangential directions. The reference $w(t)=t^2+t^4$ contributes respectively $Q^2(2+12t^2)$ and $Q^2(2+4t^2)$. This proves both inequalities in (K.7a.3) for EW6.

For SAW1 define its exact source functions
$$
f_\theta(s)=\sum_{j=1}^3a_je^{-js^2},\qquad
T_\theta(s)=\int_s^\infty f_\theta(v)\,dv,\qquad
I_\theta(s)=\int_s^\infty(v-s)f_\theta(v)\,dv,
\qquad G_\theta(z)=I_\theta((1+z)^2).
$$
Equation (X.9.6h.5b.C9) supplies the complete additional homogeneous potential:
$$
V_\theta(H)-V_\theta(0)
=V_{\mathrm{EW6}}(H)-V_{\mathrm{EW6}}(0)
+\frac{3Q^4}{4\pi^2}
\left[G_\theta(yt)+G_\theta(-yt)-2G_\theta(0)\right].
\tag{K.7a.6}
$$
The allocation in (X.9.6h.5b.C19) fixes this sum: at zero gauge field the gauge reference has zero Higgs-only derivative; at production mass $m=Q$ the log-mass reference has zero Higgs contribution; the diagnostic factor is parked with zero production Higgs derivative. Every retained Higgs term is therefore present in (K.7a.6).

For $s>0$,
$$
\int_s^\infty e^{-jv^2}\,dv
\le\frac1s\int_s^\infty ve^{-jv^2}\,dv
=\frac{e^{-js^2}}{2js}.
$$
Using $I_\theta'=-T_\theta$ and $I_\theta''=f_\theta$, with $s=(1+z)^2$, gives
$$
G_\theta''(z)
=-2T_\theta(s)+4sf_\theta(s)
\ge\sum_{j=1}^3a_je^{-js^2}\left(4s-\frac1{js}\right).
\tag{K.7a.7}
$$
For $|z|\le1/10$, one has $81/100\le s\le121/100$ and
$$
4s-\frac1{js}\ge\frac{81}{25}-\frac{100}{81}
=\frac{4061}{2025}>0.
$$
Thus $G_\theta''>0$ uniformly over the profile box. The paired function $G_\theta(yt)+G_\theta(-yt)-2G_\theta(0)$ is even, has zero first derivative at zero, and has positive second derivative. Its radial Hessian and outward radial force are nonnegative. Adding it preserves (K.7a.3).

Both source potentials have zero gradient at the origin. Integrating the Hessian along the segment from $0$ to $h$ also gives
$$
V(h)-V(0)\ge\left(1+\frac d2\right)Q^2|h|^2.
$$
The force inequality excludes every nonzero stationary point, and the energy inequality proves uniqueness of the minimum. Finally, the constant change of coordinates has inverse Jacobian $Z^{-1/2}I_4$, giving the stated canonical Hessian and transported domain. ∎

<a id="corollary-k7b-fixed-count-schur-join-obstruction-and-required-scalar-force"></a>**Corollary K.7b (Fixed-Count Schur-Join Obstruction and Required Scalar Force).** Retain a fixed recorded count $q=N_c/n\in[0,1]$ and the source coefficients $\lambda_T>0$, $\mu>0$ and $\kappa$ of Theorem Y.8a, proof component 6, subsection 4, and put $g=\kappa^2/\mu^2$. Consider the following explicit same-doublet trial: identify that component's raw $H_T$ with the raw $H$ of Theorem K.7a, use a common homogeneous potential-density normalization, and add the two complete scalar functionals while retaining their coefficients. The resulting trial potential is

where $C$ contains the Higgs-independent auxiliary determinant and constants. Then

\nabla_h^2V_{\mathrm{join}}\succeq

and

h\cdot\nabla_hV_{\mathrm{join}}(h)

+4(1+\lambda_T)|h|^4.

In particular, $gq\le Q^2$ gives a strictly positive Hessian margin of at least $dQ^2$, including equality. A nonzero stationary point on the source ball requires

gq>\left(1+\frac d2\right)Q^2.
\tag{K.7b.4}
$$
More generally, a differentiable scalar modification $\Delta V$ producing a nonzero stationary point $h_*$ of $V+\Delta V$ must satisfy
$$
h_*\cdot\nabla_h\Delta V(h_*)
\le-(2+d)Q^2|h_*|^2-4|h_*|^4.
\tag{K.7b.5}
$$

*Proof.* In the fixed-count homogeneous block of Y.8a, complete the actual auxiliary squares:
$$
\begin{aligned}
&\mu^2|S_j|^2-\frac{\kappa}{\sqrt n}n_j
(S_j^\dagger H+H^\dagger S_j)\\
&\qquad=\mu^2\left|S_j-\frac{\kappa n_j}{\sqrt n\mu^2}H\right|^2
-\frac{\kappa^2n_j^2}{n\mu^2}|H|^2.
\end{aligned}
$$
The retained bits satisfy $n_j^2=n_j$ and $\sum_jn_j=nq$. Their complete Gaussian operator is $-D_A^2+\mu^2$, whose determinant is Higgs-independent in this variation. The homogeneous Schur contribution is therefore exactly $-gq|H|^2$, giving (K.7b.1). The real Hessian of the additional quartic is positive semidefinite, and that of $-gq|h|^2$ is $-2gqI_4$. Equation (K.7a.3) proves (K.7b.2). Its radial-force form gives (K.7b.3). At the equality threshold in (K.7b.4), the last term of (K.7b.3) remains strictly positive for $h\ne0$; below that threshold the quadratic term is nonnegative as well. This proves the strict necessary condition. At a stationary point of $V+\Delta V$, substitute $\nabla\Delta V=-\nabla V$ into (K.7a.3) to obtain (K.7b.5). ∎

Theorems T.78.14a and X.9.6h.5b supply the fixed external-source coefficient functionals used here. Y.8a supplies its distinct reducing-support, fixed-count T scalar and the held Y background. <a id="corollary-k7c-finite-potential-stability-margin"></a>**Corollary K.7c (Finite-Potential Stability Margin).** For either envelope $V$ of Theorem K.7a, let a complete finite precursor have exact real homogeneous potential $V_r=V+R_r$ on the same raw ball. If its full residual satisfies
$$
\sup_{|h|\le Q}\|\nabla_h^2R_r(h)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\eta Q^2,\qquad \eta<2+d,
\tag{K.7c.1}
$$
then $V_r$ is strongly convex with margin $(2+d-\eta)Q^2$. Exact $\nabla V_r(0)=0$ makes the origin its unique stationary point and minimum. If instead $|\nabla V_r(0)|\le\delta$, every stationary point in the ball satisfies
$$
|h_*|\le\frac{\delta}{(2+d-\eta)Q^2}.
\tag{K.7c.2}
$$
A sufficient analytic certificate for (K.7c.1) is a holomorphic residual bounded in absolute value by the physical potential-density error $E$ on every complex coordinate polydisc of radius $b=Q/32$ centered at a real point of the ball. It gives
$$
\sup_{|h|\le Q}\|\nabla_h^2R_r(h)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\frac{5E}{b^2}=\frac{5120E}{Q^2}.
\tag{K.7c.3}
$$
Thus $E\le Q^4/10240$ gives a margin at least $(3/2+d)Q^2$.

*Proof.* Add the Hessian bounds. Integrating the resulting strong monotonicity inequality between $0$ and a stationary point gives
$$
(2+d-\eta)Q^2|h_*|^2
\le-h_*\cdot\nabla V_r(0)\le\delta|h_*|,
$$
which proves (K.7c.2); the zero-gradient case also gives the energy minimum by segment integration. Cauchy's formula bounds diagonal second derivatives by $2E/b^2$ and off-diagonal second derivatives by $E/b^2$. Each row has one diagonal and three off-diagonal entries, so its absolute sum is at most $5E/b^2$. The real Hessian is symmetric; its operator norm is bounded by this row sum, proving (K.7c.3). ∎

A finite application of K.7c requires the full-ball residual in (K.7c.1), including actual source, reference, counterterm and implementation errors. The zero-source jets (X.9.6h.5b.CJ1), (X.9.6h.5b.CJ8) and (X.9.6h.5b.CJ10) retain their stated domains; full-ball use requires recentered uniform bounds. ## K.9 Cosmology: Time-Varying Gravitational Coupling and Unified Dark Sector

**Puzzle:** Cosmological observations reveal accelerated expansion ($\sim 70$% dark energy) and structure formation governed by non-luminous matter ($\sim 25$% dark matter), yet the Standard Model contains no suitable candidates.

**PU Pathway:** The framework proposes a unified description where the late-time dark response is generated by the same PCE-driven relaxation mechanism that governs the galaxy-sector law modification of Appendix I, but applied to the homogeneous FLRW background. The vacuum parameter is supplied on an accepted Appendix U vacuum-realization branch, including Definition U.73e.6 and Theorem U.73f; the homogeneous response below is conditional on that supplied positive constant. The non-vacuum sector couples through a time-dependent effective factor.

<a id="proposition-k91-comoving-de-sitter-limit-of-the-effective-temperature"></a>**Proposition K.9.1 (Comoving de Sitter Limit of the Effective Temperature).** Assume that the additive-temperature model of Section N.3.2 applies to the registered de Sitter prediction channel, the exact de Sitter background supplies the Gibbons-Hawking bath, the comoving MPU aggregate is geodesic, and implementation-specific internal heating contributes no additional effect to that channel. Then the effective temperature entering the operational cost reduces to
$$
T_{\mathrm{eff}}^{\mathrm{cosmo}} = T_{dS} = \frac{\hbar c}{2\pi k_B}\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda}{3}}.
\tag{K.9.1}
$$

*Proof.* Section N.3.2 declares the additional model $T_{\mathrm{eff}}=T_{\mathrm{bath}}+T_U(a)$, with $T_U(a)=\hbar a/(2\pi c k_B)$. The geodesic comoving aggregate has $a=0$, so $T_U=0$. The stated background-bath identification gives $T_{\mathrm{bath}}=T_{dS}$, hence $T_{\mathrm{eff}}=T_{dS}$. Section N.3.3 treats internal heating through an implementation-specific heat-balance and prediction-channel overhead, rather than a universal additive temperature; that additional effect vanishes under the stated hypothesis. ∎

Below, the FLRW background equations are written in units $c=1$.

<a id="definition-k91a-non-vacuum-enthalpy-density"></a>**Definition K.9.1a (Non-Vacuum Enthalpy Density).** Write
$$
\rho_{nv}(t):=\rho_b(t)+\rho_r(t), \qquad p_{nv}(t):=p_r(t)=\frac{1}{3}\rho_r(t),
\tag{K.9.2}
$$
and define the homogeneous enthalpy density
$$
h_{nv}(t):=\rho_{nv}(t)+p_{nv}(t)=\rho_b(t)+\frac{4}{3}\rho_r(t).
\tag{K.9.3}
$$
For the same supplied constant $\Lambda>0$, define the vacuum density by:
$$
\rho_\Lambda:=\frac{\Lambda}{8\pi G_0}.
\tag{K.9.4}
$$

<a id="definition-k91b-cosmological-sparsity-variable"></a>**Definition K.9.1b (Cosmological Sparsity Variable).** For $h_{nv}(t)>0$ define
$$
s_{bg}(t):=\frac{\rho_\Lambda}{h_{nv}(t)},
\tag{K.9.5}
$$
and define $s_{bg}=+\infty$ on the exact de Sitter branch $h_{nv}=0$.

<a id="postulate-k92-single-scale-homogeneous-relaxation"></a>**Postulate K.9.2 (Single-Scale Homogeneous Relaxation).** Let
$$
u(s):=\frac{\Upsilon_G(s)-1}{A_c}, \qquad \Upsilon_G(t):=\frac{G_{\mathrm{eff}}(t)}{G_0},
\tag{K.9.6}
$$
where $A_c>0$ is the asymptotic homogeneous relaxation amplitude. The minimal one-scale PCE closure assumes
$$
\frac{du}{d(s^n)}=1-u, \qquad u(0)=0, \qquad n\ge 1.
\tag{K.9.7}
$$

<a id="theorem-k93-closed-time-varying-coupling-law"></a>**Theorem K.9.3 (Closed Time-Varying Coupling Law).** Under Postulate K.9.2, the effective background coupling is
$$
\Upsilon_G(t)=1+A_c\left[1-e^{-s_{bg}(t)^n}\right], \qquad G_{\mathrm{eff}}(t)=G_0\,\Upsilon_G(t).
\tag{K.9.8}
$$
Equivalently,
$$
G_{\mathrm{eff}}(t)=G_0\left[1+A_c\left(1-\exp\left[-\left(\frac{\rho_\Lambda}{\rho_b(t)+\frac{4}{3}\rho_r(t)}\right)^n\right]\right)\right].
\tag{K.9.9}
$$
This law satisfies
$$
G_{\mathrm{eff}}(t)\to G_0 \quad \text{as}\quad \rho_b+\frac{4}{3}\rho_r\to\infty,
\qquad
G_{\mathrm{eff}}(t)\to G_0(1+A_c) \quad \text{as}\quad \rho_b+\frac{4}{3}\rho_r\to 0.
\tag{K.9.10}
$$

*Proof.* The ODE (K.9.7) has the unique solution $u(s)=1-e^{-s^n}$. Substituting into (K.9.6) yields (K.9.8). Equation (K.9.9) follows from (K.9.3)-(K.9.5). The limits are immediate from $s_{bg}\to 0$ in the dense early universe and $s_{bg}\to\infty$ on the asymptotically de Sitter branch. ∎

<a id="corollary-k93a-time-derivative-of-the-coupling"></a>**Corollary K.9.3a (Time Derivative of the Coupling).** On an interval with $h_{nv}(t)>0$, if baryons and radiation satisfy the standard background continuity equations
$$
\dot\rho_b + 3H\rho_b = 0, \qquad \dot\rho_r + 4H\rho_r = 0,
\tag{K.9.11}
$$
then
$$
\dot s_{bg}
=
H\,s_{bg}\,
\frac{3\rho_b+\frac{16}{3}\rho_r}{\rho_b+\frac{4}{3}\rho_r},
\tag{K.9.12}
$$
and therefore
$$
\dot\Upsilon_G
=
A_c n\,e^{-s_{bg}^n}s_{bg}^{\,n}\,
H\,
\frac{3\rho_b+\frac{16}{3}\rho_r}{\rho_b+\frac{4}{3}\rho_r}.
\tag{K.9.13}
$$

*Proof.* Differentiate (K.9.5) and use (K.9.11). Differentiating (K.9.8) then yields (K.9.13). ∎

<a id="corollary-k93b-bianchi-consistent-effective-fluid-form-on-a-nonstationary-flrw-interval"></a>**Corollary K.9.3b (Bianchi-Consistent Effective-Fluid Form on a Nonstationary FLRW Interval).** On any time interval on which $H(t)\ne0$, the homogeneous background equations can be written as
$$
H^2 = \frac{8\pi G_0}{3}\left[\rho_\Lambda + \Upsilon_G(t)\rho_{nv}(t)\right] - \frac{k}{a^2},
\tag{K.9.14}
$$
$$
\dot H = -4\pi G_0\left[\Upsilon_G(t)h_{nv}(t) - \frac{\dot\Upsilon_G(t)}{3H}\rho_{nv}(t)\right] + \frac{k}{a^2}.
\tag{K.9.15}
$$
Equivalently, with
$$
\rho_{ad}(t):=\bigl(\Upsilon_G(t)-1\bigr)\rho_{nv}(t),
\qquad
p_{ad}(t):=\bigl(\Upsilon_G(t)-1\bigr)p_{nv}(t)-\frac{\dot\Upsilon_G(t)}{3H}\rho_{nv}(t),
\tag{K.9.16}
$$
the cosmological dynamics take the constant-$G_0$ form
$$
H^2 = \frac{8\pi G_0}{3}\left[\rho_\Lambda + \rho_{nv} + \rho_{ad}\right] - \frac{k}{a^2},
\tag{K.9.17}
$$
$$
\dot H = -4\pi G_0\left[\rho_{nv}+p_{nv}+\rho_{ad}+p_{ad}\right] + \frac{k}{a^2},
\tag{K.9.18}
$$
and the adaptive sector is conserved:
$$
\dot\rho_{ad} + 3H\bigl(\rho_{ad}+p_{ad}\bigr)=0.
\tag{K.9.19}
$$

*Proof.* Differentiate (K.9.14) and use the continuity equations (K.9.11) together with (K.9.13) to obtain (K.9.15). The definitions in (K.9.16) convert (K.9.14)-(K.9.15) to the constant-$G_0$ form (K.9.17)-(K.9.18). A direct substitution shows (K.9.19). ∎

<a id="remark-k93b1-de-sitter-consistency"></a>**Remark K.9.3b.1 (de Sitter consistency).** On the exact de Sitter branch with nonnegative baryon and radiation densities, $h_{nv}=0$ implies $\rho_{nv}=0$. The endpoint convention $s_{bg}=+\infty$ gives $\Upsilon_G=1+A_c$ and $\dot\Upsilon_G=0$. On the $H\ne0$ intervals of Corollary K.9.3b the adaptive sector vanishes, and (K.9.14) becomes $H^2=\Lambda/3-k/a^2$. Thus $H^2=\Lambda/3$ on the spatially flat branch, and $H^2\to\Lambda/3$ along an expanding limit with $a\to\infty$.

<a id="remark-k93b2-relation-to-appendix-i"></a>**Remark K.9.3b.2 (Relation to Appendix I).** Appendix I uses the same saturating exponential response for quasistatic spatial sparsity, with the environmental proxy written as $R/L_0$. The present section is the homogeneous FLRW analogue, with the non-vacuum enthalpy density $h_{nv}$ supplying the covariant background sparsity variable instead of a radial coordinate.

<a id="corollary-k93c-closed-dark-sector-equation-of-state-on-the-matter-branch"></a>**Corollary K.9.3c (Closed Dark-Sector Equation of State on the Matter Branch).** On the matter-domination branch $\rho_r=0$ of Corollary K.9.3b, on any time interval with $H(t)\ne0$ and $\rho_b>0$, write $s\equiv s_{bg}$ and $x:=s^n$. Then $\rho_b=\rho_\Lambda/s$, the adaptive sector of (K.9.16) is
$$
\rho_{ad}=\frac{A_c\left(1-e^{-x}\right)}{s}\,\rho_\Lambda,
\qquad
p_{ad}=-\frac{A_c\,n\,x\,e^{-x}}{s}\,\rho_\Lambda,
\tag{K.9.3c.1}
$$
and the dark-sector fluid $\rho_{DE}:=\rho_\Lambda+\rho_{ad}$, $p_{DE}:=-\rho_\Lambda+p_{ad}$ satisfies $\rho_{DE}\ge\rho_\Lambda>0$, obeys $\dot\rho_{DE}+3H\left(\rho_{DE}+p_{DE}\right)=0$, and has equation of state
$$
w_{DE}(s)=\frac{p_{DE}}{\rho_{DE}}
=-\,\frac{1+A_c\,n\,x\,e^{-x}/s}{1+A_c\left(1-e^{-x}\right)/s},
\qquad x=s^n,
\tag{K.9.3c.2}
$$
with $w_{DE}(s)\to-1$ as $s\to0^{+}$ and as $s\to\infty$.

*Proof.* Definition K.9.1b with $\rho_r=0$ gives $s=\rho_\Lambda/\rho_b$, hence $\rho_b=\rho_\Lambda/s$. Equation (K.9.13) with $\rho_r=0$ gives $\dot\Upsilon_G=3H\,A_c\,n\,x\,e^{-x}$. Substituting $\Upsilon_G-1=A_c\left(1-e^{-x}\right)$ from (K.9.8), $\rho_{nv}=\rho_b=\rho_\Lambda/s$, and $p_{nv}=0$ into (K.9.16) yields (K.9.3c.1). The vacuum sector is constant with $p_\Lambda=-\rho_\Lambda$, so $\dot\rho_\Lambda+3H\left(\rho_\Lambda+p_\Lambda\right)=0$; adding (K.9.19) proves the displayed conservation law. Since $\rho_{ad}\ge0$, $\rho_{DE}\ge\rho_\Lambda>0$ and $w_{DE}$ is well defined; dividing $p_{DE}$ by $\rho_{DE}$ and factoring out $\rho_\Lambda$ gives (K.9.3c.2). For the limits: as $s\to\infty$, $x\to\infty$, so $x\,e^{-x}\to0$ and $\left(1-e^{-x}\right)/s\to0$, and the numerator and denominator of (K.9.3c.2) both tend to $1$. As $s\to0^{+}$: for $n=1$, $n\,x\,e^{-x}/s=e^{-s}\to1$ and $\left(1-e^{-s}\right)/s\to1$, so the numerator and denominator both tend to $1+A_c$; for $n>1$, $n\,x\,e^{-x}/s\le n\,s^{n-1}\to0$ and $\left(1-e^{-x}\right)/s\le s^{n-1}\to0$, so both tend to $1$. In every case the ratio tends to $1$ and $w_{DE}\to-1$. ∎

<a id="theorem-k93d-phantom-divide-classification"></a>**Theorem K.9.3d (Phantom-Divide Classification).** On the matter branch of Corollary K.9.3c, for every $s>0$,
$$
\operatorname{sign}\left(w_{DE}(s)+1\right)=\operatorname{sign}\left(e^{x}-1-n\,x\right),
\qquad x=s^n.
\tag{K.9.3d.1}
$$
Consequently:

1. For $n=1$: $w_{DE}(s)>-1$ for every $s\in(0,\infty)$; the dark sector never enters the phantom regime.

2. For $n>1$: the equation $e^{x}=1+n\,x$ has exactly one root $x_c(n)$ in $(0,\infty)$, and $w_{DE}<-1$ for $0<x<x_c(n)$ while $w_{DE}>-1$ for $x>x_c(n)$. On any expanding interval ($H>0$), $s$ is strictly increasing in cosmic time, so it crosses at most once on that interval, and exactly once when the interval's sparsity range straddles $x_c(n)^{1/n}$, from $w_{DE}<-1$ to $w_{DE}>-1$.

*Proof.* From (K.9.3c.2),
$$
w_{DE}+1
=\frac{A_c\left[\left(1-e^{-x}\right)-n\,x\,e^{-x}\right]/s}{1+A_c\left(1-e^{-x}\right)/s}
=\frac{A_c\,e^{-x}\left(e^{x}-1-n\,x\right)}{s\left[1+A_c\left(1-e^{-x}\right)/s\right]}.
$$
The prefactor $A_c\,e^{-x}/s$ and the denominator are strictly positive, which proves (K.9.3d.1). Set $h_n(x):=e^{x}-1-n\,x$ on $[0,\infty)$. Then $h_n(0)=0$, $h_n'(x)=e^{x}-n$, and $h_n''(x)=e^{x}>0$, so $h_n$ is strictly convex. For $n=1$: $h_1'(x)=e^{x}-1>0$ for $x>0$, so $h_1(x)>0$ for every $x>0$, and item 1 follows from (K.9.3d.1). For $n>1$: $h_n'(0)=1-n<0$, so $h_n<0$ on some interval $(0,\epsilon)$, while $h_n(x)\to+\infty$ as $x\to\infty$. The sublevel set $\{x\ge0:h_n(x)<0\}$ is convex by convexity of $h_n$, hence an interval; it contains points arbitrarily close to $0$, is bounded above, and its supremum $x_c(n)>0$ satisfies $h_n(x_c(n))=0$ by continuity. Thus $h_n<0$ on $(0,x_c(n))$ and $h_n>0$ on $(x_c(n),\infty)$, since a zero in $(x_c(n),\infty)$ together with the zeros at $0$ and $x_c(n)$ would give the strictly convex $h_n$ three zeros. The sign pattern of item 2 follows from (K.9.3d.1). Equation (K.9.12) with $\rho_r=0$ gives $\dot s=3Hs>0$ on expanding intervals, so $x=s^n$ is strictly increasing in cosmic time and the stated interval criterion determines whether the unique crossing is contained in that interval. ∎

<a id="corollary-k93e-crossing-redshift"></a>**Corollary K.9.3e (Crossing Redshift).** On an expanding matter branch with scale factor normalized to $a_0=1$ and present sparsity $s_{bg,0}=\rho_\Lambda/\rho_{b,0}$, the continuity equation (K.9.11) gives $s_{bg}(a)=s_{bg,0}\,a^{3}$, and for $n>1$ the crossing of Theorem K.9.3d occurs at
$$
1+z_\times=\left(\frac{s_{bg,0}}{x_c(n)^{1/n}}\right)^{1/3},
\tag{K.9.3e.1}
$$
where $x_c(n)$ is the unique positive root of $e^{x}=1+n\,x$. The crossing lies in the past, $z_\times>0$, exactly when $s_{bg,0}^{\,n}>x_c(n)$.

*Proof.* With $\rho_r=0$, (K.9.11) gives $\rho_b(a)=\rho_{b,0}\,a^{-3}$, so $s_{bg}(a)=\rho_\Lambda/\rho_b(a)=s_{bg,0}\,a^{3}$. The crossing condition $s_{bg}^{\,n}=x_c(n)$ of Theorem K.9.3d then reads $a_\times^{3}=x_c(n)^{1/n}/s_{bg,0}$, which is (K.9.3e.1) with $1+z_\times=1/a_\times$. Finally $z_\times>0$ is $a_\times<1$, equivalent to $x_c(n)^{1/n}<s_{bg,0}$, equivalent to $s_{bg,0}^{\,n}>x_c(n)$. ∎

**Observational Signatures:**
- Early-universe suppression: $1-e^{-x}\le\min\{1,x\}$ gives the exact bound $\Upsilon_G-1\le A_c\min\{1,s_{bg}^{\,n}\}$, which bounds the homogeneous response in the dense regime. The radiation and perturbation maps determine the BBN and CMB observables.
- Late-time growth modification: the background factor $\Upsilon_G(a)$ enters the registered perturbation and lensing equations through their projection certificates.
- Effective negative pressure: in matter domination, $p_{ad} = -\dot\Upsilon_G\rho_b/(3H)$.
- Phantom-divide structure: by Theorem K.9.3d, $w_{DE}>-1$ throughout for $n=1$, and for $n>1$ each expanding interval whose sparsity range straddles the threshold has one phantom-divide crossing, from $w_{DE}<-1$ to $w_{DE}>-1$, at the redshift (K.9.3e.1).
- Coupling cap: $\Upsilon_G<1+A_c$ at every finite $s_{bg}$, with saturation only in the de Sitter limit (K.9.10); on the capacity-tracking branch of Definition K.9.5e the cap is exactly $2$.
- Local gravity tests constrain the drift predicted by a registered background-to-local coupling and screening map, including its clock conversion. A direct constraint on the homogeneous ratio $|\dot\Upsilon_G/\Upsilon_G|$ requires that map to identify it with the tested local drift. On the matter branch the homogeneous ratio is $\dot\Upsilon_G/\Upsilon_G=3H\,A_c\,n\,s_{bg}^{\,n}\,e^{-s_{bg}^{\,n}}\big/\left[1+A_c\left(1-e^{-s_{bg}^{\,n}}\right)\right]$.
- Tensor propagation and density history: Definition K.9.5j and Proposition K.9.5k give the siren ratio with its endpoint-transfer factor; Corollary K.9.5l removes explicit response-shape parameters from the joint consistency relation.
- Sector selectivity: the background response acts on the registered non-vacuum gravitational sector. Drift of electromagnetic, strong, or weak observables requires its own coupling map and is tested under that map's uncertainty budget.

**Current Status:** The constitutive law is closed at the homogeneous FLRW level. Corollary K.9.3c, Theorem K.9.3d, and Corollary K.9.3e close the matter-branch dark-sector equation of state, its phantom-divide classification, and the crossing redshift. On the response-cost branch below (Definition K.9.5b, Theorem K.9.5c), the exponential response profile is the unique minimizer of the registered quadratic response action. On the capacity-tracking and horizon-bath clock branches below (Definition K.9.5e, Proposition K.9.5f, Definition K.9.5g, Proposition K.9.5h), the amplitude is $A_c=1$, while the dynamical clock has dense-limit exponent $3/2$ and retains $\kappa_\sigma$. Remark K.9.5i distinguishes that ODE from the exact power-clock model. A finite entropic-bridge branch below gives the precise condition under which $(A_c,n)$ are selected by the Appendix D relaxation potential rather than stipulated. Perturbation-level confrontation with growth, lensing, BAO, and CMB data remains a separate observational branch task.

<a id="definition-k94-homogeneous-finite-entropic-bridge-branch"></a>**Definition K.9.4 (Homogeneous Finite Entropic-Bridge Branch).** Let $X_N$ be a finite coarse FLRW predictive state space with detailed-balance reference generator $L_N$ in the sense of Definition D.8.6d. Fix a finite protocol time grid
$$
0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_M=1
$$
and let $\Omega_N=X_N^{M+1}$ be the finite path ledger. Let $\mathbb P_{0,N}$ be the strictly positive reference path measure induced by the finite transition kernels of $L_N$ on this grid. Fix endpoint laws
$$
(e_0)_{\#}\mathbb P=\rho_{\mathrm{early}},
\qquad
(e_M)_{\#}\mathbb P=\rho_{\mathrm{late}},
\tag{K.9.20}
$$
and a finite PCE running cost
$$
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{PCE},N}(\omega)
=
\sum_{\ell=0}^{M-1}
(t_{\ell+1}-t_\ell)
\mathcal L_{\mathrm{PCE},N}(x_\ell,x_{\ell+1})
\ge0
$$
for $\omega=(x_0,\dots,x_M)\in\Omega_N$. The homogeneous finite entropic bridge is
$$
\mathbb P_{*,N}
=
\arg\min_{\mathbb P}
\left[
