The separately registered power clock requires $\kappa_\sigma=9/2$ for its unit dense coefficient.

*Common finite source and errors.* Fix $j\ge1$, $n=j+8$ and $\varepsilon=8^{-n}$. At each rational cut $c_{\rm cut}\in[-n,n]$, the source uses the same indexed conserved material bank, its physical action and currents, selected finite spatial mode, bath, geometric profile, nonzero perturbation amplitude and normalized nonlinear source state across all of its response records. The receiver uses the actual proper integral from label $2n$ to $c_{\rm cut}$ after the source and amplitude are set. The Ramsey and terminal predictive protocols use the full interval from $2n$ to $-n$. These are separate uses of the stated preparation, with their own measured proper-to-coordinate rates. Native safe sectors, pads, the full joint path and response stocks, the literal source words and the private records are retained.

For each member the common schedule chooses a positive regulator scale $H_{j,c_{\rm cut}}=8^{-2k}$ below the source's strict error thresholds. ## K.10 Renormalization from Operational Finiteness

The finite-throughput and Fermi-certificate boundaries of Section K.5 have an analogue in ultraviolet effective theory: each marks the domain of a registered operational description. Excluding ultraviolet modes or divergences requires the explicit lattice or bandlimit, regulator, dispersion, and matching certificate of Theorem K.10.4.

<a id="definition-k101-operational-observable"></a>**Definition K.10.1 (Operational Observable).** A quantity $\mathcal{O}$ is an operational observable if for every target precision $\epsilon>0$ there exists an MPU-admissible protocol $\mathcal{P}_\epsilon$ (a finite physically implementable procedure using the allowed interaction/update dynamics, including $\mathcal{E}_N$ updates of Definition 27) whose registered output is a finite real number, that estimates $\langle\mathcal O\rangle$ to within $\epsilon$, and that uses finite resources, i.e. it has finite predictive complexity and hence finite cost rate:
$$
R(C_P(\mathcal{P}_\epsilon)) + R_I(C_P(\mathcal{P}_\epsilon)) < \infty,
$$
where $R,R_I$ are the resource cost functions (Definition 3).

<a id="lemma-k102-operational-finiteness"></a>**Lemma K.10.2 (Operational Finiteness).** If $\mathcal{O}$ is an operational observable (Definition K.10.1), then its operational expectation value $\langle\mathcal{O}\rangle$ is finite. In particular, no finite-output additive-error protocol of Definition K.10.1 can assign $+\infty$ as its operational expectation value.

*Proof.* By Definition K.10.1, for $\epsilon=1$ there exists an MPU-admissible finite-resource protocol $\mathcal{P}_1$ producing an estimate within additive error $1$ of $\langle\mathcal{O}\rangle$. If $\langle\mathcal{O}\rangle$ were infinite, no finite real-valued estimate could satisfy an additive-error bound, contradicting the definition. Hence $\langle\mathcal{O}\rangle$ is finite. ∎

<a id="definition-k103-mpu-wavenumber-momentum-and-energy-scales"></a>**Definition K.10.3 (MPU Wavenumber, Momentum, and Energy Scales).** Define
$$
k_{\mathrm{MPU}}:=\delta^{-1},\qquad p_{\mathrm{MPU}}:=\hbar k_{\mathrm{MPU}},\qquad E_{\mathrm{MPU}}:=cp_{\mathrm{MPU}}.
$$
For ordinary wavelength $\lambda=2\pi/k$, the condition $k>k_{\mathrm{MPU}}$ is equivalent to $\lambda<2\pi\delta$. For reduced wavelength $\bar\lambda:=1/k$, it is equivalent to $\bar\lambda<\delta$. These are intrinsic comparison scales; treating them as a hard dynamical cutoff requires a separately certified lattice/dispersion realization.

<a id="theorem-k103a-operational-anti-continuum-principle"></a>**Theorem K.10.3a (Operational Anti-Continuum Principle).** Let $\mathfrak C$ be a mathematical structure whose exact physical interpretation would require uniformly refinable distinctions at all resolutions $\nu>0$ on one bounded operational domain. Let $N_{\mathfrak C}(\nu)$ be the minimum number of mutually distinguishable alternatives required to specify those distinctions to resolution $\nu$. Restrict the admitted physical instantiations $\mathcal P$ to those carrying a finite classical distinguishability certificate $B(\mathcal P)$: the same instantiation can support at most $\exp(B(\mathcal P))$ mutually distinguishable alternatives, uniformly over all resolutions asserted for it. The certificate counts initial memory, total channel uses, side information, assistance, and accessible output resources, and excludes uncharged bypass resources. A finite cost rate or finite spacing alone does not supply this total budget. If
$$
\lim_{\nu\to0}\ln N_{\mathfrak C}(\nu)=+\infty,
$$
then no single instantiation carrying that certificate represents $\mathfrak C$ exactly at every resolution. Within this certified class, operational uses are restricted to finite-resolution quotients, effective closures, or coarse-grained descriptions whose required distinctions fit the registered budget.

In particular, the theorem applies to an exact real continuum, group parameter, ontic branch label, or sub-$\delta$ field mode only when the interpretation makes its refinements independently addressable and mutually distinguishable, so that $N_{\mathfrak C}(\nu)$ diverges. A continuous group law used as an effective mathematical representation is not excluded merely by having continuously many parameter values.

<a id="corollary-k103b-operational-continuum-as-a-universality-class"></a>**Corollary K.10.3b (Operational Continuum as a Universality Class).** Let $\{\mathcal N_i,\mathcal E_i,V_i\}_{i\in I}$ be finite MPU-network descriptions with common operational resolution $\delta$, and let $\mathcal O_{\le\delta}$ be the admissible observable algebra at that resolution. If, for every pair $i,j$ and every $O\in\mathcal O_{\le\delta}$,
$$
d_{\mathrm{TV}}\!\left(P_i(O),P_j(O)\right)\le\epsilon_\delta,
$$
then the displayed family is pairwise indistinguishable within the registered tolerance on that observable algebra. When $\epsilon_\delta=0$, equality of all such outcome laws defines an equivalence relation. For positive tolerance, membership in a common operational-continuum quotient class requires a separately registered equivalence relation or partition that places the family in one class; the displayed tolerance test alone does not define that quotient. Any manifold, metric, or AQFT representative assigned to such a class also requires a construction compatible with the registered equivalence.

*Proof.* The hypothesis directly supplies the pairwise tolerance conclusion for the displayed family. Equality of all outcome laws is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive, giving the zero-tolerance quotient. The positive-tolerance relation on all finite descriptions need not be transitive: for a single binary observable with Bernoulli parameters $0$, $1/4$, and $1/2$, the two successive total-variation distances are $1/4$ but the endpoint distance is $1/2$. At tolerance $1/4$, the successive pairs pass and the endpoint pair fails. This does not contradict the assumed all-pairs bound for the displayed family; it prevents using the tolerance test as a global equivalence relation without additional structure. The quotient-class and representative conclusions therefore require the stated registration. ∎

*Proof.* Let $\mathcal P$ be one instantiation in the theorem's certified class. Its registered total distinguishability bound is
$$
B(\mathcal P)<\infty.
$$
Thus it supports at most $\exp(B(\mathcal P))$ mutually distinguishable alternatives, with every resource listed in the certificate included. This bound is an explicit premise; it is not inferred from a finite rate or from an unqualified per-channel capacity formula.

If $\mathfrak C$ were represented exactly by this one instantiation, it would have to support the distinctions required at every resolution $\nu>0$. Since $\ln N_{\mathfrak C}(\nu)\to\infty$, choose $\nu$ such that
$$
\ln N_{\mathfrak C}(\nu)>B(\mathcal P).
$$
Then $N_{\mathfrak C}(\nu)>\exp(B(\mathcal P))$, contradicting the same-instantiation certificate. Conditional Landauer accounting is not used in this contradiction: a registered reset label has conditional entropy $H(P\mid R)\le\ln N_{\mathfrak C}(\nu)$, with equality only for a conditionally uniform label without resolving side information. This upper entropy bound cannot supply a reset-cost lower bound of $\ln N_{\mathfrak C}(\nu)$. The conclusion is confined to the declared finite-total-budget class. ∎

<a id="theorem-k104-conditional-effective-cutoff-interpretation"></a>**Theorem K.10.4 (Conditional Effective-Cutoff Interpretation).** Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{phys}}(\mu)$ be an operational observable at external scale $\mu$. Its operational value is finite. The spacing $\delta$ defines the comparison scales
$$
k_{\mathrm{MPU}}=\delta^{-1},
\qquad
p_{\mathrm{MPU}}=\hbar\delta^{-1},
\qquad
E_{\mathrm{MPU}}=c\hbar\delta^{-1}.
$$
If a branch additionally supplies a microscopic lattice or bandlimit, a dispersion relation, a regulator, and a matching theorem controlling the residual error of registered observables, then its continuum representation may be treated as hard-cut off at the certified scales. Spacing and finite capacity alone do not imply that hard cutoff.

*Proof.* Lemma K.10.2 gives finiteness of every operational expectation. The three scales follow by substituting $k=1/\delta$, $p=\hbar k$, and $E=cp$. Hence
$$
k>k_{\mathrm{MPU}}
\Longleftrightarrow
\bar\lambda:=k^{-1}<\delta,
\qquad
p>p_{\mathrm{MPU}}.
$$
On the additional certificate branch, the lattice or bandlimit removes independent modes beyond its registered domain and the matching theorem transfers the regulated predictions to the retained observables. Without that hypothesis, the algebraic comparison scales impose no support condition on a continuum Fourier transform, so ordinary renormalization remains necessary. ∎

<a id="theorem-k104d-complete-finite-ring-operator-matching-and-controlled-eft-expansions"></a>**Theorem K.10.4d (Complete Finite-Ring Operator Matching and Controlled EFT Expansions).** The following exact all-N argument retains both the autonomous low-preserving grammar and the complete microscopic four-block history dictionary. Its spectral and bare-orbital thresholds are distinct. Local section numbers refer to this module.

**Exact finite-ring band matching, complete operator dictionary, and controlled expansions**

This is a self-contained mathematical result for the stated finite, one-excitation model. It does not establish a continuum, Lorentz, interacting many-body, or physical implementation claim.

## 1. Model, units, and precisely declared response cuts

Fix an odd integer $N\ge 5$, a spacing $\delta>0$, and $q=(N-1)/2$. Set

- $E=\mathbb{C}^N$, $H=E\otimes\mathbb{C}^2$;
- $l=-q,\dots,q$; $p_l=2\pi l/(N\delta)$, $x_l=p_l\delta$;
- $s_l=4\sin^2(x_l/2)$, $a(s)=2+s$, $d(s)=10+2s$, $b(s)=d-a=8+s$;
- $h(s)=\begin{bmatrix}a(s)&1\\1&d(s)\end{bmatrix}$, and $H_{\mathrm{micro}}$ is the direct sum of these momentum blocks.

All displayed energies, including $z$, are numerical values in the fixed source energy unit $E_0$. Times are numerical values in $\hbar/E_0$; $x=p\delta$ is dimensionless. To restore units, multiply every displayed energy/kernel by $E_0$ and replace $\exp(-ith)$ by $\exp(-iE_0th/\hbar)$. $\Delta$ is never set to one. No velocity or Lorentz normalization is being imposed.

There are TWO different, explicit matching statements:

(A) Autonomous low-band response cut. Preparations are supported in the exact low spectral code; dynamics is $H_{\mathrm{micro}}$; arbitrary finite-dimensional ancillas are allowed; instruments are exact lifts of arbitrary instruments on E and therefore preserve the code. Every finite adaptive history matches an autonomous N-dimensional model exactly. Outside-code inputs have a normalized terminal failure extension described below.

(B) Full microscopic response cut. Every operator in $B(H)$, every preparation, and every finite adaptive instrument history is allowed. Its exact effective dictionary consists of BOTH low/high blocks, with all high-band excursions retained. It is an algebra isomorphism, not a dimension reduction. Low external legs can be represented by an exact band-path memory expansion, but deleting the high paths is not exact. This is the full matching statement for bare local operators and arbitrary microscopic sources/instruments.

Neither statement identifies compression $O\to P_-OP_-$ with an algebra homomorphism on arbitrary microscopic operators. Neither gives an unqualified low-only Markov error bound for arbitrary microscopic histories. A spectral gap alone would not justify such a bound.

## 2. All-N bands, spectral projections, and gaps

Write $D(s)=\sqrt{(8+s)^2+4}$, taking the positive root on the real spectrum. The two exact eigenvalues are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\epsilon_-(s) &= (12+3s-D(s))/2,\\
\epsilon_+(s) &= (12+3s+D(s))/2.
\end{aligned}
$$

The allowed s values have exact minimum 0 and maximum

$$
s_N = 4 \cos^2(\pi/(2N)) < 4.
$$

Since $0<(8+s)/D(s)<1$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\epsilon_-'(s) &= 3/2 - (8+s)/(2D(s)) \text{ is in } (1,3/2),\\
\epsilon_+'(s) &= 3/2 + (8+s)/(2D(s)) \text{ is in } (3/2,2).
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the exact finite spectra have extrema

  $$
  \begin{gathered}
  \min\,\text{low}=6-\sqrt{17},\quad \max\,\text{low}=\epsilon_-(s_N), \\
  \min\,\text{high}=6+\sqrt{17},\quad \max\,\text{high}=\epsilon_+(s_N).
  \end{gathered}
  $$

Every allowed level belongs to the disjoint, N-independent enclosures

  low:  [6-sqrt(17), 12-sqrt(37)),
  high: [6+sqrt(17), 12+sqrt(37)).

The finite-system indirect spectral gap is exactly

$$
\begin{aligned}
g_N &= 6+\sqrt{17} - \epsilon_-(s_N)\\
&> \sqrt{17}+\sqrt{37}-6 > 0.
\end{aligned}
$$

The infimum over odd $N$ is $\sqrt{17}+\sqrt{37}-6$; it is approached as $N$ tends to infinity and is not attained at finite $N$. The direct gap at momentum $l$ is $D(s_l)$, at least $2\sqrt{17}$. The bottom of the one-excitation spectrum is $6-\sqrt{17}>0$; a separate vacuum at energy zero, if one is adjoined, is therefore separated by that number. Adjoining such a vacuum is not part of the present Hilbert-space assumption.

In particular, energy cut 6 includes the entire low band and excludes the entire high band, for every N. The spectral low/high threshold is 6+sqrt(17), whereas the bare-orbital elimination threshold below is 10; they are different quantities.

## 3. Exact isometries and autonomous full matrix algebra

For each momentum define

$$
\begin{aligned}
r &= 1/(d-\epsilon_-) = (D-b)/2,\\
c &= 1/\sqrt{1+r^2} = \sqrt{(1+b/D)/2},\\
t &= r c = \sqrt{(1-b/D)/2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $c,t$ are positive and $c^2+t^2=1$. The normalized eigenvectors are

$$
u_-=(c,-t)^{\mathsf T},\quad u_+=(t,c)^{\mathsf T}.
$$

Let C and T be diagonal multiplication by $c_{l}$ and $t_{l}$ on E. In the orbital order (all light, all heavy), set

$$
J_-=\begin{pmatrix}C\\-T\end{pmatrix},\quad J_+=\begin{pmatrix}T\\C\end{pmatrix},\quad U=\begin{pmatrix}J_-&J_+\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Then $J_a^*J_b=\delta_{ab}I_E$, $P_a=J_aJ_a^*$, $P_-+P_+=I_H$, and $U$ is unitary. Define $H_a=\operatorname{diag}(\epsilon_a(s_l))$. Direct multiplication gives

  $$
  \begin{gathered}
  H_{\mathrm{micro}}J_a=J_aH_a,\\
  U^*H_{\mathrm{micro}}U=\operatorname{diag}(H_-,H_+),\\
  \exp(-itH_{\mathrm{micro}})J_a=J_a\exp(-itH_a)\quad\text{for all real } t.
  \end{gathered}
  $$

The map $\iota(A)=J_-AJ_-^*$ is a $*$-isomorphism from $M_N(\mathbb{C})$ onto the corner $P_-B(H)P_-$. In particular

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\iota(AB)=\iota(A)\iota(B),\quad \iota(A^*)=\iota(A)^*,\\
&\iota(I_E)=P_-,\quad \lVert\iota(A)\rVert=\lVert A\rVert.
\end{aligned}
$$

It is unital relative to that corner, not unital into $B(H)$. All matrix units $|l\rangle\langle m|$, all position-basis matrix units, and all their combinations are matched, not merely a quadratic dispersion or a Gaussian covariance. The same assertions hold after tensoring every map with the identity on an arbitrary finite-dimensional ancilla. Dressed observables are generally spatially nonlocal.

### 3.1 Every finite adaptive low-code instrument history

At each finite outcome prefix $h$, choose any instrument $\{I_r^h\}$ on $E$, with Kraus operators $K_{r,\alpha}^h$ satisfying

$$
\begin{aligned}
&I_r^h(\rho)=\sum_\alpha K_{r,\alpha}^h \rho K_{r,\alpha}^{h*},\\
&\sum_{r,\alpha} K_{r,\alpha}^{h*} K_{r,\alpha}^h=I_E.
\end{aligned}
$$

Both the instrument and the next time interval may depend arbitrarily on h. Its code lift is

$$
\hat I_r^h(X)=J_- I_r^h(J_-^* X J_-) J_-^*.
$$

Start from $\hat{\rho}=J_-\rho J_-^*$. Interleave any finite number of these maps with free evolution, in the same adaptive order on the two sides. Induction on the history length gives, for every record $h$, the exact equality of unnormalized branch states

$$
\hat\rho_h=J_- \rho_h J_-^*.
$$

Therefore every joint record probability and every conditional probability at a positive-probability prefix agrees. Normalized conditional states also agree under J_-. At a zero-probability branch neither side has a uniquely defined normalized conditional state, and no such conditional equality is claimed. This is an equality of quantum instruments/records, not just expectation values. Finite ancillary systems, mixed preparations, non-projective measurements, multiple Kraus operators per outcome, and feedback are already covered.

### 3.2 Normalized terminal failure extension; no postselection

The code lifts alone sum to trace $P_-X$, not trace $X$. To obtain a genuine instrument on ALL microscopic inputs, choose a unit vector $q_0$ in the high eigenspace (for example $J_+|l=0\rangle$) and an orthonormal basis $\{q_j\}$ of $\operatorname{ran}P_+$. Add a terminal failure outcome with Kraus operators

$$
F_j=|q_0\rangle\langle q_j|.
$$

Their sum of effects is P_+, whereas the success Kraus effects sum to P_-. Thus the extended instrument is CP and trace preserving after summing all outcomes. Its failure map is

$$
\hat I_{\mathrm{fail}}(X)=\operatorname{Tr}(P_+ X)\, |q_0\rangle\langle q_0|.
$$

For any normalized initial $X\ge 0$, the total initial low-success weight is $w=\operatorname{Tr}(P_-X)$, the failure probability is $1-w$, and success uses the subnormalized state $J_-^*XJ_-$. This is not an assumption that $w=1$. Failure is recorded and terminal; alternatively it is absorbing under subsequent extended attempts because free evolution preserves $P_+$ and $|q_0\rangle\langle q_0|$. Low/high input coherences are discarded by this declared response cut, rather than recovered by a fictitious low-channel inverse.

Equivalently use the CPTP decoder into $E\oplus\mathbb{C}|\mathrm{fail}\rangle$:

  $$
  D_{\mathrm{flag}}(X)=(J_-^*XJ_-)\oplus\operatorname{Tr}(P_+X)|\mathrm{fail}\rangle\langle\mathrm{fail}|.
  $$

It intertwines free density-matrix evolution with H_- on E and a stationary failure flag. The extended instrument also intertwines with the corresponding low instrument plus terminal flag. Induction yields equality of every normalized full record, including failure, for arbitrary initial X. This extension only matches the stated failure grammar; it does NOT reproduce arbitrary subsequent probes of the high sector. Those require the full block dictionary next.

## 4. ALL microscopic operators, bare local probes, and exact high-excursion histories

For every $O$ in $B(H)$, define four $N$-by-$N$ blocks

$$
O_{ab} = J_a^* O J_b,\quad a,b \in \{-,+\}.
$$

The map $\Phi(O)=U^*OU$ is a unital $*$-isomorphism $B(H)\to M_2(M_N(\mathbb{C}))$, with inverse

$$
O=\sum_{ab} J_a O_{ab} J_b^*.
$$

Its multiplication rule is

$$
(O V)_{ab} = \sum_c O_{ac} V_{cb}.
$$

In particular,

  $$
  (OV)_{--}=O_{--}V_{--}+O_{-+}V_{+-},
  $$

so the low-corner compression alone is not multiplicative. All microscopic instrument Kraus operators are mapped blockwise by $\Phi$. Completeness, complete positivity, normalization, ancillas, and all finite adaptive records are preserved because $\Phi$ is unitary conjugation.

A concrete obstruction to naive compression is the bare light-orbital projection $L=\operatorname{diag}(I_E,0)$. Its blocks are

$$
\Phi(L) = \begin{bmatrix} C^2 & CT\\ TC & T^2 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Since $L^2=L$, $(L^2)_{--}=C^2$, while $L_{--}^2=C^4$; the missing term is $C^2T^2>0$. The momentum gap does not remove this term. For the position-local light projection $|j,A\rangle\langle j,A|$, the $ab$ block is $D_a|j\rangle\langle j|D_{b}$, where $D_-=C$ and $D_+=T$ after transforming $E$ to the position basis. Thus even a bare local light probe generally connects both bands.

### 4.1 Explicit band-path formula for every finite record

Fix one record $h=(r_1,\dots,r_n)$, its adaptive instrument choices, a Kraus-index sequence $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)$, and times $t_{j}$. Let

$$
W_{h,\alpha}=K_n \exp(-it_n H_{\mathrm{micro}}) \cdots K_1 \exp(-it_1 H_{\mathrm{micro}}),
$$

where $K_{j}$ denotes the selected outcome/Kraus operator at the preceding prefix. Its exact endpoint block is

$$
\begin{aligned}
W_{a_n a_0}
&= \sum_{a_1,\ldots,a_{n-1} \in \{-,+\}}\\
&\qquad K_{n,a_n a_{n-1}} \exp(-it_n H_{a_{n-1}})\\
&\qquad \cdots\\
&\qquad K_{1,a_1 a_0} \exp(-it_1 H_{a_0}).
\end{aligned}
$$

This is just repeated block multiplication, so it is valid for noncommuting spatial matrices and arbitrary finite n without any approximation. For an arbitrary initial density matrix with blocks $\rho_{ab}$, the full output blocks are

$$
\rho'_{ab}=\sum_\alpha \sum_{c,d} W_{ac}\, \rho_{cd}\, W_{bd}^*.
$$

The record probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Pr(h) &= \sum_a \operatorname{Tr}(\rho'_{aa})\\
&= \sum_\alpha \sum_{a,c,d} \operatorname{Tr}(W_{ac}\, \rho_{cd}\, W_{ad}^*).
\end{aligned}
$$

These are the explicit forward/backward band-path sums, including their interferences, not a stochastic omission of virtual paths. Summing all records gives one by instrument completeness. The entire post-instrument state, including off-diagonal low/high coherence, is available for further adaptation.

If external legs and preparation are low, set $a_0=c=d=-$ (and, for a low final amplitude, $a_n=-$), but still sum every intermediate band path. Terms involving $\exp(-itH_+)$ are exact heavy memory/nonlocal contributions. Their time-domain operator norm equals one; the spectral gap does not make arbitrary such terms small. Discarding them produces no general exact or small-error low-only history theorem.

For a time-dependent microscopic source, use the SAME block dictionary for the source Hamiltonian. Its full time-ordered propagator is exactly conjugated by U, or equivalently has the usual convergent finite-dimensional Dyson expansion with all band paths. One may not keep only its -- block unless an additional source restriction is imposed. Adding arbitrary sources can shift thresholds, so fixed free-model threshold bounds below are not silently asserted for a sourced Hamiltonian.

### 4.2 Explicit spectral-heavy kernels and their threshold

Let $\mu=6+\sqrt{17}$, the exact lowest high eigenenergy. The spectral-heavy resolvent and retarded propagation kernels in the position representation are

$$
\begin{aligned}
G_+(z;j,k) &= (1/N)\sum_l \exp(i p_l (j-k)\delta)/(z-\epsilon_+(s_l)),\\
G_+^{\mathrm{ret}}(t;j,k) &= (-i)\, 1_{t\ge 0}(1/N)\sum_l \exp(i p_l (j-k)\delta-it\, \epsilon_+(s_l)).
\end{aligned}
$$

(The retarded boundary value at $t=0$ is immaterial to an integral.) These are explicit generally nonlocal kernels. The band-path sums use these heavy segments, with the appropriate source or instrument vertices at their endpoints. For complex $|z|\le E<\mu$,

  $$
  \lVert(z-H_+)^{-1}\rVert\le 1/(\mu-E).
  $$

Its complete Taylor expansion about zero is

$$
\begin{aligned}
(z-H_+)^{-1} &= -\sum_{n=0}^M z^n H_+^{-(n+1)} + R_+(z),\\
\lVert R_+(z)\rVert &\le E^{M+1}/(\mu^{M+1}(\mu-E)).
\end{aligned}
$$

The radius $\mu$ is sharp because the $p=0$ high state exists for every N. These bounds hold for a fixed finite chain of heavy propagators with the actual vertex norms included; they do not bound an unrestricted adaptive history independently of vertex size, number, source bandwidth, or proximity to a pole.

For completeness, add a static microscopic source V and take its FULL spectral blocks $V_{ab}$. Whenever the indicated high-block inverse exists, the exact low-endpoint Schur kernel is

$$
\begin{aligned}
K_{\mathrm{low},V}(z) &= z-H_- -V_{--}\\
&\quad -V_{-+} (z-H_+-V_{++})^{-1} V_{+-},
\end{aligned}
$$

and $[(z-H_{\mathrm{micro}}-V)^{-1}]_{--}=K_{\mathrm{low},V}(z)^{-1}$, where both inverses are defined. This retains the complete heavy self-energy. In the time domain the same elimination has memory kernel generated by $H_{+}+V_{++}$, with an initial high-state term. If $V$ is self-adjoint, a sufficient lower high-block threshold is $\mu-\lVert V_{++}\rVert$, when positive; otherwise no unchanged free threshold is assumed. Arbitrary time-dependent vertices remain covered by the exact full block evolution in Section 4.1.

## 5. Exact bare light-port resolvent, residue, and wavefunction conversion

Eliminating the B/heavy ORBITAL at fixed p, rather than the high SPECTRAL band, gives the exact Schur kernel

$$
K(z,s)=z-a(s)-1/(z-d(s)).
$$

For $z\ne d(s)$, block Gaussian elimination shows

$$
\begin{aligned}
[(z-h(s))^{-1}]_{AA} &= 1/K(z,s)\\
&= (z-d(s))/((z-\epsilon_-)(z-\epsilon_+)).
\end{aligned}
$$

The rightmost rational function extends across $z=d(s)$, where the bare light-port resolvent has a zero; the Schur kernel itself has a pole there. The inverse formulas are asserted off actual full-spectrum poles. Its spectral decomposition is

$$
\begin{aligned}
g_{AA}(z,s) &= Z(s)/(z-\epsilon_-(s)) + (1-Z(s))/(z-\epsilon_+(s)),\\
Z(s) &= c(s)^2=(1+b/D)/2\\
&= [1+1/(d-\epsilon_-)^2]^{-1}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The low spectral channel instead has resolvent $(z-H_-)^{-1}$ with unit residue in the canonical effective coordinate. These two channels must not be identified. At the low pole,

$$
\partial_z K(\epsilon_-,s)=1+1/(d-\epsilon_-)^2=1/Z(s).
$$

Let $A:H\to E$ select the bare light orbital. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
&A J_-=C,\quad P_- A^*=J_- C,\\
&A P_- (z-H_{\mathrm{micro}})^{-1} P_- A^* = C(z-H_-)^{-1}C.
\end{aligned}
$$

A bare light source $f$ has projected low state $J_-Cf$ and low preparation probability $\lVert Cf\rVert^2$ when $\lVert f\rVert=1$. Its normalized canonical low state is $Cf/\lVert Cf\rVert$; the residual high component must be retained or counted as a failure. If $\phi$ is the bare light component of an already low-code wavefunction, then

  $$
  \begin{gathered}
  \text{canonical coordinate } \chi=C^{-1}\phi,\\
  \text{physical low state }=(\phi,-R\phi),\quad R=\operatorname{diag}(r_l),\\
  \lVert\chi\rVert^2=\langle\phi,(I+R^2)\phi\rangle.
  \end{gathered}
  $$

Thus residue multiplication and wavefunction conversion are actual operators, not merely an informal field redefinition. They are uniformly well conditioned:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&0<r_l\le\sqrt{17}-4,\\
&Z_l \ge (1+4/\sqrt{17})/2 > 0,\\
&\lVert C^{-1}\rVert \le \sqrt{2/(1+4/\sqrt{17})}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At a fixed momentum, a low-code density matrix represented using the bare light amplitude must use this induced normalization. Multiplying the FULL bare $g_{AA}$ by $C^{-1}$ on both sides still leaves a high-pole term; first isolate $P_-$ if a unit-residue low resolvent is wanted.

### 5.1 Exact time-domain orbital memory

In fixed energy/time units the orbital equations are

$$
i \dot A = a A+B,\quad i \dot B=A+d B.
$$

For $t\ge 0$,

  $$
  \begin{gathered}
  B(t)=\exp(-idt)B(0)-i\int_0^t\exp(-id(t-u))A(u)\,du, \\
  i\dot{A}(t)=aA(t)+\exp(-idt)B(0)-i\int_0^t\exp(-id(t-u))A(u)\,du.
  \end{gathered}
  $$

This is an exact causal memory equation, including the initial heavy-orbital term. Its frequency-domain Schur kernel is K above. It is different from the spectral high-band propagator exp(-it H_+), but both are retained exactly in their respective representations.

## 6. Complete Taylor counterterms in z, thresholds, and uniform remainder

For any integer $M\ge 0$ and $|z|<d(s)$, the exact geometric identity is

$$
\begin{aligned}
K(z,s) &= K_M(z,s)+R_M(z,s),\\
K_M(z,s) &= z-a(s)+\sum_{n=0}^M z^n/d(s)^{n+1},\\
R_M(z,s) &= z^{M+1}/(d(s)^{M+1}(d(s)-z)).
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the complete analytic counterterm expansion is

$$
\begin{aligned}
K(z,s) &= -[a(s)-1/d(s)] + [1+1/d(s)^2]\, z\\
&\quad +\sum_{n=2}^\infty z^n/d(s)^{n+1}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The $n=0$ term is the static shift, $n=1$ is the normalization at the expansion point zero, and higher powers are higher-time-derivative terms. The normalization at zero is generally NOT the exact pole normalization 1/Z.

Uniformly over every $N$, every momentum, and complex $|z|\le E_{\mathrm{cut}}<10$,

  $$
  |R_M(z,s)|\le E_{\mathrm{cut}}^{M+1}/(10^{M+1}(10-E_{\mathrm{cut}})).
  $$

This is an operator-norm bound for the diagonal spatial kernel as well. A useful common cut is $E_{\mathrm{cut}}=6$, including every low eigenenergy, for which

  $$
  \lVert R_M\rVert\le(3/5)^{M+1}/4.
  $$

The exact all-momentum Taylor radius about zero is 10 because $s=0$ occurs for every $N$ and $K(z,0)$ has a genuine pole at $z=10$. At a given momentum its radius is $d(s)$. This bare elimination threshold differs from the first high eigenenergy $6+\sqrt{17}$.

The Taylor bound is a KERNEL bound, not a uniform bound for its inverse on a disk containing low poles. If on a selected compact $z$/momentum set one additionally has $|K|\ge\kappa>0$ and the displayed remainder bound $r\le\kappa/2$, then $|K_M|\ge\kappa/2$ and

  $$
  |1/K-1/K_M|\le 2r/\kappa^2.
  $$

Without that spectral-distance condition, poles/near-poles invalidate such an inverse bound. No finite truncation is claimed to preserve exact instrument-history matching or every pole/residue.

## 7. Complete analytic spatial expansion, with two uniform versions

Let $s(x)=2-2\cos x=4\sin^2(x/2)$ and

$$
F(s)=(12+3s-\sqrt{68+16s+s^2})/2,\quad \epsilon_-(p)=F(s(p\, \delta)).
$$

### 7.1 All-lattice-mode convergent expansion in the lattice Laplacian

The branch points in the complex $s$ plane are $-8+2i$ and $-8-2i$, both at distance $\sqrt{68}>8$ from zero. Hence the branch fixed positive at $s=0$ is analytic on $|s|<\sqrt{68}$, and

$$
F(s)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty \alpha_n s^n
$$

converges for every lattice mode, since $s\le 4$. The complete coefficients have either of these exact specifications:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\alpha_0 &= 6-\sqrt{17},\\
\alpha_n &= (3/2)\, 1_{n=1}\\
&\quad -\sqrt{17} \sum_{k=\lceil n/2\rceil}^n \binom{1/2}{k} \binom{k}{n-k}\\
&\qquad (4/17)^{2k-n}(1/68)^{n-k},\quad n\ge 1.
\end{aligned}
$$

Equivalently define $d_0=2\sqrt{17}$ and, for $n\ge 1$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
d_n&=[v_n-\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}d_k d_{n-k}]/(2d_0),\\
v_1&=16,\quad v_2=1,\quad v_n=0\ \text{for } n\ge 3,\\
\alpha_n&=(3/2)1_{n=1}-d_n/2.
\end{aligned}
$$

The finite formula is coefficient extraction from the local binomial series; its derivation only needs a neighborhood of zero. The convergence claim on the larger disk uses analyticity, not the false assertion that the composed binomial argument has magnitude below one for every $s\le 4$.

On $|s|=8$ one has

  $$
  |F(s)|\le(12+24+\sqrt{68+128+64})/2=18+\sqrt{65}=M_s.
  $$

Cauchy's coefficient bound therefore gives, for $0\le s\le\sigma\le 4$,

  $$
  |F(s)-\sum_{n=0}^m\alpha_ns^n|\le M_s(\sigma/8)^{m+1}/(1-\sigma/8).
  $$

In particular the all-mode bound is $2M_s\,2^{-(m+1)}=M_s\,2^{-m}$, independent of $N$ and $\delta$. If $S_{N}$ is the positive nearest-neighbor lattice Laplacian with symbol $2-2\cos(p\delta)$, the identical bound holds in operator norm for $H_{-}-\sum\alpha_nS_N^n$. This is a complete convergent lattice-gradient expansion, not just a two-jet.

### 7.2 Ordinary spatial derivatives: a concrete safe radius 2

For complex $|x|\le R=2$,

  $$
  |s(x)|\le 4\sinh^2(|x|/2)\le B=4\sinh^2(1)<\sqrt{68}.
  $$

(The inequality follows termwise from $|\sin z|\le\sinh|z|$.) Hence $F(s(x))$ is analytic in a neighborhood of the closed disk $|x|\le 2$ and is even. Let

$$
\epsilon_-(x)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty \beta_n x^{2n}.
$$

The complete coefficients are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\beta_0 &= \alpha_0,\\
\beta_n &= \sum_{k=1}^n \alpha_k \sum_{j_1+\cdots+j_k=n,\ j_i\ge 1} \prod_i [2(-1)^{j_i+1}/(2j_i)!],\quad n\ge 1.
\end{aligned}
$$

This is an exact finite sum for every n. The first terms are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\beta_1 &= 3/2-2\sqrt{17}/17,\\
\beta_2 &= -1/8+65\sqrt{17}/6936,\\
\beta_3 &= 1/240-721\sqrt{17}/3537360.
\end{aligned}
$$

Set

$$
M_x = 6+(3/2)B+(1/2)\sqrt{68+16B+B^2}.
$$

Then $|\epsilon_-(x)|\le M_x$ on $|x|=2$, so $|\beta_n|\le M_x/2^{2n}$. For every chosen $0\le\rho<2$ and integer $m\ge0$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\sup_{|x|\le\rho} \Bigl|\epsilon_-(x)-\sum_{n=0}^m \beta_n x^{2n}\Bigr|\\
&\quad \le M_x (\rho/2)^{2m+2}/(1-(\rho/2)^2).
\end{aligned}
$$

This also holds on the real momentum subset $|p\delta|\le\rho$. On that spectral subspace, with $P_{N}$ the self-adjoint Fourier differentiation operator whose eigenvalues are the declared principal $p_{l}$,

$$
H_- = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \beta_n \delta^{2n} P_N^{2n},
$$

with the same uniform operator truncation bound. In trigonometric-interpolation notation $P_N^{2n}=(-\partial_x^2)^n$. The assertion is restricted to $|p\delta|\le\rho<2$; most finite rings contain modes outside it, so the ordinary derivative Taylor series is NOT used as an unproved all-mode expansion. Section 7.1 supplies the all-mode convergent alternative.

## 8. Finite Fourier interpolation, aliases, and exact finite representations

For site $x_j=j\delta$, the unitary $N$-point Fourier map uses $\exp(ip_lx_j)/\sqrt{N}$. Momenta $p$ and $p+2\pi k/\delta$ have exactly the same character on every site. Thus unrestricted continuum momentum is not observable from $N$ sampled sites: aliases are exact, not a UV approximation. Choosing $l=-q,\dots,q$ is a Brillouin representative convention; odd $N$ avoids a two-fold Nyquist representative.

Every N-by-N translation-invariant operator has an exact cyclic Fourier kernel

$$
\begin{aligned}
T_{jk} &= \tau_{j-k},\\
\tau_r &= (1/N)\sum_l T(p_l) \exp(i p_l r \delta),\quad r \bmod N.
\end{aligned}
$$

For $H_-$, $\epsilon_-(p_l)$ is real and even, so $\tau_r=\tau_{-r}$ is real. The exact low-band Hamiltonian is generally long range on the finite ring. Its exact Fourier interpolation is finite, but that does not make an arbitrary continuum interpolation unique: one can add any function vanishing at all sampled modes.

The $q+1$ numbers $s_0,\dots,s_q$ are distinct. Consequently the exact Lagrange polynomial

$$
F_N(s)=\sum_{k=0}^q F(s_k) \prod_{j\ne k}(s-s_j)/(s_k-s_j)
$$

has degree at most $q$ and satisfies $H_-=F_N(S_N)$ exactly. This finite-$N$ identity coexists with the infinite convergent expansion; $F_{N}$ depends on $N$, is not a universal continuum polynomial, and does not authorize extrapolation beyond the finite sampled spectrum.

## 9. What is and is not proved

PROVED analytically for all odd $N\ge 5$ and all $\delta>0$:

1. Exact spectra, exact finite extrema, and strict uniform band separation.
2. Exact low-code isometry, all of $M_N(\mathbb{C})$, and every finite adaptive code-preserving instrument history, including ancillas.
3. A normalized terminal failure extension for every outside-code input.
4. The exact full $M_{2N}(\mathbb{C})$ block dictionary for every microscopic operator and instrument, with exact forward/backward band-path records retaining all heavy excursions.
5. Exact bare-port Feshbach kernel, actual residue and wavefunction conversion, and the distinction from the spectral low channel.
6. Complete analytic energy and spatial series with explicit, uniform truncation remainders and correctly separated thresholds/domains.
7. Exact finite Fourier interpolation and aliasing statements.

NOT PROVED or assumed: a compressed algebra for arbitrary bare operators; a low-only Markov description of arbitrary high-exciting histories; locality of dressed operators; any continuum limit, Lorentz invariance, interacting many-body extension, physical resource cost, or source/clock implementation claim. Numerical checks below are diagnostics for selected finite cases, not substitutes for the all-N proofs.

<a id="theorem-k104e-physical-two-band-lattice-predictive-update-and-paid-estimation-source"></a>**Theorem K.10.4e (Physical Two-Band Lattice, Predictive Update and Paid Estimation Source).** The following placed source, controller and complete clock/resource instrument populate the construction on the same finite carrier. **Physical finite lattice and complete two-band EFT matching**

## 2. Actual source cells, excitation sector and Hamiltonian

Fix odd $N\ge 5$, a positive measured cell spacing $\delta$, energy $E_\star$ and time $\tau_\star=\hbar/E_\star$. Physically place $N$ addressable cells around a ring of circumference $N\delta$. $\delta$ is calibrated arc spacing of source ports. The coordinate $j\delta$ is tied to the actual addressed cell, rather than to an unrelated abstract Fourier label. The actual cyclic translation port permutes cell contents $j\to j+1$ and has the same response on translated source/readout programs.

Each cell has eight orthogonal levels: vacuum, $L$, $H$ and five unused failure levels. Define $a_{j,L}=|\mathrm{vac}\rangle\langle L|$ and $a_{j,H}=|\mathrm{vac}\rangle\langle H|$, acting on the actual tensor product. The microscopic Hamiltonian in $E_\star$ units is

$$
\begin{aligned}
H&=\sum_j[2n_{j,L}+10n_{j,H}+a^\dagger_{j,L}a_{j,H}+a^\dagger_{j,H}a_{j,L}+32P_{j,\mathrm{fail}}]\\
&\quad+\sum_j[(a_{j,L}-a_{j+1,L})^\dagger(a_{j,L}-a_{j+1,L})\\
&\quad+2(a_{j,H}-a_{j+1,H})^\dagger(a_{j,H}-a_{j+1,H})].
\end{aligned}
$$

It is positive: the onsite two-orbital matrix $\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\1&10\end{bmatrix}$ is positive, and every edge term is $B^\dagger B$. A conservative full-carrier norm bound is $44N$. Vacuum has energy zero. The total $L/H$ excitation number commutes with $H$. The invariant one-excitation code has dimension $2N$ and basis $|j,L\rangle,|j,H\rangle$. Code preparation and its success/failure instrument are actual finite unitaries/projectors; no claim about the uncontrolled multiexcitation or failure sectors is inferred from one-excitation matching.

The source comparison includes every finite computably specified preparation, unitary, instrument and effect on this code, with a complete output record. Outside-code inputs have an explicit projection/failure branch, and their physical residual states are retained in the full source record whenever subsequent queries to those states are admitted. A terminal-failure abstraction is used only for a grammar that terminates that branch. No discarded failure is assigned the success law.

The free dynamics is generated by this same H on every protocol. Source controllers and their work are separate from free lattice propagation and receive their own clock/price record.

## 3. Exact dispersion, operational cutoff and interpolation

Let $p_l=2\pi l/(N\delta)$, $l=-(N-1)/2,\dots,(N-1)/2$, and $s_l=4\sin^{2}(p_l\delta/2)$. The physical translation has character $\exp(ip_l\delta)$. The discrete Fourier transform block-diagonalizes the actual Hamiltonian into

in $E_\star$ units. This is the declared dispersion, not an assumed relativistic $E=c|p|$ law. Momentum means the calibrated translation quasimomentum $\hbar p$. Energy cutoff and momentum cutoff are related by this measured dispersion, not by an unsupported linear conversion.

The source's independent spatial coordinates are exactly the N site amplitudes per orbital. Trigonometric interpolation gives an isometry to the N-dimensional band span with these $p_{l}$. Sampling that span at the physical sites is invertible by the discrete Fourier transform. Inputs with wavenumbers differing by 2 pi/delta have identical samples and therefore the same complete source response under the declared sample-addressed input port. p_{\mathrm{cut}}=\hbar \pi(1-1/N)/\delta.
$$

Thus $\xi_{\mathrm{cut}}=\pi(1-1/N)$ is explicitly registered for this odd-$N$ finite ring. The conventional enclosing Brillouin interval is $[-\pi/\delta,\pi/\delta)$; it contains no additional source coordinate. Arbitrarily fine estimation of a parameter within this finite mode space is not an extra spatial mode. The source has no fixed finite-total-budget claim for all precisions.

Spatially distinct microscopic environments or continuous fields outside the declared address port are not declared physically identical. The cutoff is operational for this source/readout grammar. Allowing new subcell ports would change the source certificate.

## 4. Exact low/high spectral dictionary

Let $U_-$ and $U_+$ be the normalized low/high eigenvector isometries, including the physical discrete Fourier transform. Their phases are fixed by taking the low $L$ component positive. They give a unitary $U=(U_-,U_+)$ from $\mathbb{C}^N\oplus\mathbb{C}^N$ to the one-excitation carrier, and

$$
U^\dagger HU=\operatorname{diag}(H_-,H_+),\quad H_\pm=\operatorname{diag}_p \epsilon_\pm(s_p).
$$

The low band lies in $[6-\sqrt{17},12-\sqrt{37})$, and the high band in $[6+\sqrt{17},12+\sqrt{37})$. In particular their indirect gap is greater than $\sqrt{17}+\sqrt{37}-6>4.2$. The concrete energy separator $8E_\star$ lies strictly between them for every $N$. These actual thresholds define the low/high matching scheme.

For every physical operator O retain ALL FOUR blocks

$$
O_{ab}=U_a^\dagger O U_b,\quad a,b \in \{-,+\}.
$$

The full dictionary is an algebra $*$-isomorphism $O\to U^\dagger OU$. For every preparation retain all four density blocks; for every instrument retain all four blocks of every Kraus operator, including its classical output label. Their exact products use the sum over the intermediate band. Dropping that sum would be wrong.

For a finite history, insert these identities between every physical operation and free wait. Its amplitude is the finite sum over band paths of products of $O_{ab}$ and $\exp(-itH_a/\tau_\star)$. Its probability is the corresponding forward/backward path sum with the initial density blocks and final effect blocks. This is exactly the original normalized instrument law, including adaptive choices based on earlier retained outcomes. Positivity and normalization follow from its equality to the actual full instrument, rather than from termwise positivity of path amplitudes.

Eliminating the heavy band therefore gives a specified memory kernel with propagation $\exp(-itH_+/\tau_\star)$ and all the source vertices $O_{-+}$, $O_{+-}$, $O_{++}$. This exact influence record contains every heavy-mediated insertion and contact contribution. It is not asserted to be a memoryless low-band channel. Threshold excitations produced by energetic probes remain represented by these blocks.

For the physically registered low-band-preserving grammar, preparations lie in $\operatorname{ran}U_-$ and every Kraus operator preserves that subspace. Then the exact EFT Kraus operator is $U_-^\dagger KU_-$ and the free Hamiltonian is $H_-$. Every finite adaptive instrument history is identical without a heavy memory. Arbitrary instruments on $\mathbb{C}^N$ are physically realized by conjugating their dilations with $U_-$ and extending them on the full carrier, so this grammar contains the entire matrix algebra $M_{N}$, not merely its Gaussian covariance or spectral eigenvalues.

## 5. Matching coefficients, thresholds and local expansions

The bare L-port resolvent at fixed p is

$$
\begin{aligned}
&G_{LL}(z,p)=[z-a(p)-1/(z-d(p))]^{-1},\\
&a=2+s,\quad d=10+2s.
\end{aligned}
$$

This Feshbach formula retains the heavy-source denominator and all its poles/zeros with their actual signs. Its light-port residue is not generally one. At the low eigenvalue it equals the squared $L$ component of the exact low eigenvector, or equivalently $[1+1/(\epsilon_--d)^{2}]^{-1}$. The $U_-$ dictionary supplies the corresponding source normalization; one does not equate a bare $L$ probe with a canonically normalized low-band probe.

For $|z|\le E_{\mathrm{cut}}<10$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
1/(z-d) &= -\sum_{n=0}^m z^n/d^{n+1}+R_m,\\
|R_m| &\le E_{\mathrm{cut}}^{m+1}/[d^{m+1}(d-E_{\mathrm{cut}})].
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the exact mass, wavefunction and higher-time-derivative counterterms are all fixed by the same microscopic Hamiltonian. No unspecified threshold correction is fitted. The remainder is uniform over the full Brillouin zone. A bound on the self-energy alone does not bound the full resolvent at a pole; the response bound additionally records the distance to the retained poles or an explicit resolvent norm bound.

The spatial low-band action is the exact matrix $H_-$, with all $N$ Fourier coefficients retained. A derivative/local-stencil expansion is an optional truncation of that exact record. The function $\epsilon_-(s)$ is analytic away from branch points $-8\pm 2i$. A Cauchy circle of radius 8 gives an explicit uniform Taylor remainder on $0\le s\le 4$. This covers the whole finite Brillouin band, unlike a naive binomial expansion in $(16s+s^{2})/68$. Every coefficient is fixed by the closed function above. Details and explicit remainder constants are supplied in the independent algebra companion.

For a fixed finite history, approximate the full dressed Hamiltonian by $\operatorname{diag}(H_-^{(m)},H_+)$ while leaving the exact operator dictionary unchanged. If $\lVert H_-^{(m)}-H_-\rVert\le\eta E_\star$, Duhamel gives unitary error at most $\eta|t|/\tau_\star$. Channel telescoping then bounds the trace-distance error of the complete adaptive history by the sum over its actual waits and instrument errors. This controls arbitrary inserted operators without an artificial exponential loss from separately estimating every band path. The high block and all heavy source vertices remain exact in this optional approximation.

The finite single-excitation theory has no independent interaction vertices or vacuum loops beyond this complete finite matrix/influence dictionary. Gaussian functional determinants, if a second-quantized Gaussian reformulation is used, are not silently substituted for this one-excitation source. No absent interaction is assigned a fitted zero coefficient; it is excluded by the actual declared preparation/update algebra and Hamiltonian.

## 6. Actual predictive update and finite-resource admission

The source includes a real Definition 27 update on an explicit eight-dimensional controller with three binary registers for current outcome, prediction and arming/context. The local sharp binary readout and conditional memory operation are normalized instruments on this actual C8 controller, with its ordered computational-basis perspective. Larger pointer alphabets are read by finitely many such binary events with fresh retained archive slots; they are not mislabeled as one eight-dimensional outcome register.

For a concrete nonvacuous predictive loop, prepare a fair mixture of two distinct low-band energy eigenstates, for example momenta $l=0$ and $l=1$. Read their distinguishing projectors with a normalized sharp instrument, retaining the outcome and a private pointer copy. A predictor copies that outcome into its memory and commits it as its prediction for the next repeat measurement. After any declared positive free wait, the energy eigenstates retain their projector labels. The next outcome is predicted with probability1, versus1/2 for a predictor with no initial record. This is an actual source response, not an MPU label attached to a cell dimension.

The arming predicate is receipt of the registered service signal at a ready port. For each allowed instrument $\{I_i^N\}$, $I_i^N(\rho)=\sum K_{i\alpha}\rho K_{i\alpha}^\dagger$ and $\sum_{i\alpha}K_{i\alpha}^\dagger K_{i\alpha}=I$ on the declared code, with its explicit normalized outside-code extension. The displayed code instrument is implemented through the preceding actual controller events; it is not a claim that the $2N$-dimensional lattice code is itself one C8 MPU. Choose the actual measured controller basis as the perspective context. The conditional perspective kernel is $\delta$ on that context, which is normalized. The outcome-conditioned state and retained prediction memory constitute $E_{N}$ as in Definition 27. All readout and copy environments remain in the apparatus; no implicit Landauer reset is asserted.

Finite physically implemented preparation, instrument dilation, clock and epsilon-estimation records are supplied below. They establish source admission under K.10.1 without a new Definition 23 minimum claim.

## 7. Positive physical controls, clocks and source ownership

### 7.1 Finite protocol parameters

A registered query specifies N, its input state, an adaptive instrument tree of depth at most L, at most R outcomes and K Kraus operators per node, and a maximum total free-wait time $T_{\mathrm{free}}$ along every branch. A declared retained reference has finite dimension $d_{\mathrm{ref}}\ge 1$, supplied as part of the query. All matrices and times are supplied as computable coefficients with explicit precision moduli. The control program is a bounded straight-line pulse/parameter description of length at most b; no arbitrary algorithm is presumed to halt within a slot bound.

The active working Hilbert space includes the N three-qubit cells and at most

$$
A=8(L+2) \lceil\log_2(K+R+4)\rceil+\lceil\log_2(2N)\rceil+\lceil\log_2(d_{\mathrm{ref}})\rceil+64
$$

ancilla qubits for dilations, pointers, private copies, reference, context and branch records. Earlier archives can instead be stored outside the active bus and acted on by identity. Set $D_{\mathrm{work}}=2^{3N+A}$, a deliberately conservative finite dimension. Every admitted density matrix on the $2N$-dimensional code has a purification of rank at most $2N$ in the explicitly counted purification register. The separate reference allowance counts any additionally supplied retained reference; no purification claim is made about arbitrary states on $D_{\mathrm{work}}$ including their own purifier. All source/environment states, including discarded-from-the-task private pointers, remain physically accounted.

The physical control bus has a measured finite service speed $v_{\mathrm{bus}}$. Choose $\tau_0\ge\max(\tau_\star,N\delta/v_{\mathrm{bus}})$. Its programmed interactions are finite source controls, not a new relativistic propagation law. They do not identify the bus metric with the lattice free-dispersion metric. Every control pulse and every negative/controlled logical wait uses its actual positive laboratory duration.

### 7.2 Calibrated positive pulse compiler

Use the positive finite-Hamiltonian construction of F.10.4c.22 on this actual carrier. Let $H_{\mathrm{code}}=E_\star H$, extended by zero on degenerate ancillas, and $E_{\max}=44NE_\star$. Put

$$
\begin{aligned}
H_0 &= 4 \pi \hbar/\tau_0\, I+H_{\mathrm{code}},\\
R(t) &= \exp(-iH_0 t/\hbar).
\end{aligned}
$$

For a desired finite unitary $V$, choose a Hermitian logarithm $G$ with $\lVert G\rVert\le 2\pi$ and $R(\tau_0)\exp(-iG)=V$. A branch cut off the finite spectrum gives a computable choice with its certified spectral gap. Let $s(t)=3(t/\tau_0)^{2}-2(t/\tau_0)^{3}$. The control

$$
C(t)=\hbar s'(t) R(t)G R(t)^\dagger
$$

has $C(0)=C(\tau_0)=0$, $\sup\lVert C\rVert\le 3\pi\hbar/\tau_0$, and $\int\lVert C\rVert dt\le 2\pi\hbar$. The exact propagator is $R(t)\exp(-is(t)G)$; at $\tau_0$ it is $V$, including its scalar and controlled-arm phases. The total Hamiltonian stays positive because the baseline shift dominates the control norm.

A finite instrument is implemented by a Stinespring unitary, actual pointer readout, and retained private copy. A contraction uses its complete Halmos dilation with the success/failure flag retained. The finite working dimension above includes these objects. Dense controls have at most $D_{\mathrm{work}}^{2}$ complex matrix entries; finite elementary-gate decompositions are an alternative with their actual gate counts recorded. No polynomial efficiency claim is used.

The net work in one service interval is its endpoint change of $\langle H_{\mathrm{code}}\rangle$, bounded in absolute value by $E_{\max}$. For a conservative gross switching reserve, differentiating $C$ gives

$$
\int\lVert dC/dt\rVert\, dt \le 6 \pi \hbar/\tau_0+4 \pi E_{\max}.
$$

The scalar baseline $E_{\mathrm{shift}}=4\pi\hbar/\tau_0$ is retained on the active source throughout the whole padded trial, including free waits. Its initial stored energy is explicitly funded below; it is never switched off for free. It commutes and does not enter the commutator bound. If the service switches this baseline at the trial boundaries, reserve an additional $2E_{\mathrm{shift}}$ for those switches, as included below. Its common free phase cancels from ordinary density-matrix evolution, while the compiler retains every controlled-arm phase. Thus work, pulse norm, elapsed time and storage are separate finite recorded resources. The exact work record retains any negative/recovered work; it is not renamed heat.

### 7.3 Full-window resource ledger

Let

$$
\begin{aligned}
Q_{\mathrm{trial}} &= 64(L+1)(D_{\mathrm{work}}+1)^{2}(b+1),\\
W_{\mathrm{gate}} &= E_{\max}+6 \pi \hbar/\tau_0+4 \pi E_{\max},\\
E_{\mathrm{shift}} &= 4 \pi \hbar/\tau_0.
