The registered program contains no more than $Q_{\mathrm{trial}}$ service macros; unused macros are idle padding. Preparations, context changes, controlled waits, unitary extensions, source/effect dilations, pointer copies and readouts all belong to this schedule. A trial takes exactly $T_{\mathrm{trial}}=T_{\mathrm{free}}+Q_{\mathrm{trial}}\tau_0$ after padding every adaptive branch to that window. Free negative logical times are not negative physical durations: their encoded unitaries use a service macro.

For $n$ repetitions, supply fresh source copies and fresh ancillas, retaining all old records. Use total time $T_{\mathrm{run}}=nT_{\mathrm{trial}}$ and reserve

$$
B=2^{20} n Q_{\mathrm{trial}} (3N+A+b+L+1)
$$

three-level cells for record/control/payment stock in addition to the explicitly counted source copies. A common service invoice is

$$
F=\gamma B(1+T_{\mathrm{run}}/\tau_0)+n Q_{\mathrm{trial}} W_{\mathrm{gate}}+n(E_{\max}+3 E_{\mathrm{shift}}),
$$

where $\gamma>0$ is the registered storage/control price in energy units. This is a conservative quoted reservation fee, not a claim that every reserve is dissipated. It funds all initial source preparation, clock, bus, control, record and readout services in this finite instance. If a different precision or query tree requires more resources, its n,b,L,K,R and invoice change explicitly.

An owned donor/provider token pair with gap F transfers the invoice once by an excitation-conserving SWAP. Readiness is computed into a fresh saved flag before swapping, and success/failure records remain distinct. Readiness depends on stock and classical program readiness, never on a coherent interferometer arm. The token free Hamiltonians remain on and commute with the payment operation; their gap is not inserted into their own switching-work reserve. This avoids a self-referential invoice. Source/control provider, user and archive ownership are recorded; there is no assumed cyclic reset or free erasure.

## 8. Complete implementation and estimation errors

All analytic equalities above refer to the ideal controlled source. For a finite implementation, a gate with operator-norm error $\eta$ has completely bounded output trace-norm error at most $2\eta$, including arbitrary retained reference systems. A free-wait coefficient/Hamiltonian error $\delta H$ gives unitary error at most $|t|\,\lVert\delta H\rVert/\hbar$; clock error $\Delta t$ adds $|\Delta t|\,\lVert H\rVert/\hbar$. The same bounds apply to the exact spectral dictionary and its physical basis-change compiler. Matrix-function approximation uses the explicit gap and analytic eigenvector formulas, not an unstable arbitrary eigenbasis choice at a degeneracy.

For an adaptive tree, use the sum of errors along the worst allowed branch, or an explicit full-tree instrument-channel bound. Store the classical history as part of the quantum-classical output. Contractivity and telescoping then bound the complete output trace norm, including failures and private reference correlations. A bound for an unnormalized successful branch is not assigned unchanged to a normalized postselected state; the latter requires its actual success-probability denominator.

For a bounded registered Hermitian score $O$ on the complete retained output, let $B_O\ge\max(1,\lVert O\rVert)$. Exact finite instruments estimate its expectation; a normalized Halmos/interferometric readout can alternatively use outcomes in $[-B_O,B_O]$, with failure outcomes retained as specified. Fix requested additive error $\epsilon>0$ and failure probability $0<\zeta<1$. Choose the spatial/energy EFT truncation and physical control precision so that each contributes at most $\epsilon/3$ to the score expectation. For example a complete output trace-norm error at most $\epsilon/(3B_O)$ suffices for one contribution. Errors are controlled for the entire finite adaptive history, using its bounded total wait time.

Choose

$$
n\ge 18 B_O^{2} \epsilon^{-2} \log(2/\zeta).
$$

Hoeffding's inequality for independent fresh trials gives sampling error at most epsilon/3 with probability at least 1−zeta. Summing the two certified biases and sampling error gives the registered $\epsilon$ guarantee. Exact matching permits setting the EFT bias to zero; no asymptotic series is required when the exact finite matrices are used. Other requested confidence conventions must be registered separately. The estimate is always a finite real output.

Every such source protocol has a finite program description, finite matrix/precision record, finite number of source cells and ancillas, finite energy bound, finite physical duration, and finite paid rate $F/T_{\mathrm{run}}$. Its program supplies a finite upper bound on predictive description complexity in the admitted source grammar; no attained minimum or equality of complexity with a qubit count is asserted. Together with the actual $E_{N}$ instrument of Section 6, this instantiates the finite-resource K.10.1 admission condition for every fixed $\epsilon$ and $\zeta$. The growing family of precision-dependent instances is not advertised as one fixed total-budget device.

## 9. Exact scope and falsification targets

The physical substrate's retained one-excitation source algebra is finite and complete. The discrete Fourier band is a registered operational representation of that source, with actual spacing, translation, dispersion and clock calibration. Exact low-band matching contains every low-band-preserving instrument. The complete bare-operator matching retains all heavy blocks and all finite histories, with their threshold memory. No uncontrolled heavy-mediated effect is discarded.

The complete operator/counterterm record is the exact finite matrix/function dictionary plus the optional controlled expansions. It is not a Gaussian two-jet. The absence of unrelated interaction vertices is a fact about the declared microscopic source, not a theorem about arbitrary physical EFTs. The cutoff is neither a universal Planck bound nor a claim that all outside physical environments are absent.

Falsifiers include an input pair with identical admitted site data but different registered response; a violation of the stated spectral separation; a full history absent from the dressed block sum; an omitted heavy contact/source term; a failed uniform residual away from its stated poles; an unpriced or unbounded control/clock entry; or an $\epsilon$ protocol missing its normalized failure record.

<a id="definition-k104a-hadamard-subtracted-microlocal-admissibility-functional"></a>**Definition K.10.4a (Hadamard-Subtracted Microlocal Admissibility Functional).** Let $U$ be a relatively compact normal neighborhood in the regular AQFT branch of Theorem F.10.2. Let $\omega_2$ be the two-point distribution of a quasifree local state on $U$, and let $H_U$ be the local Hadamard parametrix with the same antisymmetric commutator singularity. Define the Hadamard-subtracted remainder
$$
r_U:=\omega_2-H_U.
\tag{K.10.4a.1}
$$
Choose a countable family $\{Q_j\}_{j\ge1}$ of properly supported order-zero pseudodifferential cutoffs with compact base localization such that their elliptic sets cover $T^*(U\times U)\setminus0$. For every integer Sobolev order $m\ge0$, define the ordinary Sobolev norm
$$
N_{j,m}(r_U):=\lVert Q_jr_U\rVert_{H^m(U\times U)}.
$$
The compact base localization makes this a numerical norm, and elliptic coverage ensures that finiteness for every $j,m$ detects every nonzero wavefront direction.
The local microlocal regularity functional is
$$
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{Had}}(\omega;U)
:=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{j,m\ge1}2^{-j-m}
\frac{N_{j,m}(r_U)}{1+N_{j,m}(r_U)},
&
N_{j,m}(r_U)<\infty\ \text{for all }j,m,\\[1.2em]
+\infty,
&
\text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\tag{K.10.4a.2}
$$
The global regularity condition holds when (K.10.4a.2) is finite on every normal-neighborhood member of an admissible finite cover.

<a id="theorem-k104b-hadamard-microlocal-regularity-gate"></a>**Theorem K.10.4b (Hadamard Microlocal Regularity Gate).** On the regular quasifree AQFT branch, the functional $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{Had}}(\omega;U)$ of Definition K.10.4a is finite if and only if the two-point function $\omega_2$ of the state $\omega$ is Hadamard:
$$
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{Had}}(\omega;U)<\infty
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\omega_2\ \text{is Hadamard on }U.
\tag{K.10.4b.1}
$$
Equivalently,
$$
\operatorname{WF}(\omega_2)
=
\{(x,k_x;y,-k_y):(x,k_x)\sim(y,k_y),\ k_x\in\overline V^+_x\}
\tag{K.10.4b.2}
$$
on the regular branch. This is a registered continuum regularity criterion, not a resource-derived PCE cost. A physical PCE interpretation or exclusion of non-Hadamard states requires an independent protocol-to-Sobolev-complexity bridge.

*Proof.* A distribution $u$ is smooth on $U\times U$ if and only if every microlocal cutoff $Q_j u$ belongs to $H^m_{\mathrm{loc}}(U\times U)$ for every $m\ge0$. The family $\{Q_j\}$ covers all nonzero cotangent directions, so this criterion applies to $r_U=\omega_2-H_U$.

If $\omega_2$ is Hadamard, the local Hadamard theorem gives
$$
\omega_2=H_U+s_U
$$
with $s_U\in C^\infty(U\times U)$. Hence $r_U=s_U$, so $N_{j,m}(r_U)<\infty$ for all $j,m$. The sum in (K.10.4a.2) is then bounded by
$$
\sum_{j,m\ge1}2^{-j-m}<\infty,
$$
and $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{Had}}(\omega;U)<\infty$.

Conversely, suppose $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{Had}}(\omega;U)<\infty$. Then every $N_{j,m}(r_U)$ is finite. Hence $Q_jr_U$ is in all local Sobolev spaces for every $j$. Since the $Q_j$ cover every nonzero cotangent direction, $r_U$ has empty wavefront set. Thus $r_U$ is smooth. Therefore $\omega_2$ differs from the local Hadamard parametrix by a smooth remainder, which is equivalent to the microlocal Hadamard spectrum condition (K.10.4b.2).

If $\omega_2$ is not Hadamard, then $r_U$ is not smooth on some normal neighborhood. Its wavefront set contains a nonzero covector. Some $Q_j$ is elliptic on a conic neighborhood of that covector, so $Q_jr_U$ is not in $H^m_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for some $m$. By Definition K.10.4a the cost is $+\infty$. ∎

<a id="corollary-k104c-stress-energy-and-null-energy-regularity-gate"></a>**Corollary K.10.4c (Stress-Energy and Null-Energy Regularity Gate).** The MPU stress-energy source construction, the local Rindler/KMS horizon branch, and the predictive null-energy inequality have the stated point-split continuum representatives on their respective physical branches with the Hadamard microlocal condition. On that sector the smooth Hadamard-subtracted remainder supplies all local derivatives required in the point-split stress tensor and Wick powers. Outside that sector, Theorem K.10.4b does not guarantee these representatives; the existence of a particular finite-order coincidence limit requires a separate regularity analysis.

*Proof.* The point-splitting construction subtracts the universal Hadamard singularity before taking the coincidence limit. By Theorem K.10.4b the subtracted remainder is smooth exactly on the Hadamard microlocal sector, so every finite-order local derivative required by the stated constructions exists there. Failure of smoothness means that some regularity order fails; it does not imply failure of every lower-order derivative or coincidence limit. The theorem therefore supplies the Hadamard sufficient regularity gate without excluding every finite-order point-split quantity outside that sector. ∎

<a id="theorem-k105-conditional-operational-continuum-exit-boundary"></a>**Theorem K.10.5 (Conditional Operational Continuum-Exit Boundary).** Assume jointly: (i) the microscopic lattice or bandlimit and matching certificate of Theorem K.10.4; (ii) the framed Fermi-expansion certificate of Lemma K.5.3 at resolution $\delta$; and (iii) the finite-area boundary-link and clock hypotheses of Theorem K.5.1. Then the cited continuum representation loses its PU certificate whenever it requires independent modes beyond the certified bandlimit, continuation of the controlled Fermi expansion after its remainder bound fails, or unbounded retained information throughput through the fixed finite boundary. This is an operational domain-of-validity theorem. It does not prove that every continuum loop integral is finite, remove ordinary renormalization, prove that curvature singularities are absent, or construct a horizon, bounce, or successor state.

| Continuum extrapolation | Formal expression | Certified operational boundary |
|:------------------------|:------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Trans-bandlimit QFT modes | $k>k_{\mathrm{cut}}$, with $k_{\mathrm{cut}}$ supplied by the registered bandlimit | Theorem K.10.4's lattice/bandlimit and matching certificate |
| Strong-curvature local expansion | $\|R\|_{\mathrm{fr},\delta}\to\infty$ | Loss of Lemma K.5.3's sufficient Fermi-expansion estimate |
| Finite-area information extraction | unbounded $I/T$ through fixed $A(S)$ | Theorem K.5.1's finite-link, finite-capacity, positive-clock bound |

*Proof.* Under item (i), Theorem K.10.4 removes independent retained modes beyond the registered bandlimit and controls their effect on retained observables by its matching theorem. Without item (i), $\hbar/\delta$ is only a comparison scale. Under item (ii), Lemma K.5.3 gives the sufficient control conditions
$$
C_1\|R\|_{\mathrm{fr},\delta}\delta^2\ll1,
\qquad
C_2\delta^3\ll1.
$$
If the framewise norm diverges along a curve with the same positive coefficient $C_1$ and the same resolution $\delta>0$ throughout, the first condition eventually fails, as in Theorem K.5.4; this proves loss of that local expansion certificate and nothing about the microscopic continuation. Under item (iii), Theorem K.5.1 gives a finite throughput bound proportional to the finite effective link count. Hence a protocol demanding unbounded retained throughput lies outside that certified channel class. These are three instances of certificate exit, not proofs that the corresponding mathematical continuum objects cease to exist. ∎

<a id="corollary-k105a-finite-substrate-cutoff-and-continuum-exit-wall"></a>**Corollary K.10.5a (Finite-Substrate Cutoff and Continuum-Exit Wall).** On the residual-budget, throughput-saturated, ideal-packing branch of Appendix Q, the MPU spacing is
$$
\delta=\sqrt{8\ln2}\,L_P
$$
and the corresponding MPU comparison momentum scale (Definition K.10.3) is
$$
\Lambda_{\mathrm{MPU}}
=
\frac{\hbar}{\delta}
=
\frac{m_Pc}{\sqrt{8\ln2}}.
$$

On a branch carrying Theorem K.10.4's microscopic lattice or bandlimit and matching certificate, the physical momentum cutoff is $\Lambda_{\mathrm{cut}}=\xi_{\mathrm{cut}}\hbar/\delta$ with $\xi_{\mathrm{cut}}>0$ specified by that certificate. The displayed comparison scale equals the cutoff only on the registered normalization $\xi_{\mathrm{cut}}=1$. Without that certificate it imposes no hard support condition on a continuum Fourier transform. Consequently, on the respective certified branches:

1. **No modes beyond the certified bandlimit.** With angular wavenumber $k$ and reduced wavelength $\bar\lambda:=1/k$, the momentum condition $p>\Lambda_{\mathrm{cut}}=\xi_{\mathrm{cut}}\hbar/\delta$ is equivalent to
   $$
   k>\xi_{\mathrm{cut}}\delta^{-1}
   \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
   \bar\lambda<\delta/\xi_{\mathrm{cut}}.
   $$
   For ordinary wavelength $\lambda:=2\pi/k$, the equivalent condition is $\lambda<2\pi\delta/\xi_{\mathrm{cut}}$. The ultraviolet lattice or bandlimit and matching certificate of Theorem K.10.4 excludes these modes as independent retained degrees of freedom. The thresholds $p>\Lambda_{\mathrm{MPU}}$ and $\bar\lambda<\delta$ coincide with these certified thresholds only when $\xi_{\mathrm{cut}}=1$.

2. **Exit of the certified local curvature expansion.** On a branch satisfying Lemma K.5.3, let
   $$
   \|R\|_{\mathrm{fr},\delta}
   =\sup_{x\in U_\delta}\max_{a,b,c,d}|R_{abcd}(x)|
   $$
   in the declared parallel orthonormal frame. The sufficient Fermi-expansion certificate requires
   $$
   C_1\|R\|_{\mathrm{fr},\delta}\delta^2\ll1,
   \qquad
   C_2\delta^3\ll1.
   $$
   A trajectory with constant $C_1>0$ and constant $\delta>0$, along which $\|R\|_{\mathrm{fr},\delta}\to\infty$, exits this certificate at a finite value of the framewise curvature scale. No single Lorentzian scalar contraction is used as an equivalent tensor norm.

3. **Finite-area throughput bound.** On Theorem K.5.1's finite-link, no-bypass, memoryless-channel, aggregate-capacity, and positive-clock branch, exterior-accessible information throughput through a finite-area boundary $S$ is bounded. A continuum extrapolation demanding unbounded retained information flux through that boundary lies outside the certified protocol class. A finite rate bound alone does not bound the information accumulated over an unbounded elapsed time.

The resulting obstruction is a **continuum-exit wall**: the cited continuum, curvature-expansion, or finite-throughput description cannot be asserted beyond the domain of its registered certificate. The corollary does not prove a smooth bounce, horizon, absence of a curvature singularity, or post-wall successor dynamics; those require additional theorems.

*Proof.* The value
$$
\delta=\sqrt{8\ln2}\,L_P
$$
is Equation Q.18 on the residual-budget, throughput-saturated, ideal-packing branch. Definition K.10.3 gives the comparison momentum
$$
\Lambda_{\mathrm{MPU}}=\hbar/\delta.
$$

For item 1, Theorem K.10.3a excludes exact uniformly refinable distinctions for one instantiation carrying its finite-total-distinguishability certificate. The stronger exclusion at $p>\Lambda_{\mathrm{cut}}$ uses the additional lattice or bandlimit and matching certificate of Theorem K.10.4. Since $\xi_{\mathrm{cut}}>0$, the displayed wavenumber and wavelength thresholds follow by division and inversion. Replacing $\Lambda_{\mathrm{cut}}$ by $\Lambda_{\mathrm{MPU}}$ requires the registered normalization $\xi_{\mathrm{cut}}=1$.

For item 2, Lemma K.5.3 supplies only the sufficient framed estimates
$$
C_1\|R\|_{\mathrm{fr},\delta}\delta^2\ll1,
\qquad
C_2\delta^3\ll1.
$$
At constant $C_1>0$ and constant $\delta>0$, divergence of $\|R\|_{\mathrm{fr},\delta}$ forces exit from that certificate at finite framewise curvature. It does not prove failure of every manifold description or determine a microscopic continuation.

For item 3, Theorem K.5.1 supplies its rate bound under the stated channel, aggregate-capacity, and clock hypotheses. A positive finite rate is compatible with arbitrarily much accumulated information if elapsed time is unbounded. Theorem K.5.4 proves loss of the Fermi certificate, not a capacity-saturation/horizon dichotomy. Thus all three items are conditional operational scope boundaries. ∎

<a id="definition-k105b-mpu-diffusion-certificate"></a>**Definition K.10.5b (MPU Diffusion Certificate).** A branch supplies an **MPU diffusion certificate** when it specifies finite response data
$$
\mathcal D_{\mathrm{MPU}}
=
(G_\delta,m,\Delta_{\mathrm{MPU}},K_\sigma)
$$
with the following components:

1. a finite or locally finite MPU graph or network $G_\delta$ with operational edge scale $\delta$;

2. a positive vertex or cell measure $m$;

3. a Markov or heat generator $\Delta_{\mathrm{MPU}}$ on retained scalar response classes, with the corresponding semigroup
   $$
   K_\sigma=e^{-\sigma\Delta_{\mathrm{MPU}}},
   $$
   where $\sigma$ is diffusion time with dimensions of length squared;

4. positivity preservation and mass conservation:
   $$
   K_\sigma f\ge0\quad\text{when }f\ge0,
   \qquad
   K_\sigma 1=1;
   $$

5. a return kernel
   $$
   P_\sigma(x,x)
   :=
   K_\sigma(x,x)
   $$
   defined with respect to $m$;

6. compatibility with the finite MPU propagation and locality bounds of Appendix E / Appendix F;

7. on continuum branches, a convergence statement identifying the mesoscopic limit of $\Delta_{\mathrm{MPU}}$ with a Laplace-type diffusion operator on the emergent regular manifold.

On such a branch, the local spectral dimension at probe scale $\ell$ is defined by
$$
D_s(x,\ell)
:=
-2
\left.
\frac{\partial\ln P_\sigma(x,x)}
{\partial\ln\sigma}
\right|_{\sigma=\ell^2}.
\tag{K.10.5b.1}
$$

If a spatial average over a finite region $U$ is required, define
$$
\overline D_s(U,\ell)
:=
-2
\left.
\frac{\partial}{\partial\ln\sigma}
\ln
\left(
\frac{1}{m(U)}
\sum_{x\in U}m_xP_\sigma(x,x)
\right)
\right|_{\sigma=\ell^2}.
\tag{K.10.5b.2}
$$

Without an MPU diffusion certificate, $D_s$ is not a PU-defined observable. A Lieb--Robinson or serialized-propagation bound supplies locality and finite signal speed; it does not by itself define a diffusion semigroup or a heat-kernel return probability.

<a id="theorem-k105c-cutoff-and-serialized-propagation-do-not-determine-spectral-dimension"></a>**Theorem K.10.5c (Cutoff and Serialized Propagation Do Not Determine Spectral Dimension).** The intrinsic MPU cutoff
$$
\delta
$$
and the serialized propagation bound
$$
v_{\max}=\delta/\tau_{\min}
$$
do not determine the cutoff-scale spectral dimension.

More precisely, the data
$$
(\delta,\tau_{\min},v_{\max})
$$
together with nearest-neighbor locality or a Lieb--Robinson-type finite-propagation constraint are insufficient to derive a theorem-level value or interval such as
$$
D_s(\delta)\in[1,2].
$$

A theorem-level statement about $D_s(\ell)$ requires an MPU diffusion certificate in the sense of Definition K.10.5b.

*Proof.* The serialized propagation bound controls how quickly operational influence can cross MPU links. It is a causal or locality constraint. Spectral dimension, by contrast, is defined from the logarithmic scaling of the heat-kernel return probability
$$
P_\sigma(x,x).
$$
These are distinct data.

To compare the diffusion response at the stated probe scale, take
$$
X_d=(\mathbb Z/3\mathbb Z)^d,\qquad d\in\{1,4\},
$$
with edge length $\delta$, normalized vertex measure $m_d(x)=3^{-d}$, and the same physical rule permitting at most one edge traversal per update time $\tau_{\min}$. Both physical update models have the serialized bound $v_{\max}=\delta/\tau_{\min}$. Supply, independently, the nearest-neighbor diffusion generator
$$
(\Delta_df)(x)=\delta^{-2}\sum_{a=1}^d
\bigl(2f(x)-f(x+e_a)-f(x-e_a)\bigr).
$$
The matrix $-\Delta_d$ has nonnegative off-diagonal entries and zero row sums, so $e^{-\sigma\Delta_d}$ preserves positivity and mass. Diffusion time $\sigma$ is the probe parameter of Definition K.10.5b; this heat semigroup is not identified with real-time signal propagation. Relating it to the physical update clock is additional diffusion-certificate data.

For one coordinate, the three Fourier eigenvalues are $0,3/\delta^2,3/\delta^2$. The product Fourier basis therefore gives the diagonal kernel with respect to $m_d$,
$$
P^{(d)}_\sigma(x,x)=\left(1+2e^{-3\sigma/\delta^2}\right)^d.
$$
This is the same finite Fourier construction as Theorem K.10.5f, with three sites per direction and the displayed spacing. Differentiating its logarithm at $\sigma=\delta^2$ gives
$$
D_s^{(d)}(\delta)
=\frac{12d\,e^{-3}}{1+2e^{-3}}.
$$
Thus
$$
D_s^{(1)}(\delta)=0.543342\ldots<1,
\qquad
D_s^{(4)}(\delta)=2.173368\ldots>2.
$$
For the strict inequalities, $10<e^3<22$ suffices. The lower bound follows from the first four terms of the exponential series; the sum through degree six is $19.4125$, and its remaining tail is at most $(3^7/7!)/(1-3/8)<0.695$, proving the upper bound.

These finite diffusion completions share the spacing and serialized physical speed but have different cutoff-scale logarithmic return derivatives, including values outside $[1,2]$. Hence those data alone determine neither the value nor that interval. Identifying either completion with a realized MPU diffusion process, including its locality and physical-clock compatibility, requires the separate certificate of Definition K.10.5b. ∎

<a id="corollary-k105d-continuum-spectral-dimension-under-a-quantitative-heat-kernel-certificate"></a>**Corollary K.10.5d (Continuum Spectral Dimension under a Quantitative Heat-Kernel Certificate).** Suppose a branch satisfies the operational-continuum package of Theorem 43.5, the regular-manifold closure hypotheses of Theorem 44a, and the four-dimensional tangent-cell selector of Theorem Z.11, and supplies an MPU diffusion certificate together with the quantitative diagonal heat-kernel estimate
$$
P_\sigma(x,x)=(4\pi\sigma)^{-2}[1+r_\delta(x,\sigma)]
$$
throughout $\delta^2\ll\sigma\ll L_{\mathrm{curv}}^2$, where $|r_\delta|\le1/2$ and
$$
|r_\delta(x,\sigma)|
+
\left|\sigma\partial_\sigma r_\delta(x,\sigma)\right|
\le
C\left(\frac{\sigma}{L_{\mathrm{curv}}^2}+\frac{\delta^2}{\sigma}\right).
$$
Then
$$
D_s(x,\sqrt\sigma)
=4+O\left(\frac{\sigma}{L_{\mathrm{curv}}^2}\right)
+O\left(\frac{\delta^2}{\sigma}\right).
$$

*Proof.* Taking logarithms gives
$$
\ln P_\sigma=-2\ln(4\pi\sigma)+\ln(1+r_\delta).
$$
Hence
$$
-2\frac{\partial\ln P_\sigma}{\partial\ln\sigma}
=4-\frac{2\sigma\partial_\sigma r_\delta}{1+r_\delta}.
$$
Because $|r_\delta|\le1/2$, one has $|1+r_\delta|^{-1}\le2$. The derivative bound therefore yields
$$
|D_s-4|
\le4C\left(\frac{\sigma}{L_{\mathrm{curv}}^2}+\frac{\delta^2}{\sigma}\right),
$$
which proves the result. ∎

<a id="remark-k105e-status-of-dimensional-flow-and-bounce-claims"></a>**Remark K.10.5e (Status of Dimensional Flow and Bounce Claims).** Corollary K.10.5a proves a finite-substrate cutoff and continuum-exit wall. It does not prove a smooth bounce, nor does it specify the post-wall MPU successor dynamics.

Definition K.10.5b and Theorem K.10.5c show that spectral dimension is not determined by the cutoff alone. A scale-dependent spectral-dimension flow
$$
D_s(\ell)
$$
requires a branch supplying an explicit MPU diffusion certificate. If that branch also satisfies the continuum, regular-manifold, four-dimensional selector, and quantitative heat-kernel hypotheses of Corollary K.10.5d, then
$$
D_s\to4
$$
in the joint mesoscopic limit $\delta^2/\sigma\to0$ and $\sigma/L_{\mathrm{curv}}^2\to0$. The cutoff-scale endpoint
$$
D_s(\delta)
$$
and any monotone interpolation between $D_s(\ell\gg\delta)=4$ and $D_s(\delta)$ remain branch-level until the discrete MPU diffusion generator is explicitly computed.

Thus the theorem-level PU content is:

1. the comparison spacing on Equation Q.18's branch,
   $$
   \delta=\sqrt{8\ln2}\,L_P;
   $$

2. non-instantiation of modes beyond the bandlimit certified under Theorem K.10.4: for $k_{\mathrm{cut}}=\xi_{\mathrm{cut}}/\delta$ with $\xi_{\mathrm{cut}}>0$, this means reduced wavelength $\bar\lambda<\delta/\xi_{\mathrm{cut}}$; the sub-$\delta$ threshold uses the registered normalization $\xi_{\mathrm{cut}}=1$;

3. the finite-area throughput bound for the registered channel-and-clock class;

4. exit of the sufficient framed Fermi certificate when its explicit tolerance is exceeded;

5. the requirement of a diffusion certificate before any spectral-dimension endpoint can be claimed.

This is an operational finite-substrate result.

<a id="theorem-k105f-exact-four-torus-diffusion-and-scale-uniform-heat-trace-limit"></a>**Theorem K.10.5f (Exact Four-Torus Diffusion and Scale-Uniform Heat-Trace Limit).** For $N\ge3$, let
$$
X_N=(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^4,
\qquad
\delta_N=N^{-1},
\qquad
m_N(x)=N^{-4},
\tag{K.10.5f.1}
$$
and define the positive nearest-neighbor graph Laplacian
$$
(\Delta_Nf)(x)
=N^2\sum_{a=1}^4
\bigl(2f(x)-f(x+e_a)-f(x-e_a)\bigr).
\tag{K.10.5f.2}
$$
Then $K_{N,\sigma}=e^{-\sigma\Delta_N}$ preserves positivity and mass, and its diagonal kernel with respect to $m_N$ is independent of $x$ and equals
$$
P_N(\sigma)
=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z_N^4}e^{-\sigma\lambda_N(k)},
\qquad
\lambda_N(k)=4N^2\sum_{a=1}^4
\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\pi k_a}{N}\right).
\tag{K.10.5f.3}
$$
Its exact spectral-dimension flow is
$$
D_{s,N}(\sqrt\sigma)
=2\sigma
\frac{\sum_k\lambda_N(k)e^{-\sigma\lambda_N(k)}}
     {\sum_k e^{-\sigma\lambda_N(k)}}.
\tag{K.10.5f.4}
$$
For every $0<\sigma_0<\sigma_1<\infty$, both $P_N$ and $\partial_\sigma P_N$ converge uniformly on $[\sigma_0,\sigma_1]$ to the unit flat four-torus heat trace
$$
P_\infty(\sigma)
=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^4}e^{-4\pi^2\sigma|k|^2},
\tag{K.10.5f.5}
$$
and $D_{s,N}\to D_{s,\infty}$ uniformly there. Moreover,
$$
\lim_{\substack{\sigma_N\downarrow0\\N^2\sigma_N\to\infty}}
D_{s,N}(\sqrt{\sigma_N})=4,
\tag{K.10.5f.6}
$$
while for every fixed finite $N$,
$$
\lim_{\sigma\downarrow0}D_{s,N}(\sqrt\sigma)=0,
\qquad
\lim_{\sigma\to\infty}D_{s,N}(\sqrt\sigma)=0.
\tag{K.10.5f.7}
$$
Thus this fully specified finite graph has an exact zero-dimensional ultraviolet endpoint, a four-dimensional mesoscopic window, and a zero-dimensional compact-volume infrared endpoint. No monotonicity is asserted.

*Proof.* Fourier characters diagonalize (K.10.5f.2) and give (K.10.5f.3). The matrix $Q_N:=-\Delta_N$ has nonnegative off-diagonal entries, zero row sums and nearest-neighbor support, so $e^{\sigma Q_N}=e^{-\sigma\Delta_N}$ is a Markov semigroup. Differentiating the finite heat trace gives (K.10.5f.4).

Choose symmetric representatives $|k_a|\le N/2$. For such representatives,
$$
16|k|^2\le\lambda_N(k)\le4\pi^2|k|^2,
$$
and $\lambda_N(k)\to4\pi^2|k|^2$ for every fixed $k$. Gaussian domination therefore applies simultaneously to the trace and its derivative, uniformly for $\sigma\in[\sigma_0,\sigma_1]$, proving (K.10.5f.5) and the uniform quotient limit.

For $N^{-2}\ll\sigma_N\ll1$, split the sum at $|k|=R/\sqrt{\sigma_N}$. On the inner part,
$$
\lambda_N(k)=4\pi^2|k|^2
+O(|k|^4/N^2)
$$
uniformly, and $N^2\sigma_N\to\infty$ makes the exponent error vanish after first fixing $R$. The outer part is uniformly Gaussian-small. Poisson summation for the limiting lattice sum gives
$$
P_N(\sigma_N)=(4\pi\sigma_N)^{-2}(1+o(1)),
\qquad
\sigma_N\partial_{\sigma}P_N(\sigma_N)
=-2P_N(\sigma_N)(1+o(1)),
$$
which proves (K.10.5f.6). At fixed $N$, the finite numerator in (K.10.5f.4) is multiplied by $\sigma$ as $\sigma\downarrow0$, while as $\sigma\to\infty$ every positive eigenmode is exponentially suppressed and only the zero mode remains. This proves (K.10.5f.7). ∎

<a id="definition-k105g-qualified-mpu-local-attempt-torus-source"></a>**Definition K.10.5g (Qualified-MPU Local-Attempt Torus Source).** Fix the following ideal finite-source family, the local-attempt torus source. Each finite grade has the following complete source, operational geometry, independently calibrated clocks, local primitives, retained outputs and positive resource tariff.

### 1. Actual cores, supplied physical geometry, and finite grades

For every integer $N\ge 3$ let $V_N=(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^4$, $M=N^4$, and let $E_{N}$ contain the $8M$ directed nearest-neighbor edges $e=(x,x\pm e_j)$, $j=1,\dots,4$. These fixtures, their labels, preparation records and retained local readout are purchased below. A comparison of different $N$ holds $L$ fixed. The normalized counting measure is $m_N(x)=N^{-4}$; it is a mathematical normalization, not the physical mass or procurement price of a host.

Each node owns a complete independent canonical R14 ready apparatus, with the nominal motor, predictor, environment, protected archive, three snapshots/verifier calls, timing supply, counters, shadows, ROM and energy stocks. Its semantics is the normative specification R14-ByteExact-StackSemantics-v2 of Definition 2.4.1i, with the source law of Definition 2.4.1g and Theorem 2.4.1h. Each node also owns its two-state token occupancy $O_{x}$, its eight outgoing edge banks/ports, and the independent paid delivered-prediction module below. Incoming edge ports may act on $O_{x}$ but never on any core variable. Every edge bank is physically assigned to its origin node. The complete Hilbert carrier is a finite tensor product of these node factors, with a classical/diagonal operational grammar.

A finite descriptor is indexed by $(N,L,\sigma_{\max},B)$, with $\sigma_{\max}>0$, $B$ a positive integer, physical directed-edge attempt rate $\kappa=1\,\text{second}^{-1}$, and live horizon

$$
T_N = \sigma_{\mathrm{max}}/(\kappa\delta_N^{2}).
$$

Here $\sigma$ is the diffusive observation parameter, with physical units length squared; it is not silently identified with laboratory seconds. Each individual descriptor has finite $T_{N}$, finite installed stocks and finite prices. No resource bound uniform in $N$, $B$ or $T_{N}$ is claimed. The ideal heat-limit comparison fixes $\sigma$ while physical observation time grows as $\delta_N^{-2}$. It does not assert a nontrivial fixed-physical-time continuum limit.

### 2. Local actual finite attempts and the exact classical marginal

Before activation, prepare exactly one occupied token, at a supplied basis node x0, and zero occupancy elsewhere. The label x0 is a finite preparation-menu input; its preparation receipt is retained. A diagonal mixture of such preparations is also allowed if its finite probability law and preparation are supplied and charged. No unknown quantum state is needed. During the live window each directed edge has its own independent Poisson attempt clock of physical rate $\kappa$. A regular attempt applies the deterministic local token rule

$$
(O_x,O_y)=10 \to 01;\quad 00,01,11 \to \text{themselves}.
$$

The moving component is the usual local $\sigma_y^+\sigma_x^-$ jump. The complete admitted attempt instrument additionally contains retained no-move attempts. These have genuine clock, record and energy costs. The independent clocks never inspect the core, future target, readout coin or other edge histories. The complete uncapped network attempt rate is $\Lambda_N=8M\kappa$. In the one-excitation sector only the occupied node's eight outward edges change occupancy, so the token's actual move hazard is $8\kappa$. These two rates are different.

For the ideal uncapped token law $p_x(t)=\Pr(O_x(t)=1)$, the local update rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
d p_x/dt &= \kappa \sum_{y\sim x}(p_y-p_x) \\
&= -\kappa\delta_N^{2} (\Delta_N p)_x, \\
\Delta_N f(x)&=\delta_N^{-2} \sum_{j=1}^{4} [2f(x)-f(x+e_j)-f(x-e_j)].
\end{aligned}
$$

The same generator acts on a single-token test function. The heat equation in the rescaled coordinate $\sigma=\kappa\delta_N^2t$ is therefore $dp/d\sigma=-\Delta_Np$. For each directed edge, let $a=4\lceil\log_2 N\rceil$, $c=\lceil\log_2(B+2)\rceil$, and $r=2a+c+6$. $$

Initially $n_e=z_e=0$, $q_e=B+1$, all slots/overflow zero. When $n_e<B$, the next native attempt applies the local token rule, writes the next fresh slot and increments $n_e,z_e$ while decrementing $q_{e}$. For a literal finite open realization, enumerate the valid active basis states s of the two endpoint occupancy bits and this edge bank. For each supply the native rank-one channel

where $F_{e}$ is exactly the full update above. The sum of $J^*J$ is $\kappa$ times the active-sector projector. ### 3. Finite-cap comparison, locality, and the actual observation cut

Couple the finite and uncapped systems using the same independent per-edge clocks and initial token. They agree until the first local overflow attempt. <a id="theorem-k105h-same-source-diffusion-calibrated-cutoff-and-prediction-response-export"></a>**Theorem K.10.5h (Same-Source Diffusion, Calibrated Cutoff and Prediction-Response Export).** The family of Definition K.10.5g realizes the retained scalar generator and all-mode four-torus family of Theorem K.10.5f under the physical conversion $\sigma=\kappa\delta_N^2t$. Every finite horizon and precision has a finite paid realization with controlled return/derivative/flow error; the calibrated cutoff, original compact-time/mesoscopic limits and actual delivered-prediction exporter are as follows.

*Proof.*

### 1. Same network, calibrated units and original generator

For every integer $N\ge 3$ fix $V_N=(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^4$ with $n=N^4$ vertices. Each vertex contains an unchanged qualified MPU core and a separate paid local occupancy register. One excitation is prepared at a registered origin $o$. The declared physical operational four-torus has circumference $L>0$ in each marked direction and edge length $\delta_N=L/N$. $L$ is an independent native length calibration; its supplied marked geometry is an express source assumption, not a deduction from an integer graph. There is no claim of embedding this four-dimensional metric isometrically into three-dimensional Euclidean laboratory space.

Every directed nearest-neighbor edge owns a local native attempt clock of independently calibrated rate $\kappa>0$ per physical second. At an attempt it transfers occupancy $10\to 01$ and otherwise leaves occupancies unchanged; every attempt, including a self attempt, appends its local record and consumes its owned resource quantum. The complete uncapped attempt rate is $\Lambda_N=8n\kappa$, not $8\kappa$. The single excitation nevertheless moves to each neighbor with rate $\kappa$. Its actual uncapped marginal generator is

$$
Q_N f(x)=\kappa \sum_{a=1}^4[f(x+e_a)+f(x-e_a)-2f(x)].
$$

The physical heat-clock conversion is $D_N=\kappa\delta_N^{2}$, $\sigma=D_Nt$, with $\sigma$ in $\text{length}^{2}$ and $t$ in seconds. Thus $Q_N=-D_N\Delta_N$, where

$$
\Delta_N f(x)=\delta_N^{-2} \sum_a[2f(x)-f(x+e_a)-f(x-e_a)].
$$

This is exactly the original K.10.5f family, with explicit length unit $L$ rather than an unlabelled unit torus. The normalized cell measure is $m_N(x)=1/n$. No continuum limit at fixed physical time is asserted: $\kappa$ and $L$ are fixed, so achieving a fixed positive $\sigma$ requires $t=\sigma N^{2}/(\kappa L^{2})$. All such finite times are individually owned. No strict positive traversal duration is claimed for this native continuous-time local branch.

### 2. Complete local records and uniform local strength

Every directed edge has its own B ordinary event slots plus one overflow slot. Its counter, energy reservoir/receipt, before/after occupancy records and stop flag are local to that edge. The (B+1)st event writes its overflow record and disables only that edge. No remote edge is stopped by this flag. All flags are collected only after the predeclared external time horizon freezes the already nominated local clock services.

Group all orthogonal local history/occupancy sectors into one local CPTP map $\Phi_{e}$: active sectors undergo the specified update and append; stopped sectors are the identity. On the invariant classical response algebra the native generator is $L_e=\kappa(\Phi_e-\mathrm{id})$. Its full native Lindblad extension is $\sum_sJ_s\rho J_s^*-\{\sum_sJ_s^*J_s,\rho\}/2$; equality with $\kappa(\Phi_e-\mathrm{id})$ is not asserted off that algebra. The Heisenberg jump-map cb norm is at most $\kappa$ because $\sum_sJ_s^*J_s\le\kappa I$, and the anticommutator norm is at most $\kappa$. Hence the full local generator has cb norm $\le 2\kappa$ independently of the number of local history states and of $B$. Individual rank-one port counts affect price, not this norm. Each $\Phi_{e}$ has support only on the two endpoint occupancy factors and that edge's records and supplies. The degree is eight and the number of incident directed channels is sixteen, uniformly in $N$. Unchanged core generators and local readout/preparation act at their own sites; none provides a new intersite path.

On the registered classical response algebra an explicit graphical influence bound follows. Potential directed-edge events are independent rate $\kappa$ Poisson clocks; stopped updates may be represented as identity events for this mathematical bound, without asserting physical consumption after stop. To influence a set $S$ from beyond hop radius $r$, the graphical history must contain a chronologically ordered path of at least $r$ edge events. An undirected edge has total event rate $2\kappa$ and there are at most 8 choices per step. A union bound over paths and ordered times gives

 $$
 \operatorname{Prob}[\text{influence from beyond }r]\le|S|\sum_{j\ge r}(16\kappa t)^j/j!\le|S|\exp(16e\kappa t-r).
 $$

For any bounded scalar output $A$ on $S$, changing the exterior initial data changes its expectation by at most $2\lVert A\rVert$ times this probability. This is an exponentially tailed finite propagation estimate with physical velocity $16e\kappa\delta_N$ in the declared edge metric. It is not a strict support cone or the separate serialized minimum-traversal-time branch. Local finite caps can remove updates, but cannot add an influence path. The bounded local CP-generator description also supplies the usual local open-system branch of Appendix F. No full AQFT continuum net is claimed.

### 3. Exact ideal heat trace and calibrated cutoff

Fourier characters exhaust all n modes. Define

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lambda_N(k) &= 4\delta_N^{-2} \sum_a \sin^{2}(\pi k_a/N),\\
P_N(\sigma) &= \sum_k \exp(-\sigma\lambda_N(k)),\\
p_N(t;o,o) &= P_N(D_N t)/n.
\end{aligned}
$$

$P_{N}$ is the diagonal kernel with respect to normalized $m_N$; $p_N$ is the actual ordinary return probability. The factor $n$ is independently known from the physical vertex census, not fitted to the returned signal. Their logarithmic derivatives agree. The original full scalar flow is

$$
D_{s,N}(\sqrt{\sigma})=2\sigma\, \Bigl[\sum_k \lambda_N(k)e^{-\sigma\lambda_N(k)}\Bigr]/P_N(\sigma).
$$

No mode is discarded. For every finite $N$, the formal ultraviolet $\sigma\downarrow 0$ and compact-volume infrared $\sigma\to\infty$ endpoints are both 0. The actual calibrated cutoff scale $\ell=\delta_N$ instead means $\sigma=\delta_N^{2}$ and physical $t=1/\kappa$. Its value is

$$
\begin{aligned}
D_{\mathrm{cut},N} &= 8\, \Bigl[\sum_{j=0}^{N-1} a_j e^{-a_j}\Bigr]\Big/\Bigl[\sum_j e^{-a_j}\Bigr],\\
a_j &= 4\sin^{2}(\pi j/N).
\end{aligned}
$$

This value is not the formal $\sigma\to 0$ endpoint. For example $N=3$ gives $D_{\mathrm{cut},3}=48e^{-3}/(1+2e^{-3})$. No universal cutoff interval $[1,2]$ is asserted.

Under the original full-family mesoscopic limits $\delta_N^{2}\ll\sigma_N\ll L^{2}$, $D_{s,N}\to 4$. At every fixed positive $\sigma$ the heat trace and derivative converge to those on the marked flat four-torus of circumference $L$. These are the accepted K.10.5f Fourier/Taylor/Gaussian conclusions with units restored. The physical-time conversion above is retained in every export, so this does not assert a uniform fixed-$t$ physical continuum limit.

### 4. Finite realization and derivative error

For any registered finite horizon $H>0$, couple the actual local-cap process to the uncapped native reference using the same attempted events and marks. Until the first local overflow all output states agree. A sufficient conservative failure probability is

$$
\delta_{\mathrm{cap}}(N,B,H)\le\Pr[\operatorname{Poisson}(\Lambda_N H)\ge B+1].
$$

This counts every self attempt, not merely token hops. A cap can always be chosen finitely for any fixed $N,H$ and desired positive bound. For instance choose integer $b=B+1\ge 6\Lambda_NH$ and $b\ge\log_2(1/\epsilon)$; then Chernoff and $e<3$ give $\delta_{\mathrm{cap}}\le 2^{-b}\le\epsilon$. Every such $b$ implies a new fully paid finite inventory. There is no infinite-stock exact finite apparatus or uniform resource bound in $N,H$.

For derivative export use the larger near-cap allowance $\delta_*=\Pr[\mathrm{Poisson}(\Lambda_NH)\ge B]$, because an edge with $B$ filled ordinary slots may already have a different next-event update. The same Chernoff recipe applies with $b=B$, and $\delta_{\mathrm{cap}}\le\delta_*$. This avoids deriving a generator error from state total variation alone.

Write $p(t)$ for ideal return probability and $p_B(t)$ for actual capped return probability. Coupling gives $|p_B-p|\le\delta_{\mathrm{cap}}$ uniformly for $0\le t\le H$. The ideal return drift has magnitude at most $8\kappa$ on any position and the capped drift at most $8\kappa$. The two drifts agree on coupled histories before any edge reaches the near-cap sector, giving $|p'_B-p'|\le 16\kappa\delta_*$ at any fixed $t$. Since $p\ge 1/n$ and $|p'|/p\le 16\kappa$ by the complete nonnegative Fourier weights, if $\delta_*<1/n$ then

 $$
 |-2tp'_B/p_B-D_{s,N}(\sqrt{D_Nt})|\le 64\kappa t\delta_*/(1/n-\delta_*).
 $$

This is a finite derivative-response allowance, not an assertion that the capped marginal has exactly generator $Q_{N}$ after overflow. At $t=0$ the logarithmic flow is zero by its continuous limit. Observed score-based finite-difference estimates may instead use the explicit rule in the forward packet, with their own finite-difference error. Neither path conditions on no overflow.

### 5. Actual prediction-task response and finite test map

Let $A_*$ be the protected R14 raw forecast accuracy, derived from its source law in Definition 2.4.1g and Theorem 2.4.1h. The complete token clocks, local supplies and independent flip coins are independent of every core input, motor, reference delivery and fallback. After the diffusion clocks freeze, a local measured occupancy $Z_x\in\{0,1\}$ is held fixed. At the raw second-forecast commitment, the newly supplied native local delivery instrument appends

$$
F'_x=F_x \oplus (Z_x C_x),
$$

where $C_{x}$ is an independent $\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\varepsilon)$ coin, $\varepsilon=1/1024$, prepared before any core target disclosure. The raw core's own forecast, verification, update, stop/failure and timestamps are unchanged by projection; it remains the accepted qualified MPU factor. The whole enlarged apparatus is not claimed to be a new cost-minimal MPU. The delivered forecast is committed before its target and has an actual retained correctness score. The added commit instrument, its coin and all records are expressly new paid source ports, not a post-outcome relabeling.

Conditional on the full token history and its counters, the core law remains the original law and hence $\Pr[F_x=Y_x]=A_*$. Elementary conditioning gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{correct}'_x\mid Z_x]&=A_*-gZ_x,\\
g&=\varepsilon(2A_*-1)>0.
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{correct}'_x]=A_*-gp_x$. In the accepted R14 notation $A_*=1/2+s_{14}/4$, so $g=\varepsilon s_{14}/2$, with $s_{14}$ fixed by that actual core source. This gain is derived, not fitted to heat-trace output. The normalized-kernel extractor is $P_N=n(A_*-\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{correct}'_o])/g$. The calibration/error tuple $(L,\kappa,A_*,\varepsilon,N,B,H)$ is shared by every observable; no separate per-output gain is chosen. Raw qualification and delivered performance are explicitly distinct.

The ordinary local position records also supply the finite capped drift: given all terminal local counters, let $a_{e}=1$ exactly when the edge was cap-eligible for a normal occupancy update immediately before the scheduled timeout, otherwise0. Ignore the subsequently set timeout flag in this pre-timeout eligibility test. Then

$$
d_o=\kappa\Bigl[\sum_{y\sim o} a_{y\to o} Z_y-\sum_{y\sim o} a_{o\to y} Z_o\Bigr]
$$

is the instantaneous backward-generator action on the return indicator. $\mathbb{E}[d_o]=p'_B(H-)$, the left derivative of the pre-timeout capped law. Equivalently this is the derivative of the protocol family as its nominated horizon varies; it is not the zero post-freeze generator of one already stopped apparatus. Its numerical value is bounded by $8\kappa$ in magnitude. The same quantity can be reconstructed from actual delivered correctness scores using conditional independence:

$$
\mathbb{E}[a_e Z_x]=\mathbb{E}[a_e(A_*-\mathrm{correct}'_x)]/g.
$$

Hence the derivative is a retained prediction-response observable with a finite bounded estimator, not a new unobserved analog differentiator. Collecting counters and scores occurs after freezing and does not send a live nonlocal control signal. To compare with the uncapped original formula, apply the near-cap derivative bound already stated.

For any N,H and integer accuracy parameter $r\ge 1$ choose

$$
B=\max\{\lceil 6\Lambda_N H\rceil, r+\lceil\log_2 n\rceil+1,1\}.

Then $\delta_*\le 2^{-B}\le 2^{-r}/(2n)$, including all self attempts. This supplies a finite error-controlled original scalar-response instrument for every member and finite time of the mathematical family. Increasing $N$, $H$ or requested precision changes the inventory and is never free.

A formal forward packet may retain exact predicted return, score and flow expressions with certified rational enclosures, observed intervals for the bounded scores/drift records, their common source errors and a finite compatibility rule. Observed data are not invented. A verdict of interval compatibility remains compatible-unresolved, not a claim of unique microscopic identification. The calibration at $\ell=\delta_N$ must use its explicit finite-$N$ formula; the formal UV 0, mesoscopic 4 and compact-volume IR 0 are different statements and remain separately labeled.

### 6. Physical finite-budget export along the original refinement

The finite-cap errors can be made uniform on each original compact diffusion-time interval $0<\sigma_0\le\sigma\le\sigma_1$. Choose $H_N=\sigma_1/(\kappa\delta_N^{2})$, $r_N=N+40$ and the displayed $B$ recipe with this $H_{N}$. <a id="corollary-k106-certificate-gated-divergent-complexity-cost"></a>**Corollary K.10.6 (Certificate-Gated Divergent Complexity Cost).** On a declared task class carrying certificate $\mathfrak C_{B.2}$, let
$$
\delta_{\mathrm{SPAP}}:=\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}-\alpha\in(0,1).
$$
Theorem 14 and Appendix B, Equation (B.5), give
$$
C_{\mathrm{uni}}(\delta_{\mathrm{SPAP}})
=\Omega\!\left(
\frac{\log(1/\delta_{\mathrm{SPAP}})}{\delta_{\mathrm{SPAP}}^2}
\right).
$$
Consequently $C_{\mathrm{uni}}(\delta_{\mathrm{SPAP}})\to\infty$ as $\delta_{\mathrm{SPAP}}\downarrow0$, so no finite-complexity system in that certified task class attains zero error margin.

*Proof.* By the meaning of the $\Omega$ bound, there are $c>0$ and $\delta_0\in(0,1)$ such that
$$
C_{\mathrm{uni}}(\delta)
\ge c\frac{\log(1/\delta)}{\delta^2}
$$
for $0<\delta<\delta_0$. Both $\log(1/\delta)$ and $\delta^{-2}$ diverge to $+\infty$ as $\delta\downarrow0$, so their positive product and hence $C_{\mathrm{uni}}$ diverge. ∎

<a id="theorem-k107-scope-of-the-frg-to-pce-comparison"></a>**Theorem K.10.7 (Scope of the FRG-to-PCE Comparison).** Let $\Gamma_k$ be an effective average action satisfying the regulated FRG equation
$$
\partial_k \Gamma_k[\phi]
=\frac12\,\mathrm{STr}\!\left[(\Gamma_k^{(2)}[\phi]+R_k)^{-1}\partial_kR_k\right].
$$
This equation supplies a continuum coarse-graining flow. It does not by itself identify that flow with PCE minimization. Such an identification requires a scale-dependent map from retained MPU models to $\Gamma_k$, a declared PCE functional on its image, and a proof that the mapped flow is a descent or stationary flow of that functional. Likewise, identifying RG stationary data with PCE equilibria requires a proved correspondence between dimensionless RG $\beta$ functions and the PCE gradient.

*Proof.* The right-hand side of the FRG equation is determined by $\Gamma_k^{(2)}$ and the regulator $R_k$; it contains no occurrence of $C_P$, $\Delta$, or $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{PCE}}^{(k)}$. Therefore the differential equation alone imposes no variational identity involving those quantities. Near an RG scaling solution, relevance is determined by eigenvalues of the linearized dimensionless beta-function operator, including anomalous dimensions and operator mixing, not solely by canonical dimension. Consequently the FRG equation proves the coarse-graining statement, while every PCE identification requires the additional map and functional identity stated above. ∎

<a id="remark-k107a-categorical-language-for-operational-rg"></a>**Remark K.10.7a (Categorical Language for Operational RG).** A categorical formulation of Theorem K.10.7 requires an explicit identification of its operational coarse-graining. Let $\mathsf P_\Lambda$ be the finite category of MPU-admissible prediction protocols at resolution $\Lambda$, let
$$
F_\Lambda:\mathsf P_\Lambda\to\mathsf{Prob}
$$
assign outcome distributions, and let
$$
q_{\Lambda\to\mu}:\mathsf P_\Lambda\to\mathsf P_\mu
$$
be the finite coarse-graining functor that forgets protocol distinctions invisible at scale $\mu<\Lambda$. For an independently supplied lower-resolution predictive functor $F_\mu$, require a registered natural transformation $\eta:F_\Lambda\Rightarrow F_\mu\circ q_{\Lambda\to\mu}$ with this universal property: for every functor $H:\mathsf P_\mu\to\mathsf{Prob}$ and natural transformation $\alpha:F_\Lambda\Rightarrow H\circ q_{\Lambda\to\mu}$, there is a unique natural transformation $\beta:F_\mu\Rightarrow H$ such that $\alpha=(\beta\circ q_{\Lambda\to\mu})\eta$. On this descent certificate,
$$
F_\mu\simeq \operatorname{Lan}_{q_{\Lambda\to\mu}}F_\Lambda.
$$
Existence of the left Kan extension alone does not identify it with the supplied physical prediction functor. Alternatively, the extension can define a mathematical coarse-graining whose agreement with physical responses remains a separate certificate. On the identified branch, universality classes may be organized as natural-isomorphism classes of lower-resolution prediction functors.

<a id="theorem-k107b-exact-finite-linear-frg-gradient-conjugacy-criterion"></a>**Theorem K.10.7b (Exact Finite Linear FRG–Gradient Conjugacy Criterion).** Let a finite operator truncation near a scaling solution have real coefficient vector $x\in\mathbb R^n$ and linearized dimensionless flow
$$
\dot x=B(x-x_*),
\tag{K.10.7b.1}
$$
where the real matrix $B$ includes all anomalous mixing in the retained truncation. The following are equivalent:

1. there are an invertible response map $A\in GL(n,\mathbb R)$ and a symmetric positive-definite matrix $Q$ such that $y=A(x-x_*)$ conjugates (K.10.7b.1) to the Euclidean gradient flow
   $$
   \dot y=-\nabla V(y),
   \qquad
   V(y)=\frac12y^{\mathsf T}Qy;
   \tag{K.10.7b.2}
   $$
2. there is a symmetric positive-definite matrix $H$ such that
   $$
   HB=B^{\mathsf T}H,
   \qquad
   z^{\mathsf T}HBz<0
   \quad(z\ne0).
   \tag{K.10.7b.3}
   $$

Thus the finite configuration-to-action response is injective exactly when $A$ has full rank, and a strictly convex PCE-gradient conjugacy exists exactly when the complete mixing matrix is self-adjoint and negative in some positive metric. A complex eigenvalue, a nontrivial Jordan block, or a nonnegative eigenvalue of $B$ is an exact obstruction in this class.

*Proof.* If item 1 holds, then $ABA^{-1}=-Q$. Set $H=A^{\mathsf T}A$. Direct multiplication gives
$$
HB=B^{\mathsf T}H=-A^{\mathsf T}QA,
$$
which is symmetric negative definite. Conversely, factor $H=A^{\mathsf T}A$ with $A$ invertible. Equation (K.10.7b.3) makes $ABA^{-1}$ symmetric, and its quadratic form is negative definite. Hence $Q:=-ABA^{-1}$ is symmetric positive definite and (K.10.7b.2) follows. Similarity preserves spectrum and Jordan structure, so each listed obstruction is incompatible with similarity to $-Q$. ∎

The theorem completely classifies the finite linearized truncation, including anomalous mixing. A nonlinear configuration-to-$\Gamma_k$ map, control of discarded operators, and an MPU realization of the selected coefficient coordinates remain the separate bridge data required by Theorem K.10.7.

<a id="corollary-k107c-metric-free-obstructions-to-the-metric-gradient-rg-route"></a>**Corollary K.10.7c (Metric-Free Obstructions to the Metric-Gradient RG Route).** On an autonomous scale chart of Definition X.9.6c.2 with continuously differentiable $\beta$ field $\beta$, suppose that some continuously differentiable positive-definite metric $\mathcal G$ and some twice continuously differentiable potential $V_{\mathrm{RG}}$ satisfy $d_\theta V_{\mathrm{RG}}=\omega_{\mathrm{RG}}=-\mathcal G_{ij}\beta^j\,d\theta^i$. Then:

1. at every zero $\theta_*$ of $\beta$,
$$
D\beta(\theta_*)=-\mathcal G(\theta_*)^{-1}\operatorname{Hess}V_{\mathrm{RG}}(\theta_*)
\tag{K.10.7c.1}
$$
is similar to a real symmetric matrix, so its eigenvalues, the linearized scaling exponents at $\theta_*$ including anomalous mixing, are real and it has no nontrivial Jordan block;

2. $V_{\mathrm{RG}}$ strictly decreases along every nonconstant integral curve of $\beta$, so no nonconstant integral curve returns to a point it has visited.

Independently of exactness, if $\omega_{\mathrm{RG}}$ is closed for a positive metric $\mathcal G$ and $\gamma$ is a nonconstant periodic integral curve of $\beta$ with period $P$, then
$$
\oint_\gamma\omega_{\mathrm{RG}}=-\int_0^P\mathcal G(\beta,\beta)\,dt<0,
\tag{K.10.7c.2}
$$
so the class (X.9.6c.4.1) is nonzero. Consequently a complex pair of scaling exponents or a nontrivial Jordan block at a fixed point, or a nonconstant periodic RG trajectory, rejects the metric-gradient route on that chart for every continuously differentiable positive metric. On the extended-potential treatment of Theorem X.9.6c.3, the extended field $(\beta,1)$ has no zeros and no returning integral curves, so these two tests are vacuous there and that route is tested by the curl condition (X.9.6c.2.6) and the class (X.9.6c.4.1) for the extended metric.

*Proof.* Theorem X.9.6c.3 gives $\beta=-\mathcal G^{-1}d_\theta V_{\mathrm{RG}}$. Differentiating at a zero $\theta_*$, where $d_\theta V_{\mathrm{RG}}(\theta_*)=0$, removes the term containing the derivative of $\mathcal G^{-1}$ and gives (K.10.7c.1). With $G_*:=\mathcal G(\theta_*)$, the matrix $G_*^{1/2}D\beta(\theta_*)G_*^{-1/2}=-G_*^{-1/2}\operatorname{Hess}V_{\mathrm{RG}}(\theta_*)G_*^{-1/2}$ is real symmetric, hence diagonalizable with real spectrum, and similarity transfers both properties. Along an integral curve, (X.9.6c.3.3) gives $dV_{\mathrm{RG}}/d\log k=-\mathcal G(\beta,\beta)$, which is negative wherever $\beta\ne0$. By uniqueness of integral curves of a continuously differentiable field, a nonconstant integral curve never meets a zero of $\beta$, so $V_{\mathrm{RG}}$ is strictly decreasing along it and takes each value at most once. For (K.10.7c.2), $\dot\gamma=\beta$ gives $\omega_{\mathrm{RG}}(\dot\gamma)=-\mathcal G(\beta,\beta)<0$ along $\gamma$; a closed one-form with a nonzero period around a closed curve is not exact, so its de Rham class is nonzero. The extended field has last component $1$, so it never vanishes and $\log k$ strictly increases along its integral curves. ∎

<a id="theorem-k107d-exact-nonlinear-product-action-and-controller-flow-test"></a>

**Theorem K.10.7d (Exact Nonlinear Product Action and Controller Flow Test).** Retain the ideal field, regulator, perspective and forecast preparation families, calibrated coordinates and fixed normalization of Theorem X.8a.5g. Vary the acquisition-start forecast controller $x\in(-X,X)$ and regulator preparation $k\in(0,K)$ independently, with the other source settings fixed. Use the two field coordinates, regulator coordinate, uniform perspective sign and forecast coordinate as source statistics. Put $b=2+k^2$ and retain the reference measure and normalizer of (X.8a.5g.6), with the other three source laws normalized. For the perspective expectation $z\in(-1,1)$, define
$$
I(z)=\frac12\big[(1+z)\log(1+z)+(1-z)\log(1-z)\big].
$$
The complete modified Legendre action of these statistics, subtracting the regulator on its original coordinate alone, is
$$
\Gamma_{x,k}(\phi_F,\phi_R,z,\phi_P)
=\frac12\phi_F^{\mathsf T}A\phi_F+\phi_R^2
+\frac12\log b+I(z)+\frac12(\phi_P-x)^2.
\tag{K.10.7d.1}
$$
It has the following properties.

1. The two-parameter map $(x,k)\mapsto\Gamma_{x,k}$ is globally injective in the fixed coordinate and normalization convention. The regulator-only action (X.8a.5g.7) is independent of $x$, whereas the forecast probe (X.8a.5g.18a) separates every two distinct $x$. Thus the regulator-only projection identifies response-distinct members of this prepared-source family.

2. Formula (K.10.7d.1) retains every operator in these source statistics. For any integer $N\ge1$ and $0<r<1$, put
$$
I_N(z)=\sum_{n=1}^{N}\frac{z^{2n}}{2n(2n-1)}.
$$
Uniformly on $|z|\le r$,
$$
\begin{split}
0\le I-I_N&\le\frac{r^{2N+2}}{(2N+2)(2N+1)(1-r^2)},\\
|I'-I_N'|&\le\frac{r^{2N+1}}{(2N+1)(1-r^2)},\\
0\le I''-I_N''&=\frac{z^{2N}}{1-z^2}
\le\frac{r^{2N}}{1-r^2}.
\end{split}
\tag{K.10.7d.2}
$$
The field and forecast terms are exact polynomials. The Gaussian preparations, uniform sign law, field parity responses, modular-normalizer record and separating forecast probes of Theorem X.8a.5g own the displayed coefficients and their finite-response error records.

3. Write $s=\log k$ here and keep it distinct from laboratory time $t$. At fixed $x$, the original Wetterich equation with its registered regulator gives
$$
\partial_s\Gamma_{x,k}=\frac{k^2}{2+k^2}.
\tag{K.10.7d.3}
$$
For a differentiable controller path $x=x(s)$, the total derivative is
$$
\frac{d}{ds}\Gamma_{x(s),k}
=\frac{k^2}{2+k^2}-x'(s)(\phi_P-x(s)).
\tag{K.10.7d.4}
$$
The path solves the unchanged full Wetterich equation as an identity in all retained expectation fields exactly when $x'(s)=0$. The actual RC law (X.8a.5g.18), under a positive clock conversion $dt/ds>0$, contributes the second term wherever $x\ne0$. Consequently identifying these two clocks does not identify the nonstationary controller flow with this full action flow.

4. On the normalized product probability family, put $a=\frac12\log b$. The Fisher metric and pure-RG coefficient vector field are
$$
\mathcal G=dx^2+2\,da^2,
\qquad B=(0,\,1-2e^{-2a}).
$$
The RG one-form is globally exact:
$$
-\mathcal G B=-2(1-2e^{-2a})\,da=dF,
\qquad F(a)=-2a-2e^{-2a}.
\tag{K.10.7d.5}
$$
The fixed-regulator predictive comparison (X.8a.5g.20)--(X.8a.5g.21) supplies the normalized objective $\bar V(x)=x^2/2$. Its $k$-independent continuation obeys $B\bar V=0$ while $B\ne0$ throughout $k>0$. No positive-definite metric makes $B=-\operatorname{grad}\bar V$ on this chart. The same conclusion holds after adjoining $s$ for every extended potential whose value on each lifted RG trajectory equals this continuation of $\bar V$ up to a trajectorywise constant. On the retained $x$ coordinate at any fixed scale, pure RG has $\beta_x=0$ at every $x$, whereas $d_x\bar V=0$ exactly at $x=0$.

5. A physically varying regulator has a nonconstant preparation charge. The supplied squeeze work (X.8a.5g.29), with the fixed base frequency $\omega_0=2\Omega$, is
$$
W_R(k)=\frac{\hbar\omega_0 k^4}{8(2+k^2)},
\qquad
\partial_s W_R(k)=\frac{\hbar\omega_0 k^4(k^2+4)}{4(2+k^2)^2}>0.
\tag{K.10.7d.6}
$$
This charge belongs to the regulator-dependent part of the full physical ledger, which is constant in the original variable-$x$ comparison. On a differentiable joint $(x,k)$ comparison with the same additive ledger, write
$$
V_{\mathrm{joint}}(x,k)=C(k)+\frac{a_*}{2}x^2,
\qquad
B V_{\mathrm{joint}}=kC'(k),
\tag{K.10.7d.7}
$$
where $a_*=\gamma+2w_Ee_2$ retains (X.8a.5g.20), and $C(k)$ contains $w_EW_R(k)$ and all other $k$-dependent preparation, control and readout charges. For continuously differentiable $C$, a positive-definite metric $H$ on the chart with $B=-\operatorname{grad}_HV_{\mathrm{joint}}$ exists exactly when $C'(k)<0$ for every $k\in(0,K)$; the same criterion holds on the extended treatment of Theorem X.9.6c.3, for extended potentials equal to $V_{\mathrm{joint}}$ up to a trajectorywise constant. With the Fisher metric $\mathcal G$ of item 4, the identity $dV_{\mathrm{joint}}=-\mathcal GB$ fails for every $C$, because the $dx$ components are $a_*x$ and $0$. Since $kC'(k)=w_E\,\partial_sW_R+k\,\partial_k[C-w_EW_R]$ with $\partial_sW_R>0$, remaining charges that are nondecreasing in $k$ give $C'>0$ and reject the joint route for every positive-definite metric. The joint test therefore requires the complete ledger $C(k)$, of which $w_EW_R(k)$ is the evaluated term. Item 4 tests the specified normalized predictive objective.

*Proof.* The independent prepared laws in (X.8a.5g.2)--(X.8a.5g.4), (X.8a.5g.6), the uniform sign preparation, and the forecast law (X.8a.5g.13) give
$$
W_{x,k}(J)=\frac12J_F^{\mathsf T}A^{-1}J_F
-\frac12\log b+\frac{J_R^2}{2b}
+\log\cosh J_\Sigma+xJ_P+\frac12J_P^2.
$$
The Gaussian Legendre maximizers are $J_F=A\phi_F$, $J_R=b\phi_R$ and $J_P=\phi_P-x$. For the sign factor, $z=\tanh J_\Sigma$, so $J_\Sigma=\operatorname{artanh}z$ and $J_\Sigma z-\log\cosh J_\Sigma=I(z)$. Subtracting $k^2\phi_R^2/2$ leaves $(b-k^2)\phi_R^2/2=\phi_R^2$, proving (K.10.7d.1), including its additive normalizer. Equality of two such functions forces equality of their coefficients of $\phi_P$, hence $x=x'$. Equality of their remaining constants gives $b=b'$ and then $k=k'$ on the positive branch. The first paired-probe probability in (X.8a.5g.18a) is strictly increasing on $(-X,X)$ because its reference satisfies $r>X$. Its outcomes therefore distinguish the configurations lost by the regulator-only projection. The modular record (X.8a.5g.9a), its inverse (X.8a.5g.9), and the fixed $Z_0(0)=2^{-1/2}$ retain the normalizer used in this injectivity statement.

For $|z|<1$,
$$
I''(z)=\frac1{1-z^2}=\sum_{j\ge0}z^{2j}.
$$
Integrating twice with $I(0)=I'(0)=0$ gives the displayed series for $I$. The second-derivative remainder is the exact geometric tail. For the first derivative and the value, take absolute values term by term, replace $|z|$ by $r$, bound each denominator below by its first omitted value, and sum the remaining geometric series. This proves all three bounds in (K.10.7d.2). Independence makes the logarithms and their conjugates additive, and every other factor has its exact Gaussian quadratic action. Thus this expansion has no discarded mixed interactions. The named source preparations and the complete finite instruments in Theorem X.8a.5g supply the coefficient and response records stated in item 2.

On the regular expectation chart the full Hessian is $A\oplus2\oplus(1-z^2)^{-1}\oplus1$. Both $R_k$ and $\partial_sR_k$ act on the regulator line, so the full Wetterich trace is
$$
\frac12(2+k^2)^{-1}(2k^2)=\frac{k^2}{2+k^2}.
$$
Differentiating (K.10.7d.1) gives (K.10.7d.3)--(K.10.7d.4). Equality to the trace for every $\phi_P$ forces the coefficient $x'(s)$ of $\phi_P$ to vanish; that condition is also sufficient. By (X.8a.5g.18), $dx/dt=-x/\tau_P$, so $x'(s)=-(dt/ds)x/\tau_P$. This proves the controller-flow test without identifying a scale-dependent cost normalization with a physical charge.

The forecast location score has variance one. The normalized regulator density has precision $b=e^{2a}$ and score $1-bY_R^2$ in $a$. Its expectation is zero, and its variance is two because $\mathbb E(bY_R^2)=1$ and $\mathbb E(b^2Y_R^4)=3$. Independence removes the cross covariance; the fixed remaining factors contribute no $(x,a)$ score. This proves $\mathcal G$. Direct differentiation gives $da/ds=k^2/(2+k^2)=1-2e^{-2a}$ and $F'(a)=-2(1-2e^{-2a})$. The displayed global primitive proves both curl vanishing and vanishing of every period on the chart. For any positive metric $H$, an identity $B=-\operatorname{grad}_H\bar V$ implies
$$
B\bar V=-H(B,B)<0,
$$
contrary to $B\bar V=0$. Every lifted field has nonzero scale component, and an extended potential agreeing with $\bar V$ up to a constant along that trajectory has derivative zero there. The same strict inequality proves the extended statement. Finally $d_x\bar V=x\,dx$ proves the fixed-scale stationary-point comparison.

For item 5, (X.8a.5g.28)--(X.8a.5g.29) give $\rho_k^2=2/(2+k^2)$ and
$$
W_R(k)=\frac{\hbar\omega_0}{4}(\rho_k^2+\rho_k^{-2}-2).
$$
Substitution and differentiation yield (K.10.7d.6). The resource-ownership paragraph following (X.8a.5g.32a) fixes the field, RG and reference calibration protocols in the variable-$x$ comparison and retains their dependence when their own settings vary. The independent regulator programme leaves the forecast quadratic coefficient $a_*$ unchanged. Collecting the remaining terms of the same additive scalarization into $C(k)$ gives (K.10.7d.7). If $B=-\operatorname{grad}_HV_{\mathrm{joint}}$ for a positive-definite $H$, then $kC'(k)=BV_{\mathrm{joint}}=-H(B,B)<0$, because $B\ne0$ for $k>0$. Conversely, let $C'<0$ on $(0,K)$ and put $\lambda=-kC'(k)>0$. The form
$$
H=dx^2+\lambda^{-1}\,dV_{\mathrm{joint}}\otimes dV_{\mathrm{joint}}
$$
is positive-definite, because $dx$ and $dV_{\mathrm{joint}}=a_*x\,dx+C'(k)\,dk$ are linearly independent, and $H(B,\cdot)=\lambda^{-1}(BV_{\mathrm{joint}})\,dV_{\mathrm{joint}}=-dV_{\mathrm{joint}}$, because $dx(B)=0$. On the extended chart, an extended potential equal to $V_{\mathrm{joint}}$ up to a trajectorywise constant has derivative $kC'(k)$ along the lifted field $(B,1)$, and that derivative equals $-\widetilde H((B,1),(B,1))<0$ for every positive-definite extended metric $\widetilde H$ representing the lifted field. Conversely, for $C'<0$ and $B^a=1-2e^{-2a}$, the form $dx^2+(da-B^a\,ds)^2+\lambda^{-1}\,dV_{\mathrm{joint}}\otimes dV_{\mathrm{joint}}$ is positive-definite and sends $(B,1)$ to $-dV_{\mathrm{joint}}$. The $dx$ components of $dV_{\mathrm{joint}}$ and of $-\mathcal GB$ are $a_*x$ and $0$, with $a_*>0$. The decomposition $kC'(k)=w_E\,\partial_sW_R+k\,\partial_k[C-w_EW_R]$ is linearity of the derivative, and $\partial_sW_R>0$ by (K.10.7d.6), so a nonnegative second term gives $C'>0$. The known positive contribution $\partial_sW_R$ does not determine the derivative of the other charges; their complete record is required for the joint test. ∎

The theorem computes the nonlinear action, uniform operator tails and exact RG one-form on the two-parameter prepared-source family of Theorem X.8a.5g. The full-field identity separates its regulator evolution from its nonstationary predictive-controller dynamics. Theorem X.5a.3 supplies the Gaussian source with its unchanged admitted predictive core, counted auxiliaries and full-configuration PCE/action value identity. The present product-source flow test retains its original source and fixed-controller conclusion.

<a id="theorem-k107e-retained-selector-mpu-source-and-full-pce-descent"></a>

**Theorem K.10.7e (Retained-Selector MPU Source and Full PCE Descent).** There exists a finite regular retained-MPU source, formed through the unchanged qualified cores' armed auxiliary port from the actual finite prediction service of Theorem X.5a.3 and Lemma F.1c.6, for which all construction predicates of Theorem K.10.7 coexist. Its physical configuration is the selector probability $p\in I$ between two fixed legal forecast programs. Its full retained source contains the selector and the branch-gated original teacher fields. At every fixed scale the configuration-to-effective-action map is nonlinear and injective; its actual finite generators, coefficient responses and uniformly controlled finite-precision realizations are supplied below. The exact finite conjugate retains all operators, and the compact normal-source comparison has explicit mixed-operator value, gradient and Hessian tails.

Under the source's actual paid-reservation contract, the dimensionless absolute PCE objective is $U(p)=(1-p)c_0+pc_1$ with $c_1>c_0>0$, including selection, preparation, control, record, propagation and final-meter charges with their original D.1 allocation. The actual normalized exponential selector trajectory has $\beta(p)=-p(1-p)(c_1-c_0)$ and full retained response QFI $\mathcal G=dp^2/[p(1-p)]$. The regulator is chosen to be the selector cost insertion $R_s=2s\operatorname{diag}(c_0,c_1)$ with $s=\log k$, constructed in Section 4 of the proof. The scale-dependent map sends this trajectory to the complete joint-field Wetterich flow and obeys
$$

\qquad

$$
The primitive is global on the autonomous probability chart, so its local curls and all periods vanish. The branch contract fixes the two leaves, teacher, geometry, clocks, prices and reservation inventory before varying $p$. Here $I$ is one predeclared open interval with compact closure in $(0,1)$ containing the registered finite-scale trajectories, with one fixed inventory and one absolute objective throughout; its external controls and private apparatus ledger have the response cut specified in the proof.

With this choice of regulator the displayed identity is the variance identity $d\mathbb E_{p(s)}[c_L]/ds=-\operatorname{Var}_{p(s)}(c_L)$ for the cost $c_L$ of the selected program $L$ under the Gibbs tilt $p_i(s)\propto p_i^0e^{-sc_i}$. For an insertion $2s\operatorname{diag}(\tilde c_0,\tilde c_1)$ whose coefficients are specified independently of the costs, the same construction gives $-\iota_\beta\mathcal G=(\tilde c_1-\tilde c_0)\,dp$, which equals $dU$ exactly when $\tilde c_1-\tilde c_0=c_1-c_0$.

*Proof.*

#### K.10.7e — 1. Source inventory and two legal leaves

Fix one finite tensor-Hermite precursor of the source of X.5a.3/F.1c.6, on its fixed graph, fixed positive precision $K$ and fixed volume pairing. Its teacher is the actual commuting finite coordinate tuple $q_N$, prepared by the actual finite compressed unitary generators. Use the finite source after its exact observation/encoder echo and before its final error charge. The cue $b\in\{-1,1\}$ is supplied before the target, independently of $Q$. For a forecast $f$, the prediction is $bf$, emitted before the target $bQ$ is revealed, and the actual retained final charge is

H_f=\frac{E_m}{2}(q_N-f)^TK(q_N-f),\qquad
r(f)=\frac12\sum_a\nu(a)(Q(a)-f)^TK(Q(a)-f).

These are the actual polynomial meter and actual finite outcome law of F.1c.6.F1–F2, not a continuum square substituted into a finite instrument.

Choose a nonzero allowed forecast direction $v$ in the original declared nontrivial signed field neighborhood, with $f_0=m$ and $f_1=m+v$ both legal. The target preparation mean $\mu_N$ converges to $m$ by the inherited finite moment bound. Choose a finite precursor satisfying

Then its exact finite risk difference is

This selection has an explicit terminating rule: use the inherited frozen-template bound $\|\mu_N-m\|\le C_r(N+2)^{-r}$ and take the first integer $N$ with $C_r(N+2)^{-r}<v^TKv/(4\|Kv\|)$, together with the finitely many already registered source/record tolerances. The constants are the finite gate/moment bounds of F.1c.2a/F.1c.6 for the fixed source; increasing $N$ satisfies all conditions. The exact finite $r_i$ are computed from the resulting finite preparation matrices and actual coordinate codebook. They are forward source quantities, not estimates of the subsequently hidden target. The legal source programs, two forecasts, full conditional endpoint states and all fixed charges are frozen before varying the selector. No assumption that $\mu_N$ itself belongs to a lower-dimensional forecast-controller image is used.

The added selector, conditional meter and every extra source gate remain on the existing genuine armed auxiliary port. In the notation of B.8h.0.3, each finite added material generator $G$ is supplied as $P_r(v)P_r(u)\otimes G$, with the original loaded-ROM projectors retained and invariant. It vanishes off the armed sector and equals $G$ on the admitted sector. The existing ready/completion flags are loaded and charged before use. This is an owned interaction with the unchanged cores. The bare auxiliary storage endpoints and all actual conditional energy/load strokes remain those in Sections 2–3. Definition D.1f registers this complete configuration/protocol/resource contract, and D.1g supplies its branch-indexed variational grammar.

The two leaves share one teacher circuit, the same qualified cores and one completion window. Their difference is the existing legal forecast/error-meter setting. Both the cue-dependent predictive service and the original core qualification survive. The selector is committed before any teacher-coordinate readout. No branch is rejected and no failed selection record is discarded.

#### K.10.7e — 2. Exact selector circuit, correlations and preparation work

The response experiment conditions on its externally prescribed preparation setting $p$, exactly as the inherited source conditions on its geometry and forecast program. where the conditional vectors $\Xi_i$ include all host, teacher, cue, fixed leaf-forecast, archive, pointer, phase and service records in this response experiment. Every added operation is a finite unitary with an explicit finite generator. The selector pulse has $G_p=\theta(p)\sigma_y$, so its actual $H_p(t)=\hbar a(t)G_p$. The CNOT has a fixed self-adjoint logarithm of norm at most $\pi$, obtainable by its finite spectral projections.  =\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_fH_f)-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_iH_i).

Conditional gates add the maximum of the two existing finite bounds. Every further finite parameter jet is bounded on the same compact interval. #### K.10.7e — 3. Complete unchanged D.1 objective

Extend the original actual reservation inventory, not the original core complexity operator. <a id="corollary-k108-conditional-rg-universality"></a>**Corollary K.10.8 (Conditional RG Universality).** Suppose a dimensionless RG flow has a hyperbolic scaling solution with a controlled eigenoperator decomposition and a stable manifold. Perturbations along irrelevant eigenoperators decay toward the infrared according to their full scaling exponents, including anomalous dimensions, while relevant directions require a finite set of macroscopic coordinates. This gives the usual conditional universality statement. Interpreting that decay as PCE selection additionally requires the bridge data of Theorem K.10.7.

*Proof.* Linearizing the dimensionless $\beta$ functions about the scaling solution diagonalizes the flow into scaling fields $u_i$ satisfying $\partial_tu_i=y_i u_i+O(u^2)$. Along infrared flow, fields with the irrelevant sign of $y_i$ decay on the stable manifold, whereas the complementary fields parameterize departures from the universality class. The PCE reading is an additional identification because no PCE functional occurs in this linearized RG argument. ∎

<a id="theorem-k109-operational-parameter-information-criterion"></a>**Theorem K.10.9 (Operational Parameter-Information Criterion).** Let $C_P(\mu,\epsilon)$ be the infimum of the predictive complexity of descriptions that reproduce a specified operational observable at scale $\mu$ to error at most $\epsilon$.

1. If $C_P(\mu,\epsilon_0)=+\infty$ for some prescribed $\epsilon_0>0$, no finite-resource protocol realizes that target within the chosen description class.
2. If $C_P(\mu,\epsilon)<\infty$ for every $\epsilon>0$ but $C_P(\mu,\epsilon)\to\infty$ as $\epsilon\to0$, each nonzero precision may remain operationally admissible; only an exact zero-error realization is excluded by this divergence.

*Proof.* Definition K.10.1 requires a finite-resource protocol for every prescribed nonzero error. Thus $C_P(\mu,\epsilon_0)=\infty$ contradicts admissibility at that particular target. In the second case, the definition is satisfied pointwise whenever each $C_P(\mu,\epsilon)$ is finite, even though no one finite protocol can attain the limiting value $\epsilon=0$. These are distinct quantifier statements and prove the two conclusions. ∎

<a id="theorem-k1010-conditional-local-horizon-thermodynamic-gravity-bridge"></a>**Theorem K.10.10 (Conditional Local-Horizon Thermodynamic Gravity Bridge).** Assume the operational-continuum package of Theorem 43.5 and the regular-manifold closure hypotheses of Theorem 44a, together with a Lorentzian continuation, supply a regular Lorentzian continuum branch carrying, at every point and null direction, a local Rindler horizon on the complete hypotheses of Theorems 48a.0, 48a, 49, and 12.1, including the physical boost/KMS identification, the uniform entropy first-variation certificate, and the joint shrinking-patch and uniform Clausius remainder hypotheses; a constant entropy first-variation density; the equilibrium Raychaudhuri expansion with vanishing initial expansion and shear; the local KMS temperature; the Clausius relation for every generator; a symmetric conserved MPU stress-energy source; and the area-density calibration of Appendix E. Then the Jacobson local-horizon argument yields the Einstein equation with a cosmological integration constant on each connected component.
